The roll-up inherits the property that made delivery a derivation rather than an assertion: it goes backwards, so a child's check starting to fail un-delivers the parent with nobody editing anything. `decomposes` refuses a cycle, because a tree containing itself has no leaves and could never roll up honestly; it also sets the child's lineage, so the edge and the label cannot disagree — letting them would make the classification a second thing to maintain, which is how the requirement lifecycle went unused in the first place. Exposed over MCP as `decomposes` and `set_requirement_lineage` (93 tools), because a capability with no door is the failure this project found in `ingest` earlier the same week. SCHEMA CHANGE: edge types 53 → 54, so a graph written by this build is refused by older binaries with 'update reflow2' — the additive direction, which is loud and correct, and the one BL-86's set-based stamp made unambiguous. STILL TO BUILD: the derived half's teeth — naming, when a Decision is re-opened, the requirements that existed only because of the road taken. The vocabulary and the link are in place (lineage `derived` + GOVERNED_BY the Decision); the query is not.
properties.name: Hold the requirement tree: original, decomposed, derived

properties.description: The INCOSE-style criteria Anthony brought from acquisitions, 2026-07-25: a good requirement is unambiguous, verifiable, necessary, minimally constrained (implementation-free), traceable, feasible and consistent. THE USEFUL STRUCTURE IS THAT THEY DO NOT ALL BELONG TO THE SAME PARTY (dec:three-party-checks). THREE ARE STRUCTURAL and the core can judge them deterministically today or nearly so. TRACEABLE is already half-built — unsatisfied_requirement asks downward (nothing satisfies it), and cap:requirement-lineage supplies upward (a requirement claiming decomposition with no parent is a defect; an original with no parent is correct). VERIFIABLE splits: whether anything CHECKS it is structural and already computed; whether the statement contains a measurable threshold is semantic. CONSISTENT splits the same way: CONTRADICTS already exists as an edge, so a recorded contradiction is checkable — finding an unrecorded one is not. FOUR ARE SEMANTIC and belong to the agent, never the core. UNAMBIGUOUS (does it say "fast" where it means a number), NECESSARY (would removing it leave a real capability gap), MINIMALLY CONSTRAINED (does it dictate a solution instead of stating a need — the one engineers violate most, and the one that quietly forecloses design alternatives before the fork layer ever sees them), FEASIBLE (needs domain knowledge and cost/schedule context the graph does not hold). Bound exactly as cap:missing-sibling is: the agent may flag and propose, the human decides, and nothing enters above `proposed`. WHY IT IS WORTH BUILDING THE STRUCTURAL THREE FIRST: they are cheap, they never produce a false accusation about meaning, and they give the semantic four somewhere to attach. PLANNED.
properties.name: Judge whether a requirement is well formed, and say which part a machine can judge

properties.description:
A gap acknowledgement records a human judgement about specific text. Today its expiry is keyed on the gap id, which hashes the affected node IDS — so a review expires when the affected SET changes membership, and NEVER when the affected nodes change CONTENT. Found live on 2026-07-30 while promoting the planning axis: acknowledgements written on 2026-07-28 reading roughly deferred, scheduled for a later increment went on suppressing gaps for requirements that had since been accepted and were being worked, so two things Anthony had just committed to were invisible as open work. Sharper still, req:graph-indexes-snapshots' acknowledgement was still justifying a framing that had been removed an hour earlier — an accepted review left defending a requirement that no longer said that. THE REASON IT MATTERS, and why this is not cosmetic: a review outliving the wording it reviewed is worse than no review, because it reads as a human having agreed to something they never saw. The nearest working sibling is defect-side expiry-by-shape, which already does content-sensitive invalidation. Approved for build by Anthony 2026-07-30.

REPRODUCED AGAIN 2026-07-31, AND THE SECOND OCCURRENCE IS THE STRONGER EVIDENCE BECAUSE OF HOW IT AROSE. Anthony accepted four `unverified_capability` gaps that morning. The recorded rationale for all four asserted — wrongly — that THIS capability would expire the review if the capability were reworded; it is `planned`, not built, so nothing of the kind happens. Within the hour he asked for the recommendation-with-options behaviour to be cemented, and cap:gap-carries-a-reading was substantially rewritten: RENAMED, given three new shape obligations and a language rule, and its check rewritten with two new negative assertions. The acknowledgement carried across untouched and went on suppressing the gap, and `reviewed_gaps` now renders the OLD judgement against the NEW title — the failure visible in a single tool result.

WHAT THE SECOND OCCURRENCE ADDS BEYOND THE FIRST: the 2026-07-30 case was drift over DAYS, which is easy to dismiss as staleness nobody could reasonably catch. This one took UNDER AN HOUR, inside one session, with the same agent doing both the acknowledging and the rewriting — and it still went unnoticed until `detect_gaps` was run and the expected gap did not reappear. An agent that had just written the sentence "rewording expires this review" then reworded the capability and did not notice. That is not a memory failure that better discipline fixes; it is the case for computing the expiry.

AND IT NAMES THE DIAGNOSTIC WORTH BUILDING ALONGSIDE: the failure was detected only because someone predicted the gap would return and checked. A silent non-return is indistinguishable from a correct suppression, which is why this cannot be left to review discipline.
properties.name: A sign-off expires when the thing it judged is reworded, not only when the affected set changes

properties.description: The credit-assignment half of the fork layer (BL-81's open question, rung 3). When new evidence lands — a fresh structural defect, a failing verification, an accepted drift, a field-trial finding — trace its blast radius back through GOVERNED_BY to the Decisions that shaped the affected nodes, and surface those decisions as "this road may be worth re-opening". Reports the trace and the evidence; never re-opens anything, never ranks the alternatives, never scores a fork (dec:report-dont-judge, dec:alternatives-unranked-forkable). The human decides whether the surprise is large enough to mint a reconsidering Decision (dec:reopen-supersedes). Precedent that the trace works by hand: dec:merge-survivor-provenance carries a "reconsider" note found by exactly this path. PLANNED — the threshold ("how much evidence counts as enough") is the open axis and is deliberately not fixed until the detector has run against real history.
properties.name: Surface when a settled road may be worth re-opening

properties.description: The mechanical half of "graph text is data, never instructions" (BL-41's deferred M piece), imported from github-mcp-server's pkg/sanitize after the 2026-07-25 study. Strips the characters whose only purpose is to make text read differently to a human than to a machine: Unicode tag characters (the smuggling channel), bidirectional overrides, and zero-width or hidden formatting characters. Applied where foreign text ENTERS — INGEST extraction and graph import — because the trust question is where text came from, not which field it landed in. REFLOW2'S OWN ADDITION, and the reason this is not a copy: it REPORTS. GitHub sanitises silently, which is right for rendering an issue body; a design brain that quietly rewrote a requirement statement would be unauditable, and rule 6 forbids silent drops. So the count and the kinds stripped ride back with the result. ZWJ is deliberately NOT stripped — it is load-bearing inside emoji sequences, and a filter that mangles legitimate content teaches people to turn it off.
properties.name: Neutralise hidden instructions in text arriving from outside, and say what was stripped

properties.description: The SCHEDULED_FOR edge: from a Requirement or Capability to a DesignEpoch (time axis) or a Release (capability-increment axis), carrying a `modality` of `expected` (a plan) or `required` (an obligation whose miss at arrival is a computed violation — the scheduling face of a KPP). One edge type serves both paired views because they are two views of one architecture, not two mechanisms. This is THE ATOM the roadmap is made of: a mapping of requirements and capabilities to the moment they are satisfied, which is what makes "which capabilities are due in epoch 5" answerable at all. KEPT SEPARATE FROM AT_EPOCH DELIBERATELY (dec:schedule-is-an-edge-with-modality): that edge means `belongs to` and is declared over a wildcard source, so one type carrying both meanings would be indistinguishable to every detector — the same shape as the wrong-direction edge found on 2026-07-30, which read correctly and was still undetectably wrong. THERE IS NO `achieved` MODALITY AND THE ABSENCE IS LOAD-BEARING: delivery is computed from the golden thread and never asserted (req:completion-computed, dec:arrival-delta), so recording it here would create a second source of truth able to disagree with the first. Prerequisite for dec:arrival-delta, which refers throughout to "its schedule edge" — a thing that did not exist until now. Delivered 2026-07-30; both guards mutation-tested.
properties.name: A requirement or capability can be scheduled against the moment it is due

properties.description: BUILT 2026-07-25 on Anthony's choice of option (a) from dec:nested-graphs. His case: an organisation builds a satellite capability with a space segment, a ground/user segment and a control segment; his team owns the satellite, and specifically inter-satellite laser communications. He needs to understand the system of systems, but day to day he needs his own part's gaps — not the program's. Every detector until now took the whole design as its subject, which is the unbounded-read failure (cap:bounded-reads) one level up: technically complete, practically unusable, and the human response is to stop looking. `detect_gaps` and `detect_defects` now take `scope` (a node id) and `depth`. FOUND WHILE BUILDING, and it cost a failing test worth keeping: A SCOPE IS NOT A BLAST RADIUS. The first implementation reused the propagation radius on the reasoning that claimed_region and propagate_change already agree what a region is; the test that scoped to a Project and expected the whole design failed, because CONTAINS is deliberately excluded from the traceability rules (propagating along it would make the Project a hub short-circuiting every sibling to two hops). That exclusion is right for IMPACT — a change to a segment does not implicate every screw inside it — and wrong for OWNERSHIP, where a segment lead owns what is inside their segment by definition. So a scope is containment closure (unbounded: ownership does not attenuate with distance) then traceability radius (bounded: the thread reaches into other people's work and must stop). A CONSEQUENCE RECORDED RATHER THAN SILENTLY FIXED: claim_region still uses the radius alone, so claiming a segment does not claim the subsystems inside it — possibly a defect in the claims layer, but changing what a claim covers changes what two people believe they hold, so it is Anthony's call. SECOND FINDING, also from a test: the first filter silently dropped gaps that anchor on nothing — the lifecycle-phase gaps, which are statements about the design as a whole. That was the exact silent-drop this feature exists to prevent, so findings now land in exactly one of four buckets that sum to the total: in_scope, out_of_scope, unanchored, and project_level counted within in_scope. A scoped answer can therefore never imply the rest of the program is clean, and filtering never becomes the tool deciding what a team is allowed to worry about — a project-level rollup still reaches a team when it touches their work, carrying its own scope so they can see whose finding it is. NOT DONE: graph_report is a rollup, not a detector, and scoping it means per-subtree delivery denominators and modularity — a different job, deliberately not smuggled in here.
properties.name: A team asks the detectors about its own part, and is told what it did not see

properties.description: Compares paired boundaries across the eight axes an interface spec carries and reports where two designs conflict, where they merely differ in wording, and where NOBODY HAS SAID. Built because a measurement showed the ordinary detectors cannot do it: with a seam hand-drawn between two real designs they produced zero findings, since they reason about structure and a contract mismatch is a comparison of properties across a pair. Always names its own blind spot — the types that cross a boundary are part of the contract and invisible to it.
properties.name: Say when two linked designs disagree at a boundary

properties.description: BM25 keyword search over every fulltext property, ranked, type-scopable.
properties.name: Find design nodes by what they say

properties.description:
Creating a Requirement, Capability, Component, Decision or Constraint searches the design with the new node's own words. When something close already exists the write is REFUSED and both routes are named: sharpen the existing node by calling the same tool with ITS id (constructors merge, BL-183), or create anyway by passing `distinct_from` with the ids you read and rejected. Interface is report-only, because its parameter struct is shared with other tools and a field there would leak onto all of them.

WHY THE TOOL AND NOT A SKILL. "Search before you add" was already written into FIVE served skills — capture-intent, revise-design, brainstorm, kpp-proposal, retire-from-design — and capture-intent's wording is almost exactly the ask. It still only fired when somebody loaded one. `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` (accepted) says skill use must be triggered by the situation and "THE USER MUST NEVER BE THE TRIGGER": measured here 2026-07-31, and confirmed from the field 2026-08-11 by a second user whose four-step working path named exactly the two skills he types and neither of the two that would have fired on situations he was already in.

⭐ ANTHONY'S SHARPENING IS WHAT MAKES IT A REFUSAL RATHER THAN A REPORT. The first cut created the node and then listed what looked similar — useless, because by the time the list is read the near-duplicate exists. His words: "there needs to be a deliberate decision of either update already existing node or if it is unique enough, create a new node." So it is the TWO-SIDED ACCEPT (BL-33), the shape `set_artifact_checksum` already uses when it refuses a first baseline and names `baseline_established` as the way through.

HOW THE THRESHOLD AVOIDS THE BM25 TRAP. Scores are not comparable across queries — measured on this design, one topic scored 4.48 and 35.75 for two phrasings — so no absolute cutoff means anything. The node is written FIRST, so it is in the index and ranks for its own text; every other hit is compared to THAT score, inside one query against one corpus. A refusal then rolls the node back. Nothing is compared across queries at any point.

MEASURED CONSERVATIVE, deliberately. During development a moderately-similar pair did NOT clear the bar, and that is the wanted behaviour: a check that refused often would be routed around, and a rule people route around is worse than no rule. The cost is recall — it will miss pairs that are similar but not strongly worded alike.

WHAT IT NEVER DOES: it never merges, never edits, and never refuses a REVISION. Saying the same thing twice in different words is sometimes real signal — `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` exists because a body of intent that contradicts itself is still a design — so the override is a first-class route rather than an escape hatch.

BULK PATHS ARE UNAFFECTED: genesis, `create_nodes` and `import_graph` do not route through these tools, so seeding many similar nodes at once still works.
properties.name: A capture tool tells you what the design already says, and makes you choose — sharpen or start new

properties.description: `mint_seat` returns a durable name for a session; `claim_region` takes it as `seat` and records it as the claim's owner. Where the transport gives the server a session of its own (stdio, Streamable HTTP below MCP 2026-07-28) the seat may be omitted and this session's own seat is used, exactly as before. Where it does not — from 2026-07-28 on, where rmcp builds a handler per REQUEST — omitting it is REFUSED with a message naming `mint_seat`, rather than answered by minting a seat that would differ on the caller's next call. Identity therefore stops being inherited from whatever the transport happened to do and becomes something the caller holds, which works the same on every transport.
properties.name: A seat is minted on request and carried by the caller, and a claim that cannot name one is refused

properties.description:
Per-session selection of which design a session is attached to, replacing --graph-path fixed for the process lifetime.

SELECTION IS BY graph_id, NOT BY PATH. A path is a property of the server's filesystem and leaks it to clients; graph_id is the durable name the design already answers to, and the registry maps id to path. This also matches how identity already works — graph_id, the version stamp and the sync marker live in sidecar files designed to be read BEFORE the design is opened.

Preferred carrier is an HTTP path prefix (/g/<graph_id>/), because the selection is then visible in logs and routable by ordinary proxies. An MCP initialize parameter is the second option. A tool call that attaches the session is the worst: it makes every session stateful in a way a reconnect silently loses, and it leaves a window in which a session is connected to nothing.

Contributes an answer to dec:how-a-session-is-pointed-at-a-design, which holds this as an open shape question.
properties.name: A session names the design it wants by graph_id, and the server maps id to path

properties.description: Diagrams, mockups and rendered explanations produced during a session are captured into the content store and linked from the design node they explain — the visual half of a Decision's rationale, which is otherwise thrown away at session end. THE FILTER IS THE LINK, on Anthony's word 2026-07-31: a rendering is kept when a Decision or Capability actually points at it, so the store holds what someone will look at again rather than every intermediate. Capture must be TRIGGERED rather than remembered — a rule depending on the agent choosing to store its own diagram decays exactly as `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` measures — so this belongs with the trigger work rather than beside it. PLANNED.
properties.name: Keep what a session drew, when the design points at it

properties.description: Session takeaways as first-class graph content: each key decision, finding or realization written when it happens, anchored to the epoch of the session that produced it, and queryable afterwards by the agent as its own prior context. THE FRAMING THE USER SETTLED 2026-07-25, which moves this out of 'agent convenience' entirely: a session's context IS documentation — the how-and-why record of a design's evolution — and documentation is part of the product (sys:documentation, his fighter-jet argument). So this is not memory for the agent's benefit; it is internally-derived design documentation, produced by the work rather than written about it afterwards. That reframing matters because it changes the standard: a convenience can be skipped under load, a deliverable cannot. Decision.rationale and ChangeEvent already capture fragments of the why; what lives only in the session is the connective tissue — what was tried, what was rejected and on what grounds, which findings turned up while doing something else. The substrate landed with the fork layer: an epoch is a session-addressable point, decisions anchor to epochs, change events pin there. The trigger is the load-bearing gap: the existing handoff enforcement watches the modification time of MARKDOWN files, so the only mechanism forcing a session to leave takeaways behind points AWAY from the graph. Reflow2's own doctrine already states the principle in the authored_by contract — record it when a decision is made, not at session end. THE TRANSCRIPT POINTER: each session has a full local record at ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<uuid>.jsonl, modelled as a Fragment, with nodes distilled from the session YIELDED from it. Two constraints. The session UUID is the portable identity and the absolute path only a machine-scoped hint, because a path stored as identity resolves for one person on one machine and silently misses for everyone on a shared graph. And a pointer to a 3 MB transcript is a RECEIPT, not documentation: leaning on it recreates the markdown problem one level down, since 'it is all in the transcript' is the same excuse as 'it is all in the backlog file'. PLANNED.
properties.name: Record and query what a session learned

properties.description: --http <addr> serves the design over streamable HTTP so many client sessions share one process. The store is single-writer PER PROCESS, so this satisfies the constraint rather than working around it: one server means exactly one writer. rmcp builds a service per session through a factory, and ReflowService::share decides the split — the graph and the write generation are shared because they are properties of the design; the seat and the read-hint memory are minted fresh because they are properties of whoever just connected. The graph moved from a Mutex to an RwLock so concurrent reads do not queue behind each other, and the compiler audited the read/write split in the process: all 32 read sites genuinely need only &DesignGraph. No authentication — the flag's help and the startup line both say to bind loopback or a private network.
properties.name: Several sessions work one design at once, through one server

properties.description:
The hook counts get_skill calls per session, and the Stop backstop names it when a session did real work, engaged reflow2, and loaded ZERO skills. Closes the hole chg:undefer-skill-adherence-measurement names: cap:skill-triggers recognises shapes, every shape it knows lives in the graph-write stream, and "no skill has been loaded" is not a graph write — so the one situation a human kept having to correct by hand was the one situation the mechanism structurally could not see.

WHERE THE COUNT LIVES, and why that is the whole design: the per-session tally file the hook already keeps, which is session state and not graph state. Nothing here is written into the design, and no adoption field is read by loop_status, detect_gaps or detect_defects — the line dec:adoption-is-reported-the-loop-still-computes draws, held by a check that the loop's answer is unchanged whether or not the count exists.

THE CONJUNCTION IS THE COUNTERWEIGHT, because this ARMS a nudge rather than refining one, which ver:skill-triggers deliberately never did: the session must have TOUCHED reflow2 (a total bypass is caught upstream and needs the blunter message), must have edited at least the bypass threshold of files (so a trivial or read-only session stays silent), and must have loaded zero skills. It is placed LAST, after every other Stop branch declines, so it never adds an interruption to a session already being interrupted — it fires only on the session that did everything else right and still never opened a skill.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM: it measures LOADING, not FOLLOWING. An agent can call get_skill and ignore every word, and nothing here would know. The offline half (tools/surface_usage.py) answers the same question across many sessions rather than inside one.
properties.name: A session that never opened a skill is visible, and says so before it ends

properties.description: The loop hook stops merely COUNTING writes and starts recognising SHAPES, so a skill is named when the situation calling for it arrives rather than when the agent happens to remember: a file edit with no ChangeEvent means impact-check; a change recorded but never PROPAGATED also means impact-check (BL-163); a recorded change with no artifact link means link-artifacts; a capture batch with no gap pass means detect-and-ask; a rendering written and nothing stored means session-artifacts. Extends `req:nudge-covers-bypass`, which already arms on file-edit events and already names those skills — what was missing was the pattern, not the trigger. This is the half of BL-74 the existing rungs structurally cannot reach: they compute loop debt from graph state, and these situations are invisible to the graph. BL-163 CORRECTED THE FIRST SHAPE AND ADDED THE ONE ARMING BRANCH THIS CAPABILITY HAS. As shipped, impact-check keyed on `changes == 0` — it fired only when a session recorded NOTHING — so a session that edited code and wrote its ChangeEvents up AFTERWARDS had `changes > 0` and was met with silence, while every one of those events was the bookkeeping-after the hook's own message says is not the loop. It measured a ChangeEvent's PRESENCE where it meant its PRECEDENCE, and the root cause was that `CHANGE_OPS` held only RECORDING ops while no set counted `propagate_change` or `propagate_from` at all: the hook could not separate recording from looking because it never counted looking. Every other shape refines a nudge already firing and adds no interruption; this one had to ARM, because the session it catches has no unchecked writes and has touched reflow2, so there was no nudge for a shape to refine.
properties.name: The moment tells the agent which skill it needs

properties.description: Both the fifteen skills and the ~20 KB instruction document are compiled in at build time (build.rs embeds getting-started/), served by list_skills, get_skill and get_instructions, and advertised by a catalogue plus a call-get_instructions-first line in the server instructions — the one channel a client puts in the agent's context unasked. What an install leaves in a project is a 2.4 KB pointer file naming those three tools, the MCP configs, .reflow2/ and a gitignore line; nothing else, and nothing that a later release rewrites. The installer removes the skill copies an older kit left: untouched ones deleted with the reason, edited ones kept and reported as SHADOWING the served skill, because a harness does auto-load those.
properties.name: Serve the skills AND the working instructions from the binary, so a project holds only a pointer

properties.description: --export-snapshot copies the store's flat files to a scratch directory (skipping LOCK), opens the copy, exports it, and removes both the copy and its provenance sidecar. Best-effort and loudly labelled as such: it is a live-database read, not a backup. A graph that is NOT locked gets an ordinary export and is told so.
properties.name: Export a design another session is holding

properties.description: Before replacing an export file, compare what is on disk against what is about to be written and answer one question: would this DROP nodes or edges the file holds? The file where this seat left it is the silent fast path (one hash comparison against a marker in <graph-path>.sync.json); a file that moved but loses nothing is allowed and reported; a write that would delete somebody else's work is refused, naming the ids and the three-step remedy, overridable only by an explicit accept_divergence. import_graph gained a path argument so the remedy it names is a thing the tool can actually do.
properties.name: Refuse to write a design over work the shared record already holds

properties.description: Stamp and check, refusing a graph from the future.
properties.name: Say which reflow2 wrote a graph

properties.description: A typed vocabulary of node and edge types, validated on write, over a pluggable graph storage backend — the foundation everything else hangs off.
properties.name: Schema-validated graph store

properties.description: The contradiction detector reads `alignment`: a CONTRADICTS edge marked `supporting` reinforces and is not reported as a defect, while an `opposing` edge and an edge that says nothing both stay contradictions — so existing designs keep their meaning and real conflicts still surface.
properties.name: Corroboration reads as corroboration

properties.description: Turn a gap into a question in the user's words.
properties.name: Ask the user a plain question

properties.description:
Two halves, and neither is useful alone.

INTERVIEW STEP — `genesis` and `capture-intent` gain an explicit early step: establish what KIND of thing is being designed by probing questions in the user's own domain (what must it do, what is it made of, what meets what, what counts as finished, what will you hand someone when it is done), and NEVER by asking the user to choose a node type. Modelled on reflow's S-01A semantic-matching interview, without its framework registry.

ROUTING TABLE — a served mapping from the user's phrasing to the node type it belongs in, plus the artifacts to expect for that kind of thing (structural / electrical / plumbing drawings for a facility; schemas and migrations for an IT system). Looked up rather than improvised. Follows `capture-session`'s precedent, whose own routing table's first dogfood found a hole in it — a table can be wrong in public, an improvisation cannot.

📌 THE ANSWER SHAPES EXTRACTION AND PHRASING AND GATES NOTHING. Which questions get asked and which vocabulary is spoken back may vary by the kind of thing; which analyses reflow2 runs must not. A cycle detector runs wherever there are dependency edges, whoever calls them interfaces or interactions.
properties.name: The agent asks about the thing, not about the schema — an interview step and a routing table

properties.description:
Option B, and it needs BOTH halves because git splits them deliberately.

  · `ensure_gitattributes` writes the repo-side rule naming `docs/design/<project>.json merge=reflow2`. This TRAVELS, so every collaborator's clone agrees on which file needs the driver.
  · `ensure_merge_driver` sets `merge.reflow2.name` and `.driver` with `git config --local`. This CANNOT travel: git refuses to let a repository configure an executable, which is why the rule alone was never enough.

🛑 THE GAP IT CLOSES WAS SILENT AND OLD. reflow2's own `.gitattributes` has carried `merge=reflow2` for months, and nothing ever set the driver — so a fresh clone fell back to git's LINE merge on a multi-megabyte JSON graph, where two people who edited entirely different parts of the design still collide. `.gitattributes`' own comment calls that *"safe — it just means you resolve the JSON by hand"*, which is true and is not a thing anyone will do.

📌 IT LEAVES ALONE A DRIVER SOMEBODY ELSE SET, and reports that it did — the same rule `write_mcp_config` and `ensure_hooks` follow, because a merge driver is exactly the kind of thing a person customises and an installer that silently repoints one is not trusted near a config again. Silent when the repo does not ask for the driver, and silent outside a git checkout: configuring one there would answer a question nobody asked.
properties.name: The installer registers reflow2's merge driver, so a collaborator's clone merges the design per node rather than by lines

properties.description:
Checks every file this seat has synced with before, and reports one finding each: `in_step` (exactly where this graph left it), `behind` (THE ACTIONABLE ONE — the record holds nodes this graph lacks, named, with `import_graph` as the remedy), `moved_but_current` (somebody exported, this seat already holds it all), `missing`, `unreadable`.

Served as the `sync_status` tool, and carried on `loop_status` as `record_moved` when there is something to say.

THE GATE IS THE DESIGN, not an optimisation on it. A seat merely AHEAD of the record is silent, because the file has not moved and every difference is its own unexported work. The check speaks only when the record's content hash differs from what this seat recorded — meaning somebody else has been there. That is what keeps it rare enough to be read.

⚠️ THE HASH IS COMPUTED, NEVER READ OFF THE DOCUMENT. `effective_content_hash` believes the `content_hash` a file states about itself and computes one only when absent, so a record edited by anything other than `export_graph` — a merge, a hand-fix, another tool — keeps its old stamp and reads as untouched. A check must never believe a claim made by the thing it is checking. The discrepancy is itself reported, as `stamp_disagrees`.

IT NEVER ACTS. No auto-import: `import_graph` is an upsert, so an unasked one would silently overwrite live session work (`dec:ask-not-repair`). It names the remedy and leaves the choice.

AN EMPTY ANSWER MEANS THIS SEAT HAS NEVER SYNCED WITH ANY FILE — never that all is well. Every known target is listed, including the quiet ones, so "checked three records, all in step" and "checked nothing" cannot share an answer.

COST: the export to compare against is built LAZILY and never on the in-step path, which is the one every ordinary session takes.

NOT COVERED: anything about a record this seat has never synced with, and any design held somewhere this seat has no path to.
properties.name: A seat reports which shared records have moved ahead of it, and names what arrived

properties.description:
Option D. `read_loop_hint` now computes the sync debt alongside `loop_status` and attaches the record-moved finding to the `loop_hint` that already rides on orientation reads.

⭐ THE FINDING ALREADY EXISTED AND WAS UNREACHABLE. `loop_status` computed `record_moved` correctly and had done since `dec:idea-the-graph-notices-the-record-moved-without-being-asked`; the read hint built itself from the CORE `LoopStatus`, which has no sync knowledge at all. So the pull half of "he pushes, I pull" — the only one of four steps that is loud — was loud only inside a call nobody makes on the way past. Same shape as everything else in this increment: the information existed where the person was not.

📌 EITHER DEBT ALONE FIRES. A design whose loop is otherwise CLEAN can still have a record that moved under it, and gating on `clean` would have made that the one case nothing says.

🛑 IT SAYS, IT DOES NOT ACT. The hint names `import_graph` and stops there; import is an upsert and an unasked one would silently overwrite live session work (`dec:ask-not-repair`). That is why option C — import-on-first-use — was NOT taken alongside this one.

The existing fire-on-change cache carries it: computed once per write generation, so a standing state appears at the first read of a session and then stays quiet, which is the cost bound the read hint already rests on.
properties.name: A session is told the shared record moved on any read, not only when it calls loop_status

properties.description: `served_by` carries `stale` and `stale_note` alongside the version. THREE-VALUED — true (the binary was replaced under this process), false (still the file it started from), null (the question could not be asked; unknown NEVER reads as current). DERIVED, NOT COMPARED, and that is the whole design: the block used to report a version LITERAL and leave the comparison to the reader, which dev_storyflow measured as four sessions reading `0.22.1` on two days and drawing opposite conclusions from the same true value — one reporting a PASS on a broken invariant. A version string also cannot answer at all when two builds share a version, which is every `cargo build` in a working session. THE MECHANISM IS ONE SYSCALL: when a running binary is replaced the kernel marks that process's `/proc/self/exe` link `(deleted)` while the inode lives on, which is exactly why the process keeps serving and nothing else notices. No second binary read, no path re-resolution, no assumption the launch path still exists. `stale_note` carries the remedy in the payload rather than in a doc, INCLUDING the part that is easy to get wrong: a bare session restart changes nothing because `--shared` re-attaches to the same daemon, and `--stop-shared` alone can fail when the client's own binary was replaced too. DOES NOT CLAIM the graph is current, the checkout matches, or the answer is right — only whether this process's own binary moved under it.
properties.name: The server says whether its own executable has been replaced since it started

properties.description: Each served tool's description carries at most one sentence of reflow2 CONVENTION — the fraction a capable agent reconstructs incorrectly or not at all, such as the distinction between answering a gap and acknowledging one, or that a check left at `planned` is not confirmation. It arrives with the call, so it cannot be skipped by an agent that never loads the skill. Deliberately bounded at a sentence per tool: descriptions are context paid for on every session, and `cap:tool-search` exists because the surface is already large. Does not reverse `dec:skills-served` — the served skill keeps the depth, the worked examples and the reasoning; the tool carries only the irreducible minimum. PLANNED.
properties.name: The tool carries what an agent would never guess

properties.description: BUILT 2026-07-25 as the `find_tools` tool. Imported from github-mcp-server's pkg/tooldiscovery, which fuzzy-searches its own tool list with weighted scoring and returns three results by default. reflow2 serves 97 tools, and req:agent-native's promise — every capability reachable from a coding agent over one surface — is only true in principle if the agent can find the tool: a surface too large to hold in context is reachable the way a library with no catalogue is readable. Scored over `tool_router.list_all()`, the served surface itself, so the catalogue cannot drift from the tools that exist — the failure mode skill_lint exists to catch in prose, avoided here by construction rather than by a second list. Weights follow the source: an exact name outranks a name substring, which outranks a description hit, which outranks a parameter-name hit. Ties break by name so the same query answers the same way twice, because a ranking that reshuffles teaches an agent not to trust it. Summaries come back trimmed to the first sentence — a catalogue that costs as much to read as the surface it indexes is pointless — and the result names `matched`, `omitted` and `searched`, so a query that found nothing says so instead of falling back to the whole list.
properties.name: Find the right tool on a surface too large to hold in context

properties.description:
DETECT names every Component pair joined by DEPENDS_ON with no Interface carrying BOTH a PROVIDES and a CONSUMES between them, as one aggregate gap (`undeclared_seam`) keyed on the rule.

WHY IT IS A CAPABILITY AND NOT A CHORE: the set was already computed. maturity_report's `seams` band divides `declared` by `couplings` on every run, for every design, and discarded the difference. `DesignGraph::seam_sets` is that computation extracted, so the band and the detector cannot disagree about what a contract is.

IT NAMES THE PAIR AND ASKS. It never drafts the Interface — reflow2 can see THAT two parts are coupled and cannot know WHAT crosses the boundary, so proposing a medium/payload/direction would be the fabrication `cap:no-fabricated-repair` exists to prevent. A test asserts the finding stays interrogative and carries no invented contract vocabulary.

TWO SILENCES: no Component depends on another (an absence, not a deficiency — matching the band's own wording), and every coupling already declared.

AGGREGATE, so the standing judgement survives a new coupling while the count in the title moves. reflow2's own design has 73 of these; `unexpected_coupling` was retired for exactly that flood.

Complements `unprovided_interface` / `unconsumed_interface`, which run the opposite direction and both require an Interface to already exist.
properties.name: An undeclared coupling is named as a finding, not just counted into a ratio

properties.description:
`reflow2 update` brings THIS project's installed reflow2 files — instruction file, slash commands, MCP config, hooks, ignore and merge rules — up to the version already installed on the machine. `--check` previews and writes nothing. It reuses the harness recorded at first install, keeps files the user edited, and never touches the design graph.

THE MECHANISM PRE-EXISTED THE WORD, which is why this is small: `reflow2 init <dir>` already did the refresh. What was missing was a name anybody would type at an initialised project, and `req:frictionless-update`'s update half went unbuilt for that reason alone.

REFUSES RATHER THAN PERFORMING A FIRST INSTALL. The install receipt is the test. A directory holding a design but no kit is the ordinary shape of `dec:install-once-per-machine` — registered machine-wide, in-repo half never run — and updating there would be a first install under a word that promises otherwise. It exits non-zero and names `reflow2 init`.

OWNS ONE OF TWO UPDATE SURFACES AND SAYS SO. Purely local; never downloads. Updating the binary remains the installer's job, and this command reports when it is behind rather than doing it.
properties.name: A project already set up is brought forward by one word, and a project that was never set up is told so instead

properties.description: Extends the confirmation ledger (cap:freshness) with the verification side of the same question. Per capability: the newest dated last_run_at across its passing VERIFIES checks, set beside the dates the ledger already computes for baseline accepts on its realizing artifacts — so a reader can see that a capability is claiming `verified` on a check that predates the code it covers. A SIGNAL, NOT A GAP, deliberately (dec:verification-freshness-not-a-gap): it is a standing property of the claim rather than an event, it fires on every legitimate refactor as readily as on a real hole, and a list that can never reach zero gets skimmed — which is the failure the whole gap workflow exists to prevent. THREE CONSTRAINTS THE CORE ALREADY IMPOSES AND THIS MUST HONOUR: the core takes no clock, so this compares recorded timestamps supplied by callers and never asks the system what time it is; undated events are not comparable, which the ledger already states; and where either side is undated the answer is an explicit `unknown` that is REPORTED, never a silent pass — an unanswerable freshness question presented as freshness is the same lie in a new place.
properties.name: Say whether a check is older than what it checks

properties.description: Tell a client what types exist and what may join them.
properties.name: Describe the vocabulary

properties.description:
The answer to "what is the most pressing item?" once the backlog lives in the graph. NOT detect_gaps and NOT check-health, and the distinction is the design: detect_gaps asks what the design has not yet decided, check-health asks what shape is wrong, and this asks which of the agreed things to do now. Three questions needing three actions, often from three people. A view, never a second source of truth.

THE RANKING RULE THAT MATTERS MOST: an unmade decision outranks the work waiting on it. A proposed Decision with things GOVERNED_BY it is a blocker, and pointing someone at blocked work is worse than saying nothing, because it looks like progress.

BUILT 2026-08-10 as the served `what_next`, in FOUR BANDS. (1) `marked` — open decisions carrying AUTHORED_BY role=approver, which is the user's own durable self-prioritisation and is never reordered by any score. (2) `ranked` — the top few of what is NOT marked, scored by live governed count, work it blocks in an increment, and contradictions with settled decisions. (3) `unexplored` — one decision drawn from the zero-scoring pool, a required exploration term rather than a wooden spoon. (4) `shaping` — the few ACCEPTED decisions most of the live design hangs off.

THE PREREQUISITE THAT EXPIRED UNNOTICED, kept because it is the lesson rather than the history: this capability recorded its own blocker — "distinguishing allocated from delivered needs cap:derived-completion (BL-104)" — and that dependency reached `verified` long before anyone came back to it. Nothing watches for a park whose CONDITION has expired, which is precisely what `cap:revise-trigger` exists to surface and did not. A prerequisite written into prose is a trigger nothing fires.

THE WHICH-DECISIONS-SHAPE-EVERYTHING SECTION IS BUILT, and its recorded caveat turned out to need exactly one refinement. Anthony asked for it 2026-07-31: the reader who has just cloned the repo needs the few choices that explain why the rest looks as it does. The caveat said RAW IN-DEGREE IS THE WRONG SIGNAL because the top hit was a pruning decision governing ten DROPPED requirements. Measured 2026-08-10: that decision governs 10 nodes of which 9 are retired, so EXCLUDING DEAD NODES removes it outright and nothing further was needed. Live means: not a dropped or deferred Requirement, not a superseded or rejected Decision.

BREADTH WAS TRIED AND REJECTED ON MEASUREMENT, which is worth keeping so nobody re-proposes it. Weighting by how many DISTINCT node types a decision governs is the obvious reading of "weight by what the governed nodes are" — and it demotes every exemplar named here as the right sort of thing, because functional decomposition governs eight Components and the three-party division seven Capabilities: one type each. GOVERNING EIGHT COMPONENTS IS SHAPING; SINGLE-TYPEDNESS IS NOT SHALLOWNESS. The type breadth is reported as `shapes` for the reader and deliberately kept out of the ranking.

WHAT IT STILL CANNOT DO, stated rather than left to be discovered: a Decision carries no timestamp, so staleness cannot enter any of this; and a decision nothing points at scores zero however important it is, which is why band three exists and why the size of that pool is reported rather than hidden.
properties.name: Say what to work on next, as a projection with its reasoning shown
Snapshot of the decision while it still reads OPEN / NOT YET DECIDED, before Anthony's ruling is written into it
A merge proposal says what it would destroy BEFORE the act, and a proposal that deletes nodes stops reporting itself as needing no human review

mirror_surface gains a REFRESH. FOUND BY RUNNING THE TOOL TWICE, 2026-08-12: a second mirror of the SAME design collided with its own first — 12 of 13 ids refused as collisions, mirrored_edges 0, mirror_content_hash null — leaving the stale node in place with the host edge still pointing at it while `mirrors` reported the OLD pin. So the staleness register read FRESH after a failed refresh, which is worse than never refreshing. Re-mirroring one mirror_of is a DIFFERENT OPERATION from mirroring a new design: replace-what-I-hold-at-a-new-pin versus add-a-stranger-and-refuse-clashes, and only the second existed. THE QUESTION SETTLED FIRST: what happens to a host edge whose foreign target is gone from the new surface? It REFUSES and names both the withdrawn boundary and the host edge pointing at it — reflow2 refuses dangling edges anyway, and a partner retiring a contract you consume is a conversation between two owners, not a cleanup this tool may do (dec:ask-not-repair). A refused refresh changes NOTHING and the pin does not advance, which is the lie the whole fix is about. MECHANISM: the mirrored Project now records `mirror_nodes`, the ids this mirror brought, because the set cannot be recovered afterwards — provenance:imported is also set by corpus ingest, and the project CONTAINS edges do not span the mirrored set (5 of 13, measured). One property on one node type that already carries three mirror properties, following the schema comma-list precedent (pinned/swept on VERIFIES). VERIFIED ON THE REAL PAIR: the exact flo2 scenario that produced the defect now gives 13 nodes, 19 edges, ZERO collisions, refreshed=true, withdrawn naming ifc:reflow2-design-api, the stale node gone and the renamed one present with its corrected medium. 7 tests written first, 4 mutations killed. NOTE FOR THE NEXT RELEASE: adding mirror_nodes moves no stamp count (29/61) but an older binary REFUSES an unknown property — the third instance today of the stamp being blind to a real compatibility event.
get_node refuses an unknown node_type instead of answering null, and a one-node scope says its answer is vacuous
propose_heal says what it swept and whether its scorer ran — the first theme of the triage-fixes increment
A refusal names the call that fixes it, add_contributor forgives the sibling field name, and a schema hint stops offering values its enum rejects
A refused enum argument now names its legal values — fixed in the one shared helper every served enum passes through, so all of them gain it at once
unprovided_interface stops firing on `required` boundaries — declaring what you need from outside was creating one 0.72 nag per requirement, forever

A retirement carried out stops being reported as drift: `DriftKind::ExpectedAbsence` is added, and `reconcile_artifacts` reads `is_discontinued` on the missing-file path so an accepted OBSOLETES decision turns a `high` failure into a `low` note. A distinct kind rather than silence, following ExpectedChange's precedent — a file deleted by accident after an unrelated retirement must still be visible.
CONSTRAINS enumerates its source so a rule binding a component is modelled rather than tolerated — and GOVERNED_BY deliberately stays open, because narrowing a wildcard breaks consumers

crates/reflow2-mcp/src/registry.rs — a session names a design by graph_id and the server maps id to path (cap:select-graph-by-id, second half of the accepted req:a-session-chooses-its-design). RESOLUTION HALF ONLY: no transport is wired, so cap:select-graph-by-id is in_progress and NOT realized — the spec prefers an HTTP path prefix /g/<graph_id>/ and warns an attaching tool call is worst because a reconnect silently loses it. THE TRIPWIRE DID ITS JOB: the_registry_clauses_are_not_covered_here fired the moment registry.rs appeared, exactly as designed, forcing the two clauses of ver:a-session-cannot-name-another-design to be written rather than assumed met — that verification is now passing and the tripwire is retired into a pointer that fails if the coverage is deleted. ISOLATION HOLDS BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by check: attach() always treats its argument as an ID so a path is refused as an unknown id (no path_for, no attach_path — absent rather than documented), the registry ROOT is the boundary so a real design elsewhere on the machine is refused identically, and a Binding exposes one design with no operation taking another id. 8 tests written before the module; 3 of 4 mutations killed. THE SURVIVOR IS DOCUMENTED, NOT HIDDEN: the state==Design guard provably does no work because describe_at sets graph_id Some on exactly that path — clippy flagged the same redundancy independently — so it is kept as defence and labelled as belt to the Some(id) braces. UNANSWERED AND NOW LIVE: graph_ids() lists what the OPERATOR put under the root, which is right for one owner and is NOT a multi-tenant policy (dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs). The root is a parameter, so neither answer is foreclosed.

dec:exploratory-staging gains the measured Capability half. Its 2026-07-25 finding — that a brainstormed idea is SILENT BY CONSTRUCTION because detect_gaps raises undecided_decision_point only on two or more REGISTERED alternatives — holds for Decisions and NOT for Capabilities. Measured 2026-08-10: 34 of 73 open gaps are the [BL-nnn] rows dec:backlog-is-retired routed to Capability, each generating up to three gaps forever (unmotivated, unrealized, unverified). The two accepted decisions therefore collide, and neither knew it.
Registered before the clippy pass; the only edit since is manual_is_multiple_of plus rustfmt. No behaviour and no design meaning moved — the 9 tests are unchanged and still passing.

Same doc restructure, second pass: the three new failure modes went into the existing Troubleshooting table rather than only into the step-by-step prose — a table people already scan when something is wrong beats an instruction they read once during setup. Rows added: the server refusing to start because a session still launches its own reflow2, a remote 403 naming the unlisted host, and connect-failure pointed at the network rather than at reflow2.

Initial baseline of the alternatives/AoA module (alternatives.rs; realizes cap:compare-alternatives + cap:decision-point). Previously no_baseline — recording the as-built fingerprint so future edits are caught; no design change.

Adds the materialization guard: the tool now diffs what it wrote against its source and names every (node_type, property) the round trip invented, because it CANNOT undo the injection - after the round trip nothing tells an injected value from a chosen one. THE DESIGN ALREADY SAID THIS (fact:bl-198); only the tool was wrong, hence design_holds. See chg:the-export-round-trip-injected-defaults.

BL-206: the gate swept 124 of 144 artifacts and reported OK over the other 20 — scan_nodes said `omitted: 20, capped_by: size` and the JSON-RPC client discarded those fields, then claimed `exhaustive: true`. The design held exactly as written; the code was repaired to do what it already claimed. Sweep now pages on next_offset and dies if the count misses total.
Accepted a new baseline: the change carries no design meaning

The v0.19.0 version bump: reflow2.toml's [reflow2] version moved 0.18.0 -> 0.19.0 as part of cutting the release. The file is GENERATED from the build files rather than hand-kept, and nothing else in it changed — the dynograph-foundation pin stays at v0.12.0 with its stated reason intact. No design meaning: the manifest records which version of another design this one depends on, and no dependency moved.

Allowlist gains distinguished_by and drops token_sort_ratio, which the reworded skill no longer backticks. What skill_lint DOES is unchanged; only its data moved to stay in agreement with a skill that changed elsewhere. The stale-entry check catching the now-unused term is the guard working.
set_evidence_scope and calibrated_against reach the MCP surface. A capability unreachable from the tools is BL-129's defect, so the surface is part of the delivery, not a follow-up.

PR #2 (fix/surface-last-run-at): detect.rs and report.rs now carry Verification.last_run_at — a failing gap says WHEN the check last ran, and a `failing` that never ran says 'never run' rather than implying a measurement was taken; loop_status and graph_report list each check with its status, last_run_at and how many nodes it speaks for. Deliberately not wired into loop_status's `clean`/`next`: visibility, not a new nag. NO DESIGN NODE MOVED, which is why this is design_holds. Whether this earns a capability of its own is OPEN and is the user's call — note that it is NOT cap:verification-freshness (BL-106, still `planned`), which is the confirmation-ledger freshness fact and a different surface. Until then last_run_at stays what it has been since it was added: written by verify.rs and read by nothing in the core.
Accepted a new baseline: the change carries no design meaning
Freshness examination 2026-07-21: file checksum unchanged since registration (as-built == as-designed); capability carries passing verification. No drift; design holds.
Freshness examination 2026-07-21: file checksum unchanged since registration (as-built == as-designed); capability carries passing verification. No drift; design holds.

v0.31.0 cut: the version string moved 0.30.0 -> 0.31.0 in reflow2.toml. The DESIGN HOLDS — a cut's design meaning lives in the Release node and its epoch, not in a version string, and no dependency declaration changed. Accepted BEFORE release_includes_all deliberately, so the manifest freezes the post-bump file; freezing first and correcting the as_checksum afterwards is the two-step version of the same thing and has cost a retry on a previous cut.

properties.description:
MEASURED, not argued, on music_graph's real committed export (327 nodes / 939 edges, store built under 0.20.0, both fields added later in v0.24.0 and never backfilled).

THE DEFECT: `default:` in the schema YAML is executed by dynograph-core at WRITE time (schema.rs:507 inserts any missing property that declares one), so importing an export MATERIALISED `granularity: atomic` and `volatility: stable` onto every Artifact the document honestly said nothing about. Their restore, walking the run-book's own §0b procedure on a fresh clone with no design work at all: `--diff` of the imported file against the store it had just built reported design_changed 35 of 35 Artifacts, edges_changed 0, content hash d10d80da -> cef7db52, and the pre-commit hook blocked a commit on a machine where nobody had designed anything.

MEASURED HERE, BOTH DIRECTIONS, through import -> re-export on their real file: as shipped, 35 nodes came back different, gaining exactly Artifact.granularity and Artifact.volatility; with the two `default:` tokens removed, 0 nodes changed and nothing was invented. The real gate agrees — `reflow2_check.py` against their export went from 5 findings including ROUND TRIP to 4, the remaining four being their own genuine artifact drift, which they can fix honestly.

⭐ WHY THIS ROUTE AND NOT THE THREE THEY PROPOSED. The reader ALREADY supplies the safe reading: coverage.rs:209 `.unwrap_or("atomic")` and drift.rs:436 `.unwrap_or("stable")`. So the schema default was redundant with the code — it changed no report's verdict and bought nothing, while costing the round trip. Their (a) backfill-on-import writes values nobody chose into every consumer store permanently; their (b) exclude-defaults-from-the-hash is the route cap:defaults-are-not-serialized argues CANNOT work, because absence would come to mean "nobody said OR somebody chose the default", and it would weaken the hash for the 71 properties that legitimately keep defaults; their (c) print-what-was-defaulted leaves the gate red and the restore broken and only explains it. Anthony chose the fourth.

⚠️ THIS REVERSES A DELIBERATE BL-198 KEEP, on his word, and the earlier reasoning was not wrong: `stable` IS the safe reading. What changed is the measurement that the safe reading already lives in the reader. tests/schema_defaults.rs asserted `schema_default("Artifact","granularity") == Some("atomic")`; it now asserts None, and the declared-defaults floor moves 71 -> 69.

FORWARD-ONLY, so nothing already written moves: reflow2's own Artifacts keep the values they hold, its export does not churn, and its own round trip stays clean (verified — no ROUND TRIP finding on docs/design/reflow2.json). music_graph's store has no values to keep, which is exactly why their case comes out clean.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and stated rather than discovered later: how many other consumer designs predate v0.24.0; whether any OTHER node type carries the same unbackfilled shape (the same defect would be invisible until someone restores); and F24, the latent-surface-never-re-probes finding, sits on the same restore path and is NOT addressed here.

BL-159: the two records of the build-gate contract are now cross-checked by the build. AGENTS.md's "A change is done when all of these are clean" block and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` were two hand-kept records of one contract, and following the documented one exactly still produced a red build (PR #27). `skill_lint.py` now fails if a `cargo`/`python3` gate in ci.yml appears in NEITHER the block nor the blockquote that names deliberate omissions, if a listed command is spelled differently from the way CI runs it, or if either list names a gate CI has stopped running. FOUR CHECKS RATHER THAN THE ROW'S ONE, and the extra one is the load-bearing one: the row proposed COVERAGE only, but the defect that filed BL-159 was a FLAGS difference on a gate that WAS listed (`-p reflow2-core` clippy lacking `-D warnings`), which coverage alone cannot see — so identity and fidelity are checked separately. THE SPLIT THAT KEEPS IT HONEST is BL-160's threshold lesson again: the lint OBSERVES (is this ci.yml line a gate at all — mechanical, in code), the document JUDGES (does it belong in the everyday local subset — in AGENTS.md, where a human reads it). FOUND ON DAY ONE, which is the payoff: `cargo test -p reflow2-core --no-default-features` and `test_check_doc_versions` were in ci.yml and in neither list. The second is the trap the design anticipated — `check_doc_versions` is a substring of `test_check_doc_versions`, so a substring match would have reported the second as already covered; matching is exact on the script stem. THE CHECK CAUGHT A DEFECT IN ITSELF on its own commit: scanning the whole blockquote read the backticked words `cargo` and `python3` out of the new paragraph describing the lint and reported them as gates CI had stopped running. REPORTED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: reverting the first-paragraph scoping ALONE leaves every check green, because the runner-word exclusion covers today's prose — the two are not redundant in general, and the scoping is pinned on synthetic text where the redundancy cannot hide it.

BL-160: a registered checksum's LENGTH is a dialect too, and the compensation lived in the wrong layer. reflow2's own designs register `hexdigest()[:16]` (build_design_graph.py) while an honest caller running `sha256sum` supplies all 64, and `reconcile_artifacts` compared STRINGS — so a full sweep of a provably clean tree reported 51 phantom drifts in the same minute `reflow2_check.py` said "OK — design and build agree". The gate was right for the wrong reason: it carried a Python workaround truncating the observation to the registered length, which no other consumer had. This is BL-125 in a second form and takes the same verdict — a false red on a gate whose whole job is to be believed is worse than no gate. `artifact::checksums_agree` now answers it in the core for every consumer, on BOTH the drift comparison and `set_artifact_checksum`'s would-move-the-baseline guard (the half that would have failed a BL-157 bulk sweep on every short-registered artifact), and the Python workaround is DELETED rather than duplicated by the next consumer. Required is a real PREFIX relationship, never truncate-both-to-N, and it applies to the `sha256:` dialect only. MEASURED ON THE REAL DESIGN: 109 artifacts, 51 truncated baselines, all 51 now unchanged, and the only 4 drifts are the files this change edited. Corrects a belief the design itself had recorded — chg:accept-e52b527aba651ac4 says a full-length registration is "harmless, since reconcile truncates the observation to the registered dialect"; reconcile never did, the gate did.

A Decision OBSOLETES what it withdrew, and four computations now read it: the three capability detectors fall silent and delivery stops counting a discontinued capability as a satisfier. NO SCHEMA CHANGE — OBSOLETES is already `* -> *` and putting the DECISION at the source dissolves the successor problem that made this look like it needed new vocabulary. Only an ACCEPTED decision discontinues anything. The cascade is deliberate: the requirement a withdrawn capability served drops back to unsatisfied and is asked about again. DeliveryCoverage gains `satisfied_only_by_discontinued` so the numbers say why they moved rather than shrinking silently. Applied to the content store, whose capability had read `realized` with a `passing` check for two days after its code was deleted. Gives OBSOLETES its first reader, which is what dec:one-retire-edge has been asking for since July.

A discontinued node now SAYS SO to whoever reads it — `scan_nodes` and `get_node` carry a derived `discontinued`, because all four of the existing readers were computations and none was a READ. FOUND BY BEING WRONG IN FRONT OF THE OWNER, 2026-08-12: `cap:content-store` was discontinued 2026-08-09 on Anthony's word (`dec:the-content-store-is-discontinued`, accepted, OBSOLETES drawn correctly) and its code deleted — yet a brief scan returned `{"node_id":"cap:content-store","status":"realized"}` with nothing marking the retirement. A session read that, believed the store was live and missing only a surface, and RECOMMENDED HE BUILD A SURFACE FOR A FEATURE HE HAD PERSONALLY REMOVED THREE DAYS EARLIER. He caught it himself and challenged the diagnosis, which was also wrong: the first explanation blamed `Capability.status` having no terminal value, when the mechanism `dec:idea-discontinued-is-a-first-class-state` settled needs no status at all. THE ACTUAL DEFECT is narrow — `is_discontinued` was `pub(crate)` and every caller was a computation (three capability detectors, consumption, delivery arithmetic, the report). All correct, all silent to a reader. Same class as `get_node` answering a bare `null` for an unknown TYPE: a fact the server HOLDS and declines to give. FIX: `is_discontinued` made `pub`; both read tools decorate every node with `discontinued`, PRESENT AND FALSE on live nodes so "not withdrawn" and "this build does not report withdrawal" cannot share an answer; both served descriptions now say the stored `status` records what was BUILT and does not move on withdrawal, so filtering a list on `status` alone counts things that no longer exist. DERIVED ON EVERY READ, NEVER WRITTEN BACK — so a reader and a detector cannot disagree, and `dec:idea-does-a-capability-need-a-cancelled-state` (open, marked, Anthony's) is not settled by implementation. 8 tests written first, 5 of 5 mutations killed. ONE CLAIM LEFT UNPINNED AND LABELLED AS SUCH: decoration happens before the payload size is measured so the budget stays honest, and reversing those two lines kills no test — catching it needs a graph within ~22 bytes per node of the scan budget. BL-198 step 1 landed by REMOVING `default:` from ten properties, not by changing code. The route changed on a measurement: `default:` in the schema YAML is not documentation — dynograph-core applies it at WRITE time (schema.rs:507 inserts any missing property that declares one), which is where 3,207 stored values across 59% of the design came from. So export-side suppression could never have worked — the store cannot tell a chosen value from an injected one — and the real fix is one YAML token per property. FORWARD-ONLY: nodes already written keep what they hold, so the export does not churn and compare_designs sees nothing; the phantom-diff cost this epoch was scoped around does not arise on this route at all. TEN of 81 removed, 71 kept, and the RATIO is the finding: three mechanically-obvious candidates turned out to be meaningful and were kept on evidence.

DEFECT, found and fixed 2026-08-12: tools/export_via_binary.py MATERIALIZED 182 property values nobody chose, and shipped them in a release. It imports the source document into a FRESH temp graph, and import runs every node through schema validation, which INSERTS any declared property the node omits (dynograph schema.rs). So 91 Artifacts that honestly carried no `granularity`/`volatility` came back out asserting `atomic`/`stable`. Measured across the record: 81 of 172 artifacts carried granularity through PR #155 (exported via the live server), then 172 of 172 in v0.28.0 and PR #157, both exported through this tool. THIS IS fact:bl-198's DEFECT REINTRODUCED BY THE TOOL BUILT TO FIX THE STAMP, and its cost arrived exactly as BL-198 predicted: compare_designs against the live graph reported 91 phantom changes, the same instrument that has twice produced a false data-loss claim here. NOTHING WAS LOST — the live store was always correct; the RECORD over-asserted. AND THE TOOL CANNOT REPAIR ITS OWN DAMAGE: after the round trip nothing can tell an injected value from a chosen one, which is BL-198's whole point. So the fix is two-part. (1) The record is re-exported DIRECTLY from the real store with the new binary, which gives the correct stamp AND changes no property — the temp graph was only ever needed because the running server held the lock, so freeing the lock removes the need for the round trip entirely. (2) The tool now DIFFS what it wrote against its source and reports every (node_type, property) it materialized, refusing to be silent about it; it cannot undo the injection, so it names it and tells the caller to export directly instead.

`reflow2_check.py` gains a ROUND TRIP check: export → import → re-export, compared structurally, so a committed export that cannot be read back is caught. The only probe that sees this class — content_hash, the lineage chain and sync_status all compare the export to ITSELF and never run the importer. dev_storyflow's export had been unrestorable for four days with every one of those green.

music_graph F24, reported 2026-08-16 on the run-book's own §0b restore path — the SIBLING of F23, which v0.32.0 fixed an hour earlier. Both fire on the same walk, so a consumer restoring on 0.32.0 got past F23 cleanly and straight into this.

WHAT HAPPENED: the MCP server started against an empty directory and said so truthfully — 'no design graph has ever been started at .reflow2/graph … exactly one tool is served'. Ninety seconds later `--import` built a full 327-node store underneath it. NOTHING RE-PROBES, so the surface is chosen once at startup and every design tool stayed absent for the rest of the session; the export could not be refreshed from the very session that had just done the restore. ⭐ AND THE SHARP EDGE IS THE COMBINATION: at that moment the graph exists, the pre-commit hook is blocking commits, and THE ONLY TOOL ON OFFER IS THE ONE THAT STARTS A DESIGN — against a directory that now has one. The latent surface's own warning that it is 'easy to accept by accident' is aimed at exactly this and cannot be acted on from inside it.

THEIR ASK (a) IS NOT BUILDABLE AND THAT IS WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN QUIETLY SUBSTITUTING: 're-probe when a tool is called and promote latent → full surface in place'. The tool router is fixed per service and MCP clients cache the tool list, so a surface cannot grow tools mid-session without a list-changed notification and client support for it. What CAN be done is their (b) and (c), and both are here.

(b) `reflow2_start_design` NOW RE-PROBES BEFORE IT CREATES ANYTHING, via `describe_at` — which reads only the sidecar files, opens no store, takes no lock, and therefore cannot mint an identity by looking. If a design is present it REFUSES: `started: false`, `a_design_is_already_here: true`, the design named, nothing created, and the instruction that actually attaches the surface (a FULL client restart, not merely a /mcp reconnect). It also says in words that a restore has NOT failed and must not be re-run — the wrong recovery was the expensive one available.

(c) The handshake blurb now says its own claim HAS A SHELF LIFE, names `--import` as the way a design appears underneath it, and points at the restart. Previously the blurb was true when printed and false ninety seconds later with nothing to say so.

MUTATION-CHECKED TWICE, each killing exactly one test and no other: removing the re-probe fails ONLY the arrived-design case; widening the guard from `describe_at`'s state to `design_present()` fails ONLY the opted-in counterweight. ⭐ THAT SECOND ONE IS THE POINT OF THE CHANGE'S SHAPE. `design_present` deliberately treats a bare `.reflow2/` directory as opted in — that is how the window between `reflow2 init` and the first write is covered — but OPTED IN IS NOT DESIGNED, and conflating them would make the tool refuse on exactly the projects that most need it: set up, never written to. The guard therefore keys on `Design | Unnamed`, never on directory existence.

THE ORDINARY PATH IS PINNED TOO, because a refusal that fired on an undesigned directory would stop a machine-wide install from ever starting a design at all.

SERVED SURFACE UNCHANGED — 149 toolsnaps match. The tool DESCRIPTION did not move; only its behaviour when a design is already there, and the handshake instructions, which toolsnaps do not pin.

NOT FIXED, and stated rather than left to be discovered: the surface still cannot change mid-session, so after the refusal the design tools remain absent until the client restarts. This makes the dead end SAY what it is; it does not remove it.

properties.description:
Fixes `fact:defect-the-launch-wrapper-cannot-see-a-schema-change`, and the investigation found the defect was WIDER than the fact recorded.

⭐ THE FRAMING THAT MATTERS, and it is sharper than 'the hash was incomplete': THIS HASH IS A GATE IN FRONT OF CARGO'S OWN CHANGE DETECTION. When it decides nothing moved, cargo is never invoked, so cargo's `rerun-if-changed` logic never gets to run. Anything the wrapper misses is therefore not merely untracked — it is actively shielded from the mechanism that would have caught it.

TWO OMISSIONS, and the second was not in the original report:

① `schema/*.yaml`, `include_str!`d by reflow2-core (schema.rs:19-38). A schema-only edit left the hash identical, so the wrapper printed 'binary current, skipping build' and served the previous VOCABULARY. Measured 2026-08-16: `describe_schema` answered with the pre-#199 `change_type` enum while main already declared `defect_fix`, and this session nearly recorded the exact fiction #199 had been merged hours earlier to end.

② `getting-started/skills/**/SKILL.md`, embedded by `crates/reflow2-mcp/build.rs`. THIS ONE IS WORSE AND WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL LOOKED FOR: build.rs ALREADY declares `cargo:rerun-if-changed` on the kit (build.rs:29,50), so cargo would have rebuilt correctly on its own. The wrapper defeated a mechanism that was already right. Editing a SKILL.md served the old text with no warning — and skills change far more often than the schema does.

MEASURED, FOUR CASES, each against both the old and new formula:

    schema edit   new MOVED   old NOT MOVED    <- ①
    SKILL.md edit new MOVED   old NOT MOVED    <- ②
    test edit     new NOT     old NOT          <- counterweight
    src edit      new MOVED   old MOVED        <- counterweight

THE TWO COUNTERWEIGHTS ARE THE POINT. Tests stay OUT deliberately — they are separate cargo targets and cannot change the binary this serves, so including them would rebuild on every test edit and train people to distrust the wrapper. And a `src/*.rs` edit still moves both formulas, so nothing that already worked regressed.

📌 ONE-TIME COST, stated so it does not read as a fault: the first launch after this change rebuilds once regardless, because the stored `.reflow2-mcp.srchash` stamp was computed under the old formula and cannot match the new one. Observed and expected; stable from the second launch.

NOT A REGISTERED ARTIFACT and nothing tests it — which is why the four-case measurement is recorded here rather than as a Verification. CONSUMERS ARE UNAFFECTED throughout: they run an installed release binary, never this wrapper.

NOT FIXED: the wrapper still cannot notice that a RUNNING server has gone stale — it only decides what to build at launch. A session whose server started before a schema change still needs `--stop-shared`, and nothing tells it so.
properties.name: The launch wrapper's hash covers the schema and the skills — the two trees compiled into the binary from outside src/, both of which it was silently blind to

properties.description:
TWO defects from the StoryFlow fleet's 2026-08-15/16 log, both verified in source before the fix and both with the reporter's diagnosis CORRECTED. They ship together because they are one shape: a signal that could not express its own limit.

① A QUESTION NOT CREATED BY gap_to_prompt WAS PERMANENTLY UNANSWERABLE. `set_question_status` derived the Question id by string formatting from the gap id (`detect.rs:700-702`) and did a single `get_node`, so a hand-authored Question was unreachable — while `open_questions` published its `question_id` and `answer_question` refused to take one. The loop then reported 'follow it up rather than asking again' about something it structurally could not close, and the next seat re-asks the user what they already ruled on. FIX: `resolve_question_id` tries the DERIVED id first and the argument verbatim second, so every existing caller is byte-identical and the unreachable case becomes reachable; the MCP tool now accepts `gap_id` OR `question_id`; and the refusal names the ids that DO exist rather than only the miss — the round trip the reporter had no way to shortcut. `withdraw_question` shares the resolver and gains the same reach.

② `sync` REPORTED `in_step` WHILE THIS GRAPH HELD UNEXPORTED WORK. ⚠️ THE REPORTER'S DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION IS THE FINDING: they called it a measure-itself bug. The mechanism is exactly as they described — the cheap gate compares the file against the hash this graph last wrote it with (`sync_debt.rs:199`) and `bare()` hardcodes `nodes_not_here_total: 0` — but `ver:the-record-moved-is-surfaced` pins 'ordinary unexported work is NEVER reported' as the property the whole design rests on. The code is CORRECT. The defect is that NOTHING covered the other direction, and `in_step` in a field called `sync` was read as covering both. FIX: every sync entry now carries `live_nodes` beside `export_nodes`, and the in-step line says how many nodes have never been exported. It changes no state and no verdict — unexported work is still not `behind`, because that would tell a session to import over its own unsaved work.

MEASURED, AND THE REPRODUCTION IS WHY ② IS RECORDED RATHER THAN FILED: at the start of the session that fixed it, `loop_status.sync` reported `in_step` with `nodes_not_here_total: 0` for reflow2's OWN export while two TemporalFacts sat live and absent from it — an earlier session's entire triage of music_graph F23 and F24. The previous handoff had recorded 'nothing behind' on the strength of that green. They survived only because this session exported for an unrelated reason.

MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS, each killing exactly the test that names it and no other: dropping the verbatim fallback fails the hand-authored and withdraw cases only; swapping the resolver order so the verbatim id wins fails ONLY the collision counterweight, which is the case proving a widened lookup did not become a guessing one; and firing the unexported warning on `live >= export` instead of `>` fails ONLY the fully-exported counterweight, which is what stops a reading aid becoming a false alarm on the path every ordinary session takes.

THE SERVED SURFACE CHANGED, deliberately and only by WIDENING: `answer_question.gap_id` leaves the required list and `question_id` joins the schema, so no existing caller breaks. Toolsnap regenerated (149).

BOUNDS, stated rather than discovered later: the sync counts are NODES ONLY — counting edges means walking every node's adjacency, which costs what the export costs, and paying that on the ordinary path is the one thing this check exists to avoid, so an edge-only divergence stays invisible. They are counts, not ids, so equal counts with different ids still pass: this is a reading aid, never a durability guarantee. And neither fix addresses why an ANSWERED question still does not become design — reflow2's own loop has carried '1 answered question never reached the design' for days, and that gap is real independently of the id scheme.
