It'd be like if I requested you to render me an OV-1 of reflow2 right now — you'd refer to the graph and pull what you need; then you'd build me a mermaid diagram or some html file or markdown file to show what the OV-1 is. That being said, sometimes not every systems engineering view is applicable to a given design. Feel like the agent should be able to also say, 'an OV-1 isn't applicable for your design; are you sure you want me to generate?'"*

═══ 📌 THE DOCTRINE THIS RESTS ON, RECORDED SO IT STOPS BEING RE-PROPOSED ═══

**THE UAF/DoDAF VIEW CATALOGUE IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN REFLOW2.** The division is: the GRAPH stores any design structure or content; the AGENT renders the drawing, in whatever medium suits — mermaid, HTML, markdown. Enumerating standard views inside reflow2 would bind a "design anything" tool to one discipline's catalogue, and `req:design-anything` (ACCEPTED) is the requirement that forbids it.
⚠️ **A SESSION PROPOSED EXACTLY THAT AN HOUR EARLIER** — option (c) of `dec:idea-a-view-can-slice-by-altitude-not-only-by-aspect` suggested rendering CV-1/CV-2/CV-3/AV-1 as first-class outputs. **Closed on his word.** It is recorded here because the pull toward hard-coding a familiar catalogue is strong and will recur.

═══ ⭐⭐ THE FINDING: APPLICABILITY AND INVENTION ARE THE SAME QUESTION ═══

`dec:views-are-projections` already holds that **a view is a projection of the graph and renderer fill-ins are DEFECTS**; `cap:bl-40` holds SYNTHESIZE to a no-extrapolation standard.

🛑 **NOW NOTICE WHAT "NOT APPLICABLE" ACTUALLY MEANS.** A view does not apply to a design precisely when the graph lacks the material that view projects from. And if the material is absent, **rendering it anyway REQUIRES the agent to invent the content** — which is the defect the doctrine already forbids. So:

  > *"Is this view applicable?"* and *"would drawing it force me to make things up?"* are **the same question asked at two different times.**

⇒ This is not a new principle. **It is the existing no-fill-in rule moved EARLIER — from a defect caught after the fact, to a question asked before the pen touches paper.** That reframing is what makes it worth building: the rule currently has no moment at which it is enforced, because the only party who could notice is the agent that is already mid-render and motivated to produce something.

⇒ AND IT MAKES APPLICABILITY COMPUTABLE RATHER THAN A JUDGEMENT. *"Does an OV-1 apply?"* is a matter of taste. *"Does this graph hold operational actors, activities and the exchanges between them, and how many?"* is a count. **The second is answerable by reflow2 without reflow2 ever knowing what an OV-1 is.**

═══ THE SHAPE THAT KEEPS THE CATALOGUE OUT ═══

The agent DECLARES the projection it intends to draw — the node types and edge types it will read. reflow2 answers with what it actually holds and what is absent. The agent then either renders, or says *"an OV-1 isn't applicable for your design; are you sure?"* **reflow2 never learns the view's name, so the catalogue stays with the agent and the counting stays with the graph.** That division is the same one `dec:three-party-checks` already sets: the LLM speaks, the graph counts, the human decides.

⚠️ AND IT MUST ASK, NEVER REFUSE. His wording is *"are you sure you want me to generate?"* — a warning with a way through, not a block. Consistent with `dec:ask-not-repair` and `dec:report-dont-judge`. A sparse view is sometimes exactly what the user wants to see; an empty OV-1 is itself a finding about the design.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.
(a) LEAVE IT TO THE AGENT — status quo. It can already look at the graph and judge. Counter: unrepeatable between sessions, and the party judging is the one being asked to produce a deliverable, which is the weakest possible position for saying "this cannot honestly be drawn".
(b) ⭐ REFLOW2 ANSWERS A DECLARED PROJECTION — the agent names node/edge types, reflow2 returns counts and absences. Keeps the catalogue out, makes the answer computable and repeatable. Counter: an agent can declare the wrong projection and get a confident answer to the wrong question.
(c) A SERVED SKILL carries the discipline — a render-a-view skill whose steps include checking the material before drawing. Cheapest, and consistent with skills being where disciplines live. Counter: it is another instruction, and `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` is the standing evidence that instructions lose to urgency.
(d) HARD-CODE PER-VIEW APPLICABILITY RULES. **CLOSED on Anthony's word** — this is the catalogue-in-reflow2 route `req:design-anything` forbids.

🛑 THE LIMIT WORTH STATING: material presence is necessary but not sufficient. A view can be structurally renderable and still be the wrong instrument for the domain — an OV-1 of a machine shop might have actors and activities to draw and still be a category error. **Counting cannot see that; only the human can.** So (b) at its best reports *"here is what I hold and what I lack"*, and the applicability verdict stays with the person — which is the same honest division reflow2 uses everywhere else.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 be able to tell an agent that a requested view does not apply to this design, given "would rendering it require invention?" is the same question as "is it applicable?"
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill. Recorded separately from the altitude-view node because they are separately answerable: reflow2 could learn to report what a declared projection would find without ever gaining an altitude view, and vice versa. The reason this is worth a node rather than a note is the equivalence at its centre — applicability and invention turn out to be one question asked at two times — which converts a matter of taste into a count, and gives the existing no-fill-in doctrine the enforcement moment it currently lacks. Anthony's restatement of why the view catalogue is deliberately absent is recorded here too, because a session proposed hard-coding it an hour earlier and the pull toward a familiar standard catalogue will recur.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-14, after relaying a Grok 4.6 feedback file from one of Alex's projects.

HIS WORDS: *"This type of feedback is generated by the agent for a project via something like the statement of 'reflow2 is still a development project - please note any issues or gaps or opportunities to improve reflow2 at path/to/feedback.md'. Then the agent provides this feedback. It is probably more 'machine-to-machine' type feedback… we should probably formalize this feedback option within reflow2 with the specific direction of that the agent writing it can write it specifically for another agent - this is cutting out the human to provide specific feedback from one agent to another (you in this case), so it can probably be very efficient and remove any fluff that is needed when a human is in the loop."*

═══ ⭐⭐ THE EVIDENCE FOR IT IS ALREADY IN: THE INFORMAL VERSION WORKED ═══

The file this idea came from produced **four independently reproduced defects** (`fact:agent-feedback-corroborated-2026-08-14`) — the near-duplicate guard firing on golden-thread siblings and across node types, `add_decision` unable to merge without resending the body, correct capture inflating loop debt, and `get_node` missing silently on a type with one instance. **A different agent, on a different model, on a different graph, hit four of them the same day without having read the file.** That yield came from an ad-hoc prompt with no format, no channel and no tooling. Formalising raises the yield of something already proven rather than betting on an untested idea.

😀 AND THE CAPTURE OF THIS VERY NODE SUPPLIED A SEVENTH INSTANCE OF ITS OWN HEADLINE DEFECT: creating this Decision was REFUSED as a near-duplicate of `fact:agent-feedback-corroborated-2026-08-14` — the TemporalFact recording that feedback, written two minutes earlier. A fact about what was reported and a decision about what channel should carry it are not the same write.

═══ 🛑 THE COUNTER, AND IT IS ABOUT WHICH HUMAN IS BEING CUT OUT ═══

**Two different humans are in this loop, and only one of them can be removed.**
  · **THE ROUTING HUMAN** — the person who currently has to read an agent's friction note, understand it, and relay it. Removing them is pure gain and is what Anthony is describing.
  · **THE CONSENTING HUMAN** — the person whose project the feedback was written inside. `report-friction` redacts the user's design content and **never files without asking**, and the Grok file honoured that unprompted: *"Per report-friction: do not open a public issue without asking. This file is the local log."*

⚠️ **A channel that carries agent-authored feedback off the machine without that second human is an exfiltration path**, however good the intent. `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` exists for exactly this, and the file shows the discipline working — *"Product/design content is summarized by type and count, not quoted."*
⇒ THE HONEST FORM: **the agent WRITES freely for another agent; the human still decides whether it LEAVES.** Efficiency is gained in the authoring and the reading, never in the consent.

═══ 🛑 A SHARPER COUNTER TO "REMOVE THE FLUFF" ═══

**What made that file valuable was not its brevity — it was that its claims were CHECKABLE.** Item 5 named the tool, the arguments and the observed result (`get_node({node_type: Project, id: "proj:…"})` → `{node: null}`), so it could be re-run here in one call and confirmed on reflow2's own graph. Its neighbours that were only narrated could not be.

⚠️ **Optimising for compactness could delete precisely what made corroboration possible.** The right target for a machine-to-machine format is REPRODUCIBILITY, not terseness: tool name, arguments, observed result, expected result, and an honest *what I did not check*. The Grok file has all of those — including a *"Gaps (mine / process)"* section admitting it skipped `compare_designs` and guessed a Project id. **That self-reporting is not fluff, and it is the first thing a brevity-optimised format would drop.**

📌 IT ALSO SEPARATED CONFIRMED FROM UNCONFIRMED WITHOUT BEING ASKED. Its `get_instructions` truncation report did NOT reproduce here — the payload arrived complete — which is only discoverable because the report was specific enough to test. A format should make that distinction structural rather than leave it to the writer's conscience.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.
(a) EXTEND `report-friction` WITH AN AGENT-TO-AGENT MODE — one skill, a second output shape aimed at a maintainer's agent rather than a maintainer. Cheapest, and it inherits redaction discipline already written and honoured in the field.
(b) A NEW SERVED SKILL, leaving `report-friction` human-facing. Cleaner separation; two skills that must not drift apart.
(c) A STRUCTURED FORMAT (fields, not prose) so the receiving agent can parse and triage rather than read. Highest leverage for the receiver. ⚠️ The four corroborated items were reproduced from PROSE that happened to name tools and arguments, so a schema helps only if it MANDATES exactly those fields.
(d) A GRAPH NODE TYPE for feedback. 🛑 Blocked by a real constraint: the authoring agent works inside SOMEONE ELSE'S design, so the note cannot be a node in reflow2's graph without crossing a boundary. It must travel as a DOCUMENT — the same wall `dec:idea-a-top-level-graph-holds-what-the-component-graphs-share` hit, where nothing crosses between graphs but a published surface.
(e) LEAVE IT AD-HOC — the prompt already works. Counter: it worked because Anthony happened to ask for it and happened to relay it. Nothing makes that repeatable, and the second and third user reports both arrived as email.

📌 THE CONSENT HALF IS ALREADY AN OPEN NODE, AND ALEX ASKED FOR IT HIMSELF: `dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded` — *"put in an update that asks me if I want to collect feedback and store my decision in the graph."* **This is the CONTENT half of the same mechanism: his node decides whether feedback may travel, this one decides what it says and who it is written for.** Neither is built.

⚠️ THE STANDING REASON THIS MATTERS: every defect in the last two increments was found by a first-time user, by running two real projects at each other, or by an agent writing down what fought it — none by reading code, none by a gate.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 formalize agent-authored feedback written FOR another agent, and what exactly is gained by cutting the human out of the loop?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill. Two counters are recorded ahead of the options because both cut against the framing rather than against the idea, and an implementer reading only the proposal would miss them: "cutting out the human" describes two different humans and only the routing one can go, and the value of the example file came from its reproducibility rather than its economy — so a format optimised for the stated goal of removing fluff would likely delete the self-reported process gaps and the tool-and-arguments detail that made four items checkable in a single session. Kept separate from `dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded` because that node asks whether feedback may be collected at all and this asks what it contains and who writes it for whom.

properties.decision:
✅ **DECIDED 2026-08-14 ON ANTHONY'S WORD, ON THE TWO SETTLED HALVES. The third sub-question is SPLIT OUT to `dec:idea-is-allocation-running-ahead-of-the-seams` (parked, trigger named) rather than left holding this one open.**

THE IDEA, Anthony's words 2026-08-08: *"the allocation of functions to systems/services should be done as late as possible (agreeing that doing it at genesis is too early). I feel like doing it at the last possible moment before functional allocation to system/service is the right call."* It answers a caution raised against `dec:idea-the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph`, which proposed asking at GENESIS what quality attribute a system is for: the objection was that at genesis you frequently do not know yet, and premature commitment costs as much as late discovery. His resolution keeps the question and moves WHEN it is asked — to the moment allocation must actually be committed.

THE HOOK ALREADY EXISTS: `unallocated_capability` is already a detected gap, so "capabilities exist, bound to nothing" is visible from graph state alone — the same state-not-history discipline `dec:loop-status-state-not-history` commits to. Nothing new needs remembering.

**(a) PER-PROJECT OR PER-CAPABILITY — SETTLED 2026-08-08. PER-CAPABILITY SCOPE, PROJECT-LEVEL DEFAULT, RE-ASKED ONLY ON DIVERGENCE.** The schema already leans this way: DimensionAssessment attaches to ANY node, not to the Project, and a telemetry path and a config service in one system genuinely want different objectives. The recurrence worry — a mature design allocates continuously, so the moment repeats — is answered by machinery that already exists: an acknowledgement LAPSES when the shape it was accepted about changes, so the answer is recorded once and re-asked only when a new capability diverges. Recurring without being repetitive. ⚠️ Held most loosely of the three by the person who proposed it, and worth revisiting if the divergence test proves hard to state.

**(b) IS 100% ALLOCATION AGAINST 0% SEAMS AN INVERSION — MOVED OUT 2026-08-14 to `dec:idea-is-allocation-running-ahead-of-the-seams`.** It is unanswerable from data the graph holds: 156 ALLOCATED_TO edges carry only `weight_basis`, nothing dates an allocation, and 1 of 320 ChangeEvents mentions one. Its trigger is "allocation timing becomes recordable at all". **Splitting it is the ruling: two settled halves should not read as undecided because a third is blocked on a substrate that does not exist.**

**(c) A DESIGN THAT NEVER REACHES THE MOMENT — CLOSED 2026-08-08**, answered by doctrine that already existed. `maturity_report` deliberately refuses to say where a design SHOULD be, and its own output says a demonstrator *"may sit here forever and be right"*. So never allocating is a **LEGITIMATE TERMINAL STATE**, not an error or a stalled process. The only thing any future prompt owes is to be acknowledgeable like every other gap — which every gap already is.

⚠️ **COUNTER-ARGUMENT, RECORDED BESIDE THE RULING RATHER THAN ANSWERED BY IT, AND FLAGGED TO HIM BEFORE HE ACCEPTED:** the last-responsible-moment principle assumes deciding late costs less than deciding wrong, which holds only when deferral is free. Here it may not be — artifacts get written against an assumed structure long before anyone calls `allocate`. **If real files already embody a de facto allocation, then deferring the decision defers only the RECORD of it, and the graph arrives late to something the build already did.** That is the as-designed-versus-as-built gap `granularity_report` exists to surface, and it argues the trigger should watch **ARTIFACTS APPEARING** rather than the `allocate` call. Accepted with this open.
properties.name: DECIDED — allocation is deferred to the last responsible moment: per-capability scope with a project default, and never allocating is a legitimate terminal state
properties.rationale: Revised under revise-design with a snapshot taken while all three sub-questions still read open (epoch:allocation-subquestions-narrowed, seq 289), so the state before the narrowing survives. Status stays `proposed` deliberately: two sub-questions closing does not settle the parent, and flipping it would assert a decision Anthony has not made. The most valuable thing added is not either answer but the finding under (b) — that the agreed method could not be executed, and why. A parked question with a stated trigger is recognisable when someone walks past the answer months later; a parked question with none is indistinguishable from a forgotten one, which is a distinction reflow2 cannot currently draw at all (detect_defects reports parked decisions as `orphan_node`, info severity, and two of the four outstanding structural defects are exactly that).

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. Raised by an external agent-side field report, 2026-08-11 (fact:external-agent-side-report-2026-08-11, redacted).

WHAT THEY OBSERVED. Several of their acknowledgements carried explicit retirement conditions written into the reason — of the shape "revisit when the first implementation exists", "replace this when that work is scheduled". One of those conditions had been true for weeks and nothing surfaced it. `reviewed_gaps` says an acknowledgement is "worth re-reading when the design shifts" and nothing detects the shift. Their line: acknowledgements are where gaps go to be forgotten SAFELY, and the safety decays silently.

⚠️ NARROWER THAN THEY WROTE, AND THE NARROWING IS THE POINT. Expiry machinery EXISTS: a review expires when the set of nodes it judged changes, and `req:set-scoped-acknowledgement-keys-on-its-rule` (accepted) already fixed the case where a set-scoped acknowledgement expired merely because the design grew. So this is NOT "acknowledgements never expire". It is that the trigger is always the same trigger — the affected set moved — and a human-stated condition ("when an artifact of this kind first appears") is invisible to it. Recording the narrow version matters, because the wide version reads as a defect in something that works.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) A typed re-review trigger on the acknowledgement: a node type appearing, a count crossing zero, an edge arriving. Expressive, and it is a small query language nobody asked for — every one of those is a new thing to specify, validate and explain.
(b) No new vocabulary: have `loop_status` flag acknowledgements older than N design-changes as re-review candidates. Crude, cheap, and it needs no condition to be stated correctly at write time — which matters, because the person acknowledging a gap is the least likely to predict what would falsify it.
(c) Let the acknowledgement name the NODE TYPE it is waiting on, and nothing more. Covers the reported case exactly ("when the first artifact exists") at a fraction of (a)'s cost.
(d) Nothing. `req:review-expires-when-what-it-judged-changes` is already proposed and unbuilt; finish that before adding a second expiry axis beside it.

⚠️ THE TRAP: a stated condition that is WRONG is worse than no condition, because it reads as watched. An acknowledgement saying "revisit when X" that nothing evaluates is the same false-assurance shape as a `planned` verification silencing a gap — which this project already refuses. Whatever is offered must actually be evaluated, or must not be offered.

📌 SITS BESIDE `req:review-expires-when-what-it-judged-changes` (proposed): that one is about the trigger being too NARROW (only the set, not the content). This is about the trigger being SINGULAR. Same subsystem, different complaint, and they should be read together.
properties.name: OPEN — should an acknowledged gap be able to declare a machine-checkable re-review trigger, rather than stating its retirement condition in prose?
properties.rationale: A real acknowledgement carried a condition that came true and nothing noticed. But expiry machinery exists and works on a different trigger, so the honest finding is that the trigger is singular rather than absent — and a stated-but-unevaluated condition would be a worse failure than the current silence, because it would read as watched.

properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony thinking out loud 2026-08-08, immediately after `dec:an-unplanned-cut-slips-every-later-increment-by-one` was accepted and applied, and in direct response to the id-churn cost that applying it exposed. HIS WORDS: "if we can't slip a version, just add the in-between version like v0.25.1 for the planned change, then preplanned versions can stay in place (their id stays the same) and we can add unplanned versions as v0.25.1 or v0.26.4 or whatever makes sense - I'm sure this has a drawback also as it probably doesn't fit when you should do a minor bump versus whatever the third decimal place is called." (The third decimal is the PATCH number, semver's MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.) THE IDEA: an unplanned cut is numbered BETWEEN the planned ones rather than consuming one of them, so `epoch:v0260-planned` stays v0.26.0 forever, its id keeps matching its content, and nothing renumbers. WHAT IT SOLVES, and it is the real prize: the id churn is not merely reduced, it is ELIMINATED — no renaming, no risk to the snapshot history `dec:arrival-delta` reads plan movement from, and no ids that lie about their content. It also removes the cascade entirely: today's slip touched four epochs, and a scheme where planned numbers are stable touches none. THE DRAWBACK HE NAMED HIMSELF, AND IT IS REAL AND MEASURABLE ON TODAY'S CUT: patch is not a free slot. This project's CHANGELOG defines its own buckets — patch is "bug fixes, doc fixes, tests, refactors, perf, and behavior changes that make a silent failure LOUD", minor is "a change to the SHAPE of the tool surface (new/changed params, changed result shapes)". v0.25.0 was MINOR by that table for exactly two reasons: `HealProposal.would_destroy` and `HealIssue.hubs`, both new result fields. Everything else in it was fixes. So v0.25.1 would have been WRONG for what actually shipped — by a hair, and the hair matters. THE HARM IS CONCRETE RATHER THAN PURIST, and the same table states it: patch means the consumer "updates blindly; skills and calls unchanged"; minor means they "may need to notice". Numbering a shape change as a patch tells Alex he can update without looking when a result shape moved. That is a signal saying SAFE without having checked — the failure family this whole session kept finding. OTHER SHAPES, none chosen: (a) HYBRID — insert as a patch when the unplanned work genuinely IS a patch (the common case), slip only when it is genuinely minor (rarer). Keeps ids stable most of the time and keeps semver honest; costs two rules instead of one and a judgement at each cut, though that judgement is one the CHANGELOG table already forces. (b) DISSOLVE IT — name planned increments by CONTENT and assign the number at cut time from what actually shipped (`dec:idea-a-planned-increment-is-named-by-content-not-by-number`). Then neither slipping nor inserting is a problem, because no plan ever holds a number it can lose. This is the only option where the question stops existing rather than being answered. (c) REDEFINE THE BUCKETS — pre-1.0 semver gives latitude and the project has not made a stability commitment ("Major 1.0 — Deferred"), so it could declare that 0.x.y patch admits additive-but-non-breaking changes. Cheapest to write and the most expensive to be wrong about, since it weakens the one signal consumers act on blindly. (d) KEEP THE ACCEPTED RULE and pay the id cost, treating ids as birth numbers rather than delivery numbers. WORTH NOTING: (a) and (b) COMPOSE — content-named plans plus semver-honest numbering at cut time is arguably the same answer reached from two directions.
properties.name: OPEN — should unplanned work take an IN-BETWEEN version (v0.25.1) so planned increments never renumber, instead of slipping them all up one?
properties.rationale: Recorded as an idea rather than as a change because Anthony was explicitly thinking out loud, offered the counter-argument himself in the same breath, and the accepted rule it revisits was settled minutes earlier. Nothing is superseded: `dec:an-unplanned-cut-slips-every-later-increment-by-one` stands and the slip has been applied. What makes this worth a node rather than a passing remark is that it is a genuine alternative to a rule with a known cost, and the cost is what prompted it — so a later session choosing between them needs both on the record, with the semver objection attached to the idea rather than lost in conversation.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony, 2026-08-04: "It's weak at holding what we learned about the tool while using it, because that lands in markdown by convention, and markdown doesn't get queried — it gets grepped, by someone who already knows what they're looking for. this needs to be solved. I wanted to stop using the BL, but it keeps growing as you say - instead, I wanted everything in the graph." His preference is stated and is NOT recorded as settled: what "everything in the graph" means mechanically is the open part.

THE MEASUREMENT, taken 2026-08-04. `docs/backlog.md` is 3,350 lines / 581,031 bytes across 132 rows. Of the 8 rows filed in one session (BL-205..212), SIX are referenced by ZERO graph nodes. The file is not a registered Artifact, so `coverage_report` does not count it and no checksum tracks it. FOUR things were re-derived in that same session that were already written down somewhere: BL-205 (third rediscovery), `dec:export-once-per-pr` (accepted, invisible, violated and then re-announced as new), BL-70's alternatives family (nearly re-proposed), and dev_storyflow's hand-made doc-intent scope table (re-derived worse from filenames).

THE FRAME IS ALREADY ACCEPTED AND THE BACKLOG VIOLATES IT. `dec:what-lives-where` states the rule: "the design record should stop being PROSE YOU NAVIGATE and become A GRAPH YOU QUERY, with the prose kept as provenance hanging off the nodes it produced." It carries a falsifiable test — "IF REFLOW2 WORKS, STORYFLOW WOULD NOT HAVE NEEDED dev_storyflow… If a user still ends up splitting their repo to stay sane, reflow2 has not delivered what this decision claims." THE SAME TEST GENERALISES AND REFLOW2 CURRENTLY FAILS IT ON ITSELF: if reflow2 works, reflow2 would not need a 581 KB markdown backlog. It is also the exact failure the dev_storyflow api-boss measured in that fleet's MEMORY.md — "an index that must be read IN FULL to be useful has a hard ceiling", 20 KB against a 17 KB limit with everything past the line silently invisible. The backlog is 29 times that size.

WHY IT HAS RESISTED THE OBVIOUS FIX — A BACKLOG ROW IS NOT ONE THING. Reading the eight rows from one session, they are at least four: (i) DEFECTS AGAINST SHIPPED CAPABILITIES (BL-205 loop_status too large, BL-206 the gate's truncated sweep, BL-208 the inert CI guard, BL-209 the blind orphan detector); (ii) UNBUILT WORK (BL-186 the folder driver, BL-211 genesis-from-a-folder); (iii) OPEN DESIGN QUESTIONS (BL-207's fix-shape fork); (iv) DISCOVERED LIMITS (BL-212, chronology cannot be recovered from a folder). Three of those four already have a home: unbuilt work is a Capability at `planned` behind a Requirement, an open question is a `proposed` Decision — which is what this very node is — and a discovered limit is a Constraint or DesignRule.

⭐ THE ONE THAT HAS NO HOME, AND IT IS THE LARGEST CATEGORY: a defect found by USING the tool. reflow2 has no way to say "this capability is built, VERIFIED, and does not do what it claims." `Verification` answers whether a check passes — and every one of BL-205/206/208/209 sat under a passing check. `DriftEvent` answers whether the code moved away from the design — and in all four cases the code and the design AGREED, and both were wrong. HEAL's issues are computed from graph shape, not recorded observations, so they vanish between runs. That absence is why these rows land in markdown: there is nothing to write them to.

OPTIONS, none chosen. (a) ROUTE EACH ROW TO THE TYPE IT ALREADY IS and add no vocabulary. Cheapest, and it works for three categories of four. Counter: for the defect category it loses the finding — "this is broken, here is the measurement, here is how it was found" becomes "here is a need", which erases the evidence and reads as intent rather than as a bug. (b) A `Finding`/`Defect` NODE TYPE carrying claim, evidence, when observed, and what it bears on. Counter, and it is strong: this project has proposed a node type and WITHDRAWN it after measuring TWICE in one week (`Attestation` → `TemporalFact`, `Hazard` → `DesignRule` + `CONSTRAINS`), so the prior against new vocabulary is heavy — and `TemporalFact` ("a time-bounded assertion true only between two epochs") may already be the shape, since a defect is exactly "this was true of the build from epoch X until the fix". (c) EVERYTHING BECOMES A PROPOSED DECISION. Counter: 132 proposed Decisions would swamp `where-am-i` and the decision list, and most rows are not forks between real alternatives. (d) KEEP THE MARKDOWN BUT DERIVE IT FROM THE GRAPH rather than maintaining it by hand. In-house precedent exists and is unused for this: `dec:views-are-projections` ("a view is a projection of the graph; renderer fill-ins are defects") and `tools/render_views.py` already render DoDAF-flavoured views into docs/viewpoints.md. The backlog is simply not one of them. Counter: this solves RETRIEVAL and not CAPTURE — it only helps once the content is in the graph, so it composes with (a)/(b) rather than competing. (e) DO NOTHING AND ACCEPT THE COST, recorded so it is a choice rather than a default: the backlog is readable by a human today, and the re-derivation cost, while real, has been paid without anyone stopping work.

--- ADDED 2026-08-04, ANTHONY ASKED WHAT A NODE AND AN EDGE CAN ACTUALLY HOLD. THE ANSWER IS THE CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPES EVERY OPTION ABOVE, AND IT IS MEASURED. ---

WHAT A NODE CAN HOLD. The schema's whole type system is `string` (170 declarations), `enum` (89), `float` (34), `bool` (10), `int` (7). There is NO dedicated text type and NO `max_length` anywhere in any schema file — `string` IS the narrative field and it is unbounded in practice: the `decision` property of this very node runs to several thousand characters without complaint. Every type carries at least one narrative-shaped field (`Decision.decision` + `.rationale`, `Requirement.statement`, `Capability.description`, `Component.purpose`), and Decision requires only `name` and `decision`. AND THE SCHEMA IS ADDITIVE: dynograph-core's own test is named `extra_properties_allowed` — "Extra properties should be allowed (schema is additive)" — so a property the schema never declared is stored rather than refused. It validates the TYPES of declared properties and enforces the required ones; anything else passes through.

WHAT AN EDGE CAN HOLD. More than assumed: 44 of the 60 edge types carry properties, across 46 distinct property names, and several are free text — `note`, `evidence`, `rationale`, `diff_summary`. SIXTEEN CARRY NOTHING, and they are all bookkeeping or temporal: AT_EPOCH, HAS_SNAPSHOT, VALID_FROM, VALID_TO, ABOUT_ENTITY, OCCURS_DURING, PERFORMED_IN, and — worth noting against [BL-212] — PRECEDES. The edge that would say "this document came before that one" can carry no evidence for the claim.

⭐ THE STING, AND IT IS WHY THIS BELONGS ON THIS NODE RATHER THAN AS TRIVIA: ONLY 52 PROPERTIES IN THE ENTIRE SCHEMA ARE `fulltext: true`, and those are the only ones `search_design` indexes. The distribution is name 20 · description 12 · statement 5 · summary 3, then singletons: rationale, decision, purpose, question, evidence, intent, effects, design_intent, criteria, context_setter, answer, title. So `Decision.decision` IS indexed and — measured — `Decision.rationale` is NOT. Every "why" written into a rationale field is stored and unsearchable. The same is true of any extra property invented under the additive rule: stored, not indexed, not returned by `describe_schema`, read by no report. That is this project's recurring declared-and-read-by-nothing shape one rung worse, because it is UNDECLARED and read by nothing.

THE CONSEQUENCE FOR EVERY OPTION ABOVE: UNLIMITED PROSE IN A NODE IS GREP BY ANOTHER NAME. What makes the graph queryable rather than navigable is the `fulltext:` flag, the typed properties and the EDGES — not the narrative. Moving the backlog into nodes therefore helps only to the extent a row becomes STRUCTURE: which capability the defect bears on (an edge), what was measured (a typed property), whether it is still true (a status or a temporal bound), with the prose hanging off that as explanation rather than as the record. A row moved in as one long `description` rebuilds `backlog.md` inside the graph with worse ergonomics and no gain — and that failure would be invisible, because it would look like progress.

AND IT PUTS A NUMBER ON THE DEPENDENCY WITH `dec:idea-embeddings-adoption`: with 52 lexically-indexed fields and no vector half, "query the graph" today means ranked keyword search over names, descriptions and statements. Better than grep — cross-node, ranked, no filename needed — but the same KIND of retrieval. The ceiling on "an agent can work from the graph alone" is set by that open question, so the two ideas should be weighed together rather than separately.

WHAT MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED WHEN THIS IS PICKED UP: `dec:what-lives-where` (the accepted rule and its falsifiable test), `dec:views-are-projections` plus `tools/render_views.py` (the rendering half already exists), [BL-198] (a serialized default is indistinguishable from a choice — the same "what does the graph actually record" family), and [BL-209] (22 Decisions invisible because `AUTHORED_BY` counts as attachment — a graph-native backlog would land straight into that blind spot and must not).
properties.name: OPEN — should the backlog stop being a 581 KB markdown file and become graph nodes, and what is missing before it can?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill at Anthony's request. The load-bearing content is the taxonomy and the single gap it exposes: three of the four kinds of backlog row already have a node type, and the fourth — a defect in a capability that is built, verified and wrong — has none, which is why those rows have no choice but to be prose. Recording the measurement (581 KB, 6 of 8 rows with zero graph representation, four re-derivations in one session) so the next session argues from numbers rather than from the impression that the file is getting long. Extended 2026-08-04 with the data-model constraint Anthony asked for — free text is unbounded and the schema is additive, but only 52 properties are indexed and `rationale` is not one of them, so the answer turns on how much of a row becomes structure rather than prose. Note the irony worth keeping: this rationale is itself unsearchable.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-14.

═══ ⭐⭐ ADDED 2026-08-14 (LATER, SAME DAY): HIS INHERITANCE-VERSUS-COMPOSITION FRAMING, WHICH CUTS AGAINST DEPTH AND IS THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT ON THIS NODE ═══

HIS WORDS: *"it reminds me [of] a python class that inherits another class that inherits another class and on (depth). this is different from composition architectures where there is no inheritance and everything is horizontal. In [that] case, is it good that reflow2 is horizontal or would there be some advantages in making things have some level of depth?"*

⇒ **THE ANALOGY IMPORTS A SETTLED ENGINEERING ARGUMENT, AND IT ARGUES FOR THE SHAPE REFLOW2 ALREADY HAS.** "Prefer composition over inheritance" is doctrine because deep hierarchies are rigid: the taxonomy has to be right before the work is understood, a change to a base ripples to every descendant, and the ladder is expensive to re-cut once things hang off it. **On that reading reflow2's flat shape is not a deficiency to be corrected but the safer default**, and the burden falls on anyone proposing depth to say what it BUYS.

⚠️ **BUT THE ANALOGY IS IMPERFECT IN ONE SPECIFIC WAY, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS LOAD-BEARING.** In code, inheritance and composition are ALTERNATIVES — two ways to reuse behaviour, and picking one excludes the other. In this graph they are NOT alternatives, because they answer different questions: `CONTAINS` says *what is this made of*, `DEPENDS_ON` says *what does this need*, and a design legitimately has both at once. So "horizontal versus vertical" is not the same trade as "composition versus inheritance", and reading it as one would make depth look like a competing architecture when it is an orthogonal axis.

⭐ **WHERE THE ANALOGY DOES BITE, EXACTLY: `DECOMPOSES`.** That edge is the one relation here that behaves like inheritance — a child decomposes a parent and **delivery ROLLS UP**, so satisfying every child satisfies the parent. That is a base-class contract with arithmetic attached, and it is brittle in precisely the way deep inheritance is. **AND THE COST IS NO LONGER HYPOTHETICAL — IT WAS PRICED THE SAME DAY:** `req:decomposition-covers-its-parent` → `cap:decomposition-coverage-is-asked` (built 2026-08-14, PR #181) exists because the roll-up never checks that the children AMOUNT TO the parent, so a requirement split into two children addressing a tenth of it reports `delivered` the moment both close. **Depth buys computable roll-up and costs the risk that the roll-up lies.** That is the trade, stated in one line, and it did not exist on this node before he raised the analogy.

📌 SO THE QUESTION IS NARROWED, NOT ANSWERED: not *"should the design be deeper?"* but **"which of the three depth ladders earns its brittleness?"** — and each is separable. `CONTAINS` (assembly) is cheap and carries no arithmetic. `DECOMPOSES` (requirement roll-up) is the expensive one and now has its counterweight built. `Component.level` / `Capability.tier` are labels that compute almost nothing today.

═══ 🛑 RE-MEASURED 2026-08-14 AFTER HIS QUESTION — AND A THIRD UNUSED LADDER APPEARS ═══
```
DECOMPOSES ................ 0        (requirement lineage: original 164, decomposed 0, derived 0)
Component.level ........... component 48 · subsystem 8 · system 0 · SoS 0 · enterprise 0
Capability.tier ........... operational 147 · UNSET 14 · strategic 0 · tactical 0   <- NEW
Component CONTAINS ........ 42 edges over 8 parents (of 56 components)
lateral ................... DEPENDS_ON 178 · ALLOCATED_TO 178 · SATISFIES 192
PART_OF_FLOW .............. 0   (zero Flow nodes)
```
⚠️ **`Capability.tier` WAS NOT ON THIS NODE BEFORE AND IS THE SHARPEST INSTANCE: 147 of 161 capabilities carry `operational` and NOTHING carries `strategic` or `tactical`.** A three-value ladder holding one value is not a shallow hierarchy, it is an unused field — and it is the SAME vocabulary Alex's tier request (`dec:idea-a-top-level-graph-holds-what-the-component-graphs-share`) would reach for. **Measured separately the same day: `Capability.tier` carries no schema description at all**, so nothing tells an agent what it means or how it relates to `Component.level`. Three ladders exist, and all three are close to empty.

⇒ **THE HONEST READING OF ALL THREE NUMBERS: reflow2's design is not flat because someone weighed depth and chose against it. It is flat because the depth vocabulary was never filled in.** That is a different fact from "horizontal is right here", and it means the composition-versus-inheritance question **cannot be settled from this design's shape** — the evidence is absence of modelling, not evidence of a considered choice. Which is exactly what option (b) below already warned it would be measuring.

════════════ THE ORIGINAL CAPTURE, 2026-08-14 ════════════

HIS WORDS: *"I almost want 'missing the wood for the trees' to be a skill of reflow2. that sometimes somebody becomes so wrapped up in some little detail that they forget the big picture… another way to look at it is 'breadth' vs 'depth' of a design… you can probably error in going too far in one dimension without considering the other dimension - need to find the correct balance. not sure if there is a way to measure in a graph depth vs breadth? if it can be measured, then there probably becomes a ratio of depth-to-breadth that is ideal to maintain. maybe in a graph you can count all the nodes (peer to peer nodes and this is your horizontal score). then count all the components nodes that make up a system (kind of looking at system-of-systems to systems to components and so on) and this is your depth score."*

═══ ✅ YES, IT IS MEASURABLE, AND HIS PROPOSED SHAPE IS THE RIGHT ONE ═══

Run on reflow2's own export (`c18a4a1`, 2026-08-14):
```
DEPTH                                   BREADTH
  Components ................ 56          lateral edges ........... 203
  component CONTAINS ........ 42            DEPENDS_ON 178 · CONSUMES 15
  MAX NESTING DEPTH ......... 2             PROVIDES 6 · INTERACTS_WITH 4
  components with no parent . 14          hierarchical edges ...... 122 CONTAINS
  DECOMPOSES edges .......... 0                                     + 0 DECOMPOSES
  Component.level used: component 48, subsystem 8
                        system 0, system_of_systems 0, enterprise 0
  Requirements 164 · Capabilities 161, all at one level
```

🛑 **REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN IS ALMOST PURE BREADTH.** 164 requirements with **zero** decomposition; 56 components nested at most **two** deep, using two of five `level` values; 14 components parented by nothing. **The project built around `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` — *"nested as deep as the design needs"*, which Anthony called *"one of the primary things I designed it for"* — has a flat design.**

═══ ⚠️ A CORRECTION MADE BEFORE THIS NODE WAS SAVED, AND IT MATTERS ═══

This session first wrote that the blind spot had **doubled from 6 to 14** since 2026-08-07. **That was wrong.** `fact:defect-allocation-health-is-green-over-an-empty-structure` already recorded BOTH numbers on the same day — `components_outside_any_subsystem: 6` and `component_roots: 14` — as two different measures, not a before and after. **The truth is less dramatic and arguably worse: the numbers are IDENTICAL a week later.** `hierarchy_issues` 0, roots 14, max_depth 2, `DECOMPOSES` 0 — a fully measured defect, unchanged.
📌 The error was caught by the near-duplicate guard surfacing that node — the same guard this session has documented firing wrongly seven times today. **Here it was right, and it prevented a false claim entering the record.**

═══ WHAT IS GENUINELY NEW HERE, beyond the 2026-08-07 measurement ═══

  · `Component.level` uses **two of five** values — nothing is a `system`, `system_of_systems` or `enterprise`. The ladder his idea depends on is three-fifths unused.
  · **Lateral 203 vs hierarchical 122** — the breadth/depth contrast stated as a single comparison, which is his proposed metric and which nothing computes today.
  · `DEPENDS_ON` has grown 171 → 178 in the week while `DECOMPOSES` stayed at 0. **The design is getting wider and no deeper**, which is the trend his idea is for and which no report shows.
  · 📌 **IMMEDIATE CONSEQUENCE FOR WORK ACCEPTED EARLIER TODAY:** `cap:decomposition-coverage-is-asked` is planned to ask whether a decomposition's children cover their parent. **With 0 `DECOMPOSES` edges it cannot be dogfooded on this graph at all** — it would ship doing nothing here and nobody would notice. Not an argument against building it; an argument for testing it elsewhere. (BUILT 2026-08-14, PR #181, and it shipped saying exactly this about itself.)

═══ ⚠️ THE "IDEAL RATIO" IS THE OVERFIT THIS IDEA EXISTS TO PREVENT ═══

**A depth-to-breadth target derived from any one design is exactly the specialisation Anthony warned against in the same message.** A house, a beamline, a shop and an MCP server share no natural proportion, and `req:design-anything` forbids binding the tool to one discipline's habits. Two recorded failures agree:
  · `evaluate_allocation` reports **modularity 1.0 from `total_internal: 1, total_external: 0`** — a perfect score over ONE dependency while the graph holds 178 `DEPENDS_ON` edges. **A ratio over a starved denominator is that failure again.**
  · BL-5's lesson, in `detect.rs`: **a loud detector needs a different QUESTION, not a tuned number.**

⭐⭐ **THE ANTIDOTE IS ALREADY BUILT: `granularity_report`.** It answers a structurally identical question — *is the build coarser than the design?* — and its contract says *"IT NEVER SAYS 'monolith', 'too big' or 'split it', carries NO severity… THERE IS NO SIZE THRESHOLD: artifacts are compared against THIS DESIGN'S OWN DISTRIBUTION."* ⇒ **A breadth/depth measure should report the numbers and the design's own distribution, name what it cannot see, and refuse a verdict.** No universal ideal, no target, no severity. `fact:defect-allocation-health-is-green-over-an-empty-structure` reaches the same conclusion from the other side: *"what is wrong is a metric reporting a value at all when its denominator is one, instead of saying it has too little to measure."*

═══ AND ON THE SKILL ITSELF ═══

⚠️ **A SKILL ALONE REPEATS A FAILURE THIS PROJECT HAS MEASURED REPEATEDLY.** "Step back and look at the whole" is exactly what a session under load stops doing; `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` exists because an agent keeps adding nodes while the loop silently stops, and `dec:idea-a-capture-session-skill-the-user-types` settled that the manual trigger is the only one not depending on the mechanism that keeps failing. **A wood-for-trees skill nobody remembers to invoke is the joke telling itself.**

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.
(a) **A USER-TYPED SKILL, NO METRIC.** Cheap, reliable trigger (human). Counter: tells the user little they did not already suspect when they typed it.
(b) ⭐ **MEASURE + SKILL, ON `granularity_report`'s NO-THRESHOLD SHAPE** — report depth, breadth and this design's own distribution; refuse a verdict; the skill puts the question. Counter: needs an honest answer to *what counts as depth* while `DECOMPOSES` is unused and `Component.level` is three-fifths empty — today it would mostly be reporting **absence of modelling** rather than a property of the system. ⭐ **THE RE-MEASUREMENT ABOVE STRENGTHENS THIS COUNTER: with `Capability.tier` also one-valued, ALL THREE depth ladders are near-empty, so a measure shipped today would report unfilled fields in three places and call it shape.**
(c) **A RATIO WITH A TARGET.** Argued against above on this node's own evidence.
(d) **NOTHING — `where-am-i` re-orients already.** Counter: it reports what the design SAYS and has no notion of proportion; it surfaced none of the numbers above.

📌 THE HONEST OPEN QUESTION UNDER ALL OF IT: is reflow2's flat shape a DEFECT, or a correct reading of a system that genuinely has 56 peer components and little natural hierarchy? **The measure cannot answer that and must not pretend to** — which is why `granularity_report` refuses a verdict, and why this stays a question rather than becoming a check. ⚠️ **AND THE RE-MEASUREMENT NARROWS EVEN THAT: with three ladders unfilled, the flatness is at least partly unmodelled rather than observed, so this design cannot be the evidence either way.**
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 measure a design's BREADTH against its DEPTH and prompt a step back? It is measurable, reflow2's own design is nearly all breadth, and an "ideal ratio" would be the overfit the idea exists to prevent
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill and measured on reflow2's own export before anything was written, because the central question — can depth and breadth be counted — is answerable rather than arguable. The measurement confirmed his proposed shape works and showed this design is nearly all breadth despite being built around recursive decomposition. A wrong claim is recorded in the node rather than quietly dropped: this session asserted the unparented-component count had doubled, and the prior fact node showed both figures were taken the same day, so the real finding is that a fully measured defect is unchanged a week later. The "ideal ratio" half is argued against rather than deferred, since a target derived from one design is the specialisation he raised the idea to avoid, and `granularity_report` already demonstrates the correct pattern — report the distribution, name what cannot be seen, refuse the verdict.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled.

THE OBSERVATION: capabilities form a DEPENDS_ON DAG that detect_defects insists stays acyclic, and NOTHING ever asks what order it implies. reflow2 can say what is scheduled for an increment (SCHEDULED_FOR) and what is delivered (the golden thread), but not what can be started.

THE IDEA: dynograph_graph::topological_sort — Kahn's, deterministic (lexicographically smallest order), returns None on a cycle. Two distinct uses:
(a) A SIMPLIFICATION available today: budget.rs:312 hand-rolls Kahn's algorithm in about forty lines with a comment that says so. The foundation exports it.
(b) A NEW capability: given the capabilities scheduled for an increment, a valid build order — and the frontier of what has no unbuilt dependency, which is "what can I pick up now".

WHERE IT LANDS: BL-68 (TRL/MRL readiness gating) is about whether something is ready; this is about whether its DEPENDENCIES are ready, which is the other half of the same question. Also epoch planning.

CHEAP for (a). Moderate for (b), which needs a scope (a whole design? one increment? one component's subtree?) and a rendering.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS: (a) is not free — the local version works on string-id arcs while the foundation one needs a Graph built through GraphBuilder, so it trades forty lines of Kahn's for an impedance adapter, and the local one is already tested. (b) risks asserting a schedule reflow2 has no business asserting: a topological order is ONE valid order of many, and presenting it as THE order would be the same overreach dec:report-dont-judge exists to prevent. The honest output is probably the READY FRONTIER (what is unblocked) rather than a full ordering.

Filed as a backlog row on Anthony's word (2026-08-01) — the work is tracked; the shape, especially frontier-vs-order, is open.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 answer "what order can this increment be built in, and what is buildable now?"
properties.rationale: Found by grepping reflow2 for any existing ordering concept and hitting a hand-rolled Kahn's in budget.rs — evidence both that the need is real and that the foundation function was not known to be there.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's idea, 2026-08-15, framed by him as aspiration rather than intent — his own words end "but I don't think we are there yet", preserved here as part of the idea rather than trimmed off it.

HIS WORDS: "in some designs, actual design reviews are done and official direction to proceed and other formal docs are required (coming from the US Air Force and US Space Force, documentation is required — maybe we can eventually get to where the graph tracks authorizations to proceed or other official acquisitions documents are in the graph and organizations trust the graph to hold such docs and therefore, keeping external docs is no longer needed — but I don't think we are there yet)."

DELIBERATELY DISTINCT FROM `rule:design-information-lives-in-the-graph-not-in-documents`, which the guard named because this node cites it. THAT RULE GOVERNS THIS REPOSITORY and is settled and enforced. THIS IS A QUESTION ABOUT THE PRODUCT, in a domain where a document is not a convenience: a signed authorisation to proceed is what makes work lawful to start, and whether an organisation will rely on a graph instead is a question about trust, audit and legal standing rather than about storage. The rule can hold while this stays open, and it does.

WHAT ALREADY POINTS THIS WAY, so the starting position is not zero: `Contributor` with `AUTHORED_BY role: approver` records whose sign-off a node carries and when (`acted_at`); `Decision` with `status: accepted` records that something was settled and by whose word; `DesignEpoch` records when; and this project has already settled that rendered pages are ONLY projections of the graph rather than documents in their own right. An authorisation is structurally an approver plus a date plus a scope plus a decision — all four of which the schema can already say.

WHAT IS MISSING IS NOT VOCABULARY, AND THAT IS THE INTERESTING PART: it is EVIDENCE and NON-REPUDIATION. The graph can record that somebody approved something; it cannot today demonstrate to a third party that they did, that the record has not moved since, or that the approver had the authority. A `status: accepted` written by an agent and one written by a general are the same bytes.

THE OPTIONS:

(a) DO NOTHING; FORMAL DOCUMENTS STAY EXTERNAL and the graph points at them with `Artifact.location`. HONEST TODAY, costs nothing, and matches his own concession that a pointer "might be okay". COUNTER: it is exactly the arrangement the no-documents rule was made to end, so the product would be telling consumers to do what this project forbids itself.

(b) THE GRAPH HOLDS THE AUTHORISATION AS TYPED NODES, the signed document stays external as evidence. Cheap, mostly expressible already. COUNTER: it splits the record — authority in the graph, proof in a file — which is the worst of both for an auditor.

(c) THE GRAPH HOLDS THE BYTES TOO. A signed PDF is precisely "what the graph cannot hold inline", the sentence `cap:content-store` was built around — BUILT, VERIFIED, AND DISCONTINUED on his word on 2026-08-09 for zero use across three projects (`dec:the-content-store-is-discontinued`). ⭐ THIS WOULD BE THE FIRST REAL USE THAT DISCONTINUATION SAID DID NOT EXIST. COUNTER, and it is his own from that decision: bytes in a repo grow without bound, and in flo2 could reach terabytes needing backup, security and per-project separation — all MORE true, not less, for controlled or classified acquisition documents.

(d) THE DOCUMENT IS DERIVED FROM THE GRAPH — the official record is generated as a rendering, so there is one source and the document is an output rather than an input. Consistent with the settled doctrine that pages are only renderings. COUNTER: a rendering is not a signature. Something must still capture the act of approval by a person with authority, and that act happens outside reflow2.

⚠️ THE HONEST BLOCKER, stated so it is not rediscovered: whether an organisation trusts a graph is not a feature reflow2 can build. It is earned through audit, retention policy, access control and someone accepting liability. Everything above is necessary and none of it sufficient, and a version that shipped the mechanics while implying the trust would be the most damaging overclaim this project could make.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any real programme would accept it; what standard would have to be met (none has been named); and whether this is one question or two — TRACKING authorisations, versus BEING the authoritative record.
properties.name: IDEA — in acquisition work the formal documents ARE the artefact: design reviews, authorisations to proceed, official direction. Could the graph hold them well enough that an organisation trusts it and stops keeping external docs?
properties.rationale: Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`, options with counters beside them, nothing promoted. Started as a new node rather than merged into the rule after the guard named it: the rule governs this repository and is settled, while this asks whether the product could carry legal-weight documents for someone else — different scope, different decider, and merging them would bury a product question inside a house rule. His \"I don't think we are there yet\" is preserved inside the idea, because a later reader would otherwise read the aspiration as a plan.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-12, and he said plainly at capture time that he expects this to stay unaccepted — he wanted it on the record, not enacted. Nothing here is settled.

HIS WORDS: "should we have a 'purge' skill. I'm getting pretty happy with how reflow2 is now. There are a lot of still unrealized ideas and gaps that we still should work through, but say I'm happy with the current state of the project - can I just 'purge' all the additional things not yet accepted or built? It is a destructive action, but sometimes I'd like to continue reflow2 without every decision and thing I've submitted."

⭐ THE NEED IS REAL AND ALREADY EVIDENCED. `fact:the-owner-uses-reflow2-as-a-funnel-for-random-order-input` records that he pours instructions, ideas, feedback and requirements in as they occur to him. That is the tool working as intended, and its cost is exactly what he is describing: the open list grows faster than anyone decides on it, and eventually it stops being a to-do list and becomes noise.

═══ WHAT THIS WOULD TOUCH, MEASURED 2026-08-12 ═══

  Decision    proposed  104 of 341   carrying 248 edges   2 edgeless
  Requirement proposed   47 of 156   carrying 151 edges   0 edgeless
  Capability  planned    37 of 151   carrying 150 edges   0 edgeless
                        ─────────────────────────────────
                        188 nodes, ~549 edges

🛑🛑 AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT SHOULD DECIDE THIS: **26 OF THE 47 PROPOSED REQUIREMENTS ARE ALREADY SATISFIED BY SOMETHING.** They are built. Their status simply never moved off `proposed`, because status moves only on the owner's word and nobody went back to say so. A purge keyed on "not yet accepted" would delete more than half its own target set WRONGLY — deleting delivered work along with the speculation.

That is not a hypothesis. It is `req:supporting-is-not-conflict` at scale: during the 2026-07-30 prune that requirement was proposed for dropping as "an orphan in all but name", and checking its single edge revealed it was DELIVERED, by a `realized` capability. The lesson recorded then was "low edge count was read as low value, and for a requirement that has been built, edge count is exactly backwards". One hand-check caught one instance; the same reflex applied in bulk would now be wrong 26 times.

═══ THE PART THAT MAY MAKE THIS UNNECESSARY ═══

⭐ **THE THING HE WANTS MAY ALREADY EXIST, AND IT IS NOT DELETION.** `dec:proposed-requirements-pruned` (accepted, his own word, 2026-07-30) already did this once by hand — nine of twenty-six requirements retired — and its finding is the direct answer here:

> "All are `dropped`, not deleted... `dropped` also stops them raising `unsatisfied_requirement`, so the open list means what it says again."

So the BENEFIT he is asking for — an open list that means something again — is delivered by the STATUS CHANGE. Deletion adds nothing to that and additionally destroys the reasoning. That decision's rationale states the cost of going further: "Deleting them would erase why the surviving rules are shaped as they are, and would let the same captures be re-made next quarter by someone who could not see they had been weighed."

The `retire-from-design` skill already carries dropped-not-deleted as its central distinction. So what is missing is not the ACT; it is doing it in BATCH, and being prompted when the list has grown enough to be worth doing — the same shape as `dec:idea-the-graph-notices-the-record-moved-without-being-asked`, where the tool existed and the trigger did not.

═══ THE OPTIONS ═══

A — A BATCH DROP, never a delete. A skill that walks the unaccepted set in classes, proposes a disposition per class, and moves status to `dropped`/`deferred` on his word. Reuses existing vocabulary; nothing is lost; the open list clears. EXPENSIVE: it is 188 nodes, and a batch under one shared reason is precisely what `acknowledge_gaps` already REFUSES by design — "a batch under one shared reason is exactly the erosion the ask-don't-repair rule exists to prevent". So the batching has to be per-class with a stated reason each, which is what made the 2026-07-30 prune trustworthy and also what made it slow.

B — ACTUAL DELETION. What he literally asked for. Cheapest to state, and the only option that genuinely reduces graph size. EXPENSIVE, and the objections are unusually concrete: 549 edges would go with the nodes; the 26 delivered-but-unmarked requirements would go with them; and `dec:ask-not-repair` plus the whole `apply_heal` design exist to stop reflow2 destroying design without a human asserting each case.

C — SNAPSHOT-THEN-CLEAR. Export the design first, then drop hard, on the argument that git holds the memory. EXPENSIVE, and this is the one worth thinking hardest about: a design nobody can query is not memory. `search_design` cannot reach a node that only exists in a file, so "it is in git" means "nobody will ever find it again". The whole point of the graph over documents is that the record is QUERYABLE.

D — DO NOTHING NEW. `retire-from-design` exists and works; the 2026-07-30 prune proves it. What is missing is a nudge when the unaccepted set crosses some size. Free. EXPENSIVE: he has now asked for this, which is evidence the existing route is not discoverable at the moment he wants it.

E — FIX THE UPSTREAM CAUSE INSTEAD. 26 of 47 are stale STATUS, not surplus intent. A pass that asks "these 26 look delivered — accept them?" would shrink the open list by more than half WITHOUT dropping anything, and would make the remaining list honest. Not a purge at all; possibly the thing that removes most of the felt need.

═══ THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded beside the idea rather than used to kill it ═══

The brainstorm skill's own closing rule is that roads not taken are part of the design's memory — "recorded as considered, never deleted... a later session that finds an old idea knows both that it was thought of and that it was not chosen." A purge is the direct negation of that rule. If it is ever built, that rule has to be revisited deliberately rather than quietly broken, because half of what makes this graph worth keeping is that it remembers what was rejected and why.

⚠️ AND A SCOPE NOTE: "not yet accepted or built" is not one population. A `proposed` Decision that is an OPEN QUESTION is not surplus — it is unfinished thinking, and deleting it discards the question rather than answering it. A `planned` Capability nobody will build is different again. Any version of this has to say which of the three it means; the measurement above keeps them apart for that reason.

NOT DECIDED, and expected by its author to stay that way.
properties.name: OPEN — when the owner is happy with the current state, can everything not yet accepted or built be cleared in one deliberate act?
properties.rationale:
Captured on Anthony's explicit instruction to record it without pursuing it — "I expect this one to stay non-accepted, but I did want to capture." That is the funnel working exactly as `fact:the-owner-uses-reflow2-as-a-funnel-for-random-order-input` describes, and this node is itself an instance of the thing it proposes purging, which is worth noticing.

The measurement is what makes it worth keeping rather than merely polite: 26 of 47 proposed requirements are already satisfied, so the felt problem is substantially STALE STATUS rather than surplus intent, and option E addresses more of it than any purge would. The 2026-07-30 prune already established dropped-not-deleted and recorded that `dropped` alone restores the open list — so the benefit sought here is reachable without the destruction.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony, 2026-08-04, while BL-186 was mid-build: "maybe we setup an exploratory brainstorm and branch discussing the various ways that we could mass-ingest something like in dev_storyflow. then we can systematically test some different strategies and observe/measure which performs the best." Nothing here is chosen, and no option below has been costed by running it.

THE CASE, MEASURED (dev_storyflow, `/home/ajs7/project/dev_storyflow`, read-only): 1,124 markdown files, 22 MB, ~6M tokens of source text. 17 files at depth 1 and 1,107 below it, so a non-recursive ingest reads 1.5% of the corpus and reports nothing missing. docs/archive 333 files / 16.2 MB (73% of the volume, dated superseded board snapshots); memory/ 380; docs/evidence 195 md + 744 binaries; the plausibly design-bearing remainder is 216 files / 3.3 MB. The fleet's own survey (`reflow2_feedback.md`, api-boss 07426210) read samples rather than filenames and found docs/evidence is at least FIVE types, and that 102 of 334 memory files are unbuilt product intent that reflow2 already models — so a filename-level exclusion of memory/ would be wrong.

(a) INGEST EVERYTHING, RECURSIVELY, NO SELECTION. Cheapest to specify, and the only option needing no human judgement. Expensive to run (~6M tokens before the per-pass multiplier) and the yield is poor: a design dominated by 333 superseded archives. Counter-argument that is specific rather than general — the archives are dated snapshots of the SAME few boards, so they are near-identical to each other, and the DUPLICATES bridge built for corpus-scale asking would turn them into thousands of standing questions. The mechanism that makes batched asking possible is the same one that makes an unselected corpus unusable.

(b) PLAN THEN INGEST (directory triage). Walk the tree, group by directory, report counts + bytes + sample names, put THAT to the user as one batched ask about scope before any document is extracted. Cheap, one round, and it puts the judgement where it belongs — reflow2 cannot know that `archive/` is superseded, and hardcoding a skip-list is the "shaping the model until the tool goes quiet" failure docs/sharpening.md names. Honest counter-argument: directory-level judgement is wrong at file level, and the fleet's own deeper read proves it — docs/evidence holds 5 runbooks and 50 root-cause memos that are knowledge, not evidence, and excluding the directory loses them.

(c) CLASSIFY THEN ROUTE. A cheap per-document classification pass first (design intent / evidence / archive / doctrine / hazard), then route by kind: intent gets the full extraction, evidence becomes an Artifact with an anchor, archive is skipped or marked pending_expansion. More calls but each tiny, and it matches what the corpus actually is rather than what its folders are named. Counter-argument: it adds a classifier whose errors are invisible, and it is the option most likely to quietly mis-file the thing you care about.

(d) EXPLOIT THE CORPUS'S OWN SELF-LABELLING. It already declares itself: 102/334 memory files say FUTURE/parked, evidence files pin commit SHAs, grounding docs are headed "READ-ONLY GROUNDING (no code, no build)". Zero model cost for the signal. Counter-argument, measured: 117 of 334 memory files declare no type at all, and the fleet's filename convention and its frontmatter schema already disagree (`tech_` is 67 by filename and 6 by declared type) — so the labels cover most of the corpus and are silent exactly where it is messiest.

(e) HIGH-VALUE-FIRST, INCREMENTALLY. Ingest docs/architecture (20), docs/decisions (6), docs/grounding (34), briefs and the root planning docs — the 216-file remainder — measure the design that results, then decide whether more is worth it. Fastest to first value, and it composes with the resume story already settled on BL-186 (the graph IS the resume point; sweep the folder, diff against registered Fragments, the remainder is the work left). Counter-argument: it answers "is this useful" and not "does this scale", which is the question BL-186 exists to answer.

WHAT A TRIAL WOULD HAVE TO MEASURE, since none of the above is decidable by argument: documents ingested per unit cost; nodes created against merge candidates raised (signal to noise); how many candidates a HUMAN then has to rule on; coverage_report claimed against unclaimed; and the only test that actually matters, which the scope doc already states — "whether an agent reading 500 heterogeneous markdown files produces a design a human recognises is a trial, not an argument, and it should be run on a real folder before anyone promises this to a user."
properties.name: OPEN — how should a corpus like dev_storyflow's 1,124 documents actually be mass-ingested?
properties.rationale: Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the options survive as options. Anthony proposed trialling several strategies and measuring which performs best; this node holds the strategies, and dec:idea-trial-driven-choice-skill holds the separate question of whether reflow2 should have a way to run that kind of trial at all. Measurements of dev_storyflow are exact greps taken 2026-08-04; the type judgements are the fleet's own from reflow2_feedback.md, not mine — my earlier filename-level read of memory/ was wrong and is corrected above.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled.

THE IDEA: dynograph_graph::shortest_path (unused) returns the actual Path between two nodes. Two readings on a design graph:
(a) surprising_connections reports that two things bridge separate communities. It does not say through what. The path is the explanation a human needs before acting.
(b) "Why is this node in my blast radius?" propagate reports hop distance and impact direction; a named path is the artifact a person can read and check.

CHEAP: exact, already a dependency, and both call sites already hold the network.

WHERE IT LANDS: this is the BL-114 family again from a third direction — a finding that states a conclusion without stating the evidence it walked. BL-141(a) has just done exactly this for circular_dependency (name the contracts the cycle ran through), and that change was small and immediately useful on real data. The same argument applies here.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT: a shortest path is not necessarily the RESPONSIBLE path — several may exist, and showing one implies a causal story that may not be the operative one. BL-141(a) sidestepped this by naming the SET of contracts involved rather than a single route; the equivalent here might be "the edge types this coupling runs through" rather than one path. Worth deciding which before building.
properties.name: OPEN — should a finding say HOW two nodes are coupled, not only that they are?
properties.rationale: Grouped with the explain-what-you-walked family (BL-114, BL-141a) rather than presented as a new idea, because that is what it is — the third instance of the same shape.

properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, from a FIRST-PASS REVIEW OF openmbee.org — the website, the GitHub org listing and one (truncated) architecture page. Nothing here rests on reading their source or running it. Anthony intends to clone the repo for a deep review, and every reading below should be re-tested then. THE OBSERVATION: OpenMBEE's stated purpose is 'an open source collaborative engineering system' that 'enables engineers to work in the language of their choice and easily share and document their work across other tools', with the tagline 'Edit once, use everywhere'. Its answer to multi-organisation, multi-tool work is LINKED DATA — an RDF quadstore where the fourth term is a named graph, so many contexts coexist in one repository, plus transclusion so one source of truth appears in many places. WHY THIS IS THE AREA WHERE THEY ARE PLAINLY AHEAD OF reflow2, and it is not a small one: it is precisely the operating context Anthony described — several organisations with competing, partially-built, differently-motivated designs that must be made to interoperate although they were never designed to. reflow2 has `req:design-composes`, `compose_and_analyse`, `pair_designs` and `mirror_surface`, and `dec:linked-repos-poc` has sat PARKED since it was filed. Those compose EXPORTS — whole documents, pairwise — where OpenMBEE federates a live graph across repositories. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is strong: reflow2 already decided against the architecture that makes their approach possible. `dec:repo-file-embedded` (the graph lives as a repo file, embedded, not a service) and `dec:multi-writer-architecture` (many writers keep the repo file and merge on pull — no hosted service) are the opposite answer to the same question, taken deliberately. A quadstore federation is a service, and adopting the capability may mean reopening those. NOTE ALSO that `dec:central-host` and `dec:live-tier` are BOTH still proposed in this design — OpenMBEE is a fairly complete picture of what saying yes to them costs and buys, which makes it evidence for those two questions whether or not this one is ever answered. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: whether federation can be had at the EXPORT seam — `export_surface` and `mirror_surface` already publish a subset — rather than requiring a live shared store.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 federate heterogeneous designs across organisations the way OpenMBEE does, rather than composing exports?
properties.rationale: Recorded through the brainstorm skill because this is an idea from a landscape review, not intent Anthony has stated. He asked for the areas where OpenMBEE is stronger to be captured as proposed ideas ahead of a deep review, in those words. DELIBERATELY LEFT UNLINKED: `describe_schema {from: Decision, to: Decision}` reports that NO edge type models the pair and that the seventeen which validate do so only through a `*` wildcard — 'validating is not the same as meaning what you intend… prefer leaving the edge out to asserting one that is wrong'. So this will surface as an `orphan_node` info finding, exactly as `dec:linked-repos-poc` does, and that is the true description of a parked idea rather than a defect to route around.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-13, extending his own RNA analogy. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen.

HIS WORDS: "going back to the RNA pairing discussion, can we have each project have a set of defined pair types that could facilitate the combining if two projects in a much faster manner?" — and, earlier in the same message, the shape he was reaching for: "not sure if one project carries a set of one side of the pairs and that would allow the other project to only line up with its corresponding pair on the other side."

⭐ THE ANALOGY IS PRECISE ABOUT WHY PAIRING IS FAST, and that is the real content of the idea. Four bases, two valid pairs, an alphabet fixed by chemistry. Matching is a LOOKUP, not a comparison. reflow2 today does comparison: `req:complementary-pairing` keys on `medium` PLUS `transport_security` PLUS `auth`, then falls back to fuzzy name resolution with a reported middle band a human must answer. Declared pair types would replace the fuzzy step with an exact one.

🛑 AND THE ANALOGY ALSO NAMES ITS OWN LIMIT, which is the honest counterweight. Bases pair by an alphabet that chemistry fixes GLOBALLY and nobody negotiates. Two organisations have no chemistry. A shared pair-type vocabulary requires prior agreement between the parties — and working WITHOUT prior agreement is exactly what the attribute key buys, in exactly the cross-organisation context reflow2 states as its operating breadth. The idea's power and its limit come from the same property.

═══ THE OPTIONS ═══

A — NOTHING. The attribute key already pairs two designs that never coordinated. Faster matching is not obviously the constraint. CHEAPEST, and the null hypothesis.

B — A DECLARED PAIR-TYPE VOCABULARY, his idea literally: each project publishes named types, and combining is a type-name join. FASTEST when both sides share the vocabulary; USELESS when they do not, and worse than useless if two orgs use one name for different contracts — a false pair is more dangerous than no pair, which is the failure the dynograph-foundation trial already produced once from the provider side.

C — ⭐ USE `SPECIFIES`, WHICH ALREADY EXISTS AND HAS NEVER BEEN DRAWN. The schema carries it: "A machine-readable contract artifact defines an entity — an OpenAPI / protobuf / JSON-schema / IDL file SPECIFIES an Interface (its authoritative contract)", with a `format` property. MEASURED 2026-08-13: **zero SPECIFIES edges in reflow2's design.** If two designs' Interfaces are both specified by the SAME artifact, matched on content hash, that is exact pairing with NO vocabulary to negotiate — THE HASH IS THE AGREEMENT. It is the ICD made first-class, which `Interface.designation` already gestures at when it cites 10 U.S.C. 4401 and "what an ICD publishes". Needs no new node type, no new edge type, no enum change, and no stamp move.

D — HYBRID, AND THE ONE THAT DEGRADES HONESTLY: exact when a shared contract artifact is present, attribute-key-plus-fuzzy-name when it is not. Two designs that have agreed get a precise seam; two that have not still get today's answer. Costs a second matching path and a rule for which wins.

═══ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea ═══

⚠️ 1. THE STRONGEST — SPEED IS NOT THE CONSTRAINT, AND MAY NEVER BE. reflow2's own frontier reads seams 0% : ZERO of 73 component couplings run through a declared Interface. There is nothing to pair yet. Optimising the matching step while nothing is labelled is optimising past the actual blocker, which is that boundaries are unclassified.
   📌 STATUS 2026-08-13: PARTLY ADDRESSED. `cap:undeclared-seam-is-named` shipped (PR #167) and now NAMES those 73 pairs as one aggregate gap. It does not declare them — it asks. The blocker is now visible rather than silent.
⚠️ 2. THE FUZZY MIDDLE BAND IS NOT A DEFECT TO REMOVE. Asking a human about an uncertain name match is `dec:ask-not-repair` working as designed. Replacing it with exact lookup removes the question by removing the cases that raise it — which is only an improvement where the shared vocabulary is real.
