In reflow2's own graph today: 198 TemporalFacts, and SIX TemporalFact→TemporalFact edges — ALL of them CONTRADICTS, and FIVE of the six carry `alignment: supporting`, i.e. corroboration rather than conflict. Five earlier sessions independently reached for a negation type to say two findings AGREE. This is not one author's routing quirk.

AND THE CURRENT ARRANGEMENT IS CORRECT, which is the strongest argument against touching it. Both computations that read CONTRADICTS skip `supporting` deliberately — `heal.rs:917-923` and `report.rs:1751-1766` — and report.rs carries a comment naming the bug that once existed: reading only the edge TYPE 'turned every recorded corroboration into a structural defect'. So there is NO live defect. The cost is a word that says the opposite of its meaning, and an author who must find a property to negate the type they just chose.

THE TEST THAT SHOULD DECIDE IT IS ALREADY ACCEPTED DOCTRINE: `dec:edge-orthogonality` — 'a vocabulary distinction earns its keep only if a computation reads it'. So the real question is not which word is nicer. It is: SHOULD REFLOW2 COMPUTE CORROBORATION? 'This finding is independently corroborated by N sources' is the same evidence-strength signal the design already cares about everywhere else (`basis: measured`, `confidence`, the whole verification doctrine), and the five supporting edges cluster on exactly the findings that recurred to different people. If that number should be reportable, the relation earns a type. If not, it is documentation and the cheapest option wins.

THE OPTIONS.

(a) LEAVE IT. CONTRADICTS + `alignment: supporting`. Cheapest, five precedents, twice defended in code with a comment recording why. ⇒ Against: every future author reaches for a negation to express agreement, and only finds the escape hatch by reading the schema — which is how this came up.

(b) WIDEN `SUPPLEMENTS`. It already exists and is declared `from: Fragment, to: Fragment` (build.yaml:133). A from/to list edit is the exact shape of #198 (VERIFIES admits Constraint), which shipped this increment, and it does NOT move the stamp — type counts and names are unchanged, so no upgrade doc is owed and nobody is locked out. ⇒ Against, and it is serious: SUPPLEMENTS has ZERO edges anywhere in this design, and its documented meaning is narrow and different (an LLM-as-SME supplementary-analysis Fragment augmenting its source). Nothing computes it. So this moves corroboration from an edge that IS read-and-correctly-skipped to one nothing reads at all — arguably backwards by `dec:edge-orthogonality`'s own test.

(c) A NEW EDGE TYPE (`CORROBORATES`). Cleanest semantics, and the only option where the word matches the meaning. ⇒ Against: edge_types 61 → 62 MOVES THE STAMP, which owes an upgrade doc and makes older binaries refuse newer graphs. That is a real consumer cost for what may be documentation — and it only pays for itself under the computation test above.

(d) SPLIT `alignment` OUT of CONTRADICTS ENTIRELY, so conflict and corroboration are separate types. Most honest model. ⇒ Against: same stamp cost as (c) PLUS a migration of the five existing supporting edges, and it would delete a working distinction to replace it with an equivalent one.

(e) LEAVE THE SCHEMA AND FIX DISCOVERABILITY. CONTRADICTS's hint mentions the supporting case only as a trailing parenthetical — '(or, with alignment=supporting, reinforce)'. Lead with it instead. ⇒ Zero schema risk, zero stamp movement, and it addresses the ACTUAL failure, which was an author not finding the mechanism rather than the mechanism being absent. Weakest if the answer to the computation question is yes.

WHAT NOBODY HAS MEASURED, and it would settle (c) vs (a): whether any consumer design has fact→fact corroboration at all, or whether this is a self-host pattern produced by reflow2 being the only project that records its own defects as TemporalFacts. If it is self-host-only, that is an argument for (a) or (e) on `rule:the-self-host-always-trails-what-it-teaches` grounds.

RELATED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FOLDED IN: `dec:one-retire-edge` is the same shape one axis over — two edge types for retirement, neither consulted, and still open. If these are answered separately they may drift apart; whether edge-vocabulary questions should be settled as a batch is itself a question.
properties.name: OPEN — a finding that corroborates another has to say CONTRADICTS to do it, and two code paths then filter that back out. Leave it, widen an unused edge, or make corroboration something reflow2 computes?
properties.rationale:
Not a proposal and not a ranking. The five-of-six measurement is the part worth keeping whatever is decided: a corroboration relation is being expressed through a negation type, five times, by different sessions, and the code correctly filters it back out in two places. Anthony asked how to choose; the honest answer is that `dec:edge-orthogonality` already supplies the test, and applying it needs one thing nobody has decided — whether 'independently corroborated by N sources' is a number reflow2 should report.

⭐ THE OUTSTANDING MEASUREMENT WAS THEN TAKEN, 2026-08-16, AND IT LEANS HARD. The decision text asks whether any CONSUMER design has fact→fact corroboration. Measured across every committed export on this machine — dev_storyflow, dynograph-foundation, flo2, music_graph, quantum_benchmarking_initiative, storyflow — the answer is not 'no fact→fact edges'. It is ZERO TemporalFacts, in all six, full stop.

⇒ THIS IS A SELF-HOST-ONLY PATTERN. reflow2 is the only project recording its own defects as TemporalFacts, because it is the only project whose subject is reflow2. That is `rule:the-self-host-always-trails-what-it-teaches` pointing the other way for once: normally the self-host lags what it teaches; here it has invented a usage no consumer has reached for.

⇒ WHICH RE-RANKS THE OPTIONS, though it does not settle them. (c) a new edge type and (d) splitting `alignment` both move the stamp — an upgrade doc owed and older binaries refusing newer graphs — and would be paying a CONSUMER cost for a relation no consumer uses. (b) widening SUPPLEMENTS was already argued against on `dec:edge-orthogonality` grounds and this weakens it further. (e) fixing CONTRADICTS's hint so the `supporting` case leads rather than trails costs nothing, breaks nothing, and addresses the failure actually observed — an author not finding a mechanism that was already there and already correct.

⚠️ THE BOUND ON THAT MEASUREMENT, stated rather than glossed: these are COMMITTED EXPORTS, which may trail those projects' live stores — music_graph's is dated 2026-08-01, and F23 is precisely a case of a committed export being behind. So this reads 'zero in the record I can see', not 'zero in existence'. Six-for-six at zero is still a strong signal, and it would take only one consumer starting to record findings to overturn it.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Source: the SECOND half of Alex Sligar's 2026-08-05 exchange, relayed by Anthony 2026-08-06. In Alex's own words, the use case is: "I have a ton of domain/tribal knowledge about my project, beyond the code itself. For example, I know why certain UI sections were created or have talked with the users and want a better way to document this information for junior devs on my project. I'd like to brain dump a bunch of this info in a way that other devs can query it using an AI prompt." STILL OPEN.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A NODE RATHER THAN A NOD: Alex described reflow2's use case almost exactly — rationale, who asked for it, what constraint drove it, kept beside the code and queryable in natural language — and the research answered him with Notion AI, Confluence/Rovo and Cognee. reflow2 was not a candidate in an answer to the question reflow2 exists to answer. Whatever else is true, that is a finding.

WHAT REFLOW2 ALREADY HAS FOR IT: add_decision with a rationale, authored_by (whose word this is), the golden thread from requirement to capability to artifact, and search_design over all of it. Against a wiki it has one property no wiki has: a rationale in reflow2 can be shown to have gone STALE, because the thing it justified is linked and drift is computed. A Confluence page saying "the legacy report screen stays because finance uses it monthly" stays confidently wrong forever after finance stops. That is the same normative property recorded in dec:idea-normative-vs-descriptive-graph, seen from the tribal-knowledge angle.

THE TENSION, and it is with an ACCEPTED requirement, not a soft one: req:driving-agent states that the primary consumers are coding agents and "the human is reached only through the agent". Alex's junior dev is a human asking a question with no build task attached and no design intent to capture. Serving that reader well means a read-optimised, question-answering surface — closer to Q&A over the graph than to the capture-detect-ask-decide loop — and the loop is what the current skill kit is built around. It is a different product surface on the same store, which is either a natural projection (dec:views-are-projections would allow it, since answering from the graph invents nothing) or a second product, and those have very different costs.

WHAT IS CHEAP: nothing new is needed to try it. An agent with the existing read tools can already answer "why does this exist" from a well-populated graph. The cheap experiment is to have someone who did not build the design ask it questions and see what it cannot answer.

WHAT IS EXPENSIVE, AND THE HONEST OBJECTION: this reader wants to BRAIN DUMP first and get structure later, which is the opposite of the capture loop's order. cap:ingest and cap:corpus-ingest exist for exactly that shape, so the primitive is there — but the loop's habit of asking about gaps at capture time is precisely what a brain-dumping user will experience as friction, and the brainstorm skill's own rule (do not run detect-and-ask over material the user deliberately left soft) exists because of that. Whether a dump-then-structure mode is a mode, a skill, or a different reader's whole path is unsettled.

A CONCRETE DOGFOODING OPPORTUNITY, recorded because it is testable rather than arguable: Alex has the project, the tribal knowledge and the junior devs. Pointing reflow2 at his brain dump would test cap:ingest, the newcomer-query path and the tribal-knowledge story at once, on a design nobody in this repo authored. Anthony's word needed on whether that is wanted.
properties.name: OPEN — is a human newcomer asking "why does this exist" a first-class reader of the graph, when req:driving-agent says the human is reached only through the agent?
properties.rationale: Recorded as an idea because the tension is with an accepted requirement and therefore cannot be resolved by an agent — either req:driving-agent is narrower than it reads, or this reader is out of scope, and only Anthony can say which. Also recorded because the finding that prompted it (reflow2 absent from an answer to its own question) is the kind of thing that vanishes from a conversation and cannot be rediscovered.

properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-14 BY ANTHONY: **OPTION (c) — INIT ASKS.** Alex's literal request, taken over the recommendation recorded on this node, which was (b) *"apply the instruction-pointer policy to MCP configs"*. He chose with (b)'s argument and (c)'s stated costs both in front of him.

⭐ THE STRONGEST CASE FOR HIS CHOICE, which the pre-decision text under-weighted: **(b) GUESSES, AND A WRONG GUESS IS SILENT.** Detection reads a fresh repo that has no signal, falls back to the primary harness, and hands an OpenCode user a `.mcp.json` their tool never opens — with nothing to tell them anything is missing. Asking is the only option on the list that cannot be silently wrong, and a silent wrong install is the exact failure class this project keeps finding (`cap:degraded-surface`'s diagnosis not reaching a by-name caller; the loop nudge registered against a script that is not there; the pointer written into a file the harness never reads). **A question costs one prompt; a silent miss costs a user who concludes reflow2 does not work.**

⚠️ WHAT IT COSTS, RECORDED SO NOBODY IS SURPRISED LATER: the one-liner install becomes a conversation, which is in tension with `user-iterative-release-preference` (*one-liner install, one word to update*). So the non-interactive path is not optional garnish — it is part of the requirement: a flag must carry the answer, and a non-tty must never hang. CI, scripted installs and `adopt` runs are the common path, not the exception.

📌 WHAT (c) DOES NOT SETTLE: the instruction-pointer policy stays as it is (already narrow and correct), and the loop-nudge asymmetry is a separate open question (`dec:idea-the-loop-nudge-exists-for-one-harness-only`) where the problem runs the other way — too little, not too much. Option (d), labelling the generated files, was not chosen but composes with (c) and remains available.

═══ THE ANALYSIS THIS WAS DECIDED FROM, kept because `req:roads-not-taken` says the roads not taken are part of the record ═══

RAISED AS BRAINSTORMING by Alex (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-14.

HIS WORDS: *"`reflow2 init .` for a project should be more like a CLI wizard that asks you what agent harness you are utilizing (Claude, Grok, ChatGPT, open code, etc.) and only installs the necessary file changes based on your choice. It needs the correct mcp setup, the graph artifact that can be git committed and the agents.md reference."*

✅ HIS THREE NAMED ESSENTIALS ARE ALL ALREADY PRODUCED on HEAD (`cbb1a19`): the MCP setup, the committed export at `docs/design/<project>.json` (since PR #172), and the `AGENTS.md` reference. **Nothing he needs is missing — the complaint is that things nobody asked for arrive alongside them.**

⭐⭐ THE FINDING THAT REFRAMED THE QUESTION: `tools/reflow2_init.py` ALREADY IMPLEMENTS ALEX'S PRINCIPLE — for instruction files — AND THE OPPOSITE ONE FOR MCP CONFIGS, ABOUT 150 LINES APART. Both deliberate, each carrying its reasoning in a comment, and they contradict each other.

  · INSTRUCTION POINTERS (`pointer_targets`, `CREATE_IF_NO_INSTRUCTION_FILE`) — appends only to instruction files the project ALREADY OWNS; when it owns none, creates just `CLAUDE.md`. The comment rejects the alternative in as many words: *"writing GEMINI.md, .cursorrules and the rest into a repo that asked for none of them is **spam**, and the sidecar we create (AGENTS.md) already IS the agents.md convention that the others increasingly follow."*
  · MCP CONFIGS (`MCP_CONFIGS`) — writes `.mcp.json`, `opencode.json` AND `.vscode/mcp.json` unconditionally: *"One generator, several files — a project opened in a different tool should just work."*

⇒ So the question was never "should init ask?" but "which of init's two existing policies is right?" — and (c) settles it toward the narrow one, by asking rather than by inferring.

THE OPTIONS AS THEY STOOD.
(a) LEAVE IT — extras are inert. Counter: init's own code calls that spam one screen away, and a first-time user read it as clutter.
(b) APPLY THE POINTER POLICY TO MCP CONFIGS — detect, falling back to the primary harness. No prompt, internally consistent. **Counter that decided it: detection has no signal on a fresh repo, which is exactly when init runs, so it guesses — and guesses silently.**
(c) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — ASK, with `--harness=…` for non-interactive use.
(d) INSTALL ALL, BUT LABEL each file with which tool reads it and that deleting it is safe. Not chosen; composes with (c).
(e) ASK ONLY WHEN AMBIGUOUS — detect, prompt when detection is empty. Not chosen; two code paths, and behaviour that differs between a fresh and an established repo.

📌 SCOPE, because it makes the change smaller than it sounds: most of what `init` writes is HARNESS-NEUTRAL and untouched — `AGENTS.md`/`REFLOW2.md`, the committed export, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`. The harness-specific surface is the three MCP configs, the instruction pointer (already policy-correct), and the loop-nudge hook.

⚠️ VERSION CAVEAT: two of Alex's five notes describe defects already fixed, so he is probably on an older kit (`fact:second-user-notes-2026-08-14-two-items-already-fixed`). Measurements here are against HEAD; an older `init` may have written a different set of files than what he saw.
properties.name: DECIDED — `init` ASKS which harness you use and installs only that one's files (option c), settling init's two contradictory install policies in favour of the narrow one
properties.rationale: Raised under the brainstorm skill and settled the same day on Anthony's word. Two things are deliberately on the record rather than smoothed away: that the choice went AGAINST the option this node recommended, and the reason his choice is nonetheless the stronger one — detection guesses, and a wrong guess about which harness will open a repo produces a silent failure, which is the failure class this project has now hit four separate times. The pre-decision text is kept in full beneath the outcome because `req:roads-not-taken` makes the rejected options part of the record, and because the instruction-pointer contradiction it documents is a real finding about `reflow2_init.py` that survives whichever option was taken.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Surfaced 2026-08-05 by Anthony's multi-project question.

⚠️ CORRECTED WITHIN THE HOUR, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE USEFUL PART. This node first claimed "everything reflow2 has built for crossing a design boundary shares CONTRACTS... NOTHING CARRIES A DECISION OR A REQUIREMENT ACROSS." THAT IS WRONG ABOUT REQUIREMENTS, and it was wrong for the ordinary reason — the claim was made from the capability's one-line description ("the contracts others may rely on, and nothing internal") rather than from the code. Reading `export_surface` shows a second, deliberate half: `published_promises()`, behind `req:publishable-promise` (ACCEPTED — "a published surface must be able to carry a behavioural promise, not only structure"). Its own comment says why: "a structural surface says what the boundaries ARE and cannot say what any of them undertakes to DO — 'fails loud rather than falling back', 'ordering is preserved' — because a behavioural commitment lives in a Requirement and every Requirement was withheld. FOUND BY A REAL TRIAL, where the promise ended up asserted in a comment in the CONSUMER's build file, on the wrong side of the seam."

SO THE ACTUAL STATE, verified in `crates/reflow2-core/src/export.rs`: a published surface carries INTERFACES designated `published`, the artifacts that SPECIFY or REALIZE them, REQUIREMENTS the owner designated `published`, and the Project so a recipient knows whose surface it is. Everything else is withheld AND COUNTED. Opt-in throughout — designation is a deliberate act, never a default.

⭐ SO THE REAL GAP IS NARROWER AND SHARPER THAN FIRST WRITTEN: WHAT CANNOT CROSS IS THE **DECISION** — the reasoning. A consumer can learn WHAT this design promises and WHERE its boundaries are. It cannot learn WHY. "We settled that outdoor units send cumulative totals, so a lost reading heals itself" is exactly the thing a sibling project should inherit, and there is no way to publish it.

AND THE MECHANISM FOR THE PARENT DIRECTION ALREADY EXISTS: `cap:derived-completion` is VERIFIED, and `dec:nested-graphs`' second obligation names it — "a parent's view of a composed child must derive from the child's own evidence or a requirement satisfied inside the child fires unsatisfied in the parent forever". So a program-level design holding intent that child designs satisfy is ANTICIPATED and BUILT, not missing.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) NOTHING MORE CROSSES — interfaces and designated promises are the boundary, and reasoning stays private by design. Defensible and cheapest; the counter is that a sibling project then re-derives a ruling its neighbour already made, which is this project's most expensive recurring failure. (b) DECISIONS BECOME DESIGNATABLE, the same opt-in shape requirements already have. Small and consistent — the machinery, the designation vocabulary and the withheld-and-counted reporting all exist. Counter, and it is the hard one nobody has answered: IS A MIRRORED DECISION BINDING ON THE MIRRORING DESIGN, OR ONLY VISIBLE TO IT? A Decision that governs nothing on the far side is a note; one that governs is an authority claim across a boundary the whole rule exists to draw. (c) A STANDING "HOUSE RULES" DESIGN every project mirrors — one design holding what its author carries everywhere. Fits `dec:nested-graphs` cleanly because that design IS separately owned and shared. Counter: nothing models a design with no build, and it overlaps option (d) on `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects`. (d) DO NOT SOLVE IT IN THE GRAPH. Counter: "the person remembers" is what `req:no-idea-goes-quiet` (accepted the same day) exists to reject.

⚠️ THE PREREQUISITE THAT BOUNDS ALL OF IT, unchanged by the correction: reflow2's own `maturity_report` puts SEAMS at 0 OF 73. Not one coupling in this design runs through a declared Interface. So `publish-surface` and `mirror-surface` are `verified` by their own tests and have NEVER been exercised on the design that ships them — the same shape that hid [BL-176] for eleven releases and produced [BL-213] this morning. `dec:linked-repos-poc` is the trial that would fix that, and it has been parked since 2026-07-27.

THE METHOD NOTE, because this is the second time today: I asserted an absence from a capability's DESCRIPTION and the code said otherwise. The description was not wrong — "nothing internal" is true of what it withholds — it simply was not the whole surface. READ THE EXPORT, NOT THE SUMMARY.
properties.name: OPEN — a published surface already carries designated REQUIREMENTS; should DECISIONS cross a design boundary too?
properties.rationale:
Corrected an hour after it was written, on the same day, because the first version asserted an absence it had not checked — and an absence is exactly the kind of claim that hardens into folklore. The correction is kept in the node rather than silently replacing the text so the failure mode stays visible: I read a capability's one-line description and reported it as the whole mechanism.

Kept separate from `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` because that node asks WHERE the boundary goes and this asks WHAT MAY CROSS IT.

The remaining question genuinely narrowed rather than closed: requirements already cross, so the open part is Decisions, and the hard sub-question — binding or merely visible — is now the thing worth Anthony's word rather than the broad "should intent cross".

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. The most interesting idea in the batch and the least evidenced. Nothing here is settled.

THE CRATE: dynograph-game is not even a dependency of reflow2 today. It is closed-form normal-form analysis — per-player dominant strategies, pure Nash equilibria, Pareto-optimal outcomes, the interior 2x2 mixed equilibrium, and a headline classification `nash_is_pareto_suboptimal` with the Pareto outcome that dominates each suboptimal equilibrium.

THE FIT, and it is to a context Anthony has stated rather than one invented here: his real operating environment is several organisations with competing, partially-built, differently-motivated designs — A wants X, B wants Y, C built its own because it could not wait — and the job is making them interoperate when they were never designed to. That is a normal-form game. Players are organisations. Strategies are {adopt the shared interface, build our own}. And `nash_is_pareto_suboptimal` is exactly the interoperability tragedy: every organisation behaves rationally, every one builds its own, and the system of systems is collectively worse. The crate names both the equilibrium and the outcome that dominates it.

ADJACENT: dec:mosa-conformance is open, and MOSA is fundamentally an argument about the incentives to use open interfaces rather than about the interfaces themselves.

THE CONFLICT TO BE CLEAR ABOUT: the OBVIOUS application is analysis of alternatives — score the options, compute the equilibrium. That would CONTRADICT dec:alternatives-unranked-forkable, which is accepted and says "alternatives are unranked forkable siblings; the human judges in hindsight, not a stored score". Computing an equilibrium over design alternatives IS a stored recommendation. This must not be done without reopening that decision explicitly (dec:reopen-supersedes gives the mechanism). The interoperability reading does NOT conflict, because reflow2 would be reporting a structural property of an incentive situation a human described, not preferring a design — the same posture as dec:report-dont-judge.

THE HARD COST: payoffs are not in the graph and cannot be invented. This needs new vocabulary (players, strategies, payoff matrix) and a capture path, so it is M-to-L, not a spike. It is a product question about what reflow2 is for, and wants a conversation and a Decision before any code.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 model multi-organisation interoperability as a normal-form game?
properties.rationale: Recorded because the fit to the stated multi-organisation context is unusually good, and recorded WITH the conflict against dec:alternatives-unranked-forkable stated in the same node, so nobody can pick this up later without meeting the objection.

properties.decision:
🕐 **PARKED 2026-08-14 ON ANTHONY'S WORD, SPLIT OUT of `dec:idea-allocation-waits-for-the-last-responsible-moment` so that its two SETTLED halves could be accepted without this one holding them open.**

✅ **APPROVER DROPPED 2026-08-14 ON HIS WORD, AND THE PARK IS UNCHANGED — READ THIS BEFORE CONCLUDING THE EDGE WAS LOST.** The `AUTHORED_BY role=approver` edge to `who:ajs` was REMOVED DELIBERATELY, taking `loop_status`'s own second option: *"decide, or drop the approver if nobody was actually asked."*

**WHY, and it is not a downgrade of the question:** an approver edge asserts that a named person was asked to SETTLE something, and this cannot be settled by anybody. It is blocked on DATA THAT DOES NOT EXIST, not on judgement. Leaving the edge made it read as outstanding work owed by him, and the only act available to him would have been to rule without evidence — which is precisely what he refused to do when he asked for the measurement first. **A question nobody can answer is not debt; carrying it as debt teaches the loop's reader to discount the list.**

⇒ THE QUESTION IS STILL OPEN, STILL PARKED, AND STILL FINDABLE. The re-ask trigger below does the remembering. **Re-attach an approver when the trigger fires** — at that point there IS something to settle.

THE QUESTION: reflow2's own design is ~100% allocated while `maturity_report` puts seams at 0% (0 of 73 couplings declared through a contract). Is that an INVERSION — evidence that allocation ran ahead of the understanding that should precede it — or the normal shape of a design that got function right first?

═══ 🛑 WHY IT CANNOT BE ANSWERED TODAY, MEASURED 2026-08-08 ═══

Anthony agreed to a METHOD rather than an answer: do not reason about it, measure reflow2's own allocation timing first — because changing a model on a hunch is what the `unexpected_coupling` retirement already cost. **The measurement was attempted immediately and FAILED, and the failure is the finding:**
```
156  ALLOCATED_TO edges exist
  1  property on them: `weight_basis` — nothing dates an allocation
  1  of 320 ChangeEvents mentions one
```
⇒ **WHEN any allocation was made is recorded nowhere in this design.** The question is answerable in principle and unanswerable from the data that exists: **the algorithm is not the blocker, the substrate is.**

═══ 🎯 THE TRIGGER, NAMED SO THIS IS NOT INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A FORGOTTEN QUESTION ═══

Re-open when **allocation timing becomes recordable at all** — either `ALLOCATED_TO` carries a date, or allocations pass through `record_change` the way other design moves do. The trigger is NOT "run the query"; the query cannot be written today.

⚠️ **AND BUILDING THAT SUBSTRATE IS DELIBERATELY NOT SCHEDULED, 2026-08-14.** Dating `ALLOCATED_TO` is a schema change that MOVES THE STAMP and owes an upgrade doc, and it would be built to answer one question about one design. **If allocation timing turns out to matter for a user-facing reason, build it then and this unblocks for free.** Recorded so a later session does not read the trigger as a work item.

⚠️ **WHAT PARKING THIS COSTS:** until it is answered, the trajectory model's current excuse — *"bands running ahead of the frontier is the normal shape of a design that got function right first"* — **stands BY DEFAULT rather than on evidence.** That is why this is parked rather than closed.

📌 Follows the precedent `dec:the-other-uaf-domains-wait-for-a-project-that-needs-them` set: a parked question with a stated trigger is recognisable months later; one with no trigger cannot be told from a question nobody remembered.
properties.name: PARKED, TRIGGER NAMED — is 100% allocation against 0% declared seams an inversion? Unanswerable until allocation timing is recordable at all

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-12, asking whether CAP/PACELC applies to reflow2's own design. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen.

⭐ THE FINDING THAT MAKES THIS WORTH KEEPING: reflow2 HAS ALREADY MADE THESE TRADE-OFFS, REPEATEDLY AND DELIBERATELY, AND HAS NEVER NAMED THEM AS ONE CLASS. Checked against the graph rather than asserted:

THE STORE IS CP. One RocksDB store, single-writer by construction. A second writer is refused rather than served — `cap:degraded-surface` exists precisely to explain that refusal, and `dec:read-while-held-mechanism` settled what a locked-out seat gets: "a read-only view as of open, not a catchable-up secondary". That is textbook CP with a stale-read escape hatch. `cap:stale-seat-refusal` and `req:stale-seat-knows` are the write half: refuse rather than clobber.

THE RECORD IS AP. `docs/design/reflow2.json` travels by git. Everyone works offline, diverges freely, reconciles later — `cap:merge-designs`, `cap:git-merge-driver`, `cap:portability`, three-way merge with rerere. Nobody blocks. `cap:the-record-moved-is-surfaced` and `sync_status` are, precisely, an eventual-consistency staleness detector: they tell a seat the shared record moved ahead of it and name what arrived.

AND `dec:advisory-concurrency` IS AN EXPLICIT AP CHOICE WITH EMPIRICAL BACKING. Its words: "seats coordinate by announcement and provable order, NEVER BY EXCLUSION… when two claims cross, the winner is whichever landed first in git history, and both parties can verify that independently." It names what it rejected — "a coordination service or lock manager" — and why: "a lock is exactly what took FIVE OF SIX SESSIONS OFFLINE on 2026-07-25." That is choosing A over C after measuring the cost of C, which is the CAP decision made properly and never called by its name.

⇒ SO THE CANDIDATE READING IS: reflow2 is PC/EC in the store and PA/EL in the record. In normal operation it does not block on syncing the record — you work locally and export later, which is choosing L. PACELC's actual contribution here is that second half: the store-versus-record tension is NOT rare-failure behaviour, it is what every ordinary session does all day.

🛑 AND THE SHARP PART, WHICH IS WHY THIS MIGHT BE MORE THAN A RELABELLING: THE SEAM BETWEEN THE CP STORE AND THE AP RECORD IS WHERE AN UNUSUAL SHARE OF THIS PROJECT'S BUGS HAVE LIVED. Not a claim about all bugs — a pattern worth testing:
  · "the design graph does NOT branch with git" — one store serves every branch, so an export carries another branch's writes. Caught once as four phantom drifts that would have merged cleanly.
  · The whole export procedure — restore from origin/main, export exactly once, verify prev_content_hash — is a HAND-OPERATED RECONCILIATION PROTOCOL between the two models, and every one of its documented traps is a reconciliation bug.
  · The mirror-refresh defect (v0.12.0 → v0.29.0): a stale pin reporting FRESH after a failed refresh is a staleness-register lie, which is the classic AP failure mode.
  · 2026-08-12, this session: creating nodes after exporting silently put the record behind the graph. Nothing prevented it; only a later `compare_designs` would have caught it.

═══ THE OPTIONS ═══

A — NOTHING. Record the observation and stop. CHEAP, and possibly correct: nothing would compute differently, and the choices are already made, individually, with better-reasoned rationales than "CAP says so."

B — USE IT AS A LENS ONLY, in prose. Name the store/record split in AGENTS.md so a newcomer meets it once instead of rediscovering it through the export traps. Cheap, no code, no schema.

C — MAKE THE SEAM A FIRST-CLASS THING THE GRAPH KNOWS. If the record and the store are two replicas with a hand-run reconciliation protocol, then the protocol deserves to be modelled — the traps are currently memory and prose, not structure. Most expensive, and the one where something could actually compute.

D — TREAT IT AS A REQUIREMENTS SOURCE. Ask what reflow2's own availability target IS. It has never been stated, and `dec:read-while-held-mechanism` answered a CAP question without one.

═══ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea ═══

⚠️ 1. CAP IS ABOUT REPLICATED DATA UNDER NETWORK PARTITION, and reflow2's "partition" is mostly a HUMAN and PROCESS boundary — git branches, separate sessions, a person on a plane. Borrowing a theorem outside its domain is how architectures acquire vocabulary they cannot cash. The single strongest objection.

⚠️ 2. THERE IS NO REPLICATION PROTOCOL HERE. CAP's interesting cases begin with replicas that must agree. reflow2 has one writer per store and delegates the distributed half wholesale to git — so "reflow2 is AP" may be a statement about GIT, correctly, and nothing about reflow2.

⚠️ 3. THE CHOICES ARE ALREADY MADE AND ALREADY BETTER-ARGUED. `dec:advisory-concurrency` rests on a measured outage of five of six sessions. Relabelling that as "we chose AP" is strictly less information than what is recorded.

⚠️ 4. NOTHING WOULD COMPUTE DIFFERENTLY under A or B, and this project's own bar — `dec:exploratory-staging`, the ility work — is whether a distinction changes a computation.

📌 A FAIR POINT FOR THE IDEA: the export traps keep being rediscovered, session after session, and live in a memory note rather than in the design. If naming the seam is what makes them explicable rather than a list of superstitions, that is worth something even under option B.
properties.name: OPEN — is reflow2 already a CP store behind an AP record, and is that seam where its recurring bugs live?
properties.rationale: Recorded under the brainstorm skill so the thinking survives without being claimed as intent. Kept because the descriptive half is verifiable today against existing nodes — dec:advisory-concurrency, dec:read-while-held-mechanism, cap:stale-seat-refusal, cap:the-record-moved-is-surfaced — and because it offers a single explanation for a family of recurring export and staleness bugs that are currently carried as procedure rather than as design. The counter-arguments are recorded beside rather than against; the strongest is that reflow2 delegates the distributed problem to git, which would make this a statement about git.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-09, on why he built the content store in the first place: \"one of the primary reasons I had also developed the blob was to capture actual agent session context. from my limited understanding, an agent is stateless because it can't recall previous session's context. by storing in the blob, I thought I could make a session 'stateful'. ... however, every decision that an agent makes and implements is already embedded in the graph because it is already using reflow2, therefore, ingesting session context is moot or not needed?\"

⭐ THE QUESTION HAS A RECORDED ANSWER ALREADY, and it is sharper than either yes or no. cap:session-memory (PLANNED, framing settled by Anthony himself on 2026-07-25) states it directly: \"Decision.rationale and ChangeEvent already capture fragments of the why; WHAT LIVES ONLY IN THE SESSION IS THE CONNECTIVE TISSUE — what was tried, what was rejected and on what grounds, which findings turned up while doing something else.\"

So the split is:
  MOOT — the design content. Decisions, their rationale, requirements, changes, snapshots, questions and answers all land in the graph as they happen. Storing a transcript to preserve those would be a second copy of something already held better.
  NOT MOOT — the connective tissue. What was attempted and abandoned, what failed and why, what cost more than expected, what was noticed sideways. None of that is design intent, so none of it has a natural node, and it is precisely what a later session needs in order not to repeat the work.

⭐⭐ THIS SESSION IS THE EVIDENCE, and it is self-implicating rather than hypothetical. 2026-08-09 produced a great deal of design content, all of it now in the graph. It also produced process knowledge that is in NONE of it: hashing an artifact before the last edit FIVE times (because every mandatory gate — fmt, a clippy fix, a skill_lint trim — mutates the file AFTER the work looks finished); piping a gate into `tail` so the pipe returned tail's exit code and a red gate was pushed past; merging a four-PR stack in one loop so three PRs landed in already-squashed base branches and were stranded while GitHub reported all four as MERGED. **Every one of those lives in a markdown memory file OUTSIDE reflow2 entirely.** That is the connective tissue cap:session-memory names, currently housed in exactly the kind of file dec:what-lives-where was written to retire.

=== AND THE PART THAT BEARS ON THE BLOB ===

THE STORE WAS NEVER THE RIGHT MECHANISM FOR THIS, AND cap:session-memory ALREADY SAYS SO: \"a pointer to a 3 MB transcript is a RECEIPT, not documentation: leaning on it recreates the markdown problem one level down, since 'it is all in the transcript' is the same excuse as 'it is all in the backlog file'.\"

Its actual design needs no content store at all: session takeaways as FIRST-CLASS GRAPH CONTENT, written when they happen, anchored to the session's epoch, queryable afterwards. The transcript is modelled as a Fragment carrying the session UUID as portable identity — A POINTER, NOT BYTES — with the absolute path explicitly demoted to a machine-scoped hint, because a path stored as identity resolves for one person and silently misses for everyone else.

⇒ SO THE SESSION-CONTEXT JUSTIFICATION FOR THE BLOB DOES NOT SURVIVE, but not for the reason the question proposes. It is not that session context is worthless — it is that ITS VALUE IS IN DISTILLED NODES, WHICH NEED NO STORE. Storing the transcript would preserve the receipt and lose the documentation.

THE FRAMING THAT MAKES THIS MORE THAN CLEANUP, and it is Anthony's own from 2026-07-25: a session's context IS documentation — the how-and-why record of a design's evolution — and documentation is part of the product. That changes the standard rather than the mechanism: \"a convenience can be skipped under load, a deliverable cannot.\"

=== WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN ===

(1) IS THE STATELESSNESS PREMISE ALREADY ANSWERED? reflow2's whole pitch is that the graph is the memory (req:persistence). If so, a transcript store would be a SECOND, lossier memory competing with the first — and two sources of truth is the failure this project designs out everywhere else. That reading says the blob's session justification was solving a problem reflow2 already solves.

(2) WHAT FORCES THE CONNECTIVE TISSUE TO BE WRITTEN? cap:session-memory names this as its load-bearing gap: \"the existing handoff enforcement watches the modification time of MARKDOWN files, so the only mechanism forcing a session to leave takeaways behind POINTS AWAY FROM THE GRAPH.\" That is still true today — it is why this session's process findings are in a memory file. Fixing it is a nudge/hook question, not a storage question.

(3) DOES PROCESS KNOWLEDGE BELONG IN A DESIGN GRAPH AT ALL? Honest counter, recorded beside rather than argued down: \"I hashed before running fmt\" is not design intent. It may belong to the harness or to a project's own working notes, and forcing it into the design graph could make the graph a log — which is the failure mode dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written warns about from the other direction. cap:session-memory's answer is the documentation reframe; whether that reframe holds for PROCESS failures as well as DESIGN reasoning is genuinely unsettled.

NOTHING IS PROMOTED. Anthony asked a question; cap:session-memory remains PLANNED and unchanged.
properties.name: OPEN — if every decision an agent makes is already in the graph, is capturing session context moot? (No, but the part that isn't moot never needed a blob)
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill: one Decision per open question, at `proposed`, counters beside the options, nothing promoted.

Deliberately NOT folded into cap:session-memory, and not used to edit it. That capability already holds the answer to the moot question and its framing is Anthony's own; this node records that the question was asked again, what the existing answer is, and the one part that genuinely bears on the content-store decision — that the session-context justification for the blob does not survive, because the value is in distilled nodes rather than stored bytes.

Linked to dec:idea-discontinue-the-content-store because it removes one of that decision's stated motivations, which is a material change to the argument rather than a footnote.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's idea, 2026-08-15, in his words: "maybe reflow2 needs a /feedback skill to insert feedback into the graph. we have a few capture type skills already and we've used a brainstorm at times, and we have mass ingest. the thing with feedback is you don't know if it is an idea or test results or maybe it's a word by your boss on something — my point being, the feedback skill needs to determine intent/content to properly address. like I said, we have a lot of already existing skills, so this probably isn't a create-from-scratch effort, but a question of how to quickly capture external feedback in the graph."

DELIBERATELY DISTINCT FROM THE THREE NODES THE GUARD NAMED, all of which are about feedback LEAVING: `dec:idea-agent-to-agent-feedback-is-a-formal-channel` (should agents write reports for other agents), `req:agent-authored-feedback-is-reproducible-and-never-leaves-unasked` (nothing leaves without the human's word), `fact:second-user-report-2026-08-11` (one such report's content). THIS IS THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION — somebody else's report arriving, and what it becomes once it is here. Nothing in the design covers intake.

⭐ EVIDENCE FROM DOING IT BY HAND, TWICE, TODAY. This session processed two external feedback documents — a Grok session's 14 items and a US-government genesis session's 4 — and INVENTED THE SAME ROUTING BOTH TIMES with nothing to consult: verify each claim against the running build; `search_design` for an existing node before writing; defects to `TemporalFact` per `dec:defects-are-temporal-facts`; open questions to `proposed` Decisions; ideas via brainstorm; provenance via Fragments and `YIELDED`. That is knowledge re-derived per session — the exact failure `fact:defect-a-pre-served-skills-install-is-stranded` names as reflow2's own reason to exist. It is also the shape that produced `link-projects`: a process performed ad hoc, noticed, and made a served skill.

⭐⭐ THE SHARPENING, AND IT IS NOT WHAT THE QUESTION ASSUMES. He frames the discriminator as CONTENT — idea vs test result vs boss's word. Measured against what actually happened, the harder discriminator is AUTHORITY. The same sentence routes differently depending on who said it: "this should be civil-date, not UTC" from a user is an observation; from the design's owner it MOVES A STATUS. Moving a status is precisely what an agent may not do on its own (`dec:certainty-derived`). reflow2 already models this — `Contributor`, and `AUTHORED_BY` with `role: author | reviewer | approver` — and NOTHING READS IT AT INTAKE. A skill routing on content alone would take a boss's ruling and file it as somebody's opinion.

⭐⭐ AND THE FIRST STEP IS NOT RECORDING, IT IS VERIFYING. Of the 18 items processed today, FOUR were wrong as stated: `get_instructions` truncating (it was the client's cap), the export needing the server stopped (it does not), `Constraint` requiring numeric fields (it does not — and that error had already cost that project eleven permanently-open gaps), and a claim of mine that `VIOLATES` was read by nothing. A skill whose first move is "record what they said" would have written four false facts into the graph, each carrying a real source's authority. NO EXISTING CAPTURE SKILL HAS A VERIFY STEP, because `capture-intent` takes the user's words AS intent by definition — right for intent, wrong for a report about a system that can be checked.

THE OPTIONS:

(a) A NEW `feedback` SKILL THAT ROUTES — a triage front door: verify what is checkable, search for the node that already holds it, then hand off to `capture-intent` (new intent), `brainstorm` (an idea), `governance-proposal` (a rule), `revise-design` (a change to something recorded), `reconcile_verification` (a test result), or a `TemporalFact` (a defect found by use). CHEAPEST TO DESCRIBE, and it matches his read that this is composition rather than new machinery. COUNTER: a router that only routes leaves the two hard steps — verify, and read authority — to judgement, which is exactly where today's four errors would have come from.

(b) A SKILL THAT DOES THE WHOLE JOB: verify → attribute authority → search → record → link provenance → report what was refuted. STRONGEST, and it captures what was actually derived twice. COUNTER: it duplicates chunks of four existing skills, and this project has been bitten before by instructions drifting out of step with the tools they describe.

(c) NO NEW SKILL; EXTEND `capture-intent` with a triage section. No 21st skill, and capture-intent is already the front door people reach for. COUNTER: capture-intent's contract is that the user's words ARE intent; bolting "first check whether they are true" onto that changes what the skill IS.

(d) DO NOTHING — the mapping table in `capture-intent` plus judgement covers it. COUNTER, measured: judgement produced the right answer twice today at considerable cost in re-derivation, and the same judgement also produced four claims that survived only because they were checked.

⚠️ COST THAT MUST BE WEIGHED: twenty skills already ship, and eleven had no slash command until recently. A 21st has to earn its place against the context every session pays.

⚠️ AND IT INHERITS AN UNRESOLVED PROBLEM: feedback usually arrives AS A DOCUMENT, and `rule:design-information-lives-in-the-graph-not-in-documents` is now enforced while `Fragment.content_ref` is explicitly a pointer "rather than inlining" the text. Until that is scoped, a feedback skill cannot say where a report's un-distilled remainder goes.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether feedback volume justifies a skill at all — three external reports in eight days is either a trend or a coincidence.
properties.name: IDEA — external feedback arrives undifferentiated: an idea, a test result, or the boss's word. Should reflow2 have a `feedback` skill that determines what it is and routes to the skills that already exist?
properties.rationale: Recorded via the brainstorm skill: one Decision per open question, at `proposed`, options with counters beside them, nothing promoted. Started as a new node rather than merged after the guard named three near matches — all three concern feedback LEAVING the project, and this is intake, which is the opposite direction and shares only the word. The two sharpenings — that authority rather than content is the harder discriminator, and that verification precedes recording — are findings from this session's measured work, stated as findings rather than as answers.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-11, thinking out loud — nothing here is settled and nothing should be quoted back as intent.

HIS IDEA, IN HIS WORDS: "attach some type of additional parameters to each requirement or capability node. something that accounts for the full lifecycle of that requirement/capability. for instance, have fields for: develop-using, development-test-plan, operational-test-plan, production-plan, operational-deployed. there might be other 'dimensions' to a requirement node, but having something at the very beginning of design that already has an agent/user thinking from the get-go how it will eventually be fielded in an operational environment is good to have upfront. many of the things may be unknown-at-this-moment or N/A, but at least something is there to drive the thought process."

⭐ THE GOAL IS THE PROMPT, NOT THE FIELD. Read his last sentence: the value he names is that the question gets ASKED early, and he expects most answers to be empty. That is a statement about when a thought happens, not about where a value is stored — and it is what separates the options below. An option that stores five mostly-empty fields but never asks anything would miss the point entirely; an option that asks all five questions and stores nothing until there is an answer would meet it.

WHAT THE DESIGN ALREADY HOLDS, so a later reader is not re-deciding settled ground. Each of his five axes already has machinery, but scattered and edge-shaped rather than gathered on the node:
- development-test-plan / operational-test-plan — `dec:idea-verification-is-planned-with-the-requirement` is ALREADY OPEN and asks almost exactly this: "should reflow2 guide a project to plan HOW a need will be verified when the need is stated, rather than only asking for a check once something is built?" His two test-plan axes are that question, split into a development arm and an operational arm — which is a V-model distinction that open question does not currently draw.
- operational-deployed — Environment nodes, `deploy_to`, `reconcile_deployment` and `cmp:fielded` already model where something actually runs.
- production-plan / readiness to field — the Readiness layer (TRL/MRL, ReadinessAssessment, GATED_ON with a required `min_level`) already models whether a thing is mature enough to field, and `SCHEDULED_FOR` models when it is due.
- develop-using — nothing obvious models this. It is the one axis with no existing home.
- Requirement already carries a five-state lifecycle (proposed/accepted/deferred/dropped/met) of which THREE ARE UNUSED — recorded in `chg:bl104-derived-completion` as "the requirement lifecycle is 3/5 unused". Any new lifecycle vocabulary has to answer why it would fare better than the one already there and unused.

THE OPTIONS, with what is cheap and what is expensive about each.

A — PROPERTIES ON THE NODE, his literal proposal. Five enum/string fields on Requirement and Capability. Cheapest to build (schema YAML), and the fields are visible in every export and every view, so they nag by existing. EXPENSIVE: BL-198 has just spent this month REMOVING stored defaults — 3,207 of them across 59% of nodes — because a value written by the tool rather than by a person makes `compare_designs` unable to tell a default from a decision. Five fields defaulting to "unknown" on every node is that exact shape, freshly re-introduced. And "N/A" written by an agent is a judgement about scope, which `dec:readiness-is-an-observation-the-threshold-is-the-judgement` says the tool does not get to make on the user's behalf.

B — ASK THE FIVE QUESTIONS, STORE NOTHING UNTIL THERE IS AN ANSWER. A gap detector in the existing detect-and-ask loop that asks, of a requirement, "how will this be developed / checked in development / checked in operations / produced / fielded?" No schema change; nothing is stored until somebody answers, so silence stays silence and never becomes a stored "unknown". Matches the goal he actually stated, since the thought is what he wants triggered. EXPENSIVE: the loop already owes 67 unasked gaps, and five new questions on every requirement would swamp it — this needs a rule about WHICH requirements deserve the questions (and when), or it drowns the thing it is added to.

C — EDGES TO REAL NODES, which is what reflow2 does today. A test plan is a Verification, a production plan is a Release/DesignEpoch, fielding is an Environment. Nothing new at all. CHEAP and already queryable end to end. EXPENSIVE, and this is Anthony's actual complaint: it only ever happens when somebody REMEMBERS to draw the edge, so the thinking never gets prompted at the start — which is the whole thing he is asking for.

D — A SIDE NODE PER AXIS, on the DimensionAssessment pattern that already exists for cross-cutting concerns. Keeps the requirement clean, lets an axis carry its own provenance and date, and extends to "other dimensions" without another schema change each time — which is the extensibility his aside asks about. EXPENSIVE: a node per axis per requirement is a lot of graph for something usually empty, and it is the heaviest of the four.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO THE WHOLE IDEA, recorded beside it rather than used to kill it: a checklist filled with "unknown-at-this-moment" on every node teaches people to skip it, and then reflow2 holds five more fields nobody reads — the exact failure already measured twice here, in the 3-of-5 unused requirement lifecycle and in the two evidence-quality axes used zero times. Whatever is chosen has to say what READS the answer, because a marker nothing reads is a comment.

NOT DECIDED, and deliberately not ranked. B and C are not exclusive — B could be the prompt that leads to C's edges, which would need no new vocabulary at all.
properties.name: OPEN — should a Requirement/Capability carry lifecycle dimensions from the moment it is written, so fielding is thought about at the start?
properties.rationale: Anthony's, 2026-08-11: "having something at the very beginning of design that already has an agent/user thinking from the get-go how it will eventually be fielded in an operational environment is good to have upfront." The design's V-model has both arms and no rungs, and this is a proposal for rungs stated at the top of the left arm — which is why it is worth recording even though four of the five axes already have scattered machinery.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-05: "just curious if it is a hard limit for a project to be limited to one graph_id? for instance, could a project say, could list 3 different graph_ids and be able to do reflow2 operations on whichever or multiple based on the question. this would be a different way of linking multiple graphs, which was an idea that we had discussed previously."

⭐ FIRST, THE MEASURED ANSWER, BECAUSE THIS ONE IS CHECKABLE AND WAS CHECKED. IT IS NOT A HARD LIMIT AT THE STORAGE LAYER.
  - Storage keys are `{graph_id}\x00{type}\x00{id}` (`dynograph_storage::keys`), so one store namespaces many graphs by construction.
  - `DesignGraph::with_graph_id` (graph.rs:191) IS A FIELD ASSIGNMENT — `self.graph_id = id.into()`. Rebinding a handle to another graph in the same store is FREE: no reopen, no lock churn, no cost. Its own doc comment says the intent out loud: "to host several designs in one storage instance".
  - `open_in_memory_as(graph_id)` already exists for the same reason.
So "list 3 graph_ids and operate on whichever" is architecturally CHEAP TODAY. What blocks it is the SERVER, not the store: the MCP service holds one `Arc<RwLock<DesignGraph>>` bound at launch, and no tool takes a graph argument.

⭐⭐ SECOND, AND IT IS THE PART THAT DECIDES WHETHER THIS IS "LINKING" AT ALL: EDGES STILL CANNOT CROSS GRAPH_IDS, EVEN INSIDE ONE STORE. `create_edge` (graph.rs:276) resolves BOTH endpoints through `self.get_node(kind, id)`, which is scoped to the bound `graph_id` — so an edge to a node in a sibling graph is refused as `NodeNotFound`. That refusal is deliberate and well-argued (a dangling edge "is not a judgement call the user might reasonably disagree with… it is a graph that cannot be walked"), and it applies here without having been written for this case.

SO THE HONEST FRAMING OF WHAT THIS BUYS: co-location gives CHEAP SWITCHING and ONE PLACE TO LOOK. It does NOT give cross-graph edges, so it does not by itself answer [BL-214] — the prose cross-references that `detect_gaps` and `propagate_change` cannot see. What it DOES do is make cross-graph edges a much shorter path IF they are ever wanted, because the key encoding already namespaces and the endpoint check is one scope decision rather than a storage redesign.

⭐ WHY THIS IS A GENUINELY NEW OPTION RATHER THAN A RESTATEMENT. `dec:nested-graphs` (accepted 2026-07-25) weighed exactly three: (a) one graph, zoom by level; (b) a graph per system; (c) a graph per ownership boundary, which it took. ALL THREE ASSUME ONE GRAPH PER STORE — the store/graph distinction was never in play, so "many graphs, one store, switchable" was not among the roads taken OR the roads not taken. It sits between (a) and (c): more separation than one graph, less ceremony than federation, and it costs none of the three obligations (a coordinate, an evidence roll-up, a freshness check) that the accepted rule says every seam must pay — because there is no seam, only a scope.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) LEAVE IT — one graph per store, federate across stores as `dec:nested-graphs` prescribes. Counter: that is what produced prose cross-references and three stores on one repo, and federation's costs are being paid by one person with no authority boundary to justify them. (b) SEVERAL GRAPHS IN ONE STORE, ONE BOUND AT A TIME — the cheapest real change: a graph reference selects which, edges stay within a graph, reads and writes stay scoped. Counter: it makes "which design am I writing to" a per-call question, which is `dec:how-a-session-is-pointed-at-a-design`'s hazard exactly — and getting it wrong writes to the wrong design. The refuse-when-several rule recorded there applies here unchanged. (c) SEVERAL GRAPHS, QUERIED TOGETHER — "operations on multiple based on the question", Anthony's stronger reading. Counter: EVERY read is `self.engine.scan_nodes(&self.graph_id, …)`, so this is not a parameter, it is a change to how every analysis is scoped, and the reports would need to say WHICH graph each finding came from or become unreadable. (d) SEVERAL GRAPHS AND EDGES MAY CROSS THEM — the full version, and the only one that answers [BL-214]. Counter: it reopens `create_edge`'s endpoint invariant, which currently guarantees every reader a walkable graph, and it needs an answer to what a cross-graph edge MEANS when one side is exported and the other is not.

⚠️ AND THE CONSTRAINT THAT CUTS ACROSS ALL OF THEM: `req:persistence` says "the design persists in-repo alongside the code" and `dec:repo-file-embedded` says the graph lives as a repo file. A single store holding several projects' designs lives in ONE repo or in none — so (b), (c) and (d) all need that requirement revisited rather than quietly contradicted. That is the same tension `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` option (d) hit, and it is the real price here, not the code.

WHAT MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED: `with_graph_id` is free and already intended for this; `create_edge` refuses cross-scope endpoints and the refusal is deliberate; the MCP server binds one graph at launch; and `dec:nested-graphs` never considered this shape, so taking it is an addition to that decision rather than a contradiction of it.

NOT CHECKED: whether the export/import path carries `graph_id` in a way that would let one store's several graphs be exported separately — `export_graph` writes the bound graph, and `import_graph` "adopts the document's own graph_id", which suggests it would work, but nobody has tried it.
properties.name: OPEN — should a project hold SEVERAL graph_ids in one store and operate on whichever the question needs, which is a linking mechanism nested-graphs never considered?
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill at Anthony's request, and the mechanical half was CHECKED IN THE CODE BEFORE ANY OF IT WAS WRITTEN — deliberately, because three times earlier the same day this agent asserted a mechanism from a description and was wrong each time. The three facts that matter here (with_graph_id is a field assignment, create_edge scopes both endpoints, the server binds one handle) are cited to file and line so the next session argues from them rather than re-reading.

Recorded as its own node rather than folded into `dec:idea-one-owner-many-projects` because that node asks WHERE the boundary goes and this one asks WHAT A STORE MAY HOLD — they interact but are separately answerable, and one node holding both could only be half-answered.

The observation that `dec:nested-graphs` never considered this shape is the load-bearing part. That decision is accepted and its reasoning is sound; this is not a challenge to it but a fourth option it did not have, and saying so plainly is what stops a later reader treating this as reopening a settled question.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent. Anthony, 2026-08-11: "there have several times where I've forked off somebody's repo and tried something just to see if it was possible... do we allow users of reflow2 to 'fork' off a main design and explore without having the requirement for anything they build to have 'requirement' linked to it. then if the exploratory fork off main design works, is there a way to 'merge' into main?" His own lean, recorded as his: "can something merge into main design without a requirement associated with it (I'm kind of leaning towards no)".

⭐ THE QUESTION SHARPENS TO ONE THING: WHERE THE GATE SITS. Nobody is proposing that unmotivated work be invisible — `unmotivated_capability` fires today and should. The open question is whether it should be SILENT IN A FORK and BINDING AT THE MERGE, which is a different placement, not a different rule.

⚠️ THE COST OF THE CURRENT PLACEMENT IS MEASURED, and it is in `dec:exploratory-staging`: a Capability at `planned` with no Requirement raises THREE gaps — `unmotivated_capability`, `unrealized_capability`, `unverified_capability` — "THREE GAPS EACH, FOREVER, BY CONSTRUCTION". On 2026-08-10 that was 34 of 73 open gaps, 47% of the list, from backlog rows that were wishes nobody had agreed to. An exploratory fork is the same shape at speed: every spike accrues three gaps, and a fork built to answer "is this even possible" would be all noise by the end of an afternoon.

📌 SO THE FORK CASE MAY BE THE MISSING EVIDENCE `dec:exploratory-staging` IS WAITING FOR. That decision's closing question is "DOES A NOT-YET-AGREED WISH BELONG IN THE DESIGN AT ALL?" and its options (b) a `proposed` Capability status and (c) route wishes to a Decision are both about giving unagreed work a silent home. A fork is a place where unagreed work is not merely tolerated but is THE POINT, which is a stronger argument for a silent home than a backlog row ever was. These should be read together.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) GATE AT THE MERGE, NOT THE WRITE. The fork writes freely; `apply_merge` refuses to land a Capability with no incoming SATISFIES unless the merger states one or explicitly accepts it as unmotivated. This is EXACTLY the shape `apply_merge` already has — `dec:merge-three-way` makes it refuse, writing nothing, until every conflict is decided — so the mechanism is a second refusal reason rather than a new mechanism. It also matches Anthony's lean.
(b) SILENCE THE DETECTORS IN A FORK by marking the design exploratory, so gaps stay quiet until it is merged. Cheap, and it hides real findings: a fork that is quietly incoherent looks identical to one that is fine, which is the false-green class this project keeps finding.
(c) DO NOTHING. Explore in a fork, tolerate the gap noise, and let the merge be an ordinary merge. Zero build cost; the noise is the cost, and it is the cost `dec:exploratory-staging` already measured at 47% of a real gap list.
(d) REQUIRE MOTIVATION AT THE WRITE EVEN IN A FORK — the status quo. Honest and it forbids the thing Anthony is describing: you cannot try something to see if it is possible if you must first say why you want it.

⚠️ THE ARGUMENT FOR HIS LEAN, stated because it is stronger than it first looks. What lands in the primary design becomes what the golden thread computes delivery from. `req:completion-computed` (accepted) derives delivery FROM the thread rather than from a status field, so a Capability merged in with nothing behind it silently degrades the one number the design is supposed to be able to state honestly. A fork can afford incoherence because nothing computes from it; the primary design cannot.

⚠️ THE ARGUMENT AGAINST IT, equally real. `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` (proposed) exists because a body of intent that contradicts itself is still a design, and `rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party` says the target is a consumer's project — where brownfield reality is that things get built and the requirement is written afterwards, if ever. A merge gate that admits no unmotivated work forbids adopting the very case `adopt` exists for. Whatever is chosen must let a merger say "yes, this is unmotivated, and I am taking it anyway" and have that recorded rather than blocked — which is what makes (a) a two-sided accept and not a wall.

⚠️ AND THE HONEST WARNING FROM THE SAME FAMILY: the detect-and-ask skill forbids inventing a requirement to close `unmotivated_capability` — "a requirement backed out of the thing that implements it is satisfied by construction and can never contradict anything." A merge gate that demands a requirement will produce exactly those unless the accept-it-anyway route is first-class and cheap.
properties.name: OPEN — may an exploratory fork build without requirements, and is the motivation gate at the WRITE or at the MERGE?
properties.rationale: The question is not whether unmotivated work is visible but where the gate sits. Gating at the merge lets a fork do what a fork is for while keeping the primary design's delivery number honest, and it reuses apply_merge's existing refuse-until-decided shape rather than inventing one. The fork case is also stronger evidence for dec:exploratory-staging's open question than the backlog rows that raised it, since in a fork unagreed work is the point rather than a leftover.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony's idea, 2026-08-01, and the first run has already paid (BL-153/154/155). What is open is not whether the measurement is useful, but how far it should go and what it must never become.

WHAT WAS DONE, and it is now `tools/surface_usage.py`: read the retained Claude Code transcripts, count tool calls, build the tool-to-tool transition graph, and run PageRank over it with self-loops removed. 46 sessions, 6,095 calls, 10 projects.

WHY THE GRAPH OPERATION EARNS ITS KEEP: it disagrees with raw counts. Volume puts `release_includes` first (1,008 calls, bookkeeping in 7 sessions); PageRank puts `detect_gaps`, `loop_status`, `export_graph`, `detect_defects` first — the coherence loop's read side, which is what workflows route THROUGH. High-volume-low-PageRank is a batching defect; high-PageRank is load-bearing. One measurement, two questions, and the tool that tops one does not top the other.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, none answered:
(a) HOW FAR DOES IT GO? Today it is a manual, offline, read-only probe over transcripts a developer happens to have. The tempting next step is telemetry FROM the server — and that is a different product with different consent, privacy and trust properties. A design brain that watches its users is not obviously the same thing as one that keeps their design coherent.
(b) MAY ANY OF IT REACH THE GRAPH? `dec:loop-status-state-not-history` says loop debt is computed from graph state and never from run history, and 'looking is not writing' is a standing rule. That decision is about DEBT specifically, not about whether usage telemetry may exist at all — but nobody has ever said so out loud, and this is the moment to decide rather than to assume. The instrument as written writes nothing, which keeps the question open rather than answering it by accident.
(c) WHAT IS THE HONEST UNIT? Self-loop share proxies for a missing bulk form, and it worked. But a design brain optimised for fewer tool calls is not obviously optimised for better designs, and BL-23's lesson is that a number which punishes correct work needs a different question rather than a tuned threshold. There is no target self-loop share and there should not be one.
(d) OTHER PROJECTS' TRANSCRIPTS ARE OTHER PEOPLE'S WORK. Reading Anthony's own machine is one thing. If this ever runs over a consumer's sessions it needs their word first, and probably needs to never leave their machine.

THE HONEST LIMIT ALREADY FOUND: absence is weak evidence. `set_project_mode` appears as text in ten transcripts with zero recorded calls, so a tool used before the retention window is indistinguishable from one never used. Any 'unused' verdict from this instrument is a question, not a finding.
properties.name: OPEN — should real usage telemetry be a standing instrument for shaping the surface, and how far may it go?
properties.rationale: Recorded as an idea rather than a capability because the measurement is already built and useful while the QUESTIONS it raises — server-side telemetry, whether any of it may become graph state, consent over other people's transcripts — are genuinely undecided and would each be a different product. Anthony's idea; the first run produced three backlog rows.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Source: Alex Sligar's 2026-08-05 research (relayed by Anthony 2026-08-06), specifically Graphify (Tree-sitter static analysis plus LLM semantic extraction) and Understand Anything (multi-agent pipeline over every file, function, class and dependency, with architectural-layer and business-domain views on top). STILL OPEN.

THE IDEA: the adopt skill currently recovers an existing system by having an agent read it. The survey's tools do the structural half MECHANICALLY and deterministically — files, functions, classes, imports, calls, API surfaces, DB models — and spend the LLM only on summaries. Splitting adopt the same way would make the cheap half cheap and exact, and leave the agent doing only what the artifact cannot tell you: why it was built that way, who asked for it, what is now vestigial. It would also make link-artifacts and reconcile_artifacts far cheaper to keep true, since registering artifacts and their hashes is precisely a mechanical sweep.

WHAT IS CHEAP: the extraction itself is a solved problem with off-the-shelf parsers, and it is deterministic, which sits well with req:deterministic-core.

WHAT IS EXPENSIVE: a parser per language, kept current — and Anthony's real operating context is a ten-year-old Python stack (bluesky, tiled) plus beamline analysis code, so the language surface is not small and much of it is dynamic, where static analysis is weakest.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is the strong one, from reflow2's own record: dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition already decided that reflow2's systems are FUNCTIONAL, not its file tree. Mechanical extraction from source produces exactly the decomposition that decision rejected — a Component per module, an Interface per public signature — which is a map of the repository, not of the design. Feeding that in would populate the graph with structure at the wrong altitude, and the wrong altitude is harder to fix than an empty graph because it looks finished. Understand Anything's "architectural layers (API, service, data, UI)" is an attempt at the same altitude problem, and it solves it by guessing, which is what dec:views-are-projections forbids reflow2 from doing.

A NARROWER VERSION THAT MAY SURVIVE THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT: extract only ARTIFACTS and their content hashes, not Components or Interfaces. That is the layer whose identity genuinely IS the file, so no altitude claim is being made, and it is the layer reflow2 already models as files (art:*, set_artifact_checksum, cap:link-artifacts). The mechanical pass would then answer "what exists on disk and has it changed" and say nothing about what the design means. Offered as a distinction to consider, not as advocacy.

RELATED, NOT THE SAME QUESTION: whether reflow2 should CONSUME an existing code-graph tool's output rather than build extraction itself. The survey's tools all expose their graph over MCP, which would make them an ingest source rather than a rival. Unexplored.
properties.name: OPEN — should adopt extract code STRUCTURE mechanically (tree-sitter style) and reserve the agent for intent, when reflow2 has already decided decomposition is functional and not the file tree?
properties.rationale: Recorded as an idea because the mechanical/intent split is a genuinely good shape that the adopt skill does not currently have, and recording it with dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition named beside it is the point — the objection is what makes this idea usable later, and an idea killed in conversation would have lost it.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled.

THE IDEA: dynograph_graph::link_prediction_all / link_prediction_from (unused) score non-adjacent node pairs by how much their neighbourhoods overlap — common neighbours, Jaccard, or Adamic-Adar (which down-weights hubs). Read on a design graph: "these two look like they should be connected and are not — is there a missing SATISFIES, or DEPENDS_ON?"

WHERE IT LANDS: BL-114's unsolved half. That item records that disconnected_community SUGGESTS adding a bridge while its suggestion does not know the detector's own selectivity, so the advised bridge's only correct forms are edge types the measurement excludes. Link prediction would propose WHICH bridge, on evidence rather than on a template.

IT MUST BE AN ASK, NEVER A REPAIR. dec:ask-not-repair (suspected duplicates are asked, never merged) and dec:report-dont-judge both apply directly, and apply_heal already proposes-and-stops in rigid mode. A predicted edge written into the graph would be reflow2 inventing design.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it may be fatal: a golden thread is largely a TREE. Trees have very few common neighbours, so neighbourhood-overlap scores may be near-zero almost everywhere and the signal may simply not exist on this shape of graph. That is measurable BEFORE any build — run it over reflow2's own 1179-node export and see whether anything scores. docs/sharpening.md is exactly the discipline for that, and this should not be built until the instrument says there is a signal.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 propose MISSING edges from neighbourhood overlap, as a question rather than a repair?
properties.rationale: Included because it is the only unused foundation function that addresses BL-114's open half; recorded with its likely-fatal objection attached rather than argued down, so a later session inherits both.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-06, extending the federation idea into his own professional domain: "in the military, when you have a clearance, there is a 'need to know' and a person only gets what they need to know. often SAP/SAR programs are like this. reflow2 could support both this mechanically by user1 being the only person to projectA... then user2 who does not have a need to know only has access to projectB... and their projectC. mechanically, they'd have to have access to some machine that could hold the graph for the different clearance levels."

NOTE ON THE EXAMPLE: Anthony flagged immediately afterwards that he had muddled which made-up project sat at which level ("oops, I think I goofed up the clearance levels of my made up projects, but hopefully the point is still valid"). It is. Nothing below rests on the specific levels — only on the SHAPE: user1 holds {A, B}, user2 holds {B, C}, and B is the overlap. The levels are deliberately not restated here, because the slip turned out to expose a real error in the first version of this node. See the correction below.

THE STRUCTURAL ANALOGY IS EXACT, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS DANGEROUS. The federation shape recorded in dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs — each person holds their own subtree plus one hop outward, cuts overlapping at ownership seams — is, drawn on a whiteboard, indistinguishable from need-to-know compartmentation. The overlap graph is the shared compartment. Nothing about the picture is wrong.

⚠️⚠️ WHAT MUST NOT BE READ INTO IT, AND THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT LINE IN THIS NODE: reflow2 IS NOT AN ACCESS CONTROL AND MUST NEVER BE DESCRIBED AS ONE. It has NO AUTHENTICATION OF ANY KIND — recorded already in req:a-session-cannot-reach-another-designs-graph, and --http-allow-host is Host-header allowlisting for DNS-rebinding protection, not authentication. A list of graph_ids in a config file is a CONVENIENCE SCOPE: it says which designs a session bothers to load, not which designs a person is permitted to read. Anyone with filesystem read access to the store reads the entire design, config or no config. In most domains that distinction is pedantic. In THIS one it is the difference between a tool and an incident, and it is precisely the permission-versus-convenience question left open on the federation node — now with real consequences attached.

THE REAL SEPARATION IS THE ACCREDITATION BOUNDARY, NOT THE APPLICATION. Anthony said the mechanical part himself — "they'd have to have access to some machine that could hold the graph for the different clearance levels." The enclave, the system-high accreditation and whatever guard moves data between them are the controls. reflow2's honest role is to be COMPATIBLE with that separation, never to implement it.

⭐ AND HERE THE FEDERATION SHAPE EARNS ITS KEEP FOR A REASON THAT HAS NOTHING TO DO WITH CONVENIENCE. Because nobody holds the whole DAG — each person holds a local cut — the design CAN be split across enclaves at all. A design brain that required the whole federation resident in one process to answer a question would be unusable above unclassified, full stop. The local-cut property is what makes cross-enclave design possible, and that is an architectural argument for it independent of anything about laptops and subtrees.

⭐ THE FILE-BASED MODEL IS THE ONE THAT SURVIVES AN AIR GAP, AND IT IS NOT LEGACY. dec:multi-writer-architecture (ACCEPTED) keeps the design as a graph-in-a-repo-file with many writers merging on pull, and its product is an EXPORT — a single, complete, content-hashed, deterministic file, with a three-way merge that can reconcile two divergent copies. FILES ARE WHAT A CROSS-DOMAIN TRANSFER PROCESS CAN ACTUALLY MOVE. The hosted always-on server of dec:one-process-many-stores — flo2's model, proposed the previous day — is not that, and could not be.
