So reflow2 now has TWO deployment shapes serving genuinely different worlds: hosted, for flo2's non-technical browser collaborators; file-and-merge, for anything behind an accreditation boundary. Recording this because the hosted work could easily be mistaken for the direction of travel, and for this class of user the repo-file model is not the old way — it is the only way.

⚠️⚠️ THE DIRECT COLLISION WITH THE FEATURE ANTHONY ASKED FOR AN HOUR EARLIER. dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency proposes that a gap in one design automatically become a requirement in the design it depends on. IN A COMPARTMENTED SETTING, AN AUTOMATIC CROSS-GRAPH WRITE IS A CHANNEL BETWEEN COMPARTMENTS. And it is worse than the content: the mere EXISTENCE and TIMING of activity on one side can be inferable from the other — a node id, a timestamp, a counter that ticks, "someone is blocked on this" — none of which is the sensitive fact and all of which can carry it. AGGREGATION compounds it: two designs each individually releasable may not be releasable together.

⭐⭐ CORRECTION, 2026-08-06, PROMPTED BY ANTHONY'S OWN SLIP ABOUT THE LEVELS — and it changes the engineering conclusion, so it is recorded rather than quietly edited. The first version of this node said "upward may be fine, downward is spillage." THAT CONFLATED TWO DIFFERENT AXES. Dependency direction (who consumes whom) and classification direction (what is more sensitive) are INDEPENDENT, and assuming they align is exactly the mistake the muddled example accidentally surfaced.

In the example as loosely written, the most sensitive project happened to also be the most upstream, so "flows upstream" and "flows to higher classification" looked like the same sentence. THEY ARE NOT, AND REFLOW2'S OWN REAL CASE IS THE OPPOSITE ONE: dynograph-foundation is the most upstream design and the least sensitive — a public library — while its consumers are the things that could carry sensitivity. So a gap in a classified consumer flowing UP into an unclassified foundation is a flow toward LOWER classification, which is the dangerous direction. The feature's most natural and most useful direction is, in the realistic configuration, the unsafe one.

THE CONSTRAINT THEREFORE HAS TO BE STATED AGAINST THE SENSITIVITY LATTICE, NOT AGAINST THE DEPENDENCY GRAPH — "one-directional by construction" is not enough, because the design cannot know which direction is safe without being told something it currently has no vocabulary for. Which loops back to option (b) below: SOME marking axis may be unavoidable, not because reflow2 should enforce anything, but because without it the tool cannot tell the safe direction from the unsafe one and must therefore refuse to flow anything automatically at all. That is a defensible answer — refuse rather than guess is this project's standing doctrine — and it should be reached deliberately rather than by omission.

THERE IS NO MARKING VOCABULARY, AND `designation` IS NOT IT. Searched before writing: the only thing resembling a marking is `designation` on Requirements and Interfaces, whose values are `internal` / `published`. That is the SHAPE of a marking — an opt-in, per-node, computed-upon label, withheld by default and counted when withheld — but it is about PUBLICATION BOUNDARIES, not sensitivity, and reading it as a classification would be a category error. Whether reflow2 should gain a real marking axis is a schema question and therefore at least a minor version, per the CHANGELOG's own rule.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.

(a) REFLOW2 MODELS NOTHING ABOUT CLASSIFICATION. The enclave separates; reflow2 is just a design tool that happens to run inside one. Cheapest, most honest, impossible to misread. Counter: the user still has to mark things somewhere, and it will end up in prose inside node text — the shadow-list failure again, and here an unmarked-but-sensitive statement sitting in a `statement` field is a genuine problem. AND, per the correction above, this option forecloses automatic cross-graph flow entirely, because a tool with no sensitivity vocabulary cannot know which direction is safe.

(b) A DESCRIPTIVE MARKING AXIS — a sensitivity label per node or per design, never enforcing, so an export can SAY what it contains and an automatic flow can at least refuse to run toward a lower label. Counter, and it is severe: a marking that does not enforce invites exactly the misreading warned about above, and a WRONG marking is more dangerous than none, because people act on it.

(c) REFLOW2 PROMISES ONLY NEGATIVE PROPERTIES, and says so plainly: never requires the whole federation in one place, never initiates a message (already true and verified against the service — proxy.rs), never phones home, and its export is a complete, self-describing, content-hashed file a human can inspect before it crosses anything. Marketed as COMPATIBLE WITH an accreditation boundary, never as implementing one. Cheap, truthful, and very nearly the current state already.

(d) CROSS-GRAPH FLOW IS DIRECTIONAL BY CONSTRUCTION AND EVERY CROSSING IS AN AUDITABLE EVENT — with the correction above attached: the direction must be defined against sensitivity, which (a) cannot express. Worth having on its own merits even with no classification involved, because "which design wrote into mine, when, and why" is a question any consumer wants answered.

WHAT IS NOT RECORDED HERE BECAUSE ANTHONY HAS NOT SAID IT: whether this is a real requirement he intends reflow2 to meet, or an observation that the shape happens to fit a world he knows well. He called it "just another spinoff of this idea", which reads as the latter — and the difference matters enormously, because (b) and (d) are real work and (a) and (c) are mostly writing down what is already true.
properties.name: OPEN — is the per-user graph scope a convenience or a COMPARTMENT, and what must reflow2 promise (and refuse to promise) if designs are separated by clearance?
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill, 2026-08-06, as the third node in one conversation — kept separate from the ACCESS question (dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs) and the AUTHORITY question (dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency) because it asks a third thing: what reflow2 may TRUTHFULLY CLAIM about separation, which is a question about the product's promises rather than about its mechanism.

CORRECTED WITHIN THE HOUR, AND THE CORRECTION IS KEPT IN THE NODE rather than silently replacing the text — the same discipline dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs used on 2026-08-05, and for the same reason: the failure mode should stay visible. The first version asserted "upward may be fine, downward is spillage", which quietly assumed the dependency ordering and the sensitivity ordering run together. They do not, and reflow2's own dependency chain is a counterexample — dynograph-foundation is simultaneously the most upstream and the least sensitive design in it. The error surfaced only because Anthony flagged that he had muddled the levels in his own example, which forced a re-read; a tidier example would have hidden it. Recorded as chg:classification-and-dependency-are-orthogonal.

Written with a deliberate bias toward what reflow2 must NOT say. Anthony is a Space Force systems engineer and this is his working domain, so the failure mode here is not that reflow2 lacks a feature — it is that a structural resemblance between "per-user graph scoping" and "need-to-know" gets read as a security property by someone who then relies on it. The node therefore leads with the disclaimer rather than the opportunity, and the disclaimer is drawn from intent the design already holds rather than from caution: req:a-session-cannot-reach-another-designs-graph states in its own text that reflow2 has no authentication and that authorization belongs to the layer in front.

Also recorded because it re-values something that could otherwise look superseded: the repo-file-plus-merge model (dec:multi-writer-architecture, accepted) is the ONLY one of reflow2's two deployment shapes that can cross an air gap, since its product is a complete deterministic file and a three-way merge. The hosted multi-graph work of the previous day is additive, not a migration, and this is the clearest statement yet of who each shape is for.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Source: Alex Sligar's 2026-08-05 research on the emerging "graph brain around the codebase" ecosystem, relayed by Anthony 2026-08-06. STILL OPEN.

WHAT THE SURVEY SHOWS. The field has converged on two families, and reflow2 is in neither:

(1) CODE-AS-GRAPH — Graphify, Understand Anything, Sourcegraph/Cody. The graph is DERIVED from the code by static analysis plus LLM summarisation. It answers "what depends on this", "what breaks if I change this function".

(2) AGENT MEMORY — Mem0, Zep/Graphiti, Letta (MemGPT), Cognee, Supermemory, LangMem, LlamaIndex Memory. The graph is DERIVED from conversation and execution traces. It answers "what did we say before", "what worked last time".

THE READING OFFERED, and it is the agent's own analysis rather than anything Alex or the research says: both families are DESCRIPTIVE, and the property they therefore cannot have is disagreement. A graph re-derived from the code can never contradict the code — if the code drifts from intent, the graph drifts with it and reports nothing. A memory layer never contradicts anything either; it recalls. reflow2's graph is AUTHORED and sits UPSTREAM of the code, which is what lets it say the code is wrong: drift, gaps, defects, unrealized capabilities, a failing gate. That is not a feature the survey's tools lack by oversight — it is unavailable to anything whose graph is a function of the artifact.

THE OPEN QUESTION, which is a design question and not a marketing one: if that is the line reflow2 defends, several current tensions resolve one way rather than the other. Retrieval quality (dec:idea-embeddings-adoption) becomes a convenience rather than the product. The gates, drift detection and the coherence loop become the core rather than the overhead. And "reflow2 as a memory layer you sprinkle on" becomes the wrong shape, because a layer that plugs into somebody else's agent framework has no standing to refuse. Conversely, if the line is NOT defended, the honest conclusion may be that several of these tools already do most of what a user wants at a fraction of the adoption cost.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT: every tool in the survey is a LAYER — it plugs into LangGraph/LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel or Claude Code, and the user keeps everything else they had. reflow2 is a whole system: its own store, schema, skill kit, gates and vocabulary. Being normative is exactly WHY it cannot be a thin layer, so the differentiator and the adoption cost are the same fact seen twice. req:thin-install and req:frictionless-update are pushing on this, and a one-line install does not by itself make a coherence loop cheap to adopt. Whether there is a legitimate smaller entry point — read-only, query-only, no loop — or whether that entry point would be a dishonest version of the product, is part of what is open here.

WHAT IS ALSO WORTH NOTING AND IS NOT A QUESTION: Sourcegraph exposing its graph to agents over MCP is the pattern reflow2 already implements. That is validation, not a gap. Mem0's "organizational memory" tier (knowledge many agents share) is the same territory as req:many-designs-one-service and dec:central-host, which are already in flight — also validation.
properties.name: OPEN — is reflow2's differentiator that the graph can be RIGHT when the code is WRONG, and what should follow from defending that line?
properties.rationale: Recorded because there is currently NO node anywhere in the design that says what reflow2 is that comparable tools are not, and a differentiator nobody wrote down cannot be defended when a build decision quietly trades it away. The specific value of the survey is that it is the first external evidence of what the alternatives actually do, so the comparison is against real systems rather than a supposed rival.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-05, in his own words: "one idea that I've come across is that I work many inter-related projects. it seems like a reflow2 project/graph is limited to one git repo. curious if we should remove this constraint? then I can use the reflow2 graph in one project (project_x) and still use it to guide a closely related project (say project_y). the benefit of this is that a set of projects done in this manner can all influence each other. another option is to build the reflow2 graph in the parent folder of a bunch of interrelated projects. for instance, all my individual projects are in a folder called git_projects - maybe this is the appropriate place to build the graph versus within each project."

⭐ FIRST, THE PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD, AND THAT MATTERS BEFORE ANY OPTION IS WEIGHED. There is NO CONSTRAINT TO REMOVE. `--graph-path` is an ordinary CLI argument; this repo's `.mcp.json` passes `./.reflow2/graph` and that is a CONVENTION, not a binding. Verified the same day by creating graphs at arbitrary filesystem paths outside any repository during the corpus trial. `dec:install-once-per-machine` already states the position: "reflow2 installs once per machine; the in-repo half is optional and only for repos you share." So the question is not CAN the graph live elsewhere — it can, today, with no change — but WHERE IT SHOULD, which is a design question about authority rather than a limitation to lift.

SECOND, THE PLACEMENT RULE IS ALREADY DECIDED AND IT DISPOSES OF ONE OPTION OUTRIGHT. `dec:nested-graphs` (ACCEPTED, Anthony, 2026-07-25): "A design is its own graph when something at that level is separately OWNED, separately RELEASED, or separately SHARED — and a subtree of one graph otherwise. THE HIERARCHY DOES NOT DECIDE; AUTHORITY DOES." A `git_projects/` parent folder is a filesystem convention with no authority attached, so under the accepted rule it is NOT a reason to put a graph there. If those projects share a graph it must be because they share an owner, a release train or a recipient — never because they share a directory.

⭐ THIRD, AND THIS IS WHY THE QUESTION IS GENUINELY OPEN RATHER THAN ALREADY ANSWERED: THE RULE WAS WRITTEN FOR FEDERATION BETWEEN OWNERS, AND ANTHONY'S CASE IS ONE OWNER WITH MANY RELEASE TRAINS. The discriminator is a three-way OR — owned, released, OR shared — so "separately released" alone sends his projects to separate graphs. But every cost the rule cites for a seam (a coordinate, an evidence roll-up, a freshness check) is a cost of crossing an AUTHORITY boundary, and there is no authority boundary here. He is paying federation's price to solve a filing problem. The rule is not wrong; his case sits on a seam in it that multi-org federation never presented.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) ONE GRAPH FOR THE FAMILY, levels inside it. The accepted rule already blesses this "for everything inside one ownership boundary" and `cap:scoped-analysis` delivers per-level reading, so nothing new is needed. Counter, from the rule's own text: what one graph cannot give is separate write locks, separate release trains, or a way to share ONE project without shipping the others — and his projects DO release separately, which is exactly the case (a) was said not to cover. (b) A GRAPH PER PROJECT, MIRRORED. What the accepted rule prescribes, and the linking half is BUILT (`cap:mirror-surface`, `cap:publish-surface`). Counter: `dec:linked-repos-poc` names the blocker — "reflow2 structures roughly one and a half of the six characteristics an interface spec needs and puts the rest in one free-text string, so today two graphs can be linked and still not be comparable" — and reflow2's own `maturity_report` puts SEAMS at 0 of 73, so the mechanism this option rests on is the least-exercised thing in the design. (c) A GRAPH IN THE PARENT FOLDER. Ruled out by `dec:nested-graphs` as stated, but worth keeping visible because it is what Anthony reached for and the reason it fails is not obvious: a folder is where things SIT, not who decides them. (d) ONE GRAPH FOR INTENT, SEPARATE GRAPHS FOR BUILD. Not previously considered: the shared thing across his projects is what he is trying to achieve, and the separate thing is what each repo ships. Counter: reflow2 has no vocabulary for a design that holds only intent and no build, and `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` is the closest thing — which is about a corpus, not a standing hub. (e) DO NOTHING; the constraint he wanted removed does not exist, and he can point `--graph-path` wherever he likes today. Counter: that answers the mechanism and ignores the question, which is what SHOULD be one design.

WHAT MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED WHEN THIS IS PICKED UP: `dec:nested-graphs` and its four stated obligations (the coordinate, the roll-up, freshness, the seam), `dec:linked-repos-poc` and its dependency on `req:interface-spec-complete`, `req:design-composes` and `req:composed-analysis` (both accepted), and `cap:mirror-surface`/`cap:publish-surface`/`cap:composed-analysis` (all built). The LINKING half exists; the COMPARING half does not.

NOT CHECKED, and it bears directly on (b): whether `mirror_surface` and `compose_and_analyse` have ever been run on two real designs. `dec:linked-repos-poc` is one of the two parked Decisions that `detect_defects` has been reporting as governing nothing all session, which suggests not.
properties.name: OPEN — where does the graph live when ONE PERSON works many interrelated projects, which is the case dec:nested-graphs' rule was not written for?
properties.rationale:
Captured under the brainstorm skill at Anthony's request, and the search he asked for was run first — he said "I know we've discussed linking projects in the past, so there should already be some discussion on this," and he was right. Recording what already exists BEFORE recording the new question is the whole point of the exercise, and this project has spent a session establishing that the expensive failure is re-deriving what is written down.

The premise correction is on the node rather than left in conversation because it is the most perishable part: "the graph is limited to one git repo" is a reasonable thing to believe from the outside, it is false, and nothing in the repo says so plainly. If that correction lives only in a chat it will be believed again.

Deliberately NOT registered as formal alternatives — that would make this a fork the loop starts asking him to choose between, which is exactly what a brainstorm should not do. Kept separate from dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs because that one asks what may cross a boundary and this one asks where the boundary is; one node holding both could only ever be half-answered.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Recorded for completeness; this is the WEAKEST of the ideas in this batch and is written down mainly so a later session knows it was considered and not chosen.

THE UNUSED FUNCTIONS: degree_centrality (with DegreeMode), closeness_centrality, eigenvector_centrality, and clustering (local clustering coefficient). All exact, all already available.

WHAT EACH WOULD MEAN HERE: closeness = how near a node is to everything else, so "how quickly does a change here reach the whole design". Eigenvector = importance by association with important nodes. Clustering coefficient = how tightly a node's neighbourhood is interconnected, a possible signal for over-coupled subsystems.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, which is why this ranks last: betweenness is the RIGHT measure for the question reflow2 asks — how much of the golden thread routes THROUGH this node — and the others answer questions nobody has asked yet. Degree is already computed locally in structure.rs and needs no crate. Adding measures because they exist is how a report becomes a dashboard nobody reads, and reflow2 has an explicit instinct against that (dec:report-dont-judge, and BL-42's noise-floor lesson).

IF ANY: clustering coefficient is the only one with a question attached that reflow2 does not already answer — "is this subsystem more tangled inside than the design says it should be?" — and even that overlaps leiden communities.
properties.name: OPEN — is betweenness the right centrality, or should closeness / eigenvector / clustering also be read?
properties.rationale: Recorded deliberately as a considered-and-not-chosen idea. The brainstorm skill's rule is that roads not taken are part of the design's memory; without this node a later reviewer would rediscover four unused centrality functions and re-litigate them.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-11, in his words: "reflow2 has a capability to return to the agent any systems engineering data (not view) and the agent can render it. would like to actually demonstrate this in the docs of these examples of different views of reflow2 using this rendering type construct." Nothing here is intent.

⭐⭐ THIS IS ALREADY THE RECORDED DIRECTION, AND IT IS UNBUILT. `docs/viewpoints.md` §"Direction (the rest of BL-40)" says it almost exactly: "once the catalogue's shape has settled here, move the projection data into core as typed read tools on the MCP surface (the `flow_report` shape — facts plus confessions — is the template), so the in-session agent renders views deterministically instead of re-deriving them through an LLM, which is exactly where extrapolation would creep back in." Same shape as `req:what-next` last month — accepted intent, blocker unexamined, nobody built it. This is not a new idea to decide; it is an old idea to finish.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, measured 2026-08-11:
  typed report-shaped read tools on the MCP surface   15  (graph_report, flow_report, maturity_report,
                                                          granularity_report, ility_report, readiness_report,
                                                          evidence_report, coverage_report, seam_report,
                                                          budget_report, release_report, confirmation_ledger,
                                                          changelog_view, claim_report, graph_report_markdown)
  tools/render_views.py                               44 KB, renders 10 DoDAF-informed viewpoints
  docs/design/views.html                              323 KB of rendered output
So the DATA side is largely built and the RENDER side exists as deterministic Python that writes one HTML file nobody links from the reading order.

⭐ THE EVIDENCE FOR DOING IT IS FROM TODAY, AND IT IS DAMNING. Every one of these is a hand-maintained claim ABOUT THE GRAPH that the graph could have answered:
  · `docs/overview.md:52` says the schema has 60 edge types. The export stamp says 61.
  · `docs/three-axes.md` says axis Z is "MISSING". The graph holds 111 DesignEpochs, 133 TemporalFacts,
    114 Snapshots and 362 ChangeEvents. The doc that would tell a reader whether time is modelled says it is not.
  · 3 of 4 deferrals spot-checked in `requirements-coverage.md` were wrong (SP-3b, GS-17, 3AX-5).
  · `crates/reflow2-core/src/heal.rs:27-29` lists dead_end, disconnected_community and single_point_of_failure
    as deferred. All three are built.
A rendered doc cannot make any of these mistakes, because it has no opinion of its own.

⚠️⚠️ THE CENTRAL RISK, and it is this project's own doctrine pointed at the proposal. `viewpoints.md` rule 1: "A projection may sort, group, count and draw — it may not infer, default, or improvise." An LLM's default behaviour IS to improvise, and Anthony's own standing position (UAF/DoDAF-trained: views must be pure projections; a renderer fill-in is a reflow2 defect) makes an improvised sentence in a rendered doc a DEFECT REPORT, not a cosmetic issue. The existing Python renderer cannot improvise by construction. Moving rendering to the agent trades staleness for extrapolation — and the doc's own Direction paragraph names that trade explicitly as the reason to move the DATA into typed tools first, so the agent has less room to invent.

⚠️ SECOND RISK: DETERMINISM AND THE DIFF. A committed file rendered by an LLM churns on every regeneration — different wording, same facts — so `git diff` stops meaning "the design changed". `render_views.py` is deterministic and byte-stable; an agent is not.

⚠️ THIRD, AND IT IS A JUDGEMENT CALL NOT A BUG: confessions become PUBLIC. Every renderer here is also a probe, and what it cannot project it confesses. Rendering the outward-facing docs means reflow2's adoption surface carries reflow2's own gaps to a first-time reader. `partnership.md` argues credibility is decided at the front door. A confessing doc reads either as unusually honest or as unfinished, and which one it is depends on the reader, not on us.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) LIVE ONLY — the agent renders a view on demand from the typed tools; nothing is committed. Never stale by construction. Costs the browsable artifact: a stranger on GitHub sees no docs, and docs ARE the adoption surface.
(b) COMMITTED + CHECKED — render into committed files and add a CI step that re-renders and diffs, so a stale doc fails the build. Turns doc staleness into a gate, which is the actual disease. Needs determinism, which argues for keeping the renderer deterministic (Python/Rust) rather than an LLM.
(c) HYBRID — prose docs that EMBED rendered sections between markers, regenerated and diff-checked. Smallest change; keeps the argument-shaped docs intact and puts the facts under the gate. Every number that went stale today lives in an embeddable section.
(d) DEMONSTRATION ONLY — pick two or three docs, render them as worked examples of the capability, leave the rest prose. This is closest to what Anthony literally asked for, and it is the cheapest way to find out whether the output is any good before committing the whole doc set to it.

📌 SEQUENCING FINDING, recorded because it changes what to do NEXT. Anthony asked in the same breath for `genesis.md`, `artifact-linking.md`, `impact-propagation.md`, `gap-surfacing.md` and `heal-process.md` to be rewritten as outward-facing prose. Those five describe what `genesis`, `link_artifact`/`reconcile_artifacts`, `propagate_from`, `detect_gaps` and `propose_heal` DO AND RETURN — which makes them the FIRST candidates to become projections, not prose. Hand-rewriting 661 lines into a format that may be replaced is the wasteful order. Deciding (d) first costs one doc's worth of work and tells you whether the other four should be written at all.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2's outward-facing docs be RENDERED from the graph by the agent, rather than hand-written prose that goes stale?
properties.rationale: Four hand-maintained claims about the graph were found wrong in a single day, and every one was answerable from the graph. The data side is 15 typed tools already built and the direction is already recorded in viewpoints.md as the rest of BL-40. What is genuinely open is who renders — an LLM buys freshness and risks the extrapolation this project treats as a defect; deterministic code keeps the doctrine and keeps the diff meaningful.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.

⭐⭐ THE HEADLINE: AN ACCEPTED DECISION SET A CONDITION, AND THE CONDITION HAS NOW BEEN MET BY EXACTLY THE EVIDENCE IT ASKED FOR.

dec:ownership-reads-claims-before-adding-an-edge (ACCEPTED, Anthony's word 2026-08-08) says: build the first cut from CLAIMS rather than a new edge, and \"DECIDE ON OWNED_BY ONLY AFTER THAT IS BUILT AND SHOWN TO BE INSUFFICIENT.\" Its rationale names the disqualifying evidence in advance: \"If claims turn out to model the wrong thing (THEY ARE TRANSIENT WORK-IN-HAND, WHILE OWNERSHIP IS DURABLE AND SURVIVES THE SESSION), that is a real distinction and the edge becomes justified on evidence rather than on anticipation.\"

ONE DAY LATER, dev_storyflow filed precisely that distinction, and Anthony supplied the use case himself (2026-08-09, relayed by api-boss 05af57c1):

  \"As my brother and I collaborate on another project, there are areas of the design that are his and areas that are mine. This is probably a different 'ownership' of something than the claim_region type descriptor... it is probably DURABLE, SURVIVES EVERY SESSION, and SHOULD NEVER BE RELEASED.\"

⭐ THE FRAMING THAT MAKES IT LEGIBLE — reflow2 has two of the three WHO axes:
  AUTHORED_BY   who WROTE this          past tense · historical · never changes
  CLAIMS        who is IN it RIGHT NOW  transient · advisory · released at checkout
  ???           whose AREA this is      durable · standing · never released

WHY CLAIMS CANNOT BE STRETCHED TO COVER THE THIRD, which is the \"shown to be insufficient\" the accepted decision demanded, and it is operational rather than theoretical: claim_region's own description says ADVISORY and session-scoped; the parallel-work skill says release at checkout; on a shared server a claim reads `unknown` rather than `live` and NEVER EXPIRES ON ITS OWN. So standing ownership claims would permanently drown the tool's actual job — showing who is ACTIVELY in your ground. api-boss noted they hold one claim, released and re-took it once today purely to fix its note, and asked what three permanent graph-wide claims would do to that surface.

⚠️ AND THE FLEET RETRACTED ITS OWN COUNTER-ARGUMENT, which is worth more than the ask. They had argued that recording ownership in the graph duplicates their PROTOCOL.md ownership matrix and would rot the way six of their copied rules already have. Their retraction: \"That objection is specific to an organisation that ALREADY writes ownership down. A PAIR OF COLLABORATORS HAS NO MATRIX — the knowledge lives in their heads and in habit. For most projects the graph would be the FIRST place ownership was ever recorded, not the second, and the duplication risk is simply absent.\" They kept only the narrow fleet-specific form.

⭐ AND THE REFRAME THAT MATTERS MOST FOR SCOPE: every earlier version of this ask was framed around an AGENT FLEET, which invites the reply \"that is exotica\". The two-person case is not exotica. It is two people splitting a design, which is the ORDINARY case of collaborative design work.

=== WHERE THIS SITS AGAINST WHAT SHIPPED TODAY ===

cap:owed-to-a-contributor shipped `loop_status(contributor_id)` on 2026-08-09. IT IS NOT THE FIRST CUT THAT ACCEPTED DECISION SPECIFIED: it attributes via the AUTHORED_BY `role=approver` edge, not via CLAIMS. That is already recorded honestly — the SATISFIES edge to req:ownership-is-an-edge-so-debt-has-an-addressee carries `coverage: partial` and says so: \"its chosen first cut answers 'what has a named person been asked to settle', not 'which gaps are in the part of the system I own'. The fleet's ask is the second one.\"

⇒ SO THE CLAIMS-BASED FIRST CUT WAS NEVER BUILT, and the question is whether it still should be. Two readings, both honest:
  (a) The decision's build order stands: build the claims-based cut, THEN judge. The insufficiency argument above is about claims as a DURABLE record, and a claims-scoped debt report might still be useful for its actual purpose without ever being ownership.
  (b) The insufficiency is already established by inspection — claims are advisory, session-scoped and released by doctrine, so building a durable ownership view on them would be building on a foundation whose own description forbids it. Under this reading the condition is met and the edge is justified now.

AND IT FITS WHAT SHIPPED: loop_status's scoped answer deliberately attributes ONLY assignment and reports everything else under `scope.not_attributable`. AN OWNED_BY EDGE IS EXACTLY WHAT WOULD LET THE REST BECOME ATTRIBUTABLE. The restraint shipped today is waiting for this.

=== THE SHAPES, with counters beside rather than argued down ===

(A) AN OWNED_BY / ACCOUNTABILITY EDGE — Contributor → any node, explicitly NOT in the decomposition spine and NOT a traceability edge. THE PRECEDENT EXISTS TWICE: AUTHORED_BY and CLAIMS are both already deliberately excluded from impact propagation (nodes.rs structural_rule), so this would be the third of a kind rather than a novelty. COUNTER, and it is this project's own: dec:ownership-reads-claims-before-adding-an-edge warns that adding an edge type is the most expensive and least reversible change to this schema, and today's measurement found EIGHT of sixty edge types declared and reached by nothing. An unused OWNED_BY would not be a novel failure here; it is the common one.

(B) REUSE CLAIMS WITH A DURABILITY FLAG — a `durable: true` property that exempts a claim from release and from the overlap report. Cheapest, no new edge type. COUNTER: it makes one edge mean two things whose lifecycles are opposite, and the tool's descriptions would have to say both. That is how a vocabulary rots — the same sentence dec:one-retire-edge uses about two words for one relationship, running the other way.

(C) OWNERSHIP AS A PROPERTY ON THE NODE — an `owner` field. Cheapest of all to read. COUNTER: it cannot express shared or partial ownership, cannot carry a note about WHAT is owned, and puts a person's id inside design content where every export and every merge has to reconcile it.

⚠️ THE HARD PART, WHICH IS A DESIGN INPUT RATHER THAN A SETTING, and it comes from the fleet: WHICH NODE TYPES ARE OWNABLE? In their 1,127-node graph most nodes legitimately have no owner — \"a Constraint about prose rendering is nobody's in the accountability sense\" — so a naive detector fires on the majority and becomes a signal trained to be ignored. In a two-person project the design is probably mostly partitioned. ⇒ OWNABILITY LOOKS LIKE A PER-PROJECT DECLARATION, NOT A FIXED RULE, and the same feature behaves very differently at those two scales.

NOTHING IS PROMOTED. The accepted decision's condition may now be met; saying so is Anthony's to do, and dec:reopen-supersedes says a re-opening mints its own node rather than un-accepting the old one.
properties.name: OPEN — the condition dec:ownership-reads-claims-before-adding-an-edge set has now been met: are CLAIMS shown insufficient, and does OWNED_BY become justified?
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill: `proposed`, options with counters, nothing promoted.

Kept SEPARATE from dec:ownership-reads-claims-before-adding-an-edge rather than editing it, because that decision is ACCEPTED and dec:reopen-supersedes is explicit that a re-opening mints a new Decision which obsoletes the old one — the accepted one is never un-accepted. This node is the evidence arriving that its own condition named; whether that closes it is Anthony's call.

Separated from the ownership-orphan detector question (dec:idea-detect-ownership-orphans) because the edge could exist without the detector and the detector cannot exist without the edge — one node holding both could only be half-answered.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-05, closing the session and naming a tension he has been circling all day:

"The initial vision was, using a house as the delivered product, was that when you gave the house to somebody else, they would also get all the blueprints and design decisions (this would be the reflow2 graph). This would all come in a nice package that anybody else could take from there and see why you made the decisions you made and take it from there. In a code based project, your repo = implemented code + reflow graph object + other artifacts in a reflow blob storage. This would all come in one nice and complete package. However, in retrospec, this could have been done differently. The discussion earlier is more about collaboration and using multiple graphs, which somewhat break this wholistic/complete package that I had originally developed. Theoretically, there is no reason that you couldn't create a common/shared server that hosts the reflow2 mcp and everybody in the organization could access it. Not only that, a project could just point to the graph_id (or multiple graph_ids) and everybody could work collaboratively. Additionally, if people were assigned subsections of a big project, they could just point their .mcp.json at the master graph in their project and take on their subsection. So I guess what I'm stating is that to increase collaboration, we may have to remove the 'nicely wholistic combined package' that I had originally developed."

⭐ FIRST, MEASURED: BOTH HALVES ARE ALREADY ACCEPTED REQUIREMENTS, AND THE SHARED SERVER IS ALREADY BUILT.
  - `req:persistence` (ACCEPTED) — "The design persists in-repo alongside the code." The package.
  - `req:design-reachable-without-the-repo` (ACCEPTED) — "Someone without the repo can reach a design, read it, and contribute to it." The collaboration.
  - `req:content-reaches-every-seat` (ACCEPTED) — "a pointer resolves for everyone holding the design, not only for the seat that stored it."
  - `dec:central-host` — ACCEPTED (its NAME still reads "OPEN — does reflow2 gain a hosted surface…", which is stale in the same way `dec:skills-served`'s was; worth a rename, not a re-decision).
  - AND `--http` SHIPS TODAY: `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/main.rs` carries `--http`, `--http-allow-host` and `serve_http`, and its own comment says "`--http` already lets several sessions share one design, and it works."
So this is not a road not taken. The design committed to BOTH and the transport exists.

⭐⭐ SECOND, AND IT IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING: THE DICHOTOMY IS FALSE, BECAUSE THE PACKAGE AND THE WORKING MEDIUM WERE NEVER THE SAME ARTIFACT. The live store (`.reflow2/graph`) is GIT-IGNORED and always has been. What ships in the repo is `docs/design/reflow2.json` — the deterministic, self-contained, mergeable EXPORT. The house-with-blueprints has always been the export, never the store. So collaborating on a shared store does not touch the package: the package is what you export FROM it.

⚠️ THIRD, AND THIS IS WHERE HIS INSTINCT IS RIGHT AFTER ALL. The loss is real, and it is a DEFAULT rather than a capability:
  - With a per-repo store, the design is IN the repo by default and you must work to lose it.
  - With a shared server, the design is OUT of the repo by default and you must work to KEEP it.
That flip is the actual cost of collaboration, and it is not fixed by having an export format — it is fixed by something making the export happen. Which is why [BL-215] is the same finding from the other end: the hxm_program session found `.reflow2` git-ignored, and every captured decision had to be HAND-COPIED into markdown for teammates, "double bookkeeping, and only the prose copy is shared." That team already lost the package, on a per-repo store, with no shared server involved — because nothing told the project to commit its export.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) KEEP THE PER-REPO STORE AS THE DEFAULT and treat the shared server as the exception — today's shape. Counter: it is the shape that produced three stores on one repo and prose cross-references, and it makes the collaboration requirement something you configure your way into, which `reflow2_init.py`'s own comment already argues against for `--shared` ("a capability you have to reconfigure your way into is one most users never reach"). (b) SHARED SERVER AS THE DEFAULT, EXPORT AS THE DELIVERABLE — collaboration is normal, and committing the export becomes an explicit, prompted, possibly gated act. Counter: the export is only as fresh as the last person who ran it, so the package's completeness becomes a discipline rather than a property, and a stale export is a COMPLETE document that merges cleanly and silently drops work (`req:stale-seat-knows` names exactly this). (c) BOTH, WITH THE EXPORT AUTOMATED — a session-end hook or a CI job keeps the committed export fresh, so the package survives whichever medium the work happens in. Cheapest thing that preserves both accepted requirements, and it is [BL-215]'s own suggestion. Counter: nobody has said what happens when the automated export and a human's differ, and an export that writes itself is one more thing that can silently break. (d) THE PACKAGE IS THE POINT AND COLLABORATION SHOULD BEND TO IT — keep everything per-repo and solve sharing by merging exports, as `dec:multi-writer-architecture` (ACCEPTED) already says: "Many writers keep the repo file and merge on pull — no hosted service." Counter: that decision predates the field evidence, and one person on one machine already ended up with three stores and a markdown side-channel under it.

WHAT MUST NOT BE RE-DERIVED: `--http` exists and works; `req:persistence` and `req:design-reachable-without-the-repo` are BOTH accepted; the live store is git-ignored and the export is the shipped artifact; `dec:multi-writer-architecture` chose merge-on-pull over a hosted service and has not been revisited since the field reports; and `dec:central-host` is accepted despite a name that still says OPEN.

NOT CHECKED, and it bears on (b) and (c): whether a shared `--http` server can serve SEVERAL graph_ids at once, or is bound to one like the stdio server is. `dec:idea-many-graphs-one-store` measured that `with_graph_id` is free and the store namespaces by id, but nobody has looked at what the HTTP path does with that.
properties.name: OPEN — does collaborating on a shared server cost the self-contained package, or does it only flip which way the default points?
properties.rationale:
Captured at Anthony's request as the session's closing thought, and the mechanical half was checked first — which changed the answer twice. He believed he was describing a road not taken; both halves are accepted requirements and the transport ships. He believed collaboration would cost the package; the package is the export and was never the working store.

What survives his concern, and is recorded as the load-bearing sentence, is the DEFAULT flip: per-repo you must work to lose the design, shared you must work to keep it. That is a real cost, it is not an architectural one, and it is already being paid on a per-repo store by the team in [BL-215] — which is the strongest evidence that the threat was never the shared server.

Deliberately not registered as alternatives, so the loop does not start asking him to choose. He asked for this to be the last activity of the session and to keep nothing promoted; four options with their counters is the state he asked for.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Filed by dev_storyflow's dragon Boss (`853732df`) on 2026-08-15 AT ANTHONY'S EXPLICIT DIRECTION, and his framing is the better one: "if reflow2 is going to work in an environment where multiple sessions are running simultaneously (on the same computer here, but could also be across several machines), may need to make cross-talk an enduring part of reflow2 — maybe not use B.md, but some way for sessions to collaborate cleanly."

DISTINCT FROM THE TWO NEIGHBOURS THE GUARD WOULD NAME. `dec:idea-the-loop-only-sees-what-an-agent-hand-carries` asks whether the loop should SUBSCRIBE TO REALITY — CI, telemetry, the outside world. `dec:idea-agent-to-agent-feedback-is-a-formal-channel` asks whether an agent should write a REPORT for another agent to read later. THIS is neither: it is seat-to-seat exchange DURING work, where the value is in the minutes rather than the record.

⭐ THE OBSERVATION, STATED SO IT IS NOT READ AS "ADD CHAT": reflow2's multi-seat STATE model is unusually good and they list it — `mint_seat`, `claim_region`/`release_claim`/`claim_report` (advisory, seat-stamped, liveness computable), `OWNED_BY` for durable ground against `CLAIMS` for transient holding, `sync_status`, `arrival_delta`, `compare_designs`, and the whole pairing family. WHAT IS MISSING IS NOT STATE, IT IS EVENTS. The graph can say who holds what and whether you are behind the record. It has no way for one seat to SAY something to another, and no way for a seat to be TOLD.

⭐⭐ THE SHARPEST FORM, and it is an argument from reflow2's own surface rather than from their inconvenience: THE TOOLS KEEP HANDING OFF TO A CONVERSATION THEY CANNOT HOST. `sync_status`'s own description declines to answer "what will I publish that is not mine". `export_graph` publishes every attached seat's in-flight work. `add_decision` refuses a near-match and asks a human to judge it. `acknowledge_defect` demands a reason a person must supply. Every one of those ends by requiring a human exchange, and none of them can carry it.

WHAT THEY MEASURED, and it is the part that makes this more than a wish — nine exchanges in ONE day, three bosses, no workers, each producing something no single seat could:
· A PEER CORRECTED A PRESCRIPTION WITHIN THE HOUR — one seat's retrofit was replaced by another's prevention, and "a maintainer reading ⑨ alone would have built the weaker fix".
· A WARNING ARRIVED BEFORE THE DAMAGE: a peer was about to mint 25 Verifications across two graphs and replied "your warning arrived before I minted a single Verification". Hours apart it is a retrofit; minutes apart it is free.
· A PEER'S ONE-LINE CHECK RETIRED MOST OF A FEATURE REQUEST — `set_decision_status` already takes `rejected`, so a claimed missing feature was a DISCOVERABILITY failure, and the fix collapsed from a schema change to one sentence in two skills. ⭐ CROSS-TALK STOPPED A WRONG FEATURE REQUEST FROM REACHING THE MAINTAINER, which is a saving in reflow2's own backlog.
· THREE SEATS INDEPENDENTLY HIT ONE MISSING CONCEPT from three unrelated directions — "deliberately out of scope", "proposed and refuted", "deferred with a promotion trigger". One hole, not three requests, AND THE CORROBORATION IS THE EVIDENCE: any one of them filed alone reads as an edge case.
· A PEER'S FINDING MADE A SEAT RE-AUDIT WORK IT WOULD NEVER HAVE RE-OPENED, producing a defence now stated explicitly: after any `distinct_from`, run a same-type `search_design` yourself, because the guard's silence is not the check.
· ONE HAZARD CAUGHT FROM ALL THREE DIRECTIONS IN A DAY — the `--shared` export cross-carry, caught receiving, caught writing, and caught pre-emptively — turning a written rule into observed practice.

THE OPTIONS:

(a) DO NOTHING; THE FLEET'S OWN FILE IS THE ANSWER. B.md works, and it is theirs to shape. CHEAPEST and it respects that not everything belongs in the tool. COUNTER: every boss hand-rolled a 20-second `awk` poller, reflow2 is blind to the most valuable output of the day, and Anthony has now asked twice for cross-talk to be an enduring part of it.

(b) A MESSAGE OR EVENT LAYER IN THE GRAPH — seats post, seats read, delivery is recorded. Most direct reading of the ask. COUNTER, and it is severe: the graph is a DESIGN record, and a design brain that becomes a chat log acquires an unbounded write volume with no coherence meaning. `dec:defects-are-temporal-facts` was accepted partly because it added NO new node type; this would add a whole axis.

(c) MAKE THE HAND-OFFS FIRST-CLASS RATHER THAN BUILDING A CHANNEL — the tools already know the exact moments a human exchange is needed, and `open_questions` already models "somebody was asked and has not answered" for the gap→user case. Extending that shape to seat→seat is narrow, uses vocabulary that exists, and carries only exchanges the design cares about. COUNTER: it would not have carried six of their nine examples, which were warnings and corrections nothing in the design had asked for.

(d) NOTIFICATION WITHOUT CONTENT — a seat can learn that another seat wrote in its claimed region, and go look. Cheap, uses `CLAIMS` and `sync_status` machinery that exists, and adds no message store. COUNTER: it delivers the least valuable half; their examples were about MEANING ("this remedy is already possible"), not about the fact that a write happened.

⚠️ THE BOUND THEY STATE THEMSELVES, and it should survive: "I did not exercise the claim family this session, so I am describing the surface, not testing it." The state model is being praised from its documentation rather than from use.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether cross-machine is in scope (Anthony raises it, nothing measures it); whether a channel would be used by a SOLO user, who is still the common case; and whether any of this belongs in reflow2 rather than in the harness that runs the seats.
properties.name: IDEA — reflow2 models who holds what and whether you are behind the record, but gives one seat no way to SAY anything to another. The most valuable work a three-boss fleet did in a day travelled over a markdown file reflow2 cannot see.
properties.rationale: Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`, options with counters beside them, nothing promoted. Kept distinct from the subscribe-to-reality and agent-to-agent-report questions after reading both: this one is about exchange DURING work between seats on one design, where their measured value was in minutes rather than in the record. The nine examples are summarised rather than quoted whole because the corroboration pattern — three seats reaching one hole from three directions — is the evidence, and it is invisible in any single one of them.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-14.

HIS WORDS: *"I don't think it should be focused on a specific topic like software engineering as I'd like to use it for other projects like my shop."*

🛑 THE INTENT IS ALREADY ACCEPTED, SO THIS IS NOT A NEW REQUIREMENT. `req:design-anything` (ACCEPTED): *"Software, hardware, a document, a process — the vocabulary stays neutral."* What Alex hit is not the vocabulary — it is EVERYTHING WRAPPED AROUND IT. The served instructions and skills assume a codebase throughout: Artifacts are source files with checksums, `link-artifacts` opens on *"Unity C#, a spec, a doc"*, `ci-gate` is a build gate, the loop's step 3 is *"build only what the graph specifies"*, and his own example — how database migrations are performed — is the one part of his note that IS software. **The nouns are neutral and the worked examples, defaults and skills are not.**

⭐ SO THE HONEST STATEMENT OF THE GAP: reflow2 can MODEL a shop today, and nothing in what a shop owner would actually read shows them how. That is a delivery problem, and it is the same shape as two findings already on the record — `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue`, and the installer wording Alex himself caught, where the information existed somewhere the person was not.

✅ TWO MEASURED FACTS THE OPTIONS HAVE TO LIVE WITH:
  · `Project.domain` IS WRITTEN AND NEVER READ (`req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted`). The field that would carry "this is a shop, not a service" already exists and drives nothing.
  · The Environment / EnvironmentRule compliance layer was DESIGNED IN FULL AND NEVER BUILT, and `dec:idea-the-environment-compliance-layer-was-designed-and-never-built` says in as many words that it *"is what makes 'design a house' concrete"*. The non-software story has a designed, unbuilt half already sitting in the graph.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.
(a) NOTHING TO DO — the requirement is accepted and the vocabulary is neutral; a competent agent adapts. Counter: the second user, holding the tool, concluded the opposite from what he actually saw.
(b) ONE WORKED NON-SOFTWARE EXAMPLE end to end — his shop is the obvious candidate and he is volunteering to be the test case. Cheapest thing that would have prevented his impression, and it produces evidence rather than assertion.
(c) MAKE `Project.domain` READ — let it select examples and defaults. **This is the option the design's own rules already point at:** `req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read` says a distinction no computation reads should be removed or made real, and `domain` is currently the former.
(d) BUILD THE ENVIRONMENT COMPLIANCE LAYER, on the grounds that regulation and physical context are what non-software design mostly IS. Largest, and it has its own open decision already.
(e) SAY IT PLAINLY IN THE DOCS — reflow2 is software-first today, other domains work but are untravelled. Costs nothing, makes no promise it cannot keep, and is the only option that stays honest whichever of the others is chosen.

📌 WORTH KNOWING WHO IS ASKING: this is the third distinct thread where Alex's use diverges from Anthony's, and his projects are the only non-reflow2, non-flo2 evidence the design has. `dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded` — which ALEX HIMSELF ASKED FOR — is the mechanism that would stop each of these arriving as a relayed email.
properties.name: OPEN — `req:design-anything` is accepted and the DELIVERY is still software-shaped; what closes the gap between a neutral vocabulary and a toolchain full of code?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill. Recorded as an open question rather than as a requirement precisely BECAUSE the requirement already exists and is accepted: the useful question is not "should reflow2 design anything" (settled, yes) but "what is still software-shaped after that was settled", and framing it the first way would have produced a duplicate of `req:design-anything` and lost Alex's actual point.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from a review of what dynograph-foundation offers that reflow2 does not yet use (2026-08-01, at Anthony's request). Nothing here is settled.

THE OBSERVATION: propagate.rs:389 ranks impacted nodes by GLOBAL betweenness centrality — `design_network()?.betweenness()`. That answers "is this node generally important in the design?", which is not the same question as "is this node relevant to the change I just made?". IP-9's stated intent is the second one.

THE IDEA: dynograph_graph::personalized_pagerank (already a dependency, unused) is random-walk-with-restart — the teleport mass returns to a SEED SET instead of spreading uniformly, so scores measure relevance to those seeds. Seeding it on the change's own seed nodes gives exactly the missing question.

CHEAP: the crate is already pinned, the function is exact on graphs this size, and propagate already builds the network. Small.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is a real one: betweenness is not wrong, it is answering a different and also-useful question. The existing doc comment defends it — "a change landing on a high-betweenness node has a wider SECONDARY blast radius" — which is about onward propagation, not relevance. So this may be an ADDITION rather than a replacement, and two ranking columns may be worse for a reader than one. Whether a reader wants both, or one, or a blend, is undecided and is the actual open question.

Filed as a backlog row on Anthony's word (2026-08-01) — the work is tracked; this Decision records that the SHAPE is still open.
properties.name: OPEN — should a blast radius rank by relevance TO THE CHANGE rather than by global importance?
properties.rationale: Surfaced by comparing reflow2's actual imports against dynograph-graph's exports: 8 of 17 are used. This was the strongest of the unused ones because it lands on the most-read output in the system and the mismatch between the question asked and the question answered is documented in reflow2's own doc comment.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From item 1 of the Grok 4.6 agent feedback (2026-08-13), verified on reflow2's own export at `c18a4a1` on 2026-08-14.

⚠️ **SUBORDINATE TO `dec:idea-silence-is-reported-not-inferred`.** Anthony asked for this node AND for a step back, on the ground that patching one blind spot with one detector is how a tool overfits. **The narrow options below are only safe to take if they do not become the third instance of that pattern** — which is why (a), the obvious fix, is measured and argued against here.

THE MEASURED STATE (`fact:the-build-list-is-suppressed-by-realized-via-component`): `what_next` returns Decisions only — 12 of 12. `arrival_delta` needs a Release/Epoch `target_id`. 43 live planned capabilities and 9 accepted-undelivered requirements appear in no tool's answer. `unrealized_capability` fires 3 times against them, 34 of 39 silenced by `realized_via_component`.

═══ ⭐⭐ THE FINDING THAT DECIDES THE SHAPE: THE ARTIFACT LAYER CANNOT ANSWER THIS ═══

**81 of 161 capabilities have no artifact of their own.** That is not neglect — reflow2 models artifacts at COMPONENT granularity, so a capability is realized *via* the component that carries the code. `realized_via_component` is not a hack; **it encodes the modelling convention the design actually uses.**

⇒ **THEREFORE "WHICH CAPABILITY LACKS AN ARTIFACT" IS NOT A MEANINGFUL QUESTION IN THIS DESIGN, AND NO REPAIR OF THE DETECTOR MAKES IT ONE.** The build list has to be computed from `Capability.status` and the golden thread — the things that DO carry per-capability truth — not from artifact presence. That is the load-bearing conclusion, and it removes the most tempting option rather than adding one.

═══ THE OPTIONS, WITH MEASURED COSTS ═══

(a) **FIX THE GUARD** so `realized_via_component` no longer inherits the component's artifacts.
    🛑 **MEASURED COST: `unrealized_capability` goes from ~3 to ~81 gaps** — a 27× increase, every one of them firing on correct modelling. This is precisely BL-42's original failure returning at scale (*"13 of 51 gaps, every one produced by following the adopt skill's own instruction"*), and BL-5's recorded lesson says a loud detector needs a different QUESTION, not a tuned number. **Argued against on this node's own evidence.**

(b) ⭐ **A REMAINING-WORK VIEW over data already held** — accepted/scheduled Requirements and Capabilities that are not computed-delivered, excluding `dropped`/`deferred`/discontinued and acknowledged-gap targets. The Grok report's own proposal, and a *sibling of `what_next`, not a replacement*.
    Cost: a new surface to maintain. Benefit: **adds no new judgement to the instrument** — it reads `status` and the golden thread, both of which already exist — so it cannot overfit a detector, and it answers the audience half (`dec:idea-silence-is-reported-not-inferred`: the loop and the delivery plan should not share a dashboard).
    ⚠️ It inherits the drift the Grok report names separately: `status` is ASSERTED while delivery is COMPUTED, and the two disagree. A view that reads `status` will be as stale as the statuses are.

(c) **REPORT THE SUPPRESSION** — *"34 capabilities not asked about: their component already has an artifact."* Generalises beyond this case; it is option (a) of the parent node. Cost: a convention every detector must honour. Benefit: the only option that makes the NEXT blind spot visible instead of the current one.

(d) **SCHEDULE THE WORK, SO `arrival_delta` ANSWERS IT.** The machinery exists and is already the designed home for this.
    🛑 **MEASURED: 23 `SCHEDULED_FOR` edges across 122 epochs and 31 releases.** The scheduling layer is built and effectively unused, so today this option answers almost nothing — and the Grok report hit exactly that, with its remaining-work list living as prose on an accepted Decision. Their item 9 proposes a detector for that shape (*an accepted Decision whose statement is a running delivery list with no `SCHEDULED_FOR` edges*). **Not free: it asks users to schedule before they can be told what is unbuilt.**

(e) **NOTHING.** Counter: three agents in three weeks have now gone outside the graph to answer this.

📌 (b), (c) and (d) COMPOSE and are not rivals: (d) makes the plan structural, (b) reads it back for the person who asked, (c) says what neither could see. **(a) is the only one that has to be chosen against.**
properties.name: OPEN — how should "what is left to build?" be answered, given the artifact layer is modelled at COMPONENT granularity and therefore cannot answer it at all?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill, with each option's cost measured on reflow2's own export rather than estimated, because Anthony's stated worry was that a narrow fix creates the next problem and that worry cannot be settled by argument alone. The measurement changed the answer: the obvious repair — making the unrealized-capability detector honest at capability granularity — would raise gaps 27-fold against a modelling convention that is correct, so the artifact layer is the wrong source for this question entirely. Recorded as subordinate to `dec:idea-silence-is-reported-not-inferred` rather than as a standalone fix so that a future session cannot take the narrow option without meeting the general question first.

properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Raised 2026-08-04 alongside dec:idea-retrospective-review-skill, of which this is the shape question rather than the whether question. THE FORK. OPTION A — A QUESTION LIST. The skill carries Anthony's sixteen questions as prose and the agent answers them by reading the design and the code. Cheap to build, works on day one, works on any project regardless of what the graph holds, and is what a human reviewer actually does. The objection is precise and comes from reflow2's own record: BL-179 settled that reflow2 does not encode a good practice as a detector, because Anthony objected that "avoid monoliths" is "kind of a subjective ask" — and the resolution was that reflow2 reports where two records the design ALREADY HOLDS disagree and rules on neither side. Sixteen prose questions answered by an agent is subjective grading with a checklist in front of it, and the answers would vary by model, by session, and by how much of the codebase happened to fit in context. OPTION B — EVERY QUESTION BACKED BY A COMPUTATION. Each question maps to a reading that already exists or is buildable over records the graph holds, and any question with no such reading reports NOT INFORMED with the reason instead of inviting an opinion. This is exactly ility_report's discipline (BL-184) turned into a skill, and the mapping is largely already there: "too joined together" is modularity, misplaced capabilities and god-components; "did the build separate what the design distinguishes" is granularity_report; "what did we leave until last" is maturity_report's frontier; "what happens if a key part breaks" is articulation points and single points of failure; "can others read and change this" is partly coverage_report and the unregistered regions. The cost is that Anthony's speed-and-efficiency group and most of his security group have NO computation behind them today and would honestly report NOT INFORMED — which looks like a weaker skill and is a more honest one. OPTION C — THE CENSUS SHAPE, which is what actually produced BL-198..BL-203 and is neither A nor B. It asks nothing and grades nothing: it diffs artifacts the project maintains SEPARATELY and expects to agree — the schema against the graph against the tool surface, and the practice the skills PRESCRIBE against the practice the graph FOLLOWS. It surfaces disagreements and leaves every verdict to the human, which is precisely the BL-179 resolution generalised beyond detectors. Its limit is equally precise: it can only find a disagreement between two records that BOTH EXIST, so it is blind to anything nobody wrote down, and it says nothing about Anthony's speed, security or bad-input groups at all. AN HONEST OBSERVATION ABOUT THE THREE: they are not exclusive, and the census is the only one of them with evidence behind it today — six rows in one sitting, one of which (BL-199) explained a hard blocker that eleven releases of green instruments had missed. A plausible synthesis is C as the engine, B as the reporting discipline, and A kept only as the part a human is asked, never the part an agent answers. Nobody has chosen. NOT ASKED HERE, AND IT MAY MATTER MORE THAN THE FORK: whether a retrospective is worth anything when run by the same agent that built the thing. The census was, and its blind spot was real — BL-199 was found by a mechanical three-way diff, not by the agent noticing it had done something wrong.
properties.name: OPEN — should a retrospective review ASK its questions or COMPUTE them, and is it ever allowed to grade?
properties.rationale: Kept separate from dec:idea-retrospective-review-skill because one node holding two unrelated questions can never be answered, only half-answered. That node asks whether the skill should exist; this one asks what it would have to be to survive reflow2's own rule against subjective grading. Not registered as formal alternatives: registering them would make this a fork with a design behind each branch and start the loop asking Anthony to choose, which is exactly what a brainstorm should not do.

properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-04, after the "did we build this right?" census (docs/built-right-review.md, sourcing BL-198..BL-203): "this exercise of retrospective design choices I think should be a skill within reflow2. This exercise of the agent being able to see the design in the current state and say, 'you know what, we could have done this better' is a good thing... I'm not sure, but being retrospective in analyzing what you've done is probably a good thing." THE IDEA: a served skill that reads a design in its CURRENT state and reports where it would have been built differently — the counterpart to check-health (which asks how the design is SHAPED) and detect-and-ask (which asks what the design MEANS). HIS CANDIDATE QUESTION LIST, in his own words, four groups: STRUCTURE AND SETUP — did I use the right layout or pattern; is the setup easy to understand; can other people read and change this easily; did I keep things too joined together, or are they separate. SPEED AND EFFICIENCY — does this use too much time, space or power; where is the main slowdown or bottleneck; can I do tasks at the same time to speed things up; did I save data or results I do not need to keep. WEAK POINTS AND RISKS — what happens if a key part breaks right now; did I handle bad inputs or errors safely; where is the system likely to slow down or crash under heavy use; is private data or system access safe from outside threats. FUTURE CHANGES — how hard is it to add new features later; will this break if the size or user count grows ten times bigger; did I leave clear notes or guides for the next person. WHAT ARGUES FOR IT: the census that prompted this produced six backlog rows in one sitting, including BL-199, which explained why BL-176 had been invisible to self-host for eleven releases — so the exercise demonstrably finds things no existing instrument found. Several of his groups already have computations that exist and are not gathered anywhere: modularity and misplaced capabilities and god-components answer "too joined together"; granularity_report answers "did the build separate what the design distinguishes"; maturity_report's frontier answers "what did we leave until last"; ility_report already maps findings onto quality axes and reports NOT INFORMED where nothing computes. WHAT ARGUES AGAINST IT, recorded beside the idea rather than used to kill it: reflow2 has one hard-won rule against exactly this shape — BL-179, where Anthony himself objected that "avoid monoliths" is "kind of a subjective ask", and the resolution was that reflow2 does not detect monoliths, it detects that two records the design ALREADY HOLDS disagree, and RULES ON NEITHER SIDE. A skill that asks sixteen questions in prose and lets an agent answer them would reintroduce precisely the subjective grading that ruling removed. The strongest form of the idea is therefore the one where every question is backed by a computation over records the design already holds, and any question with no such computation says NOT INFORMED rather than inviting an opinion — which is ility_report's discipline applied to a skill. That is a separate open question and is recorded as dec:idea-retrospective-asks-or-computes. ALSO OPEN, NOT ASKED HERE: whether the reviewer should be the same agent that built the thing (the census was, and its blind spot was real — it took a mechanical three-way diff, not judgement, to find BL-199).
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 serve a retrospective design-review skill?
properties.rationale: Recorded so the idea is not lost while it is still an idea. Nothing here is intent: no Requirement, no Capability, and no claim that reflow2 will build this. The counter-argument is recorded beside the idea rather than used against it, per the brainstorm skill — an idea killed in conversation loses its reasoning.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Two of Alex's Opportunities, 2026-08-14 (docs/feedback/2026-08-14-alex-grok-session.md), kept together because they are one question asked of two tools — and separable if the answer differs.

HIS WORDS. On detect_gaps: "Scoped `detect_gaps`: filter to gaps whose `affected_ids` include the seed (or its SATISFIES/REALIZES neighbors), and do not raise `unverified_capability` for `planned` + zero artifacts." On loop_status: "`loop_status` session mode: 'building this Capability' hides unsurfaced project-wide gaps unless they touch the seed."

⭐ THE SHARPENING, AND IT CHANGES THE QUESTION: SCOPING IS NOT MISSING. `cap:scoped-analysis` is built and shipped — "A team asks the detectors about its own part, and is told what it did not see" (`chg:scoped-analysis-built`), and `loop_status` already takes a `contributor_id`. So this is not a request for a feature that does not exist. It is a report that THE FEATURE THAT EXISTS DID NOT HELP: he called `detect_gaps(scope: Capability)` at depth 1, 2 and 3, got `in_scope` of roughly 47–51 every time, "almost every hit `unverified_capability` on unrelated planned work", and still could not answer "is THIS Capability still in an `unrealized_capability` gap?" without grepping `affected_ids` by hand.

THAT REFRAMES IT: the scope is computed by GRAPH REACHABILITY, and on a connected design a few hops reaches most of it. The question is whether scope should mean "what the seed can reach" or "what is actually about the seed".

THE OPTIONS:

(a) FILTER BY `affected_ids` — exactly his proposal: a gap is in scope when the seed (or its SATISFIES/REALIZES neighbours) is in the gap's own affected set. CHEAP, and it answers the question he actually had. COUNTER: it narrows to gaps that already name the seed, so a gap about a neighbour that WILL matter to him drops out — and `cap:scoped-analysis`'s whole promise is that it "names what it did not see", which this makes both more necessary and more voluminous.

(b) SUPPRESS `unverified_capability` FOR `planned` + ZERO ARTIFACTS — his second clause, and independently useful. CHEAP. COUNTER: it is a phase judgement baked into a detector, and this project's standing preference is to report the fact and let the reader judge (`dec:report-dont-judge`). It may also be the same finding as `dec:should-a-design-be-able-to-say-it-describes-something-that-already-exists`, one layer along — a design that has not started building does not want build gaps at all.

(c) A SESSION MODE ON `loop_status` — "I am building this Capability". Answers the noise complaint where he actually felt it: `next[0]` was detect-and-ask all session while the work was implement → user-correct → implement. COUNTER, and it is serious: `loop_status`'s contract is that a scoped answer must never read as "the design is clean" — it already keeps unattributable debt under `scope.not_attributable` for exactly this reason. A mode that HIDES project-wide gaps is the one thing that contract forbids, so this option must be built as "rank differently", not "hide".

(d) DO NOTHING TO THE TOOLS; THE COMPLAINT IS ABOUT PHASE — he was mid-bugfix with a user watching a broken app, and reflow2 has no notion of that. His items 3 and 9 are the same complaint from the other side. COUNTER: "wait for a phase model" has been the answer to several of these, and nothing is scheduled.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether depth was the wrong control or scope was the wrong concept; and whether 47–51 in_scope on his design is large relative to the design's size, which nobody measured.
properties.name: IDEA — scoped detection is BUILT and a real session still could not ask "is this one Capability still in a gap?". Should scope filter by relevance rather than by reachability, and should loop_status get a session mode?
properties.rationale: Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`. Two ideas held in one node because they are one question asked of two surfaces; noted inside that they can be answered apart if the answer differs. The reframing — that scoping exists and did not narrow — is a finding, not a decision, and is stated as such.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, per Anthony's own standing rule that a genuinely new thing becomes a proposal one day accepted rather than a requirement written on his behalf. Nothing here is intent.

HIS WORDS, 2026-08-11: "we need to make the search the graph first a requirement that is automatic. something like anytime a user has an idea, requirement, feedback, etc - first go search the graph to see what's already there (this should prevent near duplicate nodes in the graph appearing)."

⭐⭐ THE RULE ALREADY EXISTS, IN FIVE SERVED SKILLS. Measured 2026-08-11: `capture-intent`, `revise-design`, `brainstorm`, `kpp-proposal` and `retire-from-design` all instruct it, and capture-intent's wording is almost exactly his: "Search before you add. For each candidate, `search_design` with its key words first — the design may already say this. A hit that covers the same need means you update or link the existing node, NOT create a near-duplicate that HEAL will later flag and someone must merge. No hits is also information."

So the ask is not for the rule. IT IS FOR THE TRIGGER. And the trigger is the thing this project has now confirmed three times is missing: `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` (ACCEPTED) says skill use "must be triggered by the SITUATION, not remembered — and THE USER MUST NEVER BE THE TRIGGER", measured on this repo 2026-07-31, and confirmed from the field on 2026-08-11 by the second user, who named exactly the two skills he types and neither of the two that would have fired on situations he was already in.

⭐⭐ AND THE MECHANISM IS ALREADY A REQUIREMENT, PROPOSED AND UNBUILT: `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` — "a discipline that applies mid-task is delivered at the TOOL that triggers it, not from a catalogue read once at handshake." That is precisely what he is asking for, one layer more general. This idea may not need a requirement of its own at all; it may be the first concrete instance of one that already exists and has never been accepted.

📌 THIS NODE IS ITSELF THE NINTH COLLISION recorded in fact:the-owner-uses-reflow2-as-a-funnel-for-random-order-input, and it was found BY DOING THE THING HE ASKED FOR: searching before adding. Had the search not run, this would have become a near-duplicate of a proposed requirement and a fifth restatement of an instruction already in five skills — which is the exact failure he is trying to prevent, reproduced in the act of trying to prevent it.

WHAT EXISTS ON THE DETECTION SIDE, so this is not built twice. `possible_duplicate` fires on shared allocation sets with Jaccard ≥ 0.8 and asks rather than merges (`dec:ask-not-repair`); HEAL merges only on a human-asserted DUPLICATES edge. Both are AFTER-THE-FACT and STRUCTURAL — they catch two nodes that ended up allocated the same way. Neither can see "the same idea in different words, newly written, allocated to nothing yet", which is the case he is describing. Prevention and detection are different problems here.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) Put it on the TOOL, not the skill: `add_requirement` / `add_capability` / `add_decision` return near-matches alongside the write, or refuse-and-name when a match is close enough. Reaches every session including ones that load no skill. Cost — a write tool that sometimes refuses is a new failure mode on the hottest path, and BM25 near-matches are not reliable enough to refuse on (`dec:` on BM25 scores not being comparable across queries).
(b) SEARCH ON THE WAY IN, NEVER REFUSE: the write succeeds and the response carries "3 existing nodes look close: ...". No new failure mode, no judgement, and it puts the finding where the agent is already looking. Smallest honest version.
(c) A pre-write hook or a served instruction at handshake. Cheapest to state and it is what already exists — five skills say it — so this is the option that has already been tried and is the reason he is asking.
(d) Nothing new: ACCEPT `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` and build it, since this is an instance of it rather than a separate need.

⚠️ THE TRAP: a near-match list that is usually wrong trains the agent to ignore it, which is worse than silence — the same failure `unexpected_coupling` was retired for, and the one `v0.2.0-what-we-dont-know.md` names as the sharpest thing to watch ("a gap list you skim is worse than no gap list"). Whatever surfaces matches must be precise enough to be read every time, and BM25 alone has already been shown here to score the same topic 4.48 and 35.75 across two queries.

⚠️ SECOND TRAP, AND IT CUTS AGAINST THE WHOLE IDEA: a near-duplicate is sometimes CORRECT. `req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design` exists precisely because a body of intent that contradicts itself is still a design. Suppressing a second statement of the same idea can erase that the user said it twice, in different words, at different times — which is signal about what they keep coming back to, and is what `dec:idea-what-gets-searched-repeatedly-is-becoming-important` asks about from the other direction.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SHARPENED 2026-08-12 — THE WRITE HALF SHIPPED; THE READ HALF IS WHERE IT EARNED ITS KEEP
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

⭐ THIS SECTION WAS ADDED BY THE GUARD ITSELF. An agent tried to create a NEW node about exactly this and `add_decision` REFUSED it, naming this node and both routes on. The write half works, in the field, against its own author. That is the strongest evidence this node will ever get, and it arrived by accident.

ANTHONY NAMED THE BEHAVIOUR AS SOMETHING HE VALUES, 2026-08-12: "every time I ask a question or propose an idea, you do a search/research what has already happened. then we either sharpen the previous or add new content or all sorts of things that continually improves the design - i think this is awesome!"

⭐ MEASURED IN ONE SESSION — six saves, each with what it prevented:
  - "a requirement that anything developed has something that uses it" -> already captured 2026-08-09 IN HIS OWN WORDS. A duplicate node.
  - "accept the 26 delivered requirements" -> ELEVEN were satisfied only by `planned`/`in_progress` capabilities. Asserting delivery that had not happened, eleven times.
  - "should we have a purge skill" -> `dec:proposed-requirements-pruned` had already settled DROPPED-NOT-DELETED. Re-deciding a settled question destructively.
  - "a tool that does the import step" -> `import_graph` already took a `path`. Building a tool that existed.
  - "treat the union of 2+ graphs as one graph" -> `dec:idea-a-session-holds-several-graphs`, his own federation model from six days earlier. Re-deriving his own thinking.
  - "treat one side as immutable" -> `mirror_surface`, BUILT and stamping `mirror_of` / `mirror_content_hash` / `mirrored_at`. Specifying something already shipped.
