  Plus a doc review that caught a section marked OUTSTANDING three days after the thing shipped.

🛑 AND THE ASYMMETRY THAT MATTERS: **ALL SIX HAPPENED ON THE READ PATH, WHERE NOTHING ENFORCES ANYTHING.** The refusal fires on add_requirement / add_capability / add_component / add_decision / add_constraint. It cannot fire when a user asks a question and an agent answers in prose. Those six happened because the agent chose to look.

That is `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`'s failure with the trigger moved one step — not the user reminding the agent, but the agent remembering — and it degrades silently in a long session precisely when the graph is large enough to make searching most valuable.

⭐⭐ THE OBSERVATION THAT CHANGES THE VALUE CALCULATION: the write guard catches a near-duplicate NODE. It cannot catch a near-duplicate DECISION TO BUILD. **Four of the six saves prevented WORK, not nodes** — and work is the more expensive thing. So the unguarded half is plausibly worth more than the guarded half, which inverts the obvious reading that the write path is where the value is.

⚠️ SURVIVORSHIP BIAS, NAMED SO SIX IS NOT READ AS A RATE. Only the times it worked are visible; NOTHING RECORDS A SEARCH THAT DID NOT HAPPEN. `dec:loop-status-cannot-say-it-never-looked` is the same shape already on the record — "clean" and "never scanned" are one answer.

OPTIONS FOR THE READ HALF, none taken:
  A — A READ-SIDE HINT on orientation reads. Rides the existing `loop_hint` carrier. EXPENSIVE: it needs to know what the user asked, which the tool layer never sees — so the agent must volunteer the query, which is the same trigger problem one layer down.
  B — MAKE THE ABSENCE COMPUTABLE. Do not fire at the right moment; record whether a search preceded a capture and report captures with none — `dec:loop-status-state-not-history` applied here. EXPENSIVE, and the asymmetry is already recorded above: a node created without a prior search is not distinguishable from one created after a search that found nothing.
  C — INSTRUMENT ONLY, so the habit's decay is visible. Cheapest; answers nothing.
  D — DO NOTHING; the write path guards where duplicates actually enter. Weakened by the four-of-six finding above.
properties.name: OPEN — how does "search the graph before you add" become AUTOMATIC, when it is already written into five skills and still depends on somebody loading one?
properties.rationale:
The rule Anthony asked for is already written into five served skills, and the delivery mechanism he described is already a proposed requirement. What is missing is not the instruction but the trigger — the same gap confirmed three times this week. Recording it as an instance rather than a new need, and noting that the search which found this is the very discipline in question.

SHARPENED 2026-08-12, and by the guard itself: an agent tried to open a new node on this and add_decision refused it, naming this one. Six measured saves in a single session, all on the READ path where nothing enforces the discipline — and four of them prevented WORK rather than nodes, which is the more expensive thing and inverts the assumption that the write path is where the value lies.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — from the 2026-08-01 dynograph-foundation review. Nothing here is settled.

THE OBSERVATION: cut_structure (used today) reports articulation POINTS — single nodes whose removal splits the network. That answers "what is a single point of failure". It does not answer "how separable are these two subsystems", which is a different and equally architectural question.

THE IDEA: dynograph_graph::max_flow_min_cut (Edmonds-Karp, exact, unused) returns the minimum-capacity set of EDGES whose removal disconnects a source from a target. Read on a design graph: "which contracts would you have to sever to split A from B, and how many?" Edge weights are already coupling weights, so the capacity has a meaning here rather than being invented.

WHERE IT LANDS: dec:mosa-conformance is OPEN and its own text says reflow2 "already computes most of the criteria" for modular open systems conformance. Severability is one of the ones it does not. req:modularity-computed is the standing requirement that severability be computed rather than asserted.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS: min-cut needs a SOURCE and a TARGET, and nothing in the design says which two subsystems a user wants separated — so either the user picks the pair (a new question to ask) or reflow2 runs it over community pairs from leiden (defensible, but O(pairs) and the communities are themselves computed rather than declared). Also, low cut capacity is not automatically good: two subsystems SHOULD be coupled where the design says they should be, and a detector that rewards separation everywhere would push toward a design nobody wants — the same over-selectivity trap is_single_point_of_failure already had to be tuned out of.
properties.name: OPEN — should severability be computed as a minimum EDGE CUT, not just as articulation points?
properties.rationale: Chosen from the unused set because it maps onto an OPEN decision rather than onto a hypothetical: dec:mosa-conformance already claims most criteria are computable, and this names one that is not.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — 2026-08-11, from Anthony's observation that the governance work came from a real demand signal ("it was all taken from feedback from the storyflow project... I told reflow2 to consider it and do it"). Nothing here is intent.

WHAT WAS MEASURED, and it is the reason the question exists. reflow2's own governance requirements DID come from a demand signal: `/home/ajs7/project/dev_storyflow/reflow2_feedback.md`, the GOVERNANCE-AS-DESIGN entry by api-boss, 2026-08-08. Six Requirements carry AUTHORED_BY to `who:storyflow-api-boss`, so the authorship survived. But:

  · searched every node in the design for the string `reflow2_feedback` → 12 hits, NONE of them any of the six governance requirements
  · the document is not registered as an Artifact
  · so the origin of this work exists only in Anthony's head, and he had to tell an agent where to look

⭐ THE SELF-INDICTMENT: `req:no-idea-goes-quiet` is ACCEPTED and reads "an idea in the graph stays connected to whether it was built and to where it was written — THE USER NEVER HUNTS FOR THE SOURCE DOCUMENT AGAIN." reflow2's own governance capture violates an accepted reflow2 requirement, and no detector could see it.

⭐ AND IT COST SOMETHING MEASURABLE, twice. The feedback entry ranked THREE asks. Only #1 reached the graph:
  #1  model VERIFIES onto DesignRule so enforced+no-check is detectable   → BUILT (unverified_enforced_rule)
  #2  a Role/Seat node distinct from Contributor — duties attach to the
      SEAT, not the human                                                 → ABSENT, no such node type
  #3  an `obligation` category on DesignRule: "MUST do X AT MOMENT Y"     → ABSENT; categories in use
                                                                             are convention/methodology/None
#3 carried the sharpest sentence in the entry — "our doc map recorded WHO reads a file and WHAT it holds, and never WHEN — the missing axis was TIME, and no rule was being broken because no rule named a moment." That finding is nowhere in this design. The entry did say #1 was "the whole idea's leverage and the rest is optional", so building #1 first was RIGHT — but #2 and #3 were not DEFERRED, they evaporated, which is a different thing and the one nobody can see.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) A gap for a Requirement with no incoming DOCUMENTS/Fragment/origin edge — "what asked for this?"
(b) No new detector; instead make the capture skills register the source document as an Artifact by default, so the edge exists by construction rather than by discipline.
(c) Do nothing structural, and treat the origin as prose in the requirement's own statement.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO (a), and it is the same trap that made `rule:a-design-is-named-by-an-id-not-a-path` advisory: at genesis NOBODY has a source document — intent arrives by someone talking. A detector demanding an origin edge would fire against the entire design on day one and the only way to green it would be to fabricate origins. That argues (b) is the honest shape and (a) is only safe if it fires on requirements whose provenance says they came from a DOCUMENT.

NOTE ON WHY THE DAU FRAME FITS: of the nine DAU requirement characteristics Anthony cited, TRACEABLE is defined as connecting "directly back to top-level strategic guidance and forward to system design specs." reflow2 checks FORWARD (the golden thread; unmotivated_capability fired on exactly this) and has no check at all for BACKWARD. COMPLETE failed too — 2 of 3 ranked asks are absent in any form.
properties.name: OPEN — should a Requirement with no recorded ORIGIN be a gap? The golden thread checks forward and nothing checks backward
properties.rationale: The demand signal existed and became requirements — the process was run. What broke was traceability backward to the source and completeness across the source's three asks. Both are invisible to every detector reflow2 has, and an accepted requirement already says they should not be.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — found 2026-08-11 while answering Anthony's question about work built without a requirement. Nothing here is intent.

THE ASYMMETRY, read from the code rather than assumed. `detect_status_contradictions` (detect.rs:2146) fires in exactly two places, and both are OVERSTATEMENTS:
  · a Capability at `verified` with no passing check          → 0.70
  · a Requirement at `met` with nothing satisfying it         → 0.70
Nothing anywhere looks at the opposite direction.

THE INSTANCE THAT SURFACED IT: `cap:governance-proposal` sits at `planned` while `art:governance-proposal-skill` REALIZES it, it is allocated to `cmp:skills`, and that component's check passes. The skill is being SERVED to sessions right now. The status claims less than the structure shows, and no detector has an opinion.

⭐ THIS IS A NAMED-AND-UNBUILT CASE, NOT AN OVERSIGHT I INVENTED. The test at detect.rs:1401-1407 records the same limit from the Release side and assigns it: "a status that claims less than the structure shows is `status_contradiction`'s territory, not this one's." It was allocated to that detector and never written there.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) Add the mirror rule to status_contradiction: a Capability at `planned`/`unrealized` with an incoming REALIZES, or with a passing check, is understating.
(b) Lower severity than 0.70. Overstating is a claim with nothing behind it; understating is a record that has fallen behind reality — arguably drift, not a contradiction, and drift already has its own machinery.
(c) Do nothing, on the grounds that understating harms nobody.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO (c), which is why this is worth asking at all: understating is what makes `graph_report`'s delivery count too LOW, and a design that under-reports its own completion is the one nobody trusts the numbers on. It is also the direction that silently accumulates, because nothing complains.

⚠️ SIZING CAVEAT before anyone treats (a) as small: `Release.status` and `Capability.status` both DEFAULT to `planned` (detect.rs:1401-1403 states this for Release). So "planned + realized" would fire on every capability whose status nobody ever set, which on a young design may be most of them. Whether that is signal or a flood is unmeasured, and measuring it is the first step, not the fix.
properties.name: OPEN — should a status that claims LESS than the structure shows be a gap, the way an overstated one already is?
properties.rationale: status_contradiction is one-directional and its own test file assigns the other direction to it. The instance that exposed it is shipped, served code recorded as `planned`. The open part is whether the mirror rule floods, because `planned` is a schema default nobody chose.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-12, second half of his CAP question. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen.

DISTINCT FROM `dec:idea-is-reflow2-itself-a-cp-store-behind-an-ap-record`, deliberately kept apart: that one asks whether CAP describes reflow2's OWN architecture. This one asks whether CAP is vocabulary reflow2 should HAND ITS USERS. One node holding both could only ever be half-answered.

SIBLING, NOT DUPLICATE, OF `dec:idea-the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph` (proposed, 2026-08-08). That node asks about the DIRECTION of inference — should the quality attribute drive allocation rather than be read off it. This asks whether a SPECIFIC well-known trade-off frame belongs in the vocabulary at all. Related, and the answers could differ: the ility→graph direction could be built without CAP ever appearing, and CAP could be added without changing allocation.

⭐ THE CONCRETE GAP, checked rather than asserted. `schema/dimensions.yaml` already carries NINE axes attachable to any node: reliability, performance, maintainability, security, scalability, observability, testability, coupling, maturity. **Consistency is not among them. Availability is not among them. Partition tolerance is not among them.** For a tool whose owner's stated operating context includes federated, independently-evolving systems, that is a real absence rather than a stylistic one.

AND ONE PIECE ALREADY EXISTS UNDER A DIFFERENT NAME: `cap:seam-incompatibility` — "say when two linked designs disagree at a boundary" — is, structurally, a consistency check across a partition between two independently-evolving replicas. The federation work (`cap:mirror-surface`, `cap:composed-analysis`, `cap:complementary-pairing`) is a distributed-design problem that has never been described in distributed-systems terms.

═══ THE OPTIONS ═══

A — NOTHING. CAP is domain knowledge the AGENT brings to a conversation, not vocabulary the graph must hold. An agent can already reason about it and record the resulting decision as an ordinary Decision node, today, with no change whatsoever. CHEAPEST, and the null hypothesis this has to beat.

B — ADD `consistency` AND `availability` TO THE DIMENSION ENUM. Cheap, additive, existing graphs unaffected. `ility_report` already reports NOT INFORMED with a reason for axes it cannot compute — so honest silence is the built-in default and nothing pretends. NOTE: a new enum value moves NO stamp count, which would be the fifth recorded instance of the stamp being blind to a real compatibility event.

C — ASK IT UPFRONT, at genesis or adopt: "is this system CP or AP under partition, and L or C in normal operation?" This is exactly the shape `dec:idea-the-ility-chooses-the-allocation-graph` argues for in Anthony's own words — "if you don't ask upfront, these cost a lot in having to rework services after they've been already developed." A CAP posture chosen late is a rewrite; chosen early it is a constraint everything else obeys.

D — A CONTRADICTION DETECTOR, and the only option where anything COMPUTES. A design asserting strict consistency AND high availability across a declared partition boundary is claiming something the theorem forbids. reflow2 already has the machinery: `CONTRADICTS`, `cap:kpp` for inviolable intent, `constrains`, and `cap:key-interfaces` for computing whether a change crosses a published boundary. This is a KPP breach with a known proof.

═══ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea ═══

⚠️ 1. THE STRONGEST ONE — reflow2 IS DOMAIN-NEUTRAL AND CAP IS NOT. Its stated operating breadth is greenfield and brownfield and continual, across several organisations; the owner's own context is Space Force systems engineering and a Brookhaven beamline stack. CAP is meaningless for a beamline's mechanical design or a spacecraft thermal budget. Building a distributed-systems theorem into the core vocabulary privileges software architecture over every other domain the tool claims to serve.

⚠️ 2. "PICK TWO OF THREE" IS ITSELF A MISLEADING FRAME, and shipping it would propagate the misreading. CAP forces a choice ONLY DURING a partition; in normal operation a system need not sacrifice either. That is precisely why PACELC exists. A tool that offers CAP as a first-class axis would be handing users the version practitioners most often get wrong.

⚠️ 3. VOCABULARY NOBODY USES IS THE SHAPE THIS PROJECT SPENT A MONTH REMOVING. Requirement's five-state lifecycle runs 3-of-5 unused; BL-198 was the removal work. Nine dimensions already exist and the ility report cannot inform four of them. Two more unused axes make the enum longer and the design no truer.

⚠️ 4. A PLANNED CAPABILITY COSTS THREE GAPS FOREVER (`dec:exploratory-staging`, measured: 34 of 73 open gaps came from routing wishes to Capability). Option D as a planned capability is a standing tax until someone builds it.

📌 WHERE THE IDEA IS STRONGEST, narrower than "add CAP": not as a general axis, but where reflow2 ALREADY has the substrate — the federation seam. `cap:seam-incompatibility` computes disagreement between two independently-evolving designs, which is a consistency question with a real detector behind it. If any of this earns its place, that is the door, and it needs no enum change at all.
properties.name: PARKED, NOT ACCEPTED — should consistency/availability/partition-tolerance be vocabulary reflow2 offers? The federation seam is the road if any is ever taken. Anthony, 2026-08-12: revisit later, more important things first.
properties.rationale:
PARKED ON ANTHONY'S WORD, 2026-08-12: "we can add cap:seam-incompatibility as proposed, but leave it as not accepted. one day we can come back to this — it doesn't sound like it has huge applicability, so I think there are more important things to deal with in the interim."

WHAT THAT SETTLES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It settles the ROAD: if consistency vocabulary is ever taken up, it enters through `cap:seam-incompatibility` — the federation seam, where reflow2 already computes when two independently-evolving designs disagree at a boundary — and NOT as new `dimension` enum values (option B) or a general axis. It does NOT accept the idea, schedule it, or claim it will happen. Status stays `proposed`.

🛑 DELIBERATELY NOT MINTED AS A PLANNED CAPABILITY, and this is the one judgement made on his behalf rather than by his word. He said "add cap:seam-incompatibility as proposed" — but `cap:seam-incompatibility` ALREADY EXISTS and is `realized` (it is the built detector this idea would extend), and Capability has no `proposed` status: its lifecycle is planned / in_progress / realized / verified. Creating a NEW planned Capability to hold the idea would cost THREE GAPS FOREVER — unmotivated, unrealized, unverified — which is `dec:exploratory-staging`'s measured finding (34 of 73 open gaps came from exactly that routing). Parking something explicitly because there are MORE IMPORTANT THINGS TO DEAL WITH, and paying a standing three-gap nag for it, would defeat his own stated reason. A proposed Decision is SILENT by construction — `detect_gaps` fires `undecided_decision_point` only on two or more REGISTERED alternatives — so the idea is kept, findable by search, and costs nothing until someone registers real alternatives under it.

IF HE WANTS IT TRACKED AS WORK rather than kept as a thought, that is one `add_capability` call away and the three gaps are the honest price of scheduling it. The choice is his; the default taken here is the quiet one, matching what he asked for.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex's idea, 2026-08-14 (Opportunities), in his words: "`propagate_change` summary: separate 'same Component dump' from 'crossed an Interface.' Default `full` off is right; the summary still needs a 'sibling Capabilities on the same Component, not actually impacted' band."

DISTINCT FROM `fact:defect-propagate-change-distance-two-is-not-an-edit-list`, which measures what happened (~65 named, 113 truncated, the Interface signal buried). This holds the unmade choice about the fix.

THE OPTIONS:

(a) BAND THE SUMMARY BY EDGE KIND — group the impacted set by HOW it was reached: through a shared Component, across a PROVIDES/CONSUMES Interface, along the Requirement/Decision thread. CHEAP, changes no traversal, and it makes the useful signal findable rather than smaller. COUNTER: it renames the problem if the bands are not ranked — a hundred nodes in three labelled groups is still a hundred nodes.

(b) A NAMED "NOT ACTUALLY IMPACTED" BAND, his exact phrasing — siblings on the same Component, reported as reached-but-probably-irrelevant. HONEST, and it keeps the count visible rather than filtering it away, which matters because this project's standing preference is to report rather than judge. COUNTER: "not actually impacted" is a JUDGEMENT, and the tool would be making it. A sibling Capability on a shared Component sometimes IS impacted, and a band that says otherwise will eventually be believed on the day it is wrong.

(c) WEIGHT THE TRAVERSAL rather than band the output — DEPENDS_ON already carries `weight` and `weight_basis`, and CONSUMES carries `weight` too. A radius that decayed through weak couplings would shrink honestly. COUNTER: almost nothing in a real design sets those weights, so the decay would be uniform and the answer unchanged — this is a fix that requires a habit nobody has.

(d) DO NOTHING TO THE TOOL; FIX THE INSTRUCTION. The served loop says "update ONLY what the blast radius names", which is what makes a wide answer a defect rather than information. Softening the instruction costs nothing. COUNTER: it concedes that the radius cannot be acted on, which is most of what the tool is for.

⚠️ AND A COUNTERWEIGHT FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION, measured on reflow2's own graph this session: `propagate_change` seeded from a TemporalFact returned ZERO impacted, because ABOUT_ENTITY is not traversed. ANY CHANGE HERE MUST NOT ASSUME THE TOOL'S PROBLEM IS ONLY THAT IT IS TOO WIDE. It is too wide from one seed type and silent from another, and a narrowing fix applied blind would make the silent case worse.

NOT ESTABLISHED: the ratio — he did not report his design's total node count, so whether 178 is most of it or a tenth of it is unknown, and that number decides whether this is a threshold problem or a shape problem.
properties.name: IDEA — the blast radius reports one kind of reach. Should the summary band "crossed a published Interface" apart from "sits on the same Component", and name the siblings that are not actually impacted?
properties.rationale:
⭐ SHARPENED 2026-08-16 with a measurement and a doctrine tension, both of which narrow the question.

MEASURED ON REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN: a real change event (`chg:artifact-intent-stops-being-injected`) returned 19 nodes at distance 1 and 1,068 impacted in total, and the FOUR `boundary_crossings` were the only part worth reading. So the ask is real at this scale, not hypothetical.

⇒ AND HALF OF IT IS ALREADY BUILT, which is worth stating plainly so nobody builds it twice: the summary already returns `boundary_crossings`, naming the crossed interfaces by id, alongside `risk_crossings`. 'Crossed an Interface' is ANSWERED today. What remains unbuilt is only the other side of the pairing — naming the siblings that are NOT impacted.

⚠️ AND THAT REMAINING HALF IS A NEGATIVE CLAIM, which is the actual open question rather than an implementation detail. A band labelled 'not actually impacted' asserts that sibling capabilities on one Component are unaffected — and sometimes they ARE, through exactly the shared state that put them on the same Component. Propagation found them because a path exists; calling that path uninteresting is a judgement about coupling the graph does not hold. This runs straight into `dec:report-dont-judge`, and into propagate_change's own refusal to say what to EDIT (`fact:defect-propagate-change-distance-two-is-not-an-edit-list`, which the guard surfaced beside this).

THREE HONEST FORMS IF THE VERDICT FORM IS REFUSED, none of which asserts anything the traversal did not establish: GROUP the ring by Component, so twenty siblings read as one component's worth; COUNT them — '17 of the 19 at distance 1 are capabilities on the same Component as the seed' is a fact, not a verdict, and is the sentence a reader actually needs; or SORT, putting crossings first and siblings last, changing only the reading order.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and it is the measurement that would decide between a verdict and a grouping: how often a same-Component sibling turns out to BE impacted. Nobody has looked.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex's idea, 2026-08-14 (docs/feedback/2026-08-14-alex-grok-session.md, Opportunities), in his words: "`record_change` should refuse (or warn) if the target's current hash already differs from what the caller thinks they are snapshotting — or be a required first step inside the typed merge when `status` is `accepted`."

DELIBERATELY SEPARATE FROM `fact:defect-record-change-overwrites-the-name-of-the-event-it-is-filed-under`, which the near-duplicate guard surfaced: BOTH ARE FAILURES OF THE SAME CALL AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME FAILURE. That fact is about `record_change` clobbering the ChangeEvent's `name`, found serially; this is about the SNAPSHOT capturing state that had already moved, found under parallel writes. Whether they get one fix is part of what is open here — which is an argument for keeping them separate until somebody decides, not for merging them now.

WHAT HE HIT (his item 2): in one batch he `record_change`d a Decision AFTER a sibling `add_decision` on the same id had already merged. The Snapshot stored the NEW statement. Nothing warned. In his words: "the timeline for that revision is a lie; easy for any agent that parallelizes writes."

THE OPTIONS:

(a) REFUSE ON A HASH MISMATCH — the caller states what it believes it is snapshotting; a difference is refused. CHEAP, and it matches doctrine already applied elsewhere: `set_artifact_checksum` is a two-sided accept for this reason, and `export_graph` refuses a divergent write rather than silently discarding. COUNTER: the caller has no hash in hand today, so this needs a new argument, and an agent that cannot produce one gets a tool it cannot call.

(b) WARN RATHER THAN REFUSE. CHEAP, breaks nothing. COUNTER: the loss is silent precisely because the call reports success, and a warning nobody reads is this project's own recurring failure.

(c) FOLD IT INTO THE TYPED MERGE when `status` is `accepted` — his stronger form: you cannot edit an accepted Decision without the snapshot happening first, because the tool does it. STRONGEST; removes the ordering hazard rather than reporting it. COUNTER: it makes one write path do two things, and `dec:ask-not-repair` is the standing preference for naming a problem over acting on it.

(d) DO NOTHING; THE DISCIPLINE IS THE ANSWER. COUNTER, and it is measured rather than argued: the sibling fact was found on 2026-08-15 doing exactly this, STRICTLY SERIALLY and in the order `revise-design` prescribes, and data was lost anyway. Ordering discipline is demonstrably not sufficient for this call — which is evidence against (d) rather than for any particular replacement.

NOT ESTABLISHED: how often the parallel-write case actually occurs — one report, one session.
properties.name: IDEA — the record-before-you-edit discipline can silently snapshot the NEW state. Should `record_change` refuse when the target has already moved, or be folded into the typed merge itself?
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`, options with counters beside them, nothing promoted. Kept distinct from the name-overwrite fact after the guard named it: two failures of one call, found by two different routes, and whether one fix covers both is itself part of the open question.

⭐ UPDATED 2026-08-16 — A FIFTH OPTION ARRIVED BY SHIPPING SOMETHING ELSE, and it weakens (a), (b) and (c) without settling them. v0.32.0 gave every typed constructor a `revision` block: landing on an existing node now returns the properties the call OVERWROTE, with their prior values IN FULL, plus a `changed` flag and a `prior_content_hash`. Its own note names this exact ordering — snapshot BEFORE the merge, because afterwards it files the replacement as the prior state.

⇒ (e) THE INFORMATION IS NOW IN THE REPLY, SO PERHAPS NOTHING MORE IS OWED. A caller who merges first and snapshots second is now TOLD, in the merge's own response, what the prior value was — which is the fact the lying Snapshot destroyed, handed back at the moment of destruction. COUNTER, and it is why this does not close the question: the block reports to whoever reads the reply, and the failure mode here is an agent parallelising writes and reading nothing. A value returned to a caller who does not look is not the same as a refusal. ⇒ The open question narrows usefully: it is no longer 'how do we preserve the prior value' but 'does a returned value suffice, or must the ordering be enforced'.

📌 AND THE PRIOR-HASH OBJECTION TO (a) IS NOW WEAKER TOO: the counter said a caller has no hash in hand, so refusing on a mismatch needs a new argument. `prior_content_hash` is now returned by the constructors, so a caller who has touched the node HAS one.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is intent.

⚠️ REFRAMED 2026-08-11 AFTER GETTING IT WRONG. The first version of this node asked whether reflow2 should automate git. That was not the question. Anthony: "I'm not saying that reflow2 does the actual git operations itself; I'm arguing that reflow2's own rules shouldn't be tracked by hand, but by some governance rules (and this may be different for every project, which is kind of how we designed the governance entities for reflow2 anyways)." His original words were "as part of governance", and the word was doing the work.

⭐⭐ THE FINDING, MEASURED 2026-08-11: REFLOW2 HAS A GOVERNANCE LAYER AND DOES NOT USE IT ON ITS OWN GOVERNANCE RULES.

  DesignRules in this design                                        10
  carrying a VERIFIES edge                                           1   (per-design-state-is-never-a-process-global)
  `dec:export-once-per-pr` node type                            Decision   — so `unverified_enforced_rule`,
                                                                            which scans DesignRules, CANNOT SEE IT
  Verification node for the lineage gate                          none
  `rule:nothing-lands-on-main-directly`                        advisory, unverified

AND THE GATE IS REAL. `tools/reflow2_check.py` fails the build on a broken lineage chain — it did so twice on 2026-08-11 — and its own source at line 515 says: "THE RULE THIS ENFORCES is `dec:export-once-per-pr`, accepted". THE PYTHON NAMES THE RULE IT ENFORCES AND THE GRAPH DOES NOT KNOW THE CHECK EXISTS. Delete that check tomorrow and nothing in the design notices: no gap, no defect, no unverified rule. The rule keeps reading as governing while nothing governs.

⭐ SO "CARRIED BY HAND" IS PRECISE AND IT IS NOT ABOUT GIT. The ENFORCEMENT is automated. The TRACKING of the enforcement is what is manual — a rule in one place, a check in another, and nothing joining them. That is the same shape this project keeps finding: the search-first rule living in five skills and firing only when one is loaded; the deferral discipline living in a table nothing computes on; mutation-checking practised in eight verifications and written down nowhere.

⭐⭐ AND THE GENERALISATION IS THE PRODUCT POINT, in his words: "this may be different for every project, which is kind of how we designed the governance entities for reflow2 anyways." The governance entities exist so ANY project can state its own policy and get gap detection on it — `DesignRule` with a three-state `enforced`, `unverified_enforced_rule` at 0.6, `cap:governance-proposal` to ask the consequence rather than inherit it. reflow2's own git and export policy is exactly the kind of project-specific rule that layer was built for, and it sits outside it. A consumer copying reflow2's example would copy the gap.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CHANGE, unranked:
(a) MAKE THE EXISTING RULES FIRST-CLASS. `dec:export-once-per-pr` becomes (or gains) a DesignRule so the governance detector can see it; the lineage gate becomes a Verification with a VERIFIES edge to it; `rule:nothing-lands-on-main-directly` gets the same treatment or an honest statement that it cannot be checked. Pure wiring, no new mechanism, and it makes deleting a check visible.
(b) ANSWER THE CHECKABILITY QUESTION PROPERLY. `req:a-rule-says-whether-it-can-be-checked-at-all` is ACCEPTED and unbuilt: it splits "no detector" into DEBT and ACCEPTED LIMIT. Nine of ten rules here are unverified and nothing distinguishes "nobody has written the check" from "no check is possible" — which is the difference between rule:bl-41 (LLM behaviour, arguably uncheckable) and the export rule (checked already, just not wired).
(c) BOTH, since (b) is what stops (a) turning nine rules into nine permanent 0.6 gaps.
(d) Nothing: the gate works, and wiring it into the graph changes no behaviour today.

⚠️ THE COUNTER TO (a) AND IT IS REAL: making rules first-class means `unverified_enforced_rule` starts firing on rules nobody intends to check, and this project has retired a detector before (`unexpected_coupling`) precisely for firing on correct work. That is why (b) is not optional — the enforced flag without the checkability answer converts honest advisory rules into permanent debt.

⚠️ THE NON-GITHUB CLAUSE STILL STANDS AND IS NOWHERE IN THE GRAPH. `rule:nothing-lands-on-main-directly` is stated entirely in GitHub's vocabulary — branch, open a PR, gates green, merge — and its four recorded traps are all forge mechanics. ON A BARE GIT REMOTE THERE IS NO PULL REQUEST. So the rule presumes a forge while reflow2 only requires git, and nothing says which parts survive. That is a live instance of `req:a-rule-states-its-scope-and-a-conflict-is-surfaced` (proposed): the rule does not state its scope, and on a plain remote it is partly UNFOLLOWABLE rather than merely unenforced. Any wiring must express the discipline in pure git — one commit per branch touches the export — with the PR being only where CI happens to notice.

📌 EVIDENCE OF THE COST, one day of this project's own work, four PRs all merged: two CI failures caused by the export discipline alone; roughly ten hand-driven restore-then-export-once cycles; a rebase needing a re-export because the three-way merge driver merges CONTENT correctly and cannot repair LINEAGE; the local and CI gates disagreeing in BOTH directions because one compares against HEAD and the other against main; and one PR left in draft after going green. A fleet of seven sessions reports the same and mitigates it with a social convention — "only the boss exports" — which is the shape this project treats as a finding everywhere else.

⚠️ WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN regardless: reflow2 must not push, merge or open a PR. `dec:repo-file-embedded` weighs local-first deliberately, and a design tool that writes to a remote is categorically worse than the friction it removes. Nothing in (a)–(c) requires it.
properties.name: OPEN — reflow2's own rules are tracked by hand while reflow2 has a governance layer built to track them. Should they be wired into it?
properties.rationale: Reframed after misreading the question as git automation. The measurement is the argument: 10 DesignRules, 1 verified; the export rule is a Decision so the governance detector cannot see it; and the lineage gate that enforces it exists only as Python whose own source names the rule it enforces. The enforcement is automated and the tracking of it is not — so deleting the check would be invisible to the design. That is a product gap rather than a repo-hygiene one, because the governance entities exist precisely so any project can wire its own rules in.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex's idea, 2026-08-14 (Opportunities), in his words: "Checksum accept: allow `as_built_aligned` when a Requirement did not change and the file now matches it."

DISTINCT FROM THE THREE NODES THE GUARD NAMED, and the distinction is the interesting part. `dec:idea-does-change-type-need-more-values-or-a-second-axis` and its fact concern `ChangeEvent.change_type` — WHY A CHANGE HAPPENED. This concerns `set_artifact_checksum.disposition` — WHAT A CHANGE MEANS FOR THE DESIGN. Two different enums on two different tools, answerable differently. ⭐ THAT THE SAME MISSING MEANING IS ABSENT FROM BOTH IS EVIDENCE, NOT DUPLICATION: one absence is a wording gap; two independent absences of the same category is a category the vocabulary does not have. The third node measures the case; this holds the unmade choice.

THE OPTIONS:

(a) ADD `as_built_aligned` AS A THIRD DISPOSITION — exactly his proposal. It says the true thing: the design was right, the code was wrong, the code moved to meet it, intent never changed. CHEAP — enum values are not counted by the version stamp — with a precedent in `baseline_established`, added for the same reason one category along: forcing a record-only event through a code category "writes a fiction into the ledger that exists to prevent fiction". COUNTER: three dispositions is a decision an agent must get right under pressure, and his item 8 complaint was that choosing between TWO already costs a turn mid-bugfix.

(b) LET `design_holds` CARRY IT, DOCUMENTED — say plainly that a fix restoring intended behaviour IS "no design meaning", because the design did not move. CHEAPEST, no schema change, defensible on the plain reading. COUNTER: it collapses "this change was meaningless" with "this change repaired a violation of accepted intent", and the confirmation ledger then cannot count the second — exactly the number somebody would want when asking how often code drifted from design.

(c) DERIVE IT INSTEAD OF ASKING — if the artifact REALIZES a capability satisfying a Requirement unchanged since the last baseline, the disposition is inferable and the agent should not be asked. ELEGANT, and it removes the mid-bugfix turn he complained about. COUNTER: `dec:two-sided-accept` exists because a SILENT accept "is how a design erodes into fiction over N fix cycles while reporting zero gaps". An inferred disposition is a silent accept wearing a computation, and the fix-cycle case is precisely what that decision guards.

(d) DO NOTHING — two dispositions plus a prose note is enough. COUNTER: see the two-surfaces argument above.

WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, THE INVARIANT: any new disposition must stay a DATED, ATTRIBUTABLE CLAIM counted apart in the confirmation ledger, as `baseline_established` is. The ledger's value is that it says HOW a design was confirmed, not merely that it was.

NOT ESTABLISHED: frequency. One report. The ledger could answer it by counting `design_holds` accepts whose events carry `test_failure_fix` — a cheap sweep nobody has run.
properties.name: IDEA — the two-sided accept has no answer for "the code was wrong and now matches intent that never changed". Should `as_built_aligned` be a third disposition?
properties.rationale: Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`, options with counters beside them, nothing promoted. Started as a new node rather than merged after the guard named the change_type pair: two enums on two tools answering two different questions, and the fact that the same meaning is missing from both is the evidence for acting rather than a reason to fold them together. Option (c) is included though it conflicts with an accepted decision, because it best answers his actual complaint and the conflict is worth seeing.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-14, deliberately stepping back from a specific fix.

HIS WORDS: *"sometimes I like to take a step back and ask what is the big picture and what do we want reflow2 to do. as the saying of 'missing the wood for the trees' says, I don't want to be hyper focused on solving this by creating another requirement which then causes another issue later on. I don't want this to become like a decision tree where it is so specialized to some training data that it is no longer generalizable."*

⭐⭐⭐ **THE OVERFITTING CONCERN IS EXACTLY RIGHT, AND THE PROJECT HAS ALREADY WRITTEN IT DOWN AND ALREADY FAILED IT TWICE.** `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` (ACCEPTED 2026-08-07) says in its own text:
  · *"a detector that reaches zero findings by only asking questions the graph can already answer HAS BEEN TUNED TO THE INSTRUMENT. Satisfying this requirement by adding checks that happen to pass is the failure mode, not the fix."*
  · *"One detector was added for that one case. **THE GENERAL PRINCIPLE WAS NEVER MADE A REQUIREMENT, so the next instance had to be found by hand again**, which is what happened today."*

THREE INSTANCES OF THE SAME PATTERN, EACH FOUND BY A HUMAN OR AN AGENT WORKING BY HAND:
  1. `chg:orphan-decision-degree-zero` (2026-08-01) — *"GETTING A CLEAN BILL FROM EVERY DETECTOR — detect_defects 0, hierarchy_issues 0, dimension_drifts 0, propose_heal 0 — and then counting zero-degree nodes by hand"*. One detector was added for that one case.
  2. `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` itself (2026-08-07) — six blind spots, every one found by a human querying by hand.
  3. **2026-08-14, today** — 43 live planned capabilities invisible to every tool; the Grok agent *"had to leave the graph and grep the tree"* (`fact:the-build-list-is-suppressed-by-realized-via-component`).
⇒ **Fixing #3 with a detector would be the third time the special case is patched and the general principle is not.** That is the decision-tree overfit he is describing, arrived at empirically rather than as a worry.

═══ ⭐⭐ THE WOOD: ONE SHAPE UNDER MANY FINDINGS ═══

**REFLOW2 REPEATEDLY CANNOT DISTINGUISH "NOTHING IS WRONG" FROM "I COULD NOT SEE IT."** Every instance below was found separately, and they are the same defect:

  · `unrealized_capability` suppressed by `realized_via_component` reads identically to a capability that is fine — 34 of 39 silenced (today).
  · The loop nudge state `absent` means BOTH *"not installed"* and *"this harness cannot have one"* — only one is actionable (today, `req:an-unavailable-loop-trigger-is-named-as-unavailable`).
  · `loop_status`'s sync reported the record `in_step` while `compare_designs` reported `identical: false` on the same file (today).
  · `dec:loop-status-cannot-say-it-never-looked` — ALREADY RECORDED: *"clean" and "never scanned" are one answer.*
  · `coverage_report` exists **solely** to fix this for ARTIFACTS: *"a design covering 30% of a system reports the same 0 open gaps as one covering all of it."* It is a point solution to the general problem.
  · AGENTS.md already states the rule and leaves it to the agent's virtue: *"`0 gaps` means NOTHING WAS DETECTED — never nothing is wrong."*

⇒ **THE GENERALISABLE MOVE IS NOT ANOTHER DETECTOR. IT IS MAKING NON-OBSERVATION A FIRST-CLASS RESULT** — every reported clean state carrying what it did not look at, what it suppressed and why. `coverage_report` proves the shape works; nothing generalises it.

═══ 🛑 AND THE SECOND HALF OF THE BIG PICTURE: WHO IS ASKING ═══

The other thread running through today is that **reflow2's reports have no notion of AUDIENCE OR PURPOSE**, so unrelated concerns share one surface:
  · `loop_status.next` leads with 78 never-asked gaps when the user's question was *"what do we build next?"* — the Grok report's item 8: *"the loop and the delivery plan share a dashboard and they should not."*
  · Gap ranking mixes design hygiene with unbuilt accepted scope (their item 3).
  · All ten rendered views slice by ASPECT and none by ALTITUDE (`dec:idea-a-view-can-slice-by-altitude-not-only-by-aspect`).
⇒ Coherence maintenance and delivery planning are two jobs sharing one dashboard. **A remaining-work answer may therefore be a VIEW over what the graph already computes rather than a new detector** — which is also the anti-overfit route, since a view adds no new judgement to the instrument.

═══ SO WHAT IS REFLOW2 FOR? THE ANSWER THE GRAPH ALREADY GIVES ═══

Assembled from accepted nodes rather than invented here: reflow2 is the **persistent coherent design memory** that outlives a context window — it CAPTURES intent, COMPUTES what follows from it (`req:completion-computed`: delivery is computed from the golden thread, never asserted), REPORTS rather than judges (`dec:report-dont-judge`), ASKS rather than repairs (`dec:ask-not-repair`), and leaves the deciding to the human (`dec:three-party-checks`). **Nothing in that charter says reflow2 must enumerate every possible defect kind.** It says its answers must be honest about their own reach — which is the requirement above, and which no amount of detector-adding satisfies.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.
(a) **REPORT SUPPRESSION AS DATA** — wherever a detector deliberately declines to fire, count it and say so (*"34 capabilities not asked about: their component already has an artifact"*). Generalises across every detector, adds no new judgement, and directly serves `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots`. Counter: needs a convention every detector honours, and an unhonoured convention is worse than none.
(b) **A DELIVERY VIEW SEPARATE FROM THE LOOP SURFACE** — remaining work as a projection over data already held, leaving detectors untouched. Answers the narrow question and the audience half. Counter: does not stop the next blind spot being found by hand.
(c) **A REQUIREMENT THAT EVERY REPORTED CLEAN STATE CARRIES ITS OWN REACH.** The strongest general form and the hardest: it constrains every existing report at once, and `req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read` would demand something compute it.
(d) **ADD A DETECTOR FOR THE BUILD LIST.** The narrow fix. **Named as the option this node exists to question**, and the one that has already been taken twice with the recorded result that the next instance was found by hand.
(e) **NOTHING — accept that agents must read `0 gaps` sceptically.** Counter: AGENTS.md already asks exactly that, in bold, and three agents in three weeks still had to find blind spots by hand. **An instruction that has failed three times is evidence about instructions, not about the agents.**

⚠️ THE HONEST RISK IN (a) AND (c): a report that lists everything it did not look at can drown the thing it did find. `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` already warns about the mirror failure — reaching zero findings by asking only easy questions — so both directions have a way to look good while being useless, and whichever is taken needs a measurement rather than a feeling.
properties.name: OPEN — the general question behind five separate findings: should reflow2 make "I could not see this" a reportable state, instead of adding a detector each time a blind spot is discovered?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill at Anthony's explicit request to step back before fixing. Recorded as its own question rather than folded into the remaining-work decision because the two are separately answerable and answering only the narrow one is the failure this node names. The load-bearing evidence is that the project already accepted the general principle in `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` and has now failed it three times — so the overfitting concern is measured history rather than a hypothetical, and the third instance was in hand before he raised it. The "what is reflow2 for" summary is deliberately assembled from already-accepted nodes rather than composed fresh, since a charter invented in one session to justify one fix would be the same overfit at a higher level.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — surfaced 2026-08-11 by reading reflow2's own founding docs against the build, on Anthony's rule: an already-satisfied doc requirement is dropped, a genuinely new one becomes a proposal. Nothing here is intent.

WHAT EXISTS: `docs/sme-augmentation.md`, a full design dated 2026-07-17. WHAT IS IN THE GRAPH: nothing. No Capability, no Requirement, no detector. Verified — zero occurrences of `sme_consideration` anywhere in the codebase, and `docs/requirements-coverage.md` carries it as ⬜ twice (GS-10 "SME gaps", EX-SME "SME augmentation post-pass").

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) Build it as designed — a gated pass emitting `sme_consideration` gaps with the grounding spectrum.
(b) Build only the RECORDING half: a way to mark a node as agent-proposed-not-user-stated with its grounding, and let the skills do the proposing. Much smaller; keeps the honest-provenance value and drops the pass machinery.
(c) Declare it superseded by agent-native capture and retire the doc's requirement rather than leaving it ⬜ forever.

Every option below should be judged on how well it stands in for asking him — not on how elegant the metric is.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE Q-TABLE FRAMING IS ALREADY SETTLED DOCTRINE HERE, AND IT
ARRIVES IN THIS DOMAIN WITH ONE TERM ANSWERED DIFFERENTLY
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

`dec:attention-is-measured-behaviourally-not-lexically` is **ACCEPTED** on Anthony's own word (2026-08-10). Its three consequences apply verbatim and should not be re-derived:

(1) **A Q-VALUE DECAYS AND A COUNTER DOES NOT.** Here it bites harder: "has not changed in three months" IS a recency statement.

(2) **VISIT COUNT IS NOT VALUE — and there, the analogy BROKE:** *"THERE IS NO REWARD SIGNAL… The RL framing supplies STRUCTURE (decay, exploration) and does NOT supply the thing that makes Q-learning converge."*
⭐⭐ **THIS IS WHERE THE DOMAINS PART.** A design thread HAS a reward signal already in the graph — 40 DriftEvents, verification runs with `last_run_at`, `OBSOLETES`, releases reaching an Environment. Contact with reality, observed rather than proxied. **Note this beats BOTH of Anthony's candidates on their own terms**: it is neither "was not edited" nor "was invoked often", but "was exercised and did not break."

(3) **THE EXPLORATION TRAP.** For stability it is a feedback loop with the sign wrong: the harder something is to change, the less it is revisited, the more stable it scores.

═══ HIS EMPIRICAL CLAIM, TESTED ON REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN 2026-08-13 ═══

  ChangeEvents per ACCEPTED requirement (110):  0→67  1→21  2→21  5→1
  ChangeEvents per Capability (152):            0→58  1→52  2→22  3→10  4→6  5→2  6→1  7→2
  whole-thread (req + caps + artifacts) zero-change:  6 of 110
  CHANGED edges land:  art 555 · cap 180 · req 87 · dec 62 · cmp 43 · other 59

🛑🛑 **AT NODE LEVEL THE METRIC INVERTS.** `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` carries an 8,842-character statement; the sibling node records +4,770 characters appended in a single session. Its history: **0 ChangeEvents, 0 Snapshots.** ⇒ **THE MOST HEAVILY REWRITTEN REQUIREMENT IN THE DESIGN SCORES MAXIMALLY STABLE.** It measures RECORDING DISCIPLINE.

🛑 **AT THREAD LEVEL IT FAILS THE OPPOSITE WAY**, and the thread is the unit he chose: only 6 of 110 are quiet, because artifact churn dominates. Intent-only scoping (req 87 + dec 62 = 149 against art 555) may rescue it.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none taken ═══

A — COUNT RECORDED REVISIONS, threshold into a mutability class. **The measurements say do not build it**: it ranks the worst offenders safest.

B — FIX THE RECORD FIRST, then count. Require a revision to a satisfied requirement to leave a Snapshot + ChangeEvent. Already named on the sibling node as "the cheapest honest option", and a prerequisite either way.

C — SCORE ON EVIDENCE OF EXERCISE, NOT ON SILENCE OR ON INVOCATION. Checks that have RUN and passed across releases, no DriftEvent, no OBSOLETES. The only option with a real reward term, immune to the recording hole, and **local — it needs nothing from Alex's machine**. Expensive: 37 of 139 verifications have never run.

D — SCOPE THE COUNTER TO INTENT ONLY (Requirement + Decision). Restores thread-level signal; concedes the code cannot be frozen.

E — WITHHOLD UNTIL THE HABIT EXISTS. `consumption.rs`'s `MIN_MODELLED_RATIO` shape: **absence is only informative when presence is the habit.**

F — USE-BASED, and it is a DEPENDENT rather than an alternative. Blocked on `dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded` (consent), `dec:how-should-reflow2-log-its-own-usage` (where the log lives) and `req:reflow2-can-say-which-of-its-own-skills-a-session-reached-for` (unsatisfied). Bounded by `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content`. **And measured against the one real second user it would have missed half his workflow.**

G — ASK ALEX. Returns the fact rather than a correlate, costs one message, does not generalise. **The baseline the others must beat.**

⇒ **C IS THE STRONGEST ON THE EVIDENCE** — it is the only candidate that is local, has a genuine reward term, and cannot be fooled by silence — with **B** as its prerequisite for anything history-shaped and **E** as the guard. **F is worth having for its own sake** (it answers "what do users reach for", which is an accepted unmet requirement) but is a poor instrument for THIS question. **G should happen regardless.**

═══ THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded beside the idea ═══

TIME-WITHOUT-CHANGE AND CORRECTNESS ARE NOT THE SAME THING, and neither are USE AND CORRECTNESS. A requirement nobody revisited may be settled, forgotten, or wrong in a way nobody looked hard enough to notice; a heavily-used path may be heavily used because it is unavoidable rather than because it is liked. Both proxies would make reflow2 most confident where it has looked least — and `bl-155`'s unused-versus-unreachable finding, now restated four times in this design, says the graph cannot tell the difference from inside.

NOT DECIDED. The narrow question worth answering first is unchanged and now trebly supported — by both mutability proposals and by the use branch, which cannot detect a silent rewrite either: **should a revision to a satisfied requirement be required to leave a trace?**

properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, from a first-pass review of openmbee.org — website, repository listing and one truncated architecture page. THE OBSERVATION: Flexo's stated guiding principle is 'to adopt open, web-compatible standards for data exchange at every interface, including for both data format and exchange protocols', realised as a layered stack of micro-services where each layer is independently developed, tested and replaced, and where the seams speak SPARQL, GraphQL, OSLC and SysML v2. WHY THIS ONE IS UNCOMFORTABLE RATHER THAN MERELY INTERESTING: reflow2 measured its own seam band at 0.0% on 2026-08-03 — 73 component-to-component couplings, none of them running through a declared contract that one side provides and another consumes. BL-179 establishes that this is a NORMAL POSITION for a design that correctly did function first, and that finding stands. But OpenMBEE is a design of comparable ambition that made seam declaration a FOUNDING principle rather than a later phase, and holding the two side by side is the fairest available test of whether function-first is a trajectory or an excuse. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is not weak: standards at every interface is a rule with a price — it is why Flexo is a multi-service deployment where reflow2 is a single binary and a file in a repository, and `dec:install-once-per-machine` plus `req:thin-install` are commitments in the opposite direction. An internal seam between two modules of one binary does not need SPARQL; it needs to exist and be named. THE NARROWER VERSION WORTH TAKING SERIOUSLY: not 'every interface speaks a web standard' but 'every seam is DECLARED', which is reflow2's own `req:key-interfaces` already, unmet at 0%. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: whether declaring reflow2's internal seams changes any computation — `dec:edge-orthogonality` says a distinction earns its keep only when something reads it, and today the seams band reads it, which is one reader more than there was a week ago.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 adopt OpenMBEE's rule that every interface speaks an open, published protocol?
properties.rationale: Recorded through the brainstorm skill at Anthony's request. The claim of strength here is about the PRINCIPLE as stated, not about its execution: the architecture page was truncated on fetch, no source was read, and whether Flexo's interfaces actually hold that line is unknown and is exactly what the deep review should test. Recorded beside the counter-argument per the skill's rule that an idea killed in conversation loses its reasoning while an idea recorded with its objection keeps both — and the objection here is real, since reflow2's single-binary posture is a deliberate decision rather than an oversight.

properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, from a first-pass review of openmbee.org — website and repository listing only, deep review pending. THE OBSERVATION: OpenMBEE's active development is not its stable product. MMS 4 stores models in SQL; the successor, Flexo / MMS 5, moves to an RDF quadstore and is described as 'GitHub for graphs', exposing SPARQL, GraphQL, OSLC and a SysML v2 API. A separate experimental SysML v2 execution environment (`Systemica`, Go) is also under way. Commits across those repositories were days old when reviewed (July–August 2026), so this is a live bet, not an aspiration. WHERE reflow2 STANDS: it has its own vocabulary — 29 node types, 60 edge types — and no standard interchange of any kind. It publishes three interfaces (`ifc:core-api`, `ifc:graph-export`, `ifc:mcp-tools`), and `export_surface` already emits a subset of a design deliberately. THE QUESTION IS NOT WHETHER TO ADOPT SysML v2 INTERNALLY — the vocabulary is load-bearing and `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition` and `req:functional-vocabulary-computes` both depend on it — but whether reflow2 should be able to SPEAK it at the edge, in and out. THE ARGUMENT FOR: Anthony works in a defence/aerospace systems-engineering context and will be asked, professionally, why a design tool does not interoperate with the standard his field is converging on. An export that a SysML v2 service can ingest is a different claim from an export only reflow2 reads. THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT: SysML v2 is large, its tooling is young, and a partial mapping that silently drops what it cannot express would be worse than none — reflow2's whole posture is that a lossy translation must be reported, not quietly performed. Mapping 29 types onto SysML v2 would need the same no-silent-drop discipline `changelog_view` holds with `unmapped`. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: whether a faithful SUBSET mapping exists that reports what it could not carry.
properties.name: OPEN — should reflow2 speak SysML v2 at its boundary, given that is where the standards gravity has moved?
properties.rationale: Recorded through the brainstorm skill at Anthony's request to capture, as proposed ideas, the areas where OpenMBEE is stronger than reflow2 — before a deep review he intends to run against a clone of their repository. The strength claimed here is narrow and should be read narrowly: OpenMBEE has committed to a standard interchange and reflow2 has none. Whether their SysML v2 implementation is any good is exactly what the deep review is for, and nothing in this node asserts that it is.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — surfaced 2026-08-11 reading reflow2's founding docs against the build. Nothing here is intent.

MEASURED, not assumed:
  EnvironmentRule instances in this design            0
  QualityGate instances                               0
  occurrences of `unchecked_compliance` in the code   0
  occurrences of `open_violation` in the code         0
  typed constructor for EnvironmentRule               none
`docs/requirements-coverage.md` carries it as ⬜ three times (GS-9 compliance gaps, WS-4 the write side, WS-5 QualityGate) and its own "Dormant schema scaffolding" section lists Environment compliance as deferred-not-dead.

THE IDEA, from `docs/operating-environment.md` (2026-07-17): a design never exists in a vacuum. A house in Kennewick WA must meet city ordinances, county rules, state requirements, building and fire codes, seismic provisions and occupancy limits; the same house on Mars faces 0.38 g, no atmosphere, radiation shielding, pressure vessels and life support. Change the environment, change the entire constraint space. `Project OPERATES_IN Environment`; `Environment IMPOSES EnvironmentRule[]`; compliance emits `COMPLIES_WITH` or `VIOLATES_RULE`; two detectors (`unchecked_compliance`, `open_violation`) ask the human; swapping the environment is a first-class ChangeEvent that re-evaluates every compliance edge.

⭐ THE DISTINCTION IT CARRIES IS ALREADY IN THE SCHEMA AND IS GOOD: three kinds of rule, kept apart. `Constraint` is SELF-IMPOSED ("budget under $500k"). `DesignRule` is a CHOSEN convention ("branch before pushing"). `EnvironmentRule` is EXTERNALLY IMPOSED — the design cannot negotiate it, only comply, seek a variance, or fail. Only the third is dictated by the world. reflow2 uses the middle one heavily (9 DesignRules, and this session settled the enforcement question on one); it has never used the third at all.

⚠️ THE HONEST COUNTER, and it is strong: reflow2's own domain is SOFTWARE, where the operating environment rarely imposes an authoritative external ruleset, so dogfooding will never exercise this. Every instance would come from a consumer designing a house, a spacecraft or a regulated system — and no such consumer exists yet. Building it would mean building on the doc's argument alone, with no field evidence, which is the opposite of how everything else here has been decided. `rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party` cuts BOTH ways on this: the third party is exactly who would need it, and no third party has asked.

⭐ AND IT IS ANTHONY'S ACTUAL DOMAIN. Space Force systems engineering and NSLS-II beamline work both sit in heavily-regulated operating environments with externally imposed rulesets. The one person using reflow2 is in the domain the feature was designed for and has not reached for it — which is either evidence it is not needed, or evidence that nothing surfaces it. Those are opposite readings of the same silence and nothing distinguishes them today.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) Build the whole layer — constructors, the two detectors, the swap-the-environment ChangeEvent.
(b) Build only the WRITE side (constructors for EnvironmentRule + OPERATES_IN/IMPOSES/COMPLIES_WITH) and no detector, so somebody can record a regulation and see whether the vocabulary fits before a detector is written for it. Contradicts the project's own standing rule that a write side should land WITH its read side (requirements-coverage's WS-4/WS-5 note says exactly this and defers both on purpose).
(c) Retire the scaffolding — `QualityGate` and `EnvironmentRule` are two of the five node types with zero instances, and the project's own test is "unused AND redundant → retire; unused AND not-redundant → defer".
(d) Ask a consumer first. Nothing here is urgent, and the deciding evidence is a real design in a regulated environment.
properties.name: OPEN — should the Environment / EnvironmentRule compliance layer be built? The schema declares it, nothing writes or reads it, and it is what makes "design a house" concrete
properties.rationale: Three doc requirements, a schema layer, and a worked Kennewick-vs-Mars argument, all dating to 2026-07-17 with zero instances and zero code. The vocabulary distinction it carries — self-imposed vs chosen vs externally imposed — is sound and already in the schema. What is missing is any evidence a user wants it, including from the one user whose own domain is regulated.

properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-11, Anthony's word: "yes, I like option A - let's implement." OPTION A CHOSEN — speak on read, gated on the hash. B, C and D are recorded below as considered and not taken.

HIS FRAMING, and it was the right diagnosis: "It sounds like we have the tool, just not used well or surfaced."

⚠️ THE TOOL WAS ALREADY BUILT. `import_graph` takes a `path`, so an agent catches a graph up with the committed record in ONE TOOL CALL and no terminal at all. The CLI flag `--import` is a second route for people without an agent, not the only one. So nothing new was needed on the doing side — only on the noticing side.

⭐⭐ THE MEASURED FINDING THAT SHAPED THE BUILD: `provenance::last_synced` — the content hash this seat believes is at a given path — was WRITTEN BY TWO PATHS AND READ BY ONE. `record_sync` is called by `export_graph` (exchange.rs:207) and by `import_graph` (exchange.rs:382); `last_synced()` was read at exchange.rs:171, inside `export_graph`, and nowhere else. **The design knew at the first moment of a session and spoke at the last** — when you tried to export, hours later, and the stale-seat refusal finally fired. Same family as `dec:one-retire-edge`'s "a marker nothing reads is a comment", except here something did read it, at the wrong moment.

🛑 AND THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT THIS NODE FIRST CARRIED WAS FALSE, which is why the option was buildable at all. It said "I have unexported work" and "someone else's work has arrived" look similar from inside. They do not: `crates/reflow2-core/src/sync.rs` already distinguishes them exactly. File hash == `last_synced` ⇒ the file has not moved ⇒ every difference is the caller's OWN unexported work ⇒ silent. File hash != `last_synced` ⇒ somebody else has been there ⇒ actionable. One comparison, and no false-positive mode on solo work.

WHAT WAS BUILT: `crates/reflow2-mcp/src/sync_debt.rs`, served as the `sync_status` tool and carried on `loop_status` as `record_moved` when there is something to say. One finding per file this seat has synced with — `in_step` / `behind` (the actionable one) / `moved_but_current` / `missing` / `unreadable`. The judgement is BORROWED from `sync::assess_overwrite` rather than reimplemented; this module supplies the enumeration, the gate and the wording.

WHY IT LIVES AT THE MCP LAYER: `reflow2-core` does no file I/O, deliberately and repeatedly (`reconcile_artifacts` makes the caller supply hashes; `granularity` and `consumption` both say so). So the check could NOT go into `loop_status` in core, and belongs in the crate that already does this comparison for `export_graph`.

📌 A COST DECISION, PINNED BY A TEST: the export needed to compare against is the expensive half and the hash check is the cheap half, so `mine` is passed as a CLOSURE and is never built on the in-step path — the one every ordinary session takes. `the_expensive_export_is_not_built_on_the_ordinary_path` makes that a guarantee rather than a style choice.

📌 THE DESCRIPTION BUDGET FORCED THE SHAPE OF THE SURFACE: `loop_status`'s tool description was already at 1493 of 1500 characters, so the contract could not be documented there. Hence a dedicated `sync_status` tool carrying the full contract, with `loop_status` carrying only the finding — which is a self-explaining English sentence and needs no schema to interpret.

WHAT WAS NOT CHOSEN, kept because the roads not taken are part of the design's memory:
- B — AUTO-IMPORT. Closest to what was first asked for. Rejected: `import_graph` is an UPSERT, so an unasked one silently overwrites live session work, and doing it unasked makes it invisible. `dec:ask-not-repair`.
- C — REFUSE ON FIRST READ. Rejected: a refusal on READ is heavy-handed, and a session deliberately working from an older design would meet it every time.
- D — DOCUMENTATION ONLY. Rejected: the answer this project has already found wanting twice; a discipline written down and not triggered is one that does not happen.

⭐ THE DEPENDENCY STILL HOLDS: if `dec:central-host` goes the hosted way for the flo2 case, this question DISSOLVES for those users — there is no local store to catch up, because there is one graph everyone reads live. It stays live for anyone working from a checkout.
properties.name: DECIDED — a graph reports when the shared record has moved ahead of it, gated on a computed content hash, and never acts on it
properties.rationale: Anthony chose option A on 2026-08-11 after being shown that the tool already existed and only the trigger was missing. `dec:multi-writer-architecture` (accepted 2026-07-25) had already committed this project to building "merge-on-pull ergonomics" and that clause had never been cashed, so this settles an unbuilt commitment rather than adding new scope. The node keeps its own refuted counter-argument on the record: the claim that unexported work and somebody else's arrival look alike from inside was disproved by reading sync.rs the same day, and it was that refutation which made option A buildable.

properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-14 BY ANTHONY: **BOTH (a) AND (b).** A served interview step carries *when and what to ask* — in domain language only — and a served routing table carries *how the user's words map to node types*, plus which artifacts to expect for that kind of thing. His reasoning: **neither half is useful alone.** A skill without a table leaves the mapping improvised, which is the failure Alex hit; a table without a skill is never consulted. Option (c), leaving it to agent judgement, is closed — it has now been observed failing on the second user's first real project. Option (d), detecting it, stays rejected-for-a-reason: the evidence never enters the graph.

⇒ SATISFIES `req:the-kind-of-system-is-established-before-its-parts-are-captured` (captured the same day on Anthony's word, from Alex's report). This decision settles HOW that requirement is delivered; the requirement states WHAT is owed.

⭐⭐ THE PRIOR ART SETTLES THE SHAPE, AND ONLY HALF OF IT SURVIVES — `reflow/workflows/00b-framework_selection.json`, read 2026-08-14 at Anthony's pointer:
  · **THE TERMINOLOGY REGISTRY** (`definitions/framework_registry.json`: node → `service`/`gene`/`agent`/`species`) was CORRECTLY REJECTED by `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` (now `dropped`) — cosmetic renaming, plus a load-bearing claim that *"framework choice determines which NetworkX analyses are available"*, which gates capability on a self-declared label. **The routing table decided here is NOT that**: it maps the user's phrasing to reflow2's own unchanged vocabulary, and gates nothing.
  · **THE SEMANTIC-MATCHING INTERVIEW** is what survives, and it is not cosmetic. S-01A: *"Framework selection is an ARCHITECTURAL DECISION, not a configuration choice. Wrong framework = wrong insights."* LESSON-04: *"Framework abstractions must match system semantics. Workflows are state machines (not services), even though both could be 'engineered systems'."* **Its first action is "Ask user to describe the system" — domain language, not node types.**

🛑 **AND THE DROPPED REQUIREMENT HAD ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN THE SURVIVOR.** `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` closes: *"domain as a hint to EXTRACTION and phrasing — what vocabulary the agent uses when talking to the user and reading their documents — without ever gating which computations run. That keeps the honest part of reflow's insight (a biologist should not be told about 'services')."* It was dropped as a registry, its surviving half was named in its own text, **nobody built it, and the second user then walked into exactly that gap.** A road correctly not taken left a fork nobody came back for.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════

RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-14.

HIS WORDS: *"It was a little unsure of how to store the data models for my project in the graph. It asked me what node types it should store them as. I didn't really know for sure so I told it to figure it out. It worked, but that might be confusing for someone who isn't technical… it should probably ask probing questions to figure this out without exposing internal components of the graph structure to the user."*

⭐ THE INVERSION IS THE FINDING. Mapping a person's words onto node types IS the agent's job and is written down as such — `capture-intent` exists to turn what the user said into Requirements / Capabilities / Components / Interfaces, and `describe_schema` exists so the AGENT can discover the vocabulary rather than guess. **The agent had both and handed the question back to the user anyway.** The schema is not under-documented here; the labour was returned to the one person in the room with no reason to know the answer.

🛑 AND REFLOW2 CANNOT SEE THIS HAPPEN. Every detector reasons over nodes already in the graph, and a leaked question leaves no node — the user's confusion lives in the conversation, never in the record. `loop_status` would have read perfectly clean through the whole exchange. **Same shape as `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`: a discipline that exists only as an instruction, with nothing able to observe whether it held.** That is the standing argument for why the table matters as much as the skill line: a table can be wrong in public, an improvisation cannot.

📌 IT ALSO WORKED, WHICH IS THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART. He said *"I told it to figure it out"* and the result was fine. So the cost is not a wrong graph — it is that a non-technical user meeting the same prompt has no such escape, and answering it wrongly would put their design in the wrong shape without either party noticing.

THE OPTIONS AS THEY STOOD.
(a) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — an interview step in the skills: never ask for a node type; ask about the thing itself and do the mapping yourself.
(b) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — a served routing table, phrasing → node type, plus expected artifacts per kind of thing. Precedent: `capture-session` ships one and its first dogfood found a hole in it.
(c) LEAVE IT TO AGENT JUDGEMENT — **CLOSED**, observed failing.
(d) DETECT IT — rejected for a reason: the evidence never enters the graph, so any check would have to live in the harness and read the conversation.

⚠️ ONE HONEST TENSION, UNCHANGED BY THE DECISION: some vocabulary reaching the user is CORRECT. `where-am-i` reports the design back in their words and gap questions are deliberately plain, so the rule is *never make the user choose the internal category* — not *never say a word from the schema*. Drawn loosely it would produce a skill that fights `describe_schema`'s legitimate use.
properties.name: DECIDED — the agent never asks the user to pick a node type: a served interview step carries WHEN and WHAT to ask, a served routing table carries HOW their words map
properties.rationale: Raised under the brainstorm skill from Alex's report and settled the same day on Anthony's word, after reading the reflow prior art he pointed at. The reading changed the shape of the answer: reflow's S-01A turns out to contain two separable things, and reflow2 had dropped both together when only the terminology registry deserved it. Recording that split matters because the surviving half — the semantic-matching interview — was already named in the dropped requirement's own closing paragraph, and a future session finding `req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted` at `dropped` would otherwise reasonably conclude the whole idea was rejected.

properties.decision: RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-08. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen. THE IDEA, his words: allocation of functions to systems/services could be driven by what the system is for — "maybe you allocate functions based on it being fault tolerant or very highly reliable or easily maintainable or based on maximal performance" — and the agent would deduce the likely answer and then ASK ("is this design about performance or reliability or maintainability or highly secure"), because "answering that question really determines how you allocate functions to which services" and "if you don't ask upfront, these cost a lot in having to rework services after they've been already developed". It follows an earlier thought of his in the same conversation: that allocation could be decided by graph theory alone — Leiden communities for clustering, or PageRank to avoid bottlenecks and god nodes — with domain-oriented and function-oriented decomposition "thrown out the window". WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, checked rather than assumed: the `dimension` enum in schema/dimensions.yaml already carries reliability, performance, maintainability, security, scalability, observability, testability, coupling and maturity, attachable to ANY node; `propose_allocation` already clusters the weighted capability graph with Leiden and never auto-applies; `evaluate_allocation` already computes modularity, misplaced capabilities and god-components as selective articulation points; and `ility_report` (BL-184, from Anthony's own correction on 2026-08-03) already maps those computations onto the axis each one informs, emitting named findings and never a score. SO THE DIRECTION IS THE NEW PART: everything above runs GRAPH → ILITY, reading structure and saying what it implies. This idea runs ILITY → GRAPH, stating the attribute and letting it drive the allocation. Same vocabulary, opposite direction of inference, and that direction does not exist. AN OBSERVATION WORTH KEEPING WHATEVER IS DECIDED: the attribute may change not just the OBJECTIVE FUNCTION but WHICH GRAPH IS BUILT. Performance wants the call-frequency / data-volume graph and minimal cross-boundary chatter, which is what Leiden on DEPENDS_ON.weight already does. Reliability wants no articulation points and may deliberately DUPLICATE a function across services so one failure domain cannot take everything — which directly OPPOSES maximal modularity, since a modularity-optimal partition is often reliability-hostile. Maintainability wants things that change together to live together, which is a CO-CHANGE graph, a different edge set entirely. Security wants boundaries following trust and data classification with some nodes separated regardless of coupling — constrained partitioning, not clustering at all. Four attributes, four different graphs over the same functions; any single "run Leiden and allocate" answer silently picks performance. THE ONE THAT IS RUNNABLE TODAY, and it is a cheap falsifiable experiment: maintainability. reflow2 already holds 316 ChangeEvents with CHANGED edges, which IS a co-change graph, already populated, needing no instrumentation — cluster it and diff against evaluate_allocation's current map to see whether things that change together are allocated together. Performance is NOT runnable: evaluate_allocation reports total_internal 1, total_external 0, unweighted_dependencies 1 — one capability-to-capability dependency edge in the whole design, unweighted, which is why modularity reads a meaningless 1.00. Reliability and security have no substrate at all yet.
