properties.name: The ambient agent — the caller performs the LLM work and hands the answers back
properties.spec:
REQUIRED, declared 2026-08-09 on Anthony's word. THE CONTRACT: reflow2 never calls a model. It returns `status: needs_llm` with a list of AgentPrompts, and the CALLER runs them and calls back with AgentAnswers keyed by prompt id. gap_to_prompt, ingest_step and ingest_corpus_step all work this way (crates/reflow2-core/src/agent.rs, ingest.rs, corpus.rs).

WHY IT IS A REQUIRED INTERFACE AND NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION DETAIL: it is a capability reflow2 DOES NOT HAVE and cannot supply itself. A consumer without an LLM cannot use the ask half of the loop at all. That is the definition of a contract needed from outside, and it was invisible because nothing declared it.

⭐ AND IT IS PROBABLY THE PAIR THE PoC MIS-MATCHED. dec:linked-repos-poc's one true positive paired OUR `ifc:core-api` (library) against flo2's `ifc:model-provider-api` (REST) at an 80/100 NAME match — "very likely the same contract, but they cannot be connected as either is currently built." The finding was right that a seam exists there; the pairing was on spelling. flo2's model-provider-api is about LLM provision, and THIS is the interface that actually needs it. Declaring it lets the seam pair on meaning.

DELIBERATELY MEDIUM `library`: the handshake crosses reflow2's own tool boundary as JSON, but the party that must satisfy it is whatever harness or service is driving the session — an MCP client, an agent loop, or flo2's design pipeline. How they reach a model is theirs; that they must is ours.

WHAT IT DOES NOT REQUIRE: any particular model, vendor or protocol. dec:three-party-checks holds the division — the LLM speaks, the graph remembers and counts, the human decides.

properties.name: An authenticating gateway in front — reflow2 has no authentication and is not getting any
properties.spec:
REQUIRED, declared 2026-08-09 on Anthony's word. reflow2 performs NO authentication and NO authorization, by design, and this node makes that a declared dependency rather than a caveat somebody has to find.

THE PUBLISHED IMAGE SAYS IT VERBATIM in its org.opencontainers.image.description label: "NO AUTHENTICATION — deploy on a private network behind a gateway that authenticates." `--http-allow-host` is Host-header allowlisting — DNS-rebinding protection, NOT auth, and reading it as auth is the mistake this node exists to prevent.

WHY IT IS reflow2'S DEPENDENCY RATHER THAN ITS OMISSION, and rule:no-foreclosure states the principle: reflow2 must never become the thing that decides who may read what. It delegates to an authority that already exists, on the stated principle that a server must not let anyone reach more than they could reach without it. Building an account system would foreclose that by making reflow2 the authority. So the absence is a POSITION, and the gateway is a contract the deployer owes.

flo2's reflow2_updates.md lists this among the two things reflow2 will NEVER do, stated once so nothing waits on them. Declaring it `required` is what turns that sentence into something the seam machinery can compute against — an unmet need on any deployment that has not supplied one, rather than a paragraph in a tracker.

SCOPE, stated so it is not over-read: this says an authenticating layer must exist in front. It says nothing about WHICH — flo2 uses Clerk (dec:stack-clerk); anyone else may use anything.

properties.name: DesignGraph API
properties.spec: Corrected 2026-07-28: this claimed `medium: REST` because REST was the schema default, and it is a Rust library API linked directly by callers — no transport, no wire, no endpoint. The false value was never chosen by anyone; it arrived by default.

properties.name: A real local block device the store can hold an exclusive lock on — never a network filesystem
properties.spec:
REQUIRED, declared 2026-08-09 on Anthony's word. reflow2's single-writer guarantee is enforced by RocksDB's exclusive lock on the store directory, and that lock is only meaningful on a real block device or local volume.

⚠️ ON NFS THE LOCK STOPS EXCLUDING AND SINGLE-WRITER IS SILENTLY GONE — flo2's reflow2_updates.md states this as a hard constraint on their side, and it is the failure mode req:single-writer-graph exists to prevent: two writers against one store is precisely the corruption case. The failure is SILENT, which is why it belongs in the design rather than in a deployment note.

WHY IT IS AN INTERFACE RATHER THAN A CONSTRAINT: it is a contract somebody else must satisfy — the host, the orchestrator, the volume driver — and reflow2 cannot check it or enforce it. That is the shape of a required interface. Anthony chose to declare the environmental boundaries alongside the code ones (2026-08-09) so reflow2's hard requirements are computable rather than prose in a tracker.

MEDIUM `data` rather than a filesystem value, because the enum has none — the contract is a durable byte store with real exclusive locking, however it is presented.

IT ALSO BOUNDS THE HOSTING SHAPE: this container holds RocksDB open and cannot scale to zero. dec:open-hosting-shape-vs-long-lived-reflow2 remains open, and dec:stack-fly-staging-ci is scoped to api and web precisely because min_machines_running = 0 plus auto-stop would kill it.

properties.name: Design export document
properties.spec: Corrected 2026-07-28: claimed `medium: REST` by default. It is a JSON document written to a path and read back — a data contract, not a network one. Its shape is the export schema (nodes, edges, graph_id, stamp, content_hash, prev_content_hash).

properties.name: The MCP protocol revision reflow2 negotiates — a contract defined elsewhere and implemented here
properties.spec:
REQUIRED, declared 2026-08-09 on Anthony's word. reflow2 IMPLEMENTS the Model Context Protocol; it does not define it. The revision is negotiated per connection by rmcp, and reflow2 supports three transports: stdio, legacy Streamable HTTP (2025-06-18), and stateless HTTP (2026-07-28).

DISTINCT FROM ifc:mcp-tools, WHICH IS PUBLISHED. That node is reflow2's OWN tool surface — the 149 tools it offers. THIS node is the protocol those tools are carried over, which somebody else owns and can change underneath. Two different contracts pointing in opposite directions across the same wire, and only one of them is reflow2's to keep.

WHY DECLARING IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING BOOKKEEPING — flo2's reflow2_updates.md §7 names it: there are TWO version axes at this seam and only ONE negotiates. The protocol version negotiates per connection and rmcp handles it. reflow2's own tool surface does NOT, and the toolsnaps stop a surface change landing silently in THIS repo while telling a consumer nothing. A consumer that pins an image gets a surface it cannot interrogate.

THE LIVE DETAIL WORTH PINNING: rmcp 3.1.2's ProtocolVersion::LATEST is still 2025-11-25, so the sessionless path is NOT yet the default. There is a tripwire test at service.rs that fires when it crosses. dec:stateless-seat-handle turns on that boundary: on the sessionless transport the server builds a handler per REQUEST and cannot infer who is calling, so `seat` may not be omitted — a wrapper written against stdio habits works in development and is refused in production.

properties.endpoint: A stdio pipe to a launched `reflow2-mcp` process — the default transport, and the one `.mcp.json` uses. `--shared` attaches through a running `--serve-shared` daemon and is still stdio from the client's side. There is no address and no port: the caller owns the process.
properties.error_model: Two layers, and a consumer must handle both. (1) JSON-RPC 2.0 transport errors: a response carrying `error` with a code and message — this is what an unknown tool name returns, including the rmcp-generated `invalid_params` "tool not found" that a degraded surface produces (`fact:the-degraded-surfaces-diagnosis-never-reaches-a-by-name-caller`). (2) TOOL-LEVEL failures: a normal JSON-RPC result with `isError: true` and the explanation in the first content block's text. A caller that checks only for `error` will read a refused write as a success.
properties.name: MCP tool surface (stdio transport)
properties.operations: JSON-RPC 2.0 methods, as MCP defines them: `initialize`, the `notifications/initialized` notification, `tools/list` (returns every served tool with its JSON Schema), and `tools/call`. There are no other verbs — every reflow2 operation is a named tool reached through `tools/call`, never a distinct endpoint.
properties.payload_schema: Self-describing rather than published separately: `tools/list` returns each tool's `inputSchema` as JSON Schema, generated from the Rust request types, so the field-level contract travels with the surface and cannot drift from the build. Results arrive as `structuredContent` where a tool declares one, otherwise as JSON in the first content block's text.
properties.spec:
THE DEFAULT TRANSPORT: JSON-RPC 2.0 over a stdio pipe to a launched `reflow2-mcp` process. `--shared` attaches through a running `--serve-shared` daemon and is still stdio from the client's side. The streamable-HTTP transport is a SEPARATE boundary, `ifc:mcp-tools-http`.

═══ WHY THIS NODE WAS SPLIT, 2026-08-13, ON ANTHONY'S WORD ═══

UNTIL TODAY THIS NODE CLAIMED `medium: REST`, KNOWN-WRONG SINCE 2026-07-28. `REST` was the schema default before `unspecified` replaced it (`req:seam-incompatibility`) precisely because a default must not assert a technology — and reflow2's own three boundaries said REST while being a Rust library API, a document format and this tool surface.

THE CORRECTION WAS BLOCKED ON A REAL VOCABULARY QUESTION, raised for Anthony rather than guessed: MCP is JSON-RPC 2.0 over EITHER a stdio pipe OR streamable HTTP, and one node was carrying both. `REST` is wrong (not resource-oriented; the HTTP transport is a single endpoint), `cli` is wrong for the HTTP case, `gRPC` is a different protocol. The enum wanted `json_rpc`, or a way for one contract to name two media.

⭐ THE DIAGNOSIS THAT DISSOLVED IT: **one Interface was describing two boundaries**, and its own `endpoint` field said so out loud — *"a stdio pipe to a launched process, OR the address given to `--http`"*. They differ in more than medium: the HTTP one can sit behind a gateway and terminate TLS, and the stdio one cannot be reached remotely at all. Anthony chose to SPLIT rather than extend the enum — no schema change, existing vocabulary, and the transport a consumer actually pairs with becomes nameable.

⇒ FOR THIS HALF THE ENUM HAS A RIGHT ANSWER AND IT IS `cli`: a launched process spoken to on its stdin/stdout. THE PROBLEM IS NOT SOLVED, IT IS QUARANTINED — `ifc:mcp-tools-http` still has no correct enum value and stays `unspecified` rather than taking a wrong one.

═══ WHAT A CROSS-PROJECT CHECK FOUND, and it is why the rest of this spec exists ═══

Five axes were `unspecified` on this PUBLISHED boundary until `seam_report` against flo2 named them: 3 agreed, 0 incompatible, **5 stated by nobody** — and on the two that mattered, flo2 had answered and reflow2 had not (*"the side that assumed less finds out in production"*). Recorded in `fact:reflow2-flo2-seam-measured-2026-08-13`.

⭐ NOTHING INSIDE REFLOW2 WAS GOING TO ASK. `unprovided_interface` and `unconsumed_interface` read EDGES, not spec completeness, and no detector reports an under-specified published boundary. It took pointing a second design at this one.

Every value here is a FACT about what is built, not an intention:
  · `auth: none` — no authentication anywhere in `crates/`. Not a gap but the recorded position: `ifc:authenticating-gateway` is a REQUIRED boundary whose name reads "reflow2 has no authentication and is not getting any".
  · `transport_security: none` — no TLS anywhere. On THIS transport that is not even a choice: a stdio pipe between a parent and its child process has no transport to secure.

📌 THE flo2 SEAM BELONGS TO THE OTHER HALF. flo2's `ifc:reflow2-design-api` says *"MCP carried over HTTP, as reflow2 already serves with --http / --serve-shared"*, so the pair it asserts is with `ifc:mcp-tools-http`, not with this node. The `transport_security` incompatibility measured on 2026-08-13 (ours `none` against their `tls`) was recorded against this node because the split had not happened yet; **re-run it against the HTTP boundary before treating it as still true.**

properties.endpoint: The address given to `--http`, or the one a `--serve-shared` daemon announces. A SINGLE MCP endpoint, not a resource tree — every operation is a named tool reached through `tools/call`. `--http-allow-host` restricts which Host headers are accepted; that is a host allowlist, NOT authentication.
properties.error_model: Identical to `ifc:mcp-tools`: JSON-RPC 2.0 `error` responses for transport-level failures, and a normal result carrying `isError: true` with the explanation in the first content block for tool-level ones. A caller that checks only for `error` will read a refused write as a success.
properties.name: MCP tool surface (streamable HTTP transport)
properties.operations: Identical to the stdio transport, because it is the same protocol: `initialize`, the `notifications/initialized` notification, `tools/list`, and `tools/call`. The transport differs; the contract above it does not.
properties.payload_schema: Identical to `ifc:mcp-tools`: `tools/list` returns each tool's `inputSchema` as JSON Schema generated from the Rust request types, so the field-level contract travels with the surface and cannot drift from the build.
properties.spec:
SPLIT OUT OF `ifc:mcp-tools` ON 2026-08-13, ON ANTHONY'S WORD. One Interface had been describing two boundaries — its own `endpoint` said so: *"a stdio pipe to a launched process, OR the address given to `--http`"*. Everything above the transport is identical, because it is the same protocol; what differs is that this one can be reached remotely, can sit behind a gateway, and can terminate TLS, and the stdio one can do none of those.

🛑 `medium` IS DELIBERATELY `unspecified` AND THAT IS THE HONEST ANSWER, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. The enum offers REST / gRPC / event / graphql / cli / library / data / mechanical / electrical / human, and **none of them names MCP over streamable HTTP**. `REST` is wrong: this is not resource-oriented, it is a SINGLE endpoint carrying JSON-RPC 2.0, and every operation is a named tool rather than a verb on a resource. `cli` belongs to the other half. `gRPC` is a different protocol.

⭐ THE SPLIT QUARANTINED THE PROBLEM RATHER THAN SOLVING IT. Before, one wrong value (`REST`) covered both transports; now the stdio half is correctly `cli` and the missing vocabulary is isolated to this node alone. Adding `json_rpc` to the enum remains the open option — declined for now because enum values are NOT counted by the version stamp (it counts node and edge TYPES), so a new value is a compatibility event nothing can detect, which is the stamp-blindness pattern this design has already recorded four instances of.

⚠️ THE COST OF LEAVING IT UNSPECIFIED, stated because it is real: `medium` is a pairing-key axis, and `unspecified` reads as UNKNOWN and never as agreement. **So this boundary cannot pair with anything until the vocabulary question is settled** — including with flo2, whose `ifc:reflow2-design-api` says `REST`. That is a true report of the situation rather than a failure of the check: nobody can honestly say what medium this is.

📌 THIS IS THE HALF flo2 ACTUALLY MEANS. Its spec reads *"MCP carried over HTTP, as reflow2 already serves with --http / --serve-shared"*, so the correspondence a user would assert is flo2's `ifc:reflow2-design-api` ↔ THIS node, not the stdio one. The `transport_security` disagreement measured on 2026-08-13 (ours `none`, theirs `tls`) therefore lands here, and lands SHARPER: on a stdio pipe there is no transport to secure and the mismatch could be waved away as a segment artefact, but this boundary really is plain HTTP with no TLS while flo2 says `tls`. **Reading (b) — a real assumption gap — is now the more likely of the two.** Resolving it still needs flo2's side.

✅ `auth: none` and `transport_security: none` are facts: no authentication and no TLS anywhere in `crates/`. `--http-allow-host` is a Host-header allowlist. Terminating TLS and authenticating is `ifc:authenticating-gateway`'s job — a REQUIRED boundary whose name reads "reflow2 has no authentication and is not getting any".

properties.name: <graph-path>.server.json — a running server announcing, beside the store, that it holds this design and where it can be reached
Core model types (Schema, Value, DynoError)
properties.spec:
REQUIRED FROM dynograph-foundation. reflow2 links `dynograph-core`, pinned by git tag v0.12.0.

NAMED TO MATCH THE PUBLISHER DELIBERATELY, and that is a finding rather than a convenience. The first attempt declared ONE umbrella interface for the whole dynograph dependency; pairing returned NINE candidates and ZERO pairs, because a pair needs a name match at or above 85/100 and an umbrella scores 62-78 against nine crisp names. Two causes, and the first was ours: THEY DECOMPOSED AND WE LUMPED. reflow2 links five named crates that map 1:1 onto five of their published interfaces, so the honest model is five requirements at their granularity.

THE SECOND CAUSE IS WORTH REPORTING UPSTREAM: pairing matches on NAME similarity, so a long explanatory name systematically undershoots the bar while a short parallel one clears it. That rewards naming an interface for the contract rather than describing it — defensible — but it means the seam is only as good as two teams independently choosing similar words, and nothing says so.

properties.name: Graph algorithms API
properties.spec: REQUIRED FROM dynograph-foundation. reflow2 links `dynograph-graph`, pinned at v0.12.0. Traversal and the community/centrality work that propagate_change, disconnected_community and the modularity score rest on — so a change here reaches HEAL and the allocation report, not just the store.

properties.name: EntityResolver API
properties.spec: REQUIRED FROM dynograph-foundation. reflow2 links `dynograph-resolution`, pinned at v0.12.0. Entity resolution is what the duplicate detector and the corpus-ingest identity work sit on — the same machinery dec:auto-merge-at-90-destroys-sibling-names constrained, and the same path dev_storyflow's merge-survivor findings landed in.

properties.name: StorageEngine Rust API
properties.spec: REQUIRED FROM dynograph-foundation. reflow2 links `dynograph-storage` (default-features off), pinned at v0.12.0. This is the RocksDB-backed store beneath every DesignGraph write, and it is what makes ifc:exclusive-local-store a real requirement rather than a preference — the single-writer guarantee is that engine's exclusive lock.

properties.name: Vector, HNSW and statistics API
properties.spec:
REQUIRED FROM dynograph-foundation. reflow2 links `dynograph-vector`, pinned at v0.12.0.

⚠️ DECLARED BECAUSE IT IS LINKED, NOT BECAUSE IT IS USED HEAVILY. reflow2's search is lexical BM25 today and dec:idea-embeddings-adoption is still open about whether embeddings and HNSW get adopted at all. So this is a real compile-time dependency whose runtime use is thin — exactly the kind of thing req:the-design-says-what-was-built-and-never-used was captured to surface, and worth revisiting if that detector ever lands.

properties.name: How a session says which design it is attached to — graph_id in, bound session out
Reflow 2.0
properties.objective: Keep a design coherent from concept through operations

properties.answer: Anthony, 2026-07-27: "go with your recommendation: the interface." Recorded as `dec:pairing-role-placement` (accepted) and `req:complementary-pairing` moved to accepted. The role extends `Interface.designation` rather than becoming a per-node attribute — a Component both publishes and subscribes, so a per-node role collapses to `both` and pairs with everything. AMENDED 2026-07-28 after the dynograph-foundation trial refuted the first draft of the matching key: base-compatibility is `medium` PLUS `transport_security` PLUS `auth`, because role-plus-medium alone would pair a consumer requiring REST against a public unauthenticated liveness probe. The gap stays open because the requirement is accepted but NOT YET BUILT — that is the honest state, not an unanswered question.
properties.context_setter: Nothing satisfies requirement “Pair two designs by complementary role, so the seam is computed rather than hand-wired”
properties.question: Does the publish/subscribe role belong on the interface itself — extending the `published` flag with a third value meaning "I need one of these from outside" — or on every node, as you described it? Recommendation: the interface. A component both publishes and subscribes, so a single role on a component collapses to `both` and pairs with everything, which is the only reason `both` is needed at all. On an interface, `both` stays rare and means something real.

properties.answer: Keep only the diagrams and mockups that something in the design actually points at. The link is the filter — the store holds what someone will look at again, not every intermediate render. (Anthony, 2026-07-31.)
properties.context_setter: Nothing satisfies requirement “What a session PRODUCES is captured too — diagrams, mockups and rendered explanations, not just the decisions distilled from them”
properties.question: Diagrams and mock-ups an assistant makes during a session are usually thrown away, even though they are often the clearest picture of what was agreed. Should reflow2 keep them automatically — and if so, all of them, or only the ones a decision actually points at?

properties.answer:
Yes — build it. Anthony, 2026-08-07, after asking for the question in plain English and a recommendation. This is the second "yes": the 2026-08-06 one un-deferred the requirement, and this one answers the precondition that requirement carried — whether the kit may report its own ADOPTION without breaking dec:loop-status-state-not-history.

Settled as dec:adoption-is-reported-the-loop-still-computes (accepted): the distinction is REAL, because that decision protects one specific thing — the answer to "what does this design still need?" must not depend on who did what — and adoption never touches that answer. It is a different question (is the TOOL being used as intended?), for a different reader (the maintainer), changing a different thing (the tool). The line is held by three properties rather than a promise: the count lives in session state and offline transcripts, never in the graph; no adoption field is read by loop_status / detect_gaps / detect_defects; and a check asserts the loop's answer is unchanged whether or not the count exists. With both, it could tell you whether you are using the version you intended, and whether the other project has moved on since. properties.answer: Yes — build it. (Anthony, 2026-07-28: "go with req:publishable-promise next".) properties.question: When one project publishes what another may rely on, it can currently list the connection points but cannot state what any of them PROMISES to do. So dynograph's real commitment — that a missing database fails loudly rather than silently losing your data — has no way to reach the people depending on it, and today survives only as a comment in our own build file. Should I make a promise markable as publishable, so it travels with the surface and gets checked like everything else? This is my recommended next build: small, reuses machinery that already works, and until it exists every published surface reflow2 produces is missing half of what one is for.

properties.answer: "I believe documentation is part of reflow2 (not external to). I think that is true to just about any project deliverable — that documentation is part of the project. It'd be like if I designed a fighter jet using reflow2, but then didn't deliver any documentation on it to the user. Likewise, documentation is part of reflow2 itself." — Anthony, 2026-07-24. So documentation is owned by the product, not treated as material about it: a new Documentation subsystem containing a docs component now owns cap:explains-itself, and README.md and getting-started/SETUP.md are registered as checksummed Artifacts realizing it. The consequence he is asserting, taken literally: a README that drifts from what the system does is a detectable defect on the same footing as drifted code, not something someone eventually notices.

properties.notes: Cut 2026-07-25. properties.name: v0.13.0
properties.notes: Cut 2026-07-25. A minor bump — CLAIMS gains a `seat` property (additive) — with docs/upgrading-to-v0.13.0.md written. THE RELEASE THAT MAKES CONCURRENCY HONEST, and every piece of it came from Anthony's own StoryFlow fleet. (1) A DESIGN KNOWS ITS OWN NAME: an id established on first open in <graph>.id.json, a sibling of the store because the id namespaces every stored key; minted with zero coordination; refused rather than defaulted when unreadable; and a store that already holds a design under the old shared id ADOPTS it, which is what keeps every committed export valid since graph_id is inside the content hash. Two on-disk designs can finally mirror each other. (2) CLAIMS NAME THEIR SESSION and claim_report COMPUTES liveness from the OS: a claim whose session exited is `gone`, listed in `stale` with its note, and excluded from overlaps, because a collision with nobody is not a collision; another machine is `unknown` and still counts. (3) THE LOOP'S SAFETY NET IS PROVEN AND INSTALLED: the nudge path is tested by running the REGISTERED hook command as registered, the server reports installed | absent | broken | unknown, the absence rides the handshake instructions, and reflow2_init now registers the hook it never used to — into .claude/settings.local.json, pointing at the kit so it updates with the package. Manifest: 68 artifacts with frozen cut-time checksums plus cmp:docs, cmp:skills and cmp:claims. Four of the five fleet lessons are now built; req:read-while-held remains blocked on dynograph-storage exposing open_as_secondary.

properties.name: v0.14.0
properties.notes: Cut 2026-07-26. A minor bump — no schema change, nothing breaks, nothing in a consumer repository changes — so no upgrade doc; the version moves because capabilities were added, not because anything is asked of the user. THE RELEASE THAT LETS SEVERAL SESSIONS SHARE ONE DESIGN, INCLUDING ACROSS MACHINES, and the value is in the three cases being told apart rather than blurred. (1) DIFFERENT PROJECTS ON ONE MACHINE never needed anything: each has its own graph directory, so each session runs its own server and they never meet — confirmed by measurement rather than assumed. (2) THE SAME PROJECT ON ONE MACHINE needs a SERVER (--http <addr>), because the store is single-writer PER PROCESS: six processes cannot each open the directory, but one process holding it with six sessions attached still has exactly one writer, so the constraint is satisfied rather than worked around. Underneath: the graph moved Mutex→RwLock so reads stop queueing (and the compiler audited the read/write split for free — all 32 read sites genuinely need only &DesignGraph), and seats are minted per SESSION rather than per process, without which a shared server reports every client as the same owner and claim_report tells six sessions they are each other. (3) THE SAME PROJECT FROM ANOTHER MACHINE additionally needs the host NAMED (--http-allow-host), because the transport answers only requests whose Host header is allowlisted — loopback by default. That is DNS-rebinding protection, and since reflow2 has no authentication it is the only thing between a web page the user visits and their design, so reachability off-box is a deliberate act rather than a side effect of binding a public address. The flag EXTENDS the default rather than replacing it, so naming a remote machine can never lock out the local sessions already on that server; and a reachable bind with no named host now WARNS at startup instead of refusing every remote session with a bare 403 and saying nothing. LIVE SHARING HAS A CENTRE and the docs say so: the machine running the server, which cannot sleep and cannot be offline — so it does not replace the git route for two people working independently. They compose: share live while both are at it, commit and push the export when done. Proven over real HTTP against real servers, with the Host header a remote session actually sends: 9 cases in CI. Manifest: 71 artifacts with frozen cut-time checksums plus cmp:docs, cmp:skills and cmp:claims. THE GATE EARNED ITS KEEP AGAIN — cargo fmt reordered an import after the checksum baseline had been accepted, and the drift was caught rather than shipped.

properties.name: v0.15.0
properties.notes: Cut 2026-07-26, the same day as v0.14.0. A MINOR bump because the schema moved, with docs/upgrading-to-v0.15.0.md written — and the upgrade doc's honest headline is that there is nothing to do. TWO THINGS SHIP. (1) `Verification.method` gains `demonstration` and `observation`, from Anthony's own taxonomy. Test, analysis, inspection and DEMONSTRATION are the four canonical verification methods in DoD and INCOSE practice and reflow2 carried three of them, so 'we showed it working' — which is how a great deal of acceptance actually gets closed — had to be miscoded as a test; `observation` is the as-fielded method, watching a system run without changing it, which is neither inspecting an artifact nor running a contrived example. `review` and `simulation` are KEPT, because removing a value would strand every node carrying it. Additive: an older reflow2 still READS a graph containing the new values — PROVEN by building a binary with the previous value set and pointing it at one — and only refuses to write them, since validation runs on write and the stamp counts node/edge TYPES (unchanged at 28/55). (2) THE v0.14.0 REGRESSION IS FIXED, found the same day it shipped and by hand rather than by any detector: with the graph held AND --http given, the degraded surface was served over STDIO and nothing listened on the port, so every session pointed at that URL got a refused connection — indistinguishable from reflow2 never having been configured, which is exactly the outage req:never-silently-absent exists to end. serve_http is now generic over the service it carries so both arms answer on the transport requested, and the startup line distinguishes the surfaces. The four new cases were MUTATION-CHECKED: reverted against v0.14.0 all four fail with 'nothing ever listened on the port the caller asked for'. ALSO RECORDED THIS CUT, built or not: dec:read-while-held-mechanism DECIDED (a read-only view as of open, not a catchable-up secondary) and req:verification-keeps-up ACCEPTED with cap:verification-freshness planned — the design now knows that a passing check proves only the paths it drives, which is the general form of the bug this release fixes. Manifest: 72 artifacts with frozen cut-time checksums plus cmp:docs, cmp:skills, cmp:claims.

properties.name: v0.16.0
properties.notes: Cut 2026-07-27. A MINOR bump, and the FIRST since v0.11.0 that genuinely locks an older reflow2 OUT: PERFORMED_IN takes the schema from 55 edge types to 56, and the version stamp counts edge TYPES, so a reflow2 older than this refuses a design written by it — loudly, never silently half-read. Machines sharing a graph must upgrade together; docs/upgrading-to-v0.16.0.md leads with that. The enum growth in the same window (Verification.method += demonstration/observation in v0.15.0, Environment.env_type += simulation here) does NOT do this, and the doc says why. THE RELEASE THAT MAKES A PILE OF DOCUMENTS INTO A DESIGN. (1) SP-3b/BL-7 CLOSED after months: `ingest` needed a language model, reflow2 ships no provider, and the calling agent could not be reached mid-run — so the whole extraction pipeline was unreachable from a session. `ingest_step` is the repeated-round collect-then-serve handshake agent.rs had specified since SP-2 and nothing had driven; three or four rounds, NOTHING WRITTEN until the last (prepare rounds replay against a throwaway graph, so an abandoned handshake strands nothing), and NO server-side session state, so it survives a restart and works across seats. (2) It now recovers RATIONALE and TEST EVIDENCE, not requirements alone — and both land unasserted, a recovered Decision `proposed` and a recovered Verification `planned`, because an extraction is an agent's reading of somebody's document rather than the user's signature. Making that safe required tightening unverified_capability to demand a PASSING check: it had skipped on any incoming VERIFIES, so attaching a planned one silenced the question the detect-and-ask skill has always said it should not. (3) NEAR-MATCHES ARE ASKED ABOUT: ingest reads the two thresholds the schema had declared and nothing read, and the band between them reports instead of guessing; a structural token-subset pass catches what scoring cannot, since `Gateway` vs `API Gateway` scores 74 — below any threshold, because ratios fall as length differs. Imported from storyflow, which has fought this for years. (4) BL-95: coverage_report says what the design has never been TOLD ABOUT — every other check reasons about nodes already in the graph, so a design covering a third of a system reported the same `0 open gaps` as one covering all of it. Rolled up and ranked by mass, never a score: an artifact whose location is a directory claims what is beneath it. adopt now ends by asking. (5) req:design-the-simulator ACCEPTED and its first rung built: a check records WHERE it ran, so `proven only in simulation` becomes sayable — the reason for the schema change, since simulating first only pays if you can still tell model from reality afterwards. (6) BL-107: the export lineage chain is now CHECKED by the gate, found because I broke it for six commits while nothing noticed. Manifest: 78 artifacts with frozen cut-time checksums plus cmp:docs, cmp:skills, cmp:claims.

properties.name: v0.17.0
properties.notes:
Cut 2026-07-28. A MINOR bump that locks NOBODY out: no node or edge type was added, so the stamp holds at 28/56 and an older reflow2 still opens a design written by this one — the opposite of v0.16.0, and the upgrade note leads with it. The one real cost is a slow first build, because the dynograph-foundation pin moved v0.11.0 → v0.12.0.

THE RELEASE THAT MADE TWO REPOS CHECK EACH OTHER. Almost everything here was found by running reflow2 against a second real project rather than by reviewing it: dynograph-foundation published its surface, reflow2 composed against it, and each side found defects the other could not see. Three of the fixes are in reflow2 itself, and every one was invisible to inspection and obvious the moment something real ran through it.

(1) A PUBLISHED SURFACE CAN CARRY A PROMISE (req:publishable-promise). export_surface withheld every Requirement as internal, behavioural commitments LIVE in Requirements, so the document offered as 'the published surface' carried structure and no promises. Found when a real provider could not tell a real consumer the one thing it most needed — that a missing store fails loud rather than silently falling back to memory. The promise survived only as a comment in the CONSUMER's build file, on the wrong side of the seam. Requirement.designation fixes it by reusing the mechanism whose semantics were already settled, so every existing check applies unchanged rather than through a second, unchecked channel.

(2) DECLARE WHICH VERSION OF ANOTHER DESIGN YOU DEPEND ON (req:design-dependencies-declared). The trial made it load-bearing: without a recorded pin there is nothing to take a surface AS OF, and the two real consumers sit two minors apart, so an offer from main described neither. Two facts kept apart — what you MEAN to depend on, and what the build ACTUALLY resolves — because storing only one gives either a document that drifts or a fact nothing can contradict. Proven on the real dependency and on a simulated undeclared bump.

(3) TWO DESIGNS ANALYSED TOGETHER without either being written to (compose_and_analyse), and AN INTERFACE THAT PUBLISHES ITS WHOLE CONTRACT (set_interface_spec). The composition's most useful result was a ZERO: with the seam hand-drawn, the ordinary detectors found nothing, which proved they check CONNECTIVITY and not COMPATIBILITY — no ordinary detector compares two nodes' properties across a pair. That measurement is what req:seam-incompatibility now rests on.

(4) THE INSTALL REACHES THE FILE THE AGENT READS. Installing into a repo with no instruction file wrote AGENTS.md, reported success, and stayed invisible to a harness that reads CLAUDE.md first — the same defect class the installer already documented from storyflow, in the opposite direction. The rule is now REACH WHAT READS. The eight slash commands ship with the kit as the one narrow exception to serving everything (dec:commands-are-the-exception), with the single way a command can rot — naming a skill that no longer exists — closed by a lint.

(5) CORROBORATION READS AS CORROBORATION. Recording that one decision QUALIFIES another turned the graph red, because the contradiction detector read the edge type and never alignment. Fixed with both counterweights tested: an opposing edge and an edge that says nothing are still contradictions, so no design written before this release changes meaning.

THE FOUNDATION BUMP WAS NOT HOUSEKEEPING, which AGENTS.md forbids. v0.12.0 closes a type leak reflow2 was structurally exposed to — search_fulltext returned dynograph_text::TextHit, from a crate reflow2 never names and reaches only through an optional feature — and makes the rocksdb and fulltext feature NAMES a committed contract upstream. Verified safe BEFORE the tag existed by building this consumer against the provider's unreleased tree. Migration checked rather than assumed: keys.rs and backend.rs are untouched between the tags, so a graph written by v0.11.0 reads identically.

properties.name: v0.18.0
properties.notes:
Cut 2026-07-28. A MINOR bump that locks NOBODY out and rebuilds NOTHING: no node or edge type was added (stamp holds at 28/56) and the dynograph-foundation pin stays at v0.12.0.

THE RELEASE THAT MAKES INSTALL ONCE-PER-MACHINE REAL. v0.17.0's install.sh on main already promised machine-wide registration, but the v0.17.0 assets predate the promise: the kit tarball lacked reflow2_install.py and the binary refused --only-if-present, so the curl install died at its final step on every machine (observed live on the maintainer's own machine, 2026-07-28, and bridged there by a hand-rolled shim). This release is the first whose assets actually carry req:no-setup-per-project: the machine-wide installer, the latent surface (cap:latent-surface -- one tool served where no design exists, nothing created), and /genesis + /adopt as discoverable doors.

Also ships: seam disagreement reporting finished honestly -- seam_report's design parameter now DECLARES it takes an object (BL-28), the defect that held main red between the cuts, fixed with the design gate's own drift catch reconciled two-sided (chg:accept-975fcb51ce6ec113); and Interface.medium no longer defaults to REST, so two silences cannot agree on a protocol neither chose.

Verified by CI run 30371232790 (workspace tests, clippy, fmt, 117 toolsnaps, smoke over real stdio, design gate, doc versions, skill lint) -- this machine holds no Rust toolchain, so the release rides the same runners that build the binaries. Epoch note: v0.17.0 was cut without an epoch or deploy/retire bookkeeping; this cut records its own epoch (sequence 210) and the deploy is recorded separately once the published assets are observed installed.

properties.name: v0.19.0 — the planning axis runs forward: planned epochs, the satisfaction schedule, and the arrival delta
properties.notes:
Cut 2026-07-31. A MINOR bump that LOCKS OLDER REFLOW2 OUT: SCHEDULED_FOR takes the schema from 56 edge types to 57 and that moves the stamp, so a design written by this version is refused by anything earlier (BL-19/BL-94) — upgrade every machine that touches a shared graph, together. Node types hold at 28 and the dynograph-foundation pin stays at v0.12.0, so there is no slow first build. Upgrade note: docs/upgrading-to-v0.19.0.md.

THE PLANNING AXIS RUNS FORWARD. plan_epoch creates a point that has NOT happened, set_epoch_status moves it to arrived, and schedule_for hangs work off it as SCHEDULED_FOR carrying modality expected|required. arrival_delta then answers Anthony's question in his words — 'what didn't we achieve that we were supposed to in increment 10?' — with five outcomes, the fifth (outstanding) being the case the original four assumed away: nobody touched it and it did not happen. The baseline is the target's FIRST snapshot, because the last would measure only the most recent replan and the slip would vanish from the report meant to show it. Nothing about the outcome is stored; delivery stays computed from the golden thread.

THE DESIGN CAN NOW HOLD WHAT IT POINTS AT. content_put / content_get / content_exists / content_manifest — a content-addressed store, COMMITTED to the repo, for what INFORMED the design as against what it produced. Hand-rolled in the core, zero new crates compiled. The manifest is DERIVED from the graph and never stored, because a stored manifest would be a second source of truth able to drift. What bounds the store is WHAT gets stored, measured rather than assumed: 29 session transcripts came to 115.8 MB against 81 MB for the entire .git history, which inverted dec:content-manifest's assumption that images were the risk — so the control is transcripts-by-exception, not a size cap.

AND THE CUT TRIGGER STOPPED BEING VACUOUSLY TRUE. ready_to_cut now demands at least one required obligation as well as an empty miss list; an increment promising nothing used to read as ready, which is the empty-release failure dec:release-trigger was chosen to prevent arriving through its own back door.

MANIFEST: 151 INCLUDES — 98 artifacts and 53 components. THE FIRST CUT TO FREEZE as_checksum ON EVERY ARTIFACT, so this release's manifest cannot quietly rewrite itself when a baseline later moves; the nine prior cuts recorded nulls. New this release: art:content (the store), art:content-test (12 cases, registered here because every sibling core test file already was and this one was missed), art:stateless-seat-probe, and art:upgrading-v0190. Every frozen hash was verified against the file on disk after export.

epoch:v0190 at sequence 240, preceded by epoch:arrival-delta. Verified by CI on the same runners that build the release binaries.

properties.name: v0.20.0 — the changelog becomes a derived view of the graph's own delta, and three fixes found by pointing reflow2 at a real project
properties.notes:
Cut 2026-08-01. A MINOR bump that DOES NOT MOVE THE STAMP: node types hold at 28 and edge types at 57, so a design written by this version still opens in v0.19.0 and there is no upgrade doc. The dynograph-foundation pin stays at v0.12.0, so no slow first build.

THE CHANGELOG BECAME A DERIVED VIEW. changelog_view renders the delta between two moments of this design in Keep a Changelog shape, with every bucket MAPPED from vocabulary the graph already records and every entry naming the rule that placed it. It is a DRAFT by construction: no entry claims what a consumer should do, because the graph holds what moved and never what it costs downstream.

THREE FIXES, ALL FOUND BY POINTING REFLOW2 AT A REAL PROJECT — a quantum-benchmarking concept designed end to end through this tool, which logged nineteen entries of friction and produced BL-124 through BL-137. (1) A bare content hash no longer reports drift on a file nobody touched: canonical_checksum ran on the two WRITE paths and never on the comparison, so the first honest reconcile_artifacts reported 100% false drift. (2) An acknowledgement is no longer design structure: the review Decision was wired GOVERNED_BY into the island it acknowledged, enlarging it and minting a new id, which made disconnected_community permanently unclosable. Fixed at design_network() rather than the defect-id hash because that network has three consumers — and the instrument showed centrality was badly distorted (four of the eight most central nodes were review records) while surprising_connections moved the OPPOSITE way to the prediction, 16 to 32, because the bookkeeping edges were SUPPRESSING real surprises. (3) set_interface_spec accepts medium, so the library/data foundation exemption from single_point_of_failure is reachable from the tools rather than only from create_node.

AND A RELEASE THAT NAMES NO MOMENT IS NOW REPORTED. release_without_epoch found three on this project's own graph; v0.17.0 is still missing its edge to this day.

MANIFEST: 155 INCLUDES — 102 artifacts and 53 components, every artifact hash frozen as as_checksum. New this release: art:checksum-dialect-test, art:acknowledgement-not-structure-test, and art:bl124-instrument (the before/after instrument, registered because it was written during this increment and BL-95 is precisely about files the design was never told of). epoch:v0200 at sequence 243, preceded by epoch:reading-carries-options, with the three ChangeEvents of this increment pinned AT_EPOCH — the step BL-137 was filed for, because changelog_view silently drops an unpinned event.

properties.name: v0.21.0 — the quality of evidence becomes a fact the graph holds: a check's TIME, INPUT and INDEPENDENCE (BL-106/126/136), plus a cycle finding that says which edge kinds it walked (BL-141a). Re-scoped from the four agent-facing capabilities it was planned for; those remain scheduled here and report as outstanding.

v0.22.0 — the delivery epoch becomes COMPUTED rather than declared (BL-68, the board's most ambitious item: TRL/MRL readiness as an observation, the gating threshold as the user's judgement, a forecast that marks itself a projection), the impact-check trigger stops measuring bookkeeping where it means precedence (BL-163), and the bulk import door finally describes itself (BL-117/118/138). SCHEMA CHANGE: both halves of the stamp move, 28->29 node types and 58->60 edge types, the first since v0.4.0 — an upgrade doc is owed and written.
v0.22.1 — a restore stops renaming the design, and re-registering a file stops erasing what the design knew
v0.23.0 — the design brain learns to talk about its own structure
v0.24.0 — a folder of documents becomes one design, and the first real trial found what green gates could not
v0.25.0 — HEAL stops certifying a deletion as safe: a proposal says what it would destroy, a finding names its hub, and a refusal names the call that fixes it
v0.26.0 — governance becomes askable, and the server says whether it is stale
v0.26.1 — rmcp 3.1.2, with the seat probe as the verdict rather than the suite
v0.27.0 — ownership arrives, the content store leaves, and governance is integrated rather than split
v0.28.0 — the surplus half of DETECT, search-before-you-add enforced at the tool, and a seat that knows the record moved
v0.30.0 — the seam is named, the record is findable, and the linking process is served

properties.name: v0.9.0
A cluster can be declared deliberately separate, so disconnected_community reports undeclared islands instead of one permanent warning
properties.statement:
A group of nodes can be declared a DELIBERATE PARTITION — a subsystem that genuinely does not couple to the rest of the design — so `disconnected_community` reports "N declared partitions, 0 undeclared" rather than one standing warning. The value is NOT silencing the finding. It is that a NEW accidental island becomes visible against the declared ones, which today it is not.

=== ⚠️ THE CONDITION THIS IS BUILT UNDER — Anthony, 2026-08-09 ===

He settled `dec:legitimate-islands-need-the-detector-fix` as: "C now, A next with the read-back, not B, not D." THIS REQUIREMENT IS OPTION A, AND IT IS CONDITIONAL.

**THE MARKER MUST BE READ BACK, OR IT MUST NOT BE BUILT.** A report must state, for each declared partition, ITS SIZE AND WHEN IT WAS DECLARED — "declared separate 2026-08-09 at 5 nodes; now 121." A declaration that nothing reads is set once and never revisited, and a partition declared at 5 nodes is still declared at 500 with nobody looking.

WHY THE CONDITION EXISTS RATHER THAN BEING TRUST IN GOOD PRACTICE: `dec:idea-detect-vocabulary-that-nothing-reaches` warns IN ITS OWN TEXT that "another marker nothing reads" would be a fourth instance of the very disease it documents — declared vocabulary with no computation behind it. Building A without the read-back would make this design's own recorded warning come true, in the increment that was supposed to answer it. `dec:edge-orthogonality` states the same test as an accepted rule: a vocabulary distinction earns its keep ONLY IF A COMPUTATION READS IT.

SO THE ACCEPTANCE TEST IS NOT "a partition can be declared". It is: **a declared partition's size and age are visible without being asked for**, and a NEW undeclared island is distinguishable from the declared ones at a glance.

=== THE REST OF THE CASE, UNCHANGED ===

THE DEFECT IN THE CURRENT BEHAVIOUR IS THE SUGGESTED FIX, not the finding. `disconnected_community` proposes `generate_bridge` — creating edges to connect the cluster. Where the separation is correct, acting on that suggestion FABRICATES RELATIONSHIPS THAT DO NOT EXIST in order to silence a warning about a separation that is right. That is manufacturing connectivity, and it is the same act as formatting coverage into existence — with the difference that here THE TOOL PROPOSES IT. **That half is now `req:a-repair-suggestion-never-proposes-fabrication` and ships FIRST, independently of this requirement** (option C), because it is a live hazard whether or not partitions are ever declarable.

WHY ACKNOWLEDGEMENT IS NOT ENOUGH, which is the part that makes this a mechanism and not a workflow note: `acknowledge_defect` is a one-time answer to a finding whose SIZE keeps changing. Acknowledged at 88 nodes it now reads 121 — at what point is it a different finding? And an alarm that can never be cleared is one everyone learns to skip, so the real disconnection arrives inside a warning nobody reads. **MEASURED HERE, 2026-08-09: the heal id MOVED WITHIN ONE SESSION as the cluster grew 5 → 7 nodes (`heal:33d1548dae64e97a` → `heal:4dc24c4df2dd7aa7`), so an acknowledgement made at 5 would already point at a defect that no longer exists.** That is why option D was rejected.

REFLOW2 HAS ALREADY MET THIS AND WROTE DOWN THE ANSWER. dec:documentation-has-no-operational-coupling (ACCEPTED, 2026-07-24) records the identical situation — three bridges attempted, all refused as lies, the island accepted — and concludes "flagging it is a false positive of the BL-84 family, and THE FIX BELONGS IN THE DETECTOR RATHER THAN IN THE DESIGN." It also states the exact constraint storyflow independently arrived at sixteen days later: "the exemption must not be written in a way that hides a genuine disconnection." **That sentence is also why option B was rejected: an INFERRED exemption is precisely the kind that hides, and an inference cannot be argued with.**

REPRODUCED IN THIS DESIGN WITHIN THE HOUR OF THE REPORT ARRIVING: capturing four governance requirements under dec:governance-integrates-not-splits produced a 5-node disconnected cluster with `generate_bridge` proposed. No honest bridge existed, so none was drawn. Storyflow hit it at 121 nodes; reflow2 hit it at 5. Both clusters are GOVERNANCE, and both GROW as governance is properly captured — so the detector currently penalises exactly the work dec:governance-integrates-not-splits committed to.

SOURCE: storyflow gap D of the peer set — raised by storybug Boss (47accf78), characterised and filed by api-boss (05af57c1), 2026-08-09, v0.26.1. Their stated bound: the growth from 88 to 121 is suggestive, not proven, because the two measurements may not share a scope.

properties.name: A comparison says when its two sides were written by different builds
properties.statement: When two design records being compared were written by different reflow2 builds, the comparison discloses that and says that property-only differences may be attributable to the build change rather than to anything anybody decided. Every export already carries `reflow2_version` in its stamp, so the input exists and is not read. THIS IS DISCLOSURE, NOT A THRESHOLD, and the distinction is the requirement: nothing is suppressed, reweighted or hidden — the reader is told what could confound their reading, the way `propose_heal` discloses that the alphabet chose a merge survivor. Tuning severity until phantom findings fall below a cut-off is explicitly NOT this, because it silences true and false findings at the same rate. THE EVIDENCE IS TWO INCIDENTS, NOT AN ARGUMENT: 2026-08-08 and 2026-08-10 were both cross-build comparisons, both produced a confident false data-loss claim written into a PR body, and neither reader could see the confound (`fact:bl-198-cost-measured-twice-in-both-directions`). It is also what step 1 does not fix — suppressing defaults cleans the steady state and moves the disagreement to the version transition, which every upgrading consumer meets once.

properties.name: Installing reflow2 into a project leaves a committable design record in the repo — the artifact teammates read
properties.statement:
ANTHONY, 2026-08-13, after Alex's first run on a real work project: *"this is a core feature of reflow2. both my brother and I thought it already worked."*

**IT DID NOT, AND IT NEVER HAD.** `git log -S "docs/design" -- tools/reflow2_init.py` returns exactly ONE commit — the one that fixed it. The same for any non-backup export destination. So this is NOT the regression it felt like: nothing was lost, and there was never a working version to lose.

🛑 THE REASON IT WAS INVISIBLE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF WRITING THIS DOWN: **no Requirement and no Capability ever said it.** A search of every Requirement and Capability for *durable record / committed export / shareable / docs/design* returns nothing about a consumer's committable record; the nearest, `req:design-reachable-without-the-repo`, is about reaching a design WITHOUT the repo, which is a different need.

⇒ CONSEQUENCES, ALL OF WHICH ARE THE SYSTEM WORKING CORRECTLY:
  · `cap:kit` reads `verified` and is NOT lying — its scope is *"one command sets up or refreshes the design environment"*, which it does.
  · `detect_gaps` could not surface it. It finds Requirements nothing satisfies; **it cannot find a Requirement nobody wrote.**
  · Every gate was green and every gate was right.

⇒ **AN UNSTATED REQUIREMENT CANNOT BE UNMET.** That is the one class reflow2 is structurally blind to, and it produced a hole in the feature the whole tool exists for: the design record other people read.

📌 WHAT THE INSTALLER DID INSTEAD, which is why two users believed it worked: it DID export — `backup_graph` writes `.reflow2/backups/design-<stamp>.json` — and `git check-ignore` confirms that path is covered by the `.gitignore` rule THE SAME INSTALLER WRITES. **The output of the one export landed inside the ignore rule.** Everything looked present and nothing was reachable.

⚠️ AND THE PROTECTION THREAD WOULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT. `dec:idea-a-satisfied-requirement-earns-a-stricter-mutability-class` and `dec:idea-stability-is-earned-by-history-not-by-reaching-a-state` both protect what IS recorded — a satisfied requirement, an operational thread, a stable lifecycle. Alex's *"don't change core functionality"* is about DRIFT. This was ABSENCE from the first commit, so freezing, scoring or baselining would have left it exactly as open. **The measure this needs is different in kind, and confusing the two would build the wrong safeguard.**

WHAT THE REQUIREMENT IS, stated so it can be checked: after `reflow2_init.py` runs, the project contains a design export at a path git will track — `docs/design/<project>.json` — and the user is told, where they are looking, that this is the file to commit. It must hold on a BRAND-NEW project, which is the only case either user actually hit.

📌 EVIDENCE CLASS WORTH NOTING: both of Alex's reports (`fact:second-user-report-2026-08-11`, `fact:second-user-first-run-report-2026-08-13`) were found by somebody meeting the output for the first time, and neither was visible to anyone who already knew the system. That is now two data points for the same instrument.

properties.name: A claim about what the system IS carries when it was true, and is read back with its age
properties.statement: A statement about the system's CURRENT state must be recorded as a time-bounded assertion and surfaced with its age wherever it is read back, so it can go false. Prose written into a Requirement's `statement` has no expiry: it reads present-tense forever, no report flags it, and it is unfalsifiable by construction. The design already draws this line once — `dec:verification-freshness-not-a-gap` ruled that a check older than its code is a freshness FACT rather than a gap — and this is the same distinction one node type along: a claim about what the design SHOULD BE belongs in Requirement prose; a claim about what the system IS RIGHT NOW belongs in a TemporalFact, which keeps both states instead of overwriting. Reading a dated observation back to a person as settled doctrine upgrades it into a standing property that nobody chose.

properties.name: A Decision can state what it binds, and an unstated scope is visible rather than inferred
properties.statement:
A Decision can declare its SCOPE — node ids, a node type, a region, or free text — and where nobody stated one, the absence is explicit and readable rather than left to inference.

THE GAP THIS CLOSES. A Decision records WHAT was decided and WHY. It does not record WHAT IT APPLIES TO. Six weeks later the question is never "what did we decide" — it is "does that decision cover THIS?", and the node cannot answer.

THE VALUABLE HALF IS THE HONEST ABSENCE, not the field. "Nobody recorded a scope" is a different fact from "scope is everything" and from "scope is this one component", and today all three look identical. An unstated scope must be VISIBLE, not inferred — which is the same shape as the tri-state reflow2 already accepted for rule enforcement (dec:does-enforced-default-to-gate-blocking: a rule's power is stated, never defaulted) and as dec:certainty-derived's refusal to let a default assert what nobody chose.

EVIDENCE. A 2-of-3 ruling changed a trigger. Two documents were corrected; a third was found still teaching the old rule — and whether that third file was in scope had two defensible readings. The work stopped there, correctly. The stall was caused by a missing field, not by a hard question.

GENERALITY: this is not a multi-agent problem. A solo developer six months later faces the identical question about their own past decision, with no colleague to ask.

SOURCE: storyflow fleet governance report, api-boss (05af57c1), 2026-08-09, v0.26.1. Bound as stated by its author: one project, one month, one fleet shape — hypotheses to test, not requirements.

properties.name: A detector reads the properties that qualify its own finding, so recording something correctly never manufactures a defect
properties.statement:
A structural detector must consult the properties that change whether its finding IS a finding — on the edge and on both endpoints — so that modelling something the way the design prescribes never adds a defect.

THE OBSERVATION IS `fact:defect-recording-a-refutation-correctly-adds-a-structural-defect`; this is the intent behind fixing it.

THE ARGUMENT IS THE PROJECT'S OWN, ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN. `heal.rs` was fixed once for exactly this shape: reading the CONTRADICTS edge TYPE and never its `alignment` property meant "every correctly-modelled corroboration came back as a structural defect", and the comment ends "A PROPERTY THE DETECTOR IGNORES IS A PROPERTY THAT LIES." The same sentence applies one property across — the detector still never reads either endpoint's `status`, so a `rejected` Decision contradicting its successor is reported as a conflict when it is the healthy case.

⚠️ WHY THIS IS AN INCENTIVE PROBLEM AND NOT A NUISANCE: recording a refutation correctly ADDS a warning-severity defect, and burying it in prose adds none. The tool mildly penalises the discipline `rejected` exists to support, at the moment a seat is least likely to push back. The cheap wrong response is to delete the rejected node or the edge — the erasure the record exists to prevent.

MEASURED HERE: our four reported contradictions have no rejected or superseded endpoint today, so it does not fire — but the design holds 10 superseded and 1 rejected Decision and ZERO such edges, which is itself weak evidence that the relation is not being recorded.

WHAT MUST NOT BREAK: `acknowledge_defect` already handles this well — it stores the REASON rather than the suppression, and the review expires if the defect's shape changes because the id hashes the category with the affected set. Any fix must leave that intact.

NOT DECIDED: whether `superseded` and `rejected` are treated identically, and whether such pairs vanish or move to a separate band.

properties.name: A discipline that applies mid-task is delivered at the tool that triggers it, not from a catalogue read once at handshake
properties.statement:
SKILLS SPLIT INTO TWO KINDS AND THEY NEED DIFFERENT DELIVERY. A **task-skill** (genesis, adopt, capture-intent, governance-proposal, plan-increments) is reached for at a recognisable task boundary — the agent is STARTING something and asks what covers it. A **discipline-skill** (revise-design's snapshot-first, capture-intent's search-before-you-create, link-artifacts' hash-after) applies at an arbitrary instant INSIDE another task, when the agent is mid-flow and not asking anything.

THE CATALOGUE SERVES THE FIRST AND STRUCTURALLY CANNOT SERVE THE SECOND. `dec:skills-served` put the skill catalogue into the server instructions, which every client injects at handshake — deliberately, as "progressive disclosure rebuilt by hand", and it is the price of never being stale. It works: an agent that has read the catalogue reaches for the right task-skill. But a catalogue is read ONCE, and a discipline applies thousands of tokens later at a moment nothing announces. **The delivery mechanism and the trigger moment are mismatched, and no amount of restating the catalogue closes that gap.**

⭐ MEASURED ON THIS SESSION, which is the evidence rather than the theory (2026-08-09, `fact:which-skills-a-session-reached-for-and-why`): every skill used unprompted followed a task boundary the user had just created. Every skill MISSED was a discipline applying incidentally inside other work — two revisions made without loading revise-design, and two Contributors minted without the namespace search capture-intent prescribes. The snapshot discipline was followed ONLY because a consumer's report quoting it happened to be open in context. That is a near miss, not self-direction.

THE MECHANISM THAT ALREADY WORKS AND IS NOT APPLIED HERE: `loop_hint` rides on tool RESPONSES — `add_requirement` returns "when this capture batch lands, run detect_gaps" — and it demonstrably changes behaviour, because it arrives at the moment of the action rather than at the start of the session. The same carrier should name the discipline: a revising `create_node` saying "this is a revision; revise-design takes the snapshot FIRST, and after the edit it cannot be recreated"; `delete_node` / `delete_edge` likewise. This is `rule:bl-135`'s guardrail principle — state the FAILURE MODE, not the rule — applied to routing rather than to warnings, and that principle carries a blind trial behind it: an agent complied with those docstrings without knowing they were interventions.

⭐⭐ AND THE STRONGER FORM, WHICH DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE AGENT AT ALL. `dec:loop-status-state-not-history` holds that loop debt is computed from GRAPH STATE, never from run history. Apply the same rule to discipline: do not track whether a skill was INVOKED — compute whether its OUTCOME IS PRESENT. A node revised with no Snapshot at the current epoch is detectable from graph state alone, and that survives an agent which ignores every hint. dragon Boss (dev_storyflow) proposed the identical shape independently: "have delete_edge / a revising create_node report whether the target has a snapshot at the current epoch — NOT BLOCK, JUST SAY."

⚠️ THE ASYMMETRY THAT LIMITS THIS, stated so the requirement is not read as covering more than it can: a revision with no snapshot IS computable; a node created without a prior search is NOT — nothing distinguishes it from a node created after a search that found nothing. So discipline-skills split a second time. Those whose neglect leaves evidence get a detector; the rest can only ever get a hint, and a hint is what they get.

WHAT THIS MUST NOT BECOME: a blocking gate. A tool that blocks becomes a tool people route around, and then the graph stops matching reality — the one failure it cannot survive. And not another restatement in AGENTS.md: four skill-versus-tool drifts are already on record, and `req:a-rule-knows-where-else-it-is-written-down` exists because restatements rot.

RAISED BY ANTHONY, 2026-08-09: "continue to think how do we continue to improve the probability that an agent will use reflow2's skills and tools without being reminded."

properties.name: Evidence a value was fitted to cannot also count as that value's validation
properties.statement: When a value in the design was derived from a piece of evidence, the design must record what it was derived from, and must not let a check resting on that same evidence count as independent validation of it. Agreement with the anchor a value was fitted to is a fit, not a test, and must be reported as consumed. A capability whose only passing checks are consumed in this way must read as not independently verified. This cannot be computed from the strength of the evidence, only from its structure: no check internal to a design can establish its own independence, so the design must record the relation rather than attempt to detect the circularity.

properties.name: A hint that names a skill must name it as the next CALL, not as a parenthetical — a citation is read as attribution, not instruction
properties.statement:
Where reflow2 tells an agent which skill to use, it must phrase it as the call to make next rather than as a trailing reference. MEASURED, and this is the whole evidence: `add_capability` returned `loop_hint: "loop: wire satisfies to the requirement this serves, then run detect_gaps when the capture batch lands (detect-and-ask)"`. The agent that received it DID wire `satisfies` and DID run `detect_gaps` — and did NOT load `detect-and-ask`. The imperative clauses were obeyed; the skill name in parentheses was read as an attribution for where the advice came from, not as a step to take.

So the pointer already exists and already names the right skill — `cap:read-loop-hint` and the write-side `loop_hint` are both `verified` — and it still failed. That makes this cheaper than anything else in this family: the mechanism is built, delivered and correct, and only the wording is losing the effect. `run get_skill("detect-and-ask") first` is a step; `(detect-and-ask)` is a footnote.

SCOPE: every place reflow2 names a skill to an agent — the write tools' `loop_hint`, the read-side hint, `loop_nudge.py`'s Stop message, the SessionStart orientation, and the MCP server instructions. The rule is one line: if a skill is worth naming, name the call.

NOT PROPOSED: making the hints longer or more numerous. The finding is about grammar, not volume, and a hint that grows is a hint that gets skimmed — the failure `dec:read-hint-shape` already guarded against by firing only when the debt is real.

properties.name: A node can declare who may change it, so "what may I change alone?" is answerable from the graph rather than from prose
properties.statement:
A design node can carry a declared CHANGE POLICY — who may alter it, how many approvals it takes, and whether the approval must be recorded before or after the change. reflow2 REPORTS violations ("changed without the declared approval") and NEVER blocks the write.

THE GAP THIS CLOSES. reflow2 can say who AUTHORED a node — AUTHORED_BY carries role author/reviewer/approver — which is a record of what DID happen. It cannot say who MAY change it, which is a constraint on what MAY happen. Those are different facts and only the first is modelled.

WHY REPORTING AND NOT ENFORCING, which is the load-bearing half: a tool that blocks writes becomes a tool people route around, and then the graph stops matching reality — the one failure it cannot survive. Enforcement is itself a policy choice, so making it the mechanism would be reflow2 taking a position that belongs to the project. The value is that the boundary becomes QUERYABLE: "what may I change alone?" is the question every arriving session actually has, and today it can only be answered by reading prose that session may never read.

WHAT IT MUST NOT BECOME: roles, permissions, identity, or a review workflow. Just a declared constraint and a report of whether it held. Who someone IS stays the harness's problem; Contributor is enough.

GENERALITY, tested rather than assumed — the source applied the standard "could a solo hobbyist, a two-person team and a regulated enterprise each express THEIR policy with this, without reflow2 having an opinion about which is right?" Solo: nothing declared. Two people: "my areas and my brother's". Team: "two reviewers on a migration". Regulated: "QA sign-off, recorded, before release".

EVIDENCE, frequency rather than drama: one storyflow session hit "this is not mine to decide" FIVE times in a single sitting — a rule change needing multi-party agreement, an idea that must not be promoted to intent by anyone but its author, a gate-blocking flag that was the human's call, a shared file two other parties depended on, and a scope question about someone else's earlier ruling. Every one is this same missing primitive.

SOURCE: storyflow fleet governance report, api-boss (05af57c1), 2026-08-09, reflow2 v0.26.1, written to a deliberate MECHANISM-vs-POLICY frame at Anthony's request ("keep it generally applicable — give reflow2 the set of tools that can make most governance strategies possible"). Their own stated bound: one project, one month, one fleet shape, biased toward multi-agent operation — "treat the shapes as hypotheses worth testing against other projects, not as requirements."

properties.name: A write can tell it lost a race
properties.rationale: MEASURED, NOT SUPPOSED (fact:defect-write-response-describes-the-write-not-the-state): a deliberate experiment on the live 7-seat graph established that same-property concurrent writes are SILENT LAST-WRITER-WINS — no error, no warning, no version conflict, no indication a value was replaced — and, more sharply, that THE WRITE RESPONSE DESCRIBES THE WRITE RATHER THAN THE STATE: a racer received a success payload reading `statement: RACER_ONE, priority: high` when both fields were already false in the store. There is no version, rev, etag or updated_at anywhere in the payload, so a client cannot detect that it lost and has no primitive to compare-and-swap with. WHY THIS IS SHARPER THAN IT LOOKS: on a solo graph response == state, so trusting your own write-response is free, and every habit formed under the old stdio transport does exactly that. A session that writes a value and later reasons from its own return value is reasoning from something that was never durable — and nothing tells it. THE REPORTER EXPLICITLY DID NOT ASK FOR ENFORCEMENT: even an unenforced rev, merely RETURNED, lets a caller notice it was superseded, and that is most of the value. WHAT THIS MUST NOT COST, from the same experiment: per-property merge held under concurrency (a partial write EDITS and does not reset omitted fields) and concurrent writes serialize cleanly with both racers' distinct properties surviving. The reporter calls per-property merge the single most important safety property for a shared graph and lists it under what-not-to-change.
properties.statement: A node SHALL carry a monotonic revision returned on read and on write, and writes SHOULD accept an optional if_rev precondition — so a client can detect that its value was superseded. At minimum, a write response SHALL say when the node was also written by another seat since the caller's read. Requested as the #4 fleet ask by dev_storyflow's api-boss 5d608b85, 2026-08-07.

properties.name: A design records how its project actually ships
properties.statement:
A design that has Releases shall also record the ordered procedure for producing one — the steps, their order, and the external conventions they depend on — so that cutting a release is read from the design rather than reconstructed from what was done last time.

ANTHONY'S WORDS, 2026-07-31, raised while watching the v0.19.0 cut: "should every reflow2 project have a requirement to describe its 'release instructions'? ... having a set of release instructions (what are all the steps that need to occur) would be nice. Then the agent doesn't have to look at what was done previously to release or whether it was released on pypi or whatever makes sense for the project being developed."

THE VOCABULARY ALREADY EXISTS AND SHOULD BE USED RATHER THAN EXTENDED. A release procedure is an ordered process, which is what Flow models: add_flow, part_of_flow with step_order, TRIGGERS transitions carrying a role, read back by flow_report. This wants no new node type and no new document.

WHY THIS IS NOT dec:orientation-is-computed-not-written IN REVERSE. That decision refused a START-HERE file because orientation is DERIVABLE — a projection of design state, so the answer was build the view. Release steps are NOT derivable from the graph: which registry (PyPI / crates.io / GitHub releases / a manufactured build), which workflow, which credential, what the tag format is, which files carry a version claim. These are facts about the world outside the design, and no projection can compute them. The same derivability test therefore argues FOR recording them. That distinction is the load-bearing part of this requirement: record what cannot be computed, compute what can.

EVIDENCE, from the v0.19.0 cut itself. The procedure was reconstructed from `git show v0.18.0` plus grepping AGENTS.md for "release" — seven steps that exist nowhere as a list: the version in three files plus the lockfile; the CHANGELOG heading plus a fresh empty Unreleased; an upgrade doc REQUIRED IF AND ONLY IF the schema stamp moved; version claims in docs/overview.md and AGENTS.md; the graph manifest, release epoch and prior-release retirement; export exactly once onto the committed file; tag and push. At least two of those are unguessable and were discoverable only by reading a past commit message.

WHERE IT BITES AS A DETECTOR: a Project holding Release nodes with no release Flow is a gap worth surfacing, the same shape as unrealized_capability. Scope deliberately unsettled here — whether this is a reflow2-wide obligation on every governed design or advice the genesis/adopt skills ask for is Anthony's call, not this requirement's.

PROPOSED — captured in his wording, not yet his signature.

properties.name: A gap put to the user arrives with the agent's recommendation — recommending is not deciding
properties.statement:
When reflow2 puts a gap to the user, the agent's READING of it travels with the question: what it would do and why, and what would change that answer. The user still decides; the agent stops pretending it has no view.

THE READING HAS A SHAPE, AND THE SHAPE IS PART OF THE REQUIREMENT — added 2026-07-31 on Anthony's word after the pattern was used on him for the five standing gaps: "I really like when I say something like 'go through the decisions I need to make... put them in plain and simple english and offer a recommendation' and then you give me the options to select with your recommended choice on top. I believe there is already a proposed idea... but I really like this process (I think other users will really like this process also), so I'd either like to update the proposed req or cap or backlog item to CEMENT THIS BEHAVIOR."

Three obligations, and they are separable:

(1) THE OPTIONS ARE SELECTABLE, not buried in prose. The user picks rather than composing a reply. Prose that describes three courses of action still leaves them to name one; a list they can choose from does not.

(2) THE RECOMMENDATION COMES FIRST and is marked as such. Position carries meaning: an unordered menu makes the user infer which the agent favours, which is the analysis req:no-se-knowledge exists to spare them. Marking it also makes an overrule VISIBLE — the user knows they are departing from the agent's view, which is the precondition for the finding below.

(3) EVERY OPTION STILL CARRIES ITS CONSEQUENCE, including the ones not recommended. A list of bare labels is worse than prose, because it looks complete while withholding what each choice costs. The counterweight rule below is not relaxed by the format; it is what makes the format honest.

AND THE LANGUAGE IS THE USER'S, NOT ENGLISH — Anthony, same exchange: "with agents able to understand multiple languages, the 'simple english' should be 'simple whatever_language_user_is_writing_in'." The plainness obligation is about REGISTER, not about English: no jargon, no ids, short sentences, in whatever language the user is writing in. cap:surface already says "in the user's WORDS", and this makes the wider reading explicit so nobody implements it as an English-only rule. Every English-language phrasing in these design notes is an example of the register, never a specification of the language.

WHAT IS MISSING TODAY, and it is an omission rather than a prohibition. `detect-and-ask` is explicit that the agent must "never invent an answer on their behalf", which is right and must not be weakened. But the skill says nothing about offering a reading, so the default behaviour is a bare question — `gap_to_prompt` returns "is it covered, deferred, or dropped?" and the agent relays it. `cap:surface` ("turn a gap into a question in the user's words", `verified`) delivers the translation and nothing more.

WHY THAT IS A DEFECT AND NOT NEUTRALITY. `req:no-se-knowledge` says the user never needs systems engineering. A bare gap question hands them back the analysis the agent has already done and asks them to redo it in their own head — which is precisely the SE work that requirement exists to spare them. The agent has read the graph, seen the precedents, and formed a view; withholding it is not impartiality, it is making the user pay for the agent's caution.

IT IS ALSO WHAT `dec:three-party-checks` ALREADY DESCRIBES: "The LLM speaks, the graph remembers and counts, the human decides." Offering a reading IS the LLM speaking. The decision stays with the human, untouched — and `dec:certainty-derived` still governs the write, because a recommendation changes no status until the user answers.

THE LINE THAT MUST NOT BE CROSSED, stated so this cannot be read as licence. Recommending is not deciding: no requirement moves off `proposed`, no decision reaches `accepted`, no gap is acknowledged on a reading the user has not confirmed. And a recommendation must carry WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT — the condition under which the other option wins — or it is steering rather than advising.
