An option presented without its counterweight is a decision taken quietly.

THE PART WORTH RECORDING, and the reason this is design rather than style: WHEN THE USER OVERRULES A RECOMMENDATION, THAT IS INFORMATION. A design where the agent advised one way and the human chose another has learned something neither party knew alone, and today it is invisible because the recommendation was never on the record. Whether the recommendation itself should be stored beside the question is left open here rather than assumed. NOTE that obligation (2) sharpens this: marking the recommendation is what makes an overrule an identifiable EVENT rather than an unremarkable choice among equals.

MEASURED, not theorised: every gap put to Anthony on 2026-07-31 needed the recommendation added by hand, and he asked for it explicitly TWICE that day — "provide your recommendation", "present them in simple english and your recommendations for how to proceed" — and a THIRD time in the same session, at which point he asked for the behaviour to be cemented rather than repeated. A shape a user has to request each time is a default in the wrong place. This requirement's own evidence therefore accumulated by the exact mechanism it describes.

SCOPE, stated because the third request widened it: this began as a rule about GAPS, and Anthony's framing — "the decisions I need to make" — is broader. The obligation is read as covering any point where the agent puts a CHOICE to the user, not only where detect_gaps produced it. Whether that widening needs its own capability rather than riding this one is left open rather than assumed.

TENSION NAMED SO IT IS NOT CONFLATED: `dec:report-dont-judge` says the confirmation ledger reports claim history and never judges a claim. That governs what a COMPUTATION may assert about evidence. It does not govern whether an agent may advise a human who asked — different actor, different act. Conflating the two would silence exactly the party `dec:three-party-checks` puts there to speak.

properties.name: A recorded risk reaches someone — RISKS is a finding source, not an edge only propagation can see
properties.statement:
A RISKS edge is surfaced by the routine calls people actually make — `loop_status` reporting recorded risks to what you own, and `detect_gaps(scope=…)` including risks that terminate inside the region — rather than being reachable only by someone who already suspects a change and asks for its blast radius.

THE EVIDENCE IS A SUCCESS STORY WEARING A FAILURE'S CLOTHES, which is why it is worth a primitive. In storyflow, `cap:fleet_step_reset` --RISKS--> `req:fleet_no_idle_worker` was recorded in advance, verified in the committed export. Hours later that exact causal chain ran: the user reset seats, the reset seats were invisible to every boss because a roster row is the product of a WRITE and an arriving seat has not written, a boss measured an empty pool and staffed nobody, and workers idled while a boss with lanes stood by. Somebody modelled their own incident correctly and in advance — AND IT REACHED NO ONE. `loop_status` never mentions RISKS. `detect_gaps` scoped to the owning component returned 12 gaps and this was not among them, because RISKS is not a gap source. Writing it down was never the hard part.

MEASURED IN REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN, 2026-08-09: ONE RISKS edge in 7,097. And the source tells the rest — `RISKS` appears in exactly one place in the entire codebase, `crates/reflow2-core/src/propagate.rs:34`, inside a `RISK_EDGES` constant. It is therefore reachable ONLY through `propagate_change`, which a caller reaches by already knowing something changed. No detector, no gap source, no report. `BLOCKS` (2 edges) and `MASKS` (0) sit in the same constant and have the same problem.

⭐ THIS SHARPENS AN OPEN QUESTION RATHER THAN DUPLICATING IT. dec:idea-detect-vocabulary-that-nothing-reaches counts an edge type as REACHED if it is instantiated, named in the propagation table, or named anywhere in non-test Rust. RISKS PASSES THAT TEST AND IS STILL WRITE-ONLY. So the census as specified would clear it, and a second test is needed: not "is this vocabulary named in code" but "can a reader who does not already know about it ever be shown it". Declared-versus-code and code-versus-retrieval are different failures, and only the first is currently modelled.

THE COUNTER-DISCIPLINE, recorded because it is part of the proposal rather than an objection to it: two edges in a whole graph means the type is effectively unused, so surfacing it will not be noisy. If it later becomes noisy, the answer is to require an assessment date on the edge — not to stop reporting.

SOURCE: storyflow gap A of the peer set — found by storybug Boss (47accf78), filed by api-boss (05af57c1), 2026-08-09, v0.26.1.

properties.name: A refusal names what would have worked — a rejected argument comes back with its legal values, not just a verdict
properties.statement:
WHEN A SERVED TOOL REFUSES AN ARGUMENT BECAUSE IT IS NOT ONE OF A FIXED SET, THE REFUSAL NAMES THE SET. The caller should not have to make a second call to learn what would have worked.

THE GAP THIS CLOSES. `parse_enum` — the single helper every enum argument on the served surface passes through — refused with `unknown change type: "correction"` and nothing else. No enumeration, no nearest match, no pointer to `describe_schema`. The caller is usually an AGENT MID-TASK, for whom a refusal that does not say what would have worked costs a whole round trip and a context switch into schema reading.

⭐ THE VALUES WERE NEVER UNAVAILABLE, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES THIS A DEFECT RATHER THAN A FEATURE REQUEST. serde already builds `unknown variant `correction`, expected one of `requirement_creep`, `new_feature`, …` and the helper was DISCARDING it with `map_err(|_| …)`. The answer was constructed and thrown away on every rejection.

WHY THE FIX BELONGS IN THE SHARED HELPER, not at the call site that was reported: a hand-maintained list per tool rots the first time a variant is added, and one function serves every enum argument reflow2 exposes. Fixing it there means every refusal gains the list at once — which is what the reporter meant by \"this alone kills three of the eight\".

EVIDENCE. Filed by dev_storyflow 2026-08-03 (api-boss): \"enum rejections should list the legal values… this alone kills three of the eight.\" RE-CONFIRMED STILL LIVE 2026-08-09 by dragon Boss (`cca98fbf`), who recorded the cost precisely: \"one wasted call, then describe_schema{node_type: ChangeEvent, required_only: true} to learn the 11 legal values.\" And reproduced a third time the same day by a session in THIS repo while recording a correction — which is how it came to be fixed.

WHAT THIS REQUIREMENT DOES NOT SAY, so the scope is not read wider than it is: it does not ask for fuzzy nearest-match suggestions, and it does not ask that every refusal of any kind enumerate an alternative — only that a CLOSED SET, which the surface already knows, is stated rather than withheld. Where the message shape is unrecognised, the honest fallback is the underlying error's own words rather than a silent return to the bare verdict.

⚠️ A SEPARATE AND UNRESOLVED HALF, recorded here so it is not mistaken for closed: dragon Boss's second point was that NONE of the eleven legal `change_type` values means \"the record was WRONG about reality\". `resync` connotes reality moving and the design catching up. Adding a value would move the schema stamp and is Anthony's call; this requirement is only about the refusal being useful, not about the vocabulary being complete.

properties.name: A repair suggestion never proposes fabricating a relationship — where no honest fix exists, the finding says so
properties.statement:
A HEAL suggestion must not propose creating a link that does not exist. Where a finding has no honest mechanical repair, the finding is reported WITHOUT a `suggested_fix_type` that would manufacture one, and says plainly that the repair is a judgement rather than an operation.

THE CONCRETE CASE. `disconnected_community` reports a cluster with `suggested_fix_type: generate_bridge` — create edges to connect it. Where the separation is CORRECT, acting on that suggestion fabricates relationships that do not exist, in order to silence a warning about a separation that is right. In dev_storyflow's words: \"acting on the suggestion would fabricate relationships that do not exist, to silence a warning about a separation that is correct. That is manufacturing connectivity, and it is the same act as formatting coverage into existence — WITH THE DIFFERENCE THAT HERE THE TOOL PROPOSES IT.\"

⭐ WHY THIS SHIPS FIRST AND ALONE. Anthony, 2026-08-09, settling `dec:legitimate-islands-need-the-detector-fix`: \"C now, A next with the read-back, not B, not D.\" This half is a LIVE HAZARD and is true whether or not partitions ever become declarable — a tool that proposes corrupting the graph is wrong on its own terms. It needs no schema change, so it does not wait for the schema increment that `req:a-cluster-can-be-declared-deliberately-separate` belongs to.

THE GENERAL PRINCIPLE, which is what makes this a requirement rather than a one-line patch: reflow2 already refuses to let a check be attached in order to close a finding (the governance-proposal skill's standing warning against green-washing), and `dec:ask-not-repair` already holds that suspected duplicates are ASKED, never merged. THE SAME RULE HAS NOT BEEN APPLIED TO REPAIR SUGGESTIONS. A proposal to write a false edge is the mirror image of a passing check that tests nothing: both make a report go quiet without making anything true.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY: it does not ask `disconnected_community` to stop firing, and it does not ask HEAL to stop proposing repairs generally. Mechanical repairs that restore a fact the design already holds remain correct. The line is narrow and it is about INVENTION: a suggestion may reorganise or restore, never assert a relationship nobody stated.

⚠️ RELATED AND SEPARATE, so the two are not conflated: `fact:apply-heal-would-have-destroyed-the-wrong-contributor` records a different HEAL failure found the same day — a merge proposal that named the wrong survivor and DISCLOSED its own arbitrariness (\"THE ALPHABET CHOSE THE VICTIM\"). That one is about which node a correct operation destroys; this one is about an operation that should not be offered at all.

SOURCE: storyflow gap D of the peer set — raised by storybug Boss (47accf78), characterised and filed by api-boss (05af57c1), 2026-08-09, v0.26.1. Reproduced in this design the same day at 5 nodes and again at 7.

properties.name: A report says what it swept and whether its checks were exercised, so a zero cannot be mistaken for a pass
properties.statement:
A report that contributes no findings must say whether it was EXERCISED AND FOUND NOTHING or HAD NOTHING TO EXAMINE, and must describe the scope it actually covered rather than a narrower one it was never given.

DISTINCT FROM THE FACT THE GUARD NAMED, and the distinction is the whole point of this increment: `fact:defect-propose-heal-describes-neither-what-it-swept-nor-what-it-considered` is the OBSERVATION — what was measured, on which day, by whom. This is the INTENT — what must be true. The plan-increments skill requires that separation before anything can be scheduled: "an item scheduled but never captured is a promise with no requirement behind it." A TemporalFact cannot be scheduled; a Requirement can.

THE THEME IS ALREADY ACCEPTED DOCTRINE rather than a new idea: `chg:a-null-and-a-vacuous-zero-now-say-which-they-are` gave scoped `detect_gaps` exactly this treatment, and dev_storyflow's dragon Boss independently named it a WIN — "flags its own vacuous zeros". This generalises what that change did in one place.

WHAT IT COVERS TODAY, both halves reproduced on reflow2's own graph: `propose_heal` returns `operations: []` with no way to tell a scorer that RAN from one with NO INPUT — measured here, where `detect_defects` reports 16 defects and duplicate-class ZERO, so our own zero is vacuous by the identical mechanism; and it returns a `target_id` naming one Project the caller never chose while sweeping the whole design.

⚠️ THE STAKE IS NOT TIDINESS: a fleet runs `propose_heal` as the read-only evidence step of a standing stop on `apply_heal`, which DELETES NODES. A vacuous zero there is one skim away from lifting a gate on an irreversible operation. That is why this theme is first.

NOT IN SCOPE: whether every reporting tool needs this or only those whose zero is read as permission. `propose_heal` is the measured case.

properties.name: A rule the project follows is recorded with its consequence stated, and a violation is computed rather than remembered
properties.statement:
A project's own conventions — how it merges, who may sign off, what the build refuses — are part of its design and must be recordable as design, with the CONSEQUENCE of breaking each one stated by the person whose project it is. A rule whose power over the build was never chosen by anybody is not a rule the design can act on.

⚠️ STATUS: `proposed`, and it stays there until Anthony has read these words. He chose the SHAPE on 2026-08-11 — "a new requirement, mirroring KPPs" — when asked what need `cap:governance-proposal` serves (question:3f04e352bc497c5b). The wording below is an agent's draft of that shape, not his sentence, and `rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word` is the reason the distinction is being made explicitly rather than quietly resolved in the agent's favour.

THE SHAPE, deliberately mirroring `req:inviolable-intent` one layer along. That requirement says intent that must hold no matter what is recorded as inviolable, and a violation is COMPUTED, not remembered; `cap:kpp-proposal` is the capture half that asks the user whether something is a KPP rather than deciding for them. This is the same sentence about RULES rather than about intent, and `cap:governance-proposal` is its capture half. The parallel is the argument: a project's policy deserves the same treatment as its performance parameters, because both are things a person committed to and neither survives as prose.

WHAT IT REQUIRES, in three parts:
  (1) A rule is recordable as a design object rather than as a paragraph in a markdown file nobody diffs.
  (2) Its CONSEQUENCE — gate-blocking, advisory, or unstated — is the user's to state, never inherited. `DesignRule.enforced` is now genuinely three-state (schema/core.yaml:127, "Never defaulted"), so absence reads as "nobody has said" instead of as a choice.
  (3) A rule declared gate-blocking OWES a detector, and the debt is computed. That is `unverified_enforced_rule` at 0.6, and it is the part that stops governance-in-graph being prettier prose.

WHERE IT CAME FROM, recorded because this requirement exists partly BECAUSE that trace was missing. The demand signal is the GOVERNANCE-AS-DESIGN entry in dev_storyflow's `reflow2_feedback.md`, filed by api-boss (`5d608b85`) on 2026-08-08, carrying Anthony's own framing: "every project will be managed differently and have differing sets of people running it with their own practices and policies about merging and who can merge and other governing mechanisms — but allowing reflow2 to setup a generic set of nodes/edges that allow a user or set of users to define their own project management policies/governance in graph form is something that I think would be really helpful. additionally, by putting in graph form, you can start seeing issues and gaps in their policies (like we are experiencing in storyflow) and help resolve them properly."

⭐ WHY IT IS BEING WRITTEN NOW, MONTHS AFTER THE WORK SHIPPED. `cap:governance-proposal` was built, realized by `art:governance-proposal-skill`, and served to sessions while satisfying no requirement at all — surfaced as gap:3f04e352bc497c5b (unmotivated_capability, 0.55) and put to Anthony on 2026-08-11. Six sibling requirements from the same feedback entry DO exist and carry AUTHORED_BY to `who:storyflow-api-boss`; this one was the gap in that capture, not the whole of it. The honest reading is that the process ran and missed a step, not that the work was unrequested.

WHY NOT `req:defaults-do-not-assert`, considered and declined on 2026-08-11 by Anthony. That requirement names `DesignRule.enforced` explicitly and predates this skill by six weeks, so it is a genuine historical driver rather than a retro-fit. It was declined as the parent because it covers TEN defaulted-and-unread properties of which this addresses one, and because the default-asserting half has since been fixed in the schema — so a SATISFIES edge would make a tenth of that work read as delivered while nine properties stay untouched. It remains at `proposed` with nothing satisfying it.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY. It does not require any rule to be enforced — advisory is a first-class answer and six of reflow2's nine rules are advisory by the owner's explicit choice. It does not require every convention to be captured. And it says nothing about WHO may state a rule's consequence; that is `req:a-node-can-say-who-may-change-it`, still `proposed`.

HONEST BOUND: the capture half only helps a session that invokes the skill. A rule recorded by an agent that never loads `governance-proposal` still lands with `enforced` unstated — which is now reported rather than asserted, so the failure is visible, but it is not prevented.

properties.name: A rule knows where it is authoritatively stated and where else it is repeated, so an amendment can find its own stale copies
properties.statement:
A rule can name the artifact that AUTHORITATIVELY states it, and the artifacts that merely REPEAT it — and a report answers "if I change this rule, what documents claim to state it?"

THE GAP THIS CLOSES. A rule that lives in the graph is usually also written in a README, an onboarding doc, a code comment, a CI config. Amending the graph does not tell you where else the old wording lives, and a stale restatement does not lag quietly — it keeps issuing the superseded instruction to whoever reads it. `DesignRule` today has name, statement, category and enforced, and NOWHERE to put the source of record; the storyflow trial ended up writing "Source of record: PROTOCOL.md" into the free-text statement of all eight of its rules, putting the property that most needs to be queryable into prose no detector can read.

WHAT THE EDGE MAKES POSSIBLE, and this is the argument for modelling it rather than adding a string property: a rule with TWO authoritative sources is a duplication risk; a rule with NONE is folklore; an artifact that changed since the rule was recorded is a rot candidate. None of those three questions can be asked today. reflow2 already has DOCUMENTS — "this file describes that node"; what is missing is its inverse in spirit — "this file REPEATS that node's content and will go stale when it changes."

EVIDENCE. One rule existed in FIVE places. A correct amendment fixed the two a MACHINE reads and missed the three that bind HUMANS — for two days, during which the stale copies were ordering work the ruling had explicitly removed. Nobody was careless: there was no way to ask "where else is this stated?"

THE HARD HALF IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED. Detecting a CONTRADICTION between a rule and its restatement defeats every keyword method, because both copies contain the same words. reflow2 should not pretend to do it. LISTING the restatements would have prevented the incident on its own — the graph supplies the list, the human eye does the comparison.

ADJACENT SCHEMA FINDING, recorded because it is the same neglect: `describe_schema` reports that NO edge type models DesignRule → Component either. Both GOVERNED_BY and CONSTRAINS accept the pair only through a `*` wildcard. DesignRule is the least-connected type in the schema — odd for the one whose whole job is to bind other things, and precisely the catch-up debt dec:governance-integrates-not-splits names.

SOURCE: storyflow fleet governance report, api-boss (05af57c1), 2026-08-09, v0.26.1. Bound as stated by its author: one project, one month, one fleet shape — hypotheses to test, not requirements.

properties.name: A rule says whether a check is even possible, so "no detector" splits into debt and accepted limit
properties.statement:
A rule or requirement can declare its VERIFIABILITY — detectable / detectable-but-unwritten / undetectable-by-nature, with a required reason for the last — so that "which of my rules have no check?" splits into a backlog and a set of accepted limits, and only the first is debt.

THE GAP THIS CLOSES. "No check is possible" and "no check yet" are OPPOSITE states that read identically today. Both surface as "unverified". A rule about INTENT — "do not shape data to satisfy a tool" — has no detectable signature by construction, because the compliant and non-compliant artefacts are byte-identical. A rule about a file layout is merely unwritten. Reporting them the same way makes the report untrustworthy: a reader cannot tell a permanent limit from a to-do.

REFLOW2 HAS ALREADY SOLVED THIS EXACT SHAPE ONCE, one domain over, which is the strongest argument that the distinction is real and not a special case. `granularity` distinguishes `opaque` — a subtree claimed as a unit ON PURPOSE — from `pending_expansion` — a PLACEHOLDER for work not done — and reflow2's own tool documentation says they "look identical to every report today and are opposite states: a decision versus unfinished work." The same distinction is missing for verifiability. It is also the same principle as dec:does-enforced-default-to-gate-blocking, where a rule's power is stated rather than defaulted.

WHY IT MATTERS TO THE REPORT AND NOT ONLY TO THE RECORD. Of nine rules recorded in the storyflow trial, two got checks, one was detectable-but-unwritten, and THREE were undetectable by construction. Filing those three as unverified debt would misreport a third of the set forever — and a permanent red nobody can clear is how a report loses its readers.

RELATED, AND THE REASON THIS IS URGENT RATHER THAN TIDY: `unverified_enforced_rule` already fires today on `enforced: true` with no incoming VERIFIES, and rule:bl-41 is currently caught by it. Without this distinction that detector cannot tell a rule that is waiting for a detector from one that can never have one.

SOURCE: storyflow fleet governance report, api-boss (05af57c1), 2026-08-09, v0.26.1. Bound as stated by its author: one project, one month, one fleet shape — hypotheses to test, not requirements.

properties.name: A rule states the scope it binds in, and a conflict between two rules is surfaced — because a rule conflict selects against the careful
properties.statement:
A rule states the SCOPE it applies in, so a reader can tell whether it binds them; and where two rules cannot both be satisfied, that conflict is surfaced by the design rather than discovered by whoever loses work to it.

⭐ THE GENERAL FINDING, and it is not about export: WHEN TWO SAFETY RULES CONFLICT, THE PARTICIPANT WHO REASONS MOST CAREFULLY ABOUT THE CONFLICT IS THE ONE WHO DOES NOTHING — and doing nothing is often the destructive option. A conflict between two safety rules is not neutral; IT SELECTS AGAINST THE CAREFUL. That is the mechanism this requirement exists to break, and it generalises far past the case that exposed it.

THE CASE. Two rules, both correct in isolation: any session that changed the design EXPORTS BEFORE STANDING DOWN (durability), versus the export is produced ONCE PER PULL REQUEST, LAST OF ALL, because two exporting commits on one branch break the lineage chain silently (integrity — dec:export-once-per-pr here). On a shared branch with several writers, BOTH CANNOT BE SATISFIED. A storyflow boss wrote two Requirements, one Contributor and two edges, then reported: "I am NOT exporting, because I will not risk the lineage chain on a guess — and the cost of that correct-looking caution is that my writes exist in one untracked RocksDB directory on this host and nowhere else," which is precisely what the durability rule exists to prevent. Another session exported four times the same day. NEITHER BEHAVIOUR IS WRONG UNDER THE RULES AS WRITTEN.

REPRODUCED HERE THE SAME DAY, and by the careful route: this session declined to export after recording dec:governance-integrates-not-splits and four requirements, because PR #132 was open and dec:export-once-per-pr applied. The design's own answer to the tension was to leave a session's work unexported — the identical outcome, arrived at by the identical reasoning, in the project that authors the rule.

WHAT IS MISSING, in two parts. FIRST, SCOPE: the lineage warning does not say whether it is branch-local or any-branch, so a reader cannot tell whether it applies to them. This is the same missing field as req:a-decision-states-what-it-binds, one node type over — and where a single-writer discipline is required on shared state, reflow2 should be able to SAY so rather than leaving each project to find out by having someone lose work. SECOND, DETECTION: reflow2 surfaces a contradiction only where a human has already drawn a CONTRADICTS edge — two of this design's five current structural defects are exactly that. Nothing DISCOVERS a conflict between two rules nobody suspected, which is the only case that matters, because a suspected conflict is one somebody is already handling.

FILED AS A REFLOW2 SEMANTICS GAP, NOT A PROJECT ONE, in the reporter's words: a project may rule its own cadence, but it should not have to discover the conflict first.

SOURCE: storyflow gap C of the peer set — storybug Boss (47accf78), filed 2026-08-09, v0.26.1.

properties.name: A seat learns the shared record moved when it ORIENTS, not when it writes
properties.statement:
When another contributor's work has arrived in the shared design record and this graph has never seen it, the seat is told so at the point it orients itself — not at the point it tries to write, hours later.

WHY THE MOMENT IS THE REQUIREMENT AND NOT AN ERGONOMIC PREFERENCE: the signal already existed and was already correct. `provenance::last_synced` was maintained by both the export and import paths, and `sync::assess_overwrite` already turned it into a three-way verdict. It was consulted in exactly one place — inside `export_graph`. So the design knew at the first moment of a session and spoke at the last, by which point the session had done its work against a record it did not know had moved.

WHAT SATISFYING THIS MUST NOT COST: silence during ordinary work. A seat that is merely AHEAD of the record — unexported work in progress — is the normal state of every working session and must never be reported, or the signal is ignored inside a week. The distinguishing test is whether the RECORD moved, not whether the two differ.

AND IT REPORTS RATHER THAN ACTS: taking the arrived work in is an upsert over live session state, so it stays the human's call.

⚠️ WORDING IS AN AGENT'S DRAFT. Anthony chose the MECHANISM (option A, 2026-08-11) and directed the build; he has not ruled on this statement's text, which is why this sits at `proposed`.

properties.name: A payload says whether the session reading it is alone on the graph
properties.rationale: THE ROOT CAUSE BEHIND EVERY SHARED-GRAPH FAILURE THEY REPORTED, in their words: A SESSION CANNOT TELL THAT IT IS NOT ALONE. Nothing in any payload reports concurrency, so every seat reasons as if solo and the output actively encourages it. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE (fact:defect-rollups-became-fleet-numbers-without-saying-so): defects 42->6->5->12 and gaps 48->55->69 on one graph in one day by non-coordinating sessions, including a 5->12 jump delivered to a session that had done nothing; TWO BOSSES, one of them the reporter, attributed a global movement to their own change — in the flattering direction, which is the one nobody catches unaided. The reporter told the user '42 -> 6' twice as their own result. It was not. Their argument for this specific field: a seat seeing `attached: 7` CANNOT HONESTLY CLAIM A ROLLUP AS ITS OWN, so one number prevents the whole class. The alternative in force today is a hand-maintained fleet convention requiring every citation to be labelled FLEET or SCOPED — a discipline layered on a tool that could just say it, and by their own standard a defect routed around rather than fixed. NOTE THE MIGRATION HAZARD THIS ALSO NAMES: loop_status and graph_report read IDENTICALLY before and after `--shared`; only the MEANING changed, so every citation of those counts written before the migration is now subtly wrong and nothing says so.
properties.statement: Tool responses that report graph-wide state SHALL make concurrency visible — at minimum the number of currently-attached sessions, and ideally last_write_at and last_write_by — and rollups SHALL label themselves as graph-wide rather than leaving scope to the reader. Requested as the #2 fleet ask and as the single 'if only one thing changes' item by dev_storyflow's api-boss 5d608b85, 2026-08-07.

properties.name: A session bound to one design cannot read or write any other design in the same process — and this must be proven before multi-graph hosting ships
properties.statement:
When one process holds several design graphs (dec:one-process-many-stores, accepted 2026-08-06), a client session attached to design X must not be able to read or write design Y through any tool on the surface — not by passing a graph_id it was not attached to, not by a path, not by reconnecting, and not by a handler that resolves the wrong entry from the registry.

THIS IS THE SHIPPING CONDITION, not a nice-to-have. Anthony accepted dec:one-process-many-stores on 2026-08-06 conditional on exactly this: the isolation guarantee carried as its own requirement, with a check, landing BEFORE any of the multi-graph work ships. The reason is the failure mode rather than the principle — an isolation regression does not error, it CORRUPTS: a handler that reaches the wrong graph writes one design's nodes into another, and nothing in the loop would report it because both graphs would still be internally coherent. That is strictly worse than a crash, and it is invisible to every detector reflow2 has.

THE SECOND HALF, and it must be stated rather than assumed: reflow2 HAS NO AUTHENTICATION OF ANY KIND. Whoever fronts a hosted reflow2 — flo2 today — owns authentication and authorization: deciding WHICH designs a given human may reach. reflow2's obligation is narrower and absolute: given that a session has been attached to design X by the layer in front, reflow2 must not let it touch design Y. Those two are not the same guarantee and neither substitutes for the other. If this split is not written down and held, accepting dec:one-process-many-stores quietly converts an accepted "no hosted service" into a hosted service with no security story — the drift dec:reopen-supersedes exists to prevent, and the counter-argument that decision's own rationale already records.

SCOPE NOTE: this says nothing about the single-graph case, which has this property today for free because the process holds exactly one store. The requirement exists because that free guarantee is what the registry removes.

properties.name: A session bound to one design cannot address another, and that is a security property rather than a tidiness one
properties.statement:
Raised by @ajs from flo2, 2026-08-05, as the single highest-risk part of multi-graph hosting. Today isolation between designs is a CONSEQUENCE OF PROCESS SEPARATION, and it is total — nothing in the code maintains it because nothing has to. The moment one process serves several designs, isolation becomes something the code must actively maintain: every tool handler must be unable to reach a graph other than its session's.

For flo2 this is a security property, not a tidiness one: project A's design must be unreachable from project B's session. It deserves its own tests, and property tests rather than examples, because the failure is silent and severe — a handler that reaches the wrong graph CORRUPTS a design rather than erroring, and no gap detector would ever notice.

WHERE THE OBLIGATION STOPS, and this must be stated plainly rather than assumed: reflow2 has NO AUTHENTICATION OF ANY KIND today. --http-allow-host is Host-header allowlisting, which is DNS-rebinding protection only. Authorization — deciding WHICH graph a given human may reach — is the job of the layer in front, which for flo2 is flo2's own. reflow2's obligation is only that a session bound to graph X cannot address graph Y. Recording both halves matters: if only the first is remembered, a hosted reflow2 ships believing it defends itself.

The mechanism this needs already exists and is already noted as unused: req:many-designs-one-service states that "segregation is enforced by the store, not by convention: every node and edge already carries a graph_id, which is exactly the primitive this needs, and today it is pinned to the constant reflow2 — so the mechanism exists and is unused." This requirement is what makes that segregation load-bearing rather than latent.

properties.name: A session can find out what designs exist nearby and be told which one to use, rather than inheriting one from where the shell happened to be
properties.statement:
Which design a session writes to must be a STATED CHOICE, and the information needed to make that choice must be available BEFORE anything is created. Two halves: (1) an agent must be able to discover what designs exist in and around a working tree and what each one holds — label, size, when it was minted — without opening a session against each; (2) a session must be able to be pointed at a chosen design explicitly.

ANTHONY, 2026-08-05, after the hxm_program field report: "can we just pass the location of the reflow2 graph via a prompt or skill; it can default to whichever folder path that the session is opened in, but maybe we could just say 'use reflow2 graph as /path/to/reflow2/graph/to/use/for/this/session'." And on the mechanism, once told a skill could not do it alone: "I like this approach of just pointing .mcp.json at the graph_id... an agent within a session can usually change files. can a reflow2 tool be to simply return all graph_ids to the agent and the agent then can choose whichever graph_id the user specifies to use for the project?"

WHY IT IS A REQUIREMENT AND NOT A CONVENIENCE. Today the answer is implicit: the launch config passes a RELATIVE `--graph-path`, so the design a session edits is decided by where the shell was opened, with no ancestor walk and no report of what else exists. Measured consequence, on Anthony's own repo the same day: a session at the root was told "this directory has no design yet" and minted a THIRD graph while two populated ones sat one and two directories down (`dec:no-design-here-never-looked`). An implicit answer to "which design am I editing" is not a smaller version of an explicit one — it is the mechanism by which a design gets created in the wrong place and nobody is told.

THE DIVISION OF LABOUR THIS INHERITS, and it shapes the answer rather than limiting it: reflow2 performs NO FILE IO (`dec:agent-navigates-content`), so WALKING THE TREE TO FIND `.reflow2` DIRECTORIES IS THE AGENT'S JOB — Anthony's own observation that "an agent within a session can usually change files" is the same point from the other side. What only reflow2 can answer is what a store at a given path actually HOLDS. So the requirement is met by a pair, not by one tool.

⚠️ MEASURED, AND IT CORRECTS THE OBVIOUS READING OF THE ASK: "return all graph_ids" would return ONE per store today. Storage keys are `{graph_id}\x00{type}\x00{id}` and `dynograph_storage::keys::graph_prefix` exists, so many graphs per store is supported by the FOUNDATION — but reflow2 opens one graph per store by convention (`DEFAULT_GRAPH_ID`, one `.reflow2` directory per project), and the three graphs in this field report are three separate STORES. Enumerating within a store is therefore true and not useful yet; describing a store found on disk is what the case actually needs.

HOW EACH HALF STANDS, 2026-08-05. HALF (1) — DISCOVERY — has an accepted shape and a planned capability: `dec:describe-a-design-without-binding-to-it` and `cap:describe-design-at-path`. HALF (2) — BEING POINTED — has a WORKING ANSWER IN THE FIELD but not a settled one: `dec:pointing-a-session-is-project-scope-only` (accepted, executed and verified on hxm_program) says a project-scoped config override does it TODAY, with the hard rule that an absolute path must never enter a global config. Whether that remains the answer, or a graph reference carried per call replaces it, is still open at `dec:how-a-session-is-pointed-at-a-design`.

⚠️ AND THE REASON THIS REQUIREMENT IS NOT ALREADY MET BY THE FIELD FIX: PROJECT SCOPE KEYS ON THE DIRECTORY THE SESSION WAS OPENED IN. An override on a project root does nothing for a session opened in a subdirectory — which is precisely the case that produced the extra graph. So the config override satisfies this requirement for sessions started at the root and NOT OTHERWISE, and the discovery half stays necessary rather than being made redundant by it.

ACCEPTED 2026-08-05 on Anthony's explicit word ("Let's take req:a-session-chooses-its-design from proposed to accepted"), given after both halves and the surviving limitation above were read back to him.

properties.name: An output says which question it answered, and what it could not see
properties.rationale: THE REPORTER OFFERED THIS AS THE ACTIONABLE GENERALISATION over three separate incidents in one day, each a REAL, CORRECT number that answered a different question than the reader's: (1) merge scores presented as a detection report while silently feeding an irreversible deletion — two competent sessions each held half of it and neither could see the whole, because the similarity surface and the delete-proposing surface NEITHER NAMES THE OTHER; (2) open_questions returning count: 0 while the loop owed 69 gaps, 26 defects and 40 unproven/unexamined claims — both numbers correct, neither saying so; (3) per-session rollups that silently became fleet-wide under --shared. In all three the fix is the same shape: LET THE OUTPUT STATE ITS OWN SCOPE. THE STRONGEST SINGLE INSTANCE, because six independent sessions reported it without consolidating (fact:defect-scoped-detectors-do-not-flag-a-degenerate-region): a scoped detector returning in_scope: 0 over region_size: 1 reads as a pass and is the opposite — an island, where the detector had one node to look at. One reporter caught it only by running a control on a sibling node to prove the measurement could return more at all. Notably, region_size being IN the payload is what three of them credited as working; the defect is purely that the interpretation is left to a reader who, under load, will skip it. THIS IS ALSO ALREADY REFLOW2 DOCTRINE, which is the strongest argument for building it: the served AGENTS.md says in terms that a successful tool response is a claim rather than a result, that '0 gaps' means nothing was detected and never that nothing is wrong, and instructs the agent to ask what a check could not have seen. This requirement is that rule moved from the reader's discipline into the payload — which is exactly the fleet's own repeated lesson that a discipline whose only evidence is that someone runs it disappears the moment they stop.
properties.statement: A reflow2 surface that returns a count SHALL state the scope of that count — what question it answered and what it does not cover — rather than leaving a correct number to be read as an answer to a different question. Generalised by dev_storyflow's api-boss 5d608b85 from three same-day cases, 2026-08-07, and independently converged on by six sessions for the degenerate-region case.

properties.name: The rule that a vocabulary distinction must be read by a computation is itself computed, not applied by hand
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-08-09: \"agree on taking forward dec:edge-orthogonality.\"

WHAT IS BEING TAKEN FORWARD. dec:edge-orthogonality is ACCEPTED and states the principle: a vocabulary distinction earns its keep ONLY IF A COMPUTATION READS IT. It was applied ONCE, by hand, retiring the VALIDATES and ENABLES edges on exactly that reasoning. Nothing has computed it since, so the principle has been true and unenforced ever since.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT MADE THE CASE, run 2026-08-09 against reflow2's own 1,873-node design. An edge type counts as REACHED if it is instantiated in this design, OR named in structural_rule's propagation table, OR named anywhere in non-test Rust outside its own const declaration:
  EIGHT OF SIXTY EDGE TYPES fail all three — COMPLIES_WITH, CONTAINS_EPOCH, EVOLVES_INTO, IMPOSES, MITIGATES, SUPERSEDES, SUPPLEMENTS, VIOLATES_RULE.
  SEVEN OF TWENTY-NINE NODE TYPES have zero instances — Anchor, DimensionAssessment, DimensionObservation, EnvironmentRule, Flow, QualityGate, ReadinessAssessment.
  FIVE MORE EDGE TYPES are instantiated but reached only generically: ABOUT_ENTITY (117 instances), CAUSES (9), INTERACTS_WITH (4), OPERATES_IN (3), VALID_TO (2).

⭐ THREE HAD INDEPENDENT COMPLAINTS FILED BY dev_storyflow HOURS EARLIER, which is what makes this a class rather than tidiness: VIOLATES_RULE is not offered by describe_schema for the pair its name describes, so a session doing the documented thing cannot discover it and used VIOLATES instead; QualityGate drew \"I could not find an honest use, and I think that is informative\"; Anchor is already open as dec:anchor-retire-or-implement.

WHY IT NEVER SURFACED, and it is the reason a computation is needed rather than more discipline: EVERY DETECTOR IS INSTANCE-LEVEL AND THIS IS A VOCABULARY-LEVEL FACT. unsatisfied_requirement needs a Requirement, disconnected_community needs a cluster of two or more, orphan_node needs a node. A declared type with ZERO instances produces nothing for any of them to anchor on. No detector asks a question about the SCHEMA rather than about the design, so the accumulation is invisible by construction.

WHAT THIS REQUIRES: that the principle be answerable by calling something, not by remembering to look. Declared-but-unreached vocabulary must be nameable on demand — which types, and on which of the three tests they failed — so that the next accumulation is visible when it happens rather than eight items later.

⚠️ WHAT IT MUST NOT BECOME, and this is load-bearing rather than a caveat. A demonstrator legitimately does not use Flow or ReadinessAssessment; a young design legitimately has empty node types. A finding that fires on a CONSUMER'S design for not using reflow2's whole vocabulary would nag correct work, which is the failure dec:read-hint-shape and the phase-nudge doctrine exist to prevent. The defensible subject is REFLOW2'S OWN SHIPPED VOCABULARY — a fixed 60 edges and 29 node types with code behind them or not — because that is a property of the build rather than of anybody's modelling.

AND IT MUST NOT REPEAT THE DEFECT IT DESCRIBES: whatever is built here has to be READ by something, or it becomes a ninth unreached thing. That is not a joke about the requirement; it is the specific failure mode, and it has already happened to `enforced` (unread until v0.26.0) and to both retirement edges (unread today).

MECHANISM DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN — dec:idea-detect-vocabulary-that-nothing-reaches records four shapes with their counters: a census report, a low-severity gap, a tools/ maintenance instrument like toolsnap, or prune-and-accept. Anthony agreed the principle should be carried forward; he has not chosen the shape, and dec:certainty-derived forbids recording that on his behalf.

BOUND, stated rather than glossed: the measurement covered ONE design. A type with zero instances here may be in daily use in dev_storyflow or flo2. The eight unreached-on-every-test EDGES are the stronger claim, because those have no code behind them anywhere and that is a fact about the shipped build.

properties.name: A write says what it did not recognise, so a caller can tell an extension from a typo
properties.statement:
A write that stores something the schema does not describe must SAY SO in its reply — without refusing it — so that an invented field and a deliberate extension stop being indistinguishable.

THE OBSERVATIONS ARE `fact:defect-an-undeclared-property-is-stored-without-complaint` and `fact:defect-a-property-naming-a-node-is-unguarded-while-edges-are-not`; this is the intent behind fixing them. They are ONE theme in two directions: an unknown property NAME going in, and a declared property holding a DANGLING node reference coming out.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES IT A REQUIREMENT: reflow2 already refuses an unknown TOOL ARGUMENT — `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` appears 134 times in the served surface — and refuses an EDGE to a missing node through all sixteen typed helpers, with atomicity and a size-floor test. The one hole is `props`, a free object, which is exactly where a property name lands. So the vocabulary is guarded at the type level and the edge level and open at the property level in both directions.

⚠️ THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT IS PART OF THE REQUIREMENT, NOT AN OBJECTION TO IT: the store is deliberately a property BAG, and open-world properties are what let a project record what reflow2 did not anticipate. So this must NOT become strict validation. The ask is a REPORT, not a refusal — hence the wording.

MEASURED: `enforcement: "advisory"` was accepted, stored and echoed back on a DesignRule whose schema declares no such property; the real field is `enforced`, a bool. The write succeeded and meant nothing, and only an unrelated gap firing exposed it.

CHEAPEST FORM, and probably sufficient: echo which stored properties the schema does not declare. One comparison, no policy change. Naming the nearest declared property is a second step — `enforcement` vs `enforced` is one edit distance, and the near-duplicate guard already does this kind of suggestion for ids.

properties.name: A body of intent accreted over years, contradicting itself and never built, can still become a design
properties.statement:
Where a person has written down what they want to build over a long period — documents, drawings, proposals, notes — and has built NOTHING, reflow2 must be able to turn that corpus into a real design. Anthony, 2026-08-04: "a daydreamer may just document thoughts (maybe over years about some dream project) - then one day, they say, I want to actually build it… it must create a reflow2 project from multiple fragments (and potentially contradicting or imperfect requirements/ideas/proposals) and turn them into an actual reflow2 project."

THREE THINGS DISTINGUISH THIS FROM req:corpus-ingest, which is about CONVERGENCE (the same component named in forty specs resolving to one node). (1) CONTRADICTION IS THE EXPECTED STATE, NOT A DEFECT. A 2019 idea disagreeing with a 2024 one is not an error to heal — both were genuinely held, and the disagreement is the most informative thing in the corpus. The design must be able to say "you changed your mind here, forty times" as a READING rather than as forty defects. (2) THERE IS NOTHING BUILT TO RECONCILE AGAINST. Every capability is `planned`, every requirement `proposed`, and the as-built half of the loop has no subject — which is honest and must not read as catastrophic. (3) THE CORPUS IS THE ONLY ARTIFACT. For a codebase the documents are one source among several and the code arbitrates; here the documents are the whole of what exists, so nothing outside them can settle a disagreement between them and the user is the only arbiter.

IT ALSO SITS UNDER BOTH SIBLING SKILLS RATHER THAN BESIDE THEM, which is the structural half of the same observation. `adopt` is described for a system with "little or no requirements documentation" and recovers intent by reverse-engineering code — but a corpus this size falsifies that premise, and adopt's Phase 0 only REGISTERS documents as Fragments while Phase 3 is told to recover requirements ONLY from them. Measured on dev_storyflow: 17 Fragments and 9 Requirements recovered from 1,124 documents, after which a separate multi-session campaign had to read them by hand. `genesis` assumes an opening BRIEF — one statement — and has no shape for an opening FOLDER. So mass ingest is a primitive both skills should consume, not a third skill beside them.

Status deliberately `proposed`: this is Anthony's framing captured in his own words and awaiting his confirmation of the wording, not a settled requirement.

properties.name: A system that already exists can be brought under design control
properties.statement: Requirements, functions and structure can be recovered from a running system.

properties.name: Adopting an existing system reports how much of it was actually recovered
properties.statement: reflow2's adopt skill produces a graph of an existing system but has no measure of COMPLETENESS — nothing says what fraction of the codebase reached the design, so "we adopted it" cannot be distinguished from "we adopted the parts we happened to read." The original reflow gated on exactly this: workflow 01e-reverse_engineering.json step RE-06 (Validation and Gap Analysis) computed an extraction coverage percentage by validating the extracted architecture back against the code — identifying unmapped functions (code not in the architecture), undocumented interfaces, and inconsistencies between architecture and code behaviour — and its agent guidance made it a stop condition: "Extraction coverage < 80% requires manual review before proceeding." Its completion criteria repeat it as a required gate. DISTINCT FROM WHAT reflow2 ALREADY HAS. coverage_report measures whether INTENT has been delivered (requirements against the golden thread, per req:completion-computed); this measures whether the AS-BUILT LAYER IS COMPLETE — a different axis and the one adopt needs, because an honest brownfield model must be able to say what it did not see. reconcile_artifacts compares recorded artifacts against disk, which is nearer, but it checks the artifacts the design already names rather than finding the code the design never mentioned. The adopt skill's own doctrine already makes the case: "You only get what you see is not a limitation to paper over: the graph marks what was inferred, confesses what it cannot know" — a coverage figure is that confession made quantitative. Note the granularity caveat adopt is right about: node count tracks distinct contracts and capabilities, NOT lines of code (a 110k-LOC system landed at ~78 nodes while reflow2's own ~34k LOC lands near ~100), so this measure must be expressed in terms adopt actually models — unmapped entry points, unmodelled contracts, untouched modules — never as a nodes-per-LOC ratio, which would punish a coarse-but-honest model. Found 2026-07-28 reviewing the original reflow workflows. Anthony's word: capture it.

properties.name: What a session PRODUCES is captured too — diagrams, mockups and rendered explanations, not just the decisions distilled from them
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-07-31: "in many sessions, the agent will create artifacts — things like mermaid diagrams or simple html files showing how a specific feature will work or an html file showing the aesthetic layout of a webpage — having all these artifacts automatically stored in the reflow2 blob storage would be great."

THE GAP THIS NAMES. `Artifact` already exists and can point at a file with a checksum, but it models CODE the design produced — something that lives in the repo and gets built. The things a session generates to explain itself are different: a mermaid diagram of a flow, an HTML mock of a layout, a rendered comparison. They are produced to be LOOKED AT, they are usually thrown away when the session ends, and they are frequently the clearest statement of intent anyone ever made about that feature. A paragraph describing a layout is a poor substitute for the mock that was actually agreed to.

WHY IT BELONGS BESIDE THE DECISION IT SERVED: these artifacts are the visual half of `Decision.rationale`. The reasoning is recorded in text and the picture that made the reasoning obvious is not, so a later reader gets the conclusion without the thing that made it persuasive. This is the same argument `cap:session-memory` makes for the conversation — the connective tissue is what is lost — applied to output rather than dialogue.

AUTOMATICALLY is the load-bearing word, and it is the hard part. A capture that depends on the agent remembering to store its own diagram is subject to exactly the decay `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` measures. So this wants a trigger, not a convention — the same family, and it should be designed with it rather than beside it.

WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN: a store full of every intermediate render nobody will ever open. What is worth keeping is what a Decision or a Capability actually points at; the rest is session litter. Where that line falls is an open question this requirement deliberately does not answer.

properties.name: Agent-to-agent feedback is written for reproduction, not for brevity — and the human whose project it was written inside still decides whether it leaves
properties.statement:
ANTHONY, 2026-08-14, settling the two constraints on agent-authored feedback while the DELIVERY mechanism stays open on `dec:idea-agent-to-agent-feedback-is-a-formal-channel`. Both were raised as counters to his own proposal and he agreed with both.

═══ 1 · THE CONSENT BOUNDARY — who may be cut out, and who may not ═══

**TWO DIFFERENT HUMANS ARE IN THIS LOOP AND ONLY ONE MAY BE REMOVED.**
  · **THE ROUTING HUMAN** — the person who today must read an agent's friction note, understand it, and relay it onward. Pure overhead. **Removing them is the point of the whole idea.**
  · **THE CONSENTING HUMAN** — the person whose project the feedback was written INSIDE. **Not removable.**

HIS WORDS: *"the agent writes freely for another agent; the human still decides whether it leaves."*

⇒ WHAT THIS REQUIRES: an agent may compose feedback for another agent without a human in the authoring loop, at any length and in any form useful to a machine reader. **Nothing may transmit it off the machine it was written on without that project's owner deciding.** A channel that ships unasked is an exfiltration path however good the intent, because the material was produced inside someone else's design.

📌 THE DISCIPLINE ALREADY EXISTS AND WAS HONOURED UNPROMPTED IN THE FIELD. `report-friction` redacts the user's design content and never files without asking; the Grok 4.6 feedback file of 2026-08-13 wrote its own guard rail: *"Per report-friction: do not open a public issue without asking. This file is the local log."* and *"Product/design content is summarized by type and count, not quoted."* **This requirement does not invent that restraint — it says the new channel may not lose it.** `req:telemetry-carries-usage-never-design-content` is the standing rule it inherits.

📌 CONSENT IS SEPARATELY MODELLED AND UNBUILT: `dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded` — asked for by Alex himself — decides WHETHER feedback may travel. This requirement decides that it may not travel without that answer.

═══ 2 · THE FORMAT TARGET — reproducibility, not terseness ═══

HIS WORDS: *"The target should be reproducibility, not terseness."*

⇒ WHAT THIS REQUIRES: agent-authored feedback is written so a receiving agent can RE-RUN the claim, not merely read it. Each report names the tool, the arguments, the observed result, the expected result, and — explicitly — **what the author did not check.**

🛑 THE EVIDENCE, AND IT IS WHY THE OBVIOUS OPTIMISATION IS WRONG. The stated appeal of a machine-to-machine channel is that it can *"be very efficient and remove any fluff that is needed when a human is in the loop."* **But brevity is not what made the 2026-08-13 file valuable.** Four of its items were independently reproduced by a different agent on a different graph within a day (`fact:agent-feedback-corroborated-2026-08-14`), and every one of the four was reproducible **because it named the tool and its arguments**: `get_node({node_type: Project, id: "proj:…"})` returning `{node: null}` could be re-run in a single call and confirmed. Its items that were only narrated could not be checked at all.

⚠️ **A FORMAT OPTIMISED FOR COMPACTNESS WOULD DELETE EXACTLY THE PARTS THAT WORKED.** The same file carried a *"Gaps (mine / process)"* section admitting it had skipped `compare_designs`, guessed a Project id, and not exported after writing. That self-reporting reads as overhead and is the first thing terseness removes — yet it is what tells a reader which claims are load-bearing and which are unexamined.

⚠️ AND THE CONFIRMED/UNCONFIRMED SPLIT MUST BE STRUCTURAL, not left to the writer's conscience. That file's `get_instructions` truncation report did NOT reproduce here — the payload arrived complete — which was only discoverable because the claim was specific enough to test. A report that cannot be tested cannot be disconfirmed either, and an untestable claim that hardens into folklore is the failure `dec:idea-intent-crosses-designs` already recorded once about this project.

═══ WHAT THIS REQUIREMENT DOES NOT SETTLE ═══

The mechanism is open on `dec:idea-agent-to-agent-feedback-is-a-formal-channel`: extend `report-friction` with an agent-to-agent mode, a new served skill, a structured field format, or leave it ad-hoc. **Option (d), a graph node type, is blocked by a real constraint** — the authoring agent works inside someone else's design, so the note must travel as a DOCUMENT rather than as a node.

properties.name: An agent can drive the whole loop
properties.statement: Every capability is reachable from a coding agent over one surface.

properties.name: An absent property means nobody said it — a value equal to the schema default is not written
properties.statement: A design record does not serialize a property value that equals the schema's default, so the presence of a property means somebody chose it and its absence means nobody did. This is BL-198's own stated fix shape (`fact:bl-198`), captured as intent because Anthony agreed to it on 2026-08-10 (`dec:fix-the-comparison-before-pointing-it-earlier`, step 1). PARTLY LANDED ALREADY, which is why capturing it matters: 0.25.0 wrote defaults into the export and 0.27.0 does not, while BL-198 is still listed PLANNED — so satisfying this requirement is partly reconciling the plan with what shipped rather than building something new. THE POINT IS NOT BYTE SIZE. This is the property-level form of the confirmed-versus-asserted distinction the project already enforces for requirements: `graph_report`'s certainty line exists because status carries the user's word, and `dec:certainty-derived` argues that distinction must be DERIVABLE rather than stored. At property level it is currently neither, and omission makes it derivable for free.

properties.name: A registered file says what it stands for and how its content is expected to behave, because no amount of looking can tell
properties.statement:
When something is registered against the design, reflow2 must let its author state two things nothing can observe from the outside: WHAT THE NODE STANDS FOR — one finished thing, a folder deliberately claimed as a single item, or a placeholder still meant to be broken up — and WHETHER ITS CONTENT IS EXPECTED TO KEEP CHANGING. Reports must then tell those states apart rather than reading them alike.

ANTHONY, 2026-08-05, answering the standing question ("was it worth adding, and if so what problem does it solve, or should it come back out?"): KEEP IT, and write the requirement.

WHY IT IS A REQUIREMENT AND NOT A FEATURE THAT ESCAPED. The two states this distinguishes are OPPOSITE and read IDENTICALLY without it. A directory artifact claims its whole subtree — which is the adopt skill's own rule — so a registration check reported "every live doc is registered", truthfully, across 359 individually unreferenceable files, and `coverage_report` counted the directory as covering everything beneath it. "Deliberately opaque" (a settled archive, a vendored tree) and "nobody has got to it yet" are a DECISION and UNFINISHED WORK, and a report that cannot separate them is confidently wrong rather than merely incomplete. The same shape on the content side: checksumming a live append-only file fires drift forever, so the disposition is owed again on every reconcile and the signal trains its reader to ignore it.

THE GENERAL FORM, which is why this belongs in the design rather than as two properties: SOME FACTS ABOUT AN ARTIFACT ARE ONLY KNOWABLE BY THE PERSON WHO PUT IT THERE. Neither hashing a file nor walking a tree can say whether a directory was left whole on purpose or whether a file is supposed to grow. reflow2 performs no file IO by doctrine, so it cannot even try — which makes the author's declaration the only possible source, and makes its ABSENCE a silent default rather than an unanswered question.

RECORDED AS THE ANSWER TO A GAP THAT WAS RIGHT TO FIRE. `unmotivated_capability` asked why a capability existed that no requirement wanted, and the honest answer was that it was built from measured friction before the intent was written down. The gap did its job; this is the intent catching up, not the gap being explained away. Note the ordering deliberately: the capability shipped first and the requirement follows, which is the reverse of the loop this project prescribes — worth seeing rather than tidying, because the friction that produced it was real and the design was genuinely silent.

STATUS `accepted` ON ANTHONY'S EXPLICIT WORD, given 2026-08-05 in reply to the question as asked.

properties.name: A Decision left proposed AND assigned to somebody is reported by the loop; one nobody was asked to decide stays quiet
properties.statement:
Raised by @ajs from flo2, 2026-08-05, and this is the concrete instance that exposed req:the-loop-says-what-is-owed-to-a-person. A design can hold any number of Decision nodes at proposed — genuinely open choices, one of them blocking another person's work — and NOTHING REPORTS THEM.

MEASURED TWICE, ON TWO DESIGNS, INDEPENDENTLY. (1) On flo2's own design, holding EIGHT proposed decisions: detect_gaps returned 12 gaps, NONE referencing a Decision; loop_status reported unanswered_questions 0, unwritten_answers 0, and has no field that counts an open decision at all. (2) REPRODUCED ON REFLOW2'S OWN DESIGN, 2026-08-05, deliberately as a test rather than by accident: capturing this proposal created dec:one-process-many-stores at status proposed and gave it an AUTHORED_BY edge with role=approver to who:ajs — the exact shape this requirement says should be reported. loop_status then returned clean:false with unsurfaced_gaps 11, unanswered_questions 0, and NO field counting an open decision; detect_gaps returned 11 gaps of which ZERO referenced dec:one-process-many-stores. Every one of the 11 was about the capabilities and requirements captured alongside it. So the loop reported eleven things it was owed and stayed silent about the one item a named person had actually been asked to decide.

That second measurement matters more than the first: it is on the design of the tool itself, made by the tool's own instrumentation, on a node built specifically to be the positive case. The detector is not failing on an exotic shape — it is silent on the canonical one.

THE QUIET IS RIGHT; THE LACK OF AN EXIT IS NOT. This is documented and deliberate. The brainstorm skill records a musing as a proposed Decision with its options in prose precisely so the loop stays silent while somebody is still thinking, and detect_gaps fires undecided_decision_point only on a Decision holding two or more REGISTERED ALTERNATIVES — a fork with real design behind each branch. That line is a good one and must survive: a brainstormed Decision with no approver must keep costing nothing, so thinking out loud stays free.

THE PROBLEM IS THAT THERE IS NO WAY TO CROSS IT. A musing that becomes a live question owned by a named person has no state to move to. register_alternative does not fit: it requires a LOCATION per alternative — where that alternative's design export lives, branch-by-file — and the options here are prose ("connect the user's own git repo" against "provision a hosted sandbox"), neither of which has a design export. Using it would mean inventing file paths that do not exist in order to make a detector notice something true. And the Question machinery cannot be pointed at a Decision: answer_question refuses unless gap_to_prompt already recorded a question, and gap_to_prompt takes a GapCandidate from detect_gaps, so Questions are GAP-DERIVED ONLY — there is no way to raise a standalone question against a node somebody must decide on. That refusal is correct and well-explained; the limitation is upstream of it.

THE GRAPH ALREADY KNOWS, which is what makes this cheaper than it looks: AUTHORED_BY with role=approver is already the graph SAYING that a named contributor owes an answer here. The information is present and structured. Nothing computes on it.

THE DISCRIMINATOR THIS REQUIREMENT ASKS FOR: proposed AND carrying an approver edge means somebody has been asked to decide and the loop should say so. Proposed with no approver means somebody is thinking, and the loop stays silent. The graph already distinguishes these two; the loop does not read the distinction.

WHAT IT COST, which is the shape of what it will cost users: flo2's requirement was that its open decisions surface for the second contributor when he clones. The graph could not satisfy it, so it was met OUTSIDE THE GRAPH — a hand-written list in README.md plus a committed loop-nudge hook. That list is a second copy of something the graph already holds, maintained by hand, with nothing checking the two agree. It will drift the first time a decision is added or settled, and it will drift SILENTLY — the precise failure mode reflow2 exists to prevent. A design brain that holds the open decisions but cannot report them pushes its users into keeping a shadow list.

properties.name: Deleting a node is never mechanical, and never quiet on a shared graph
properties.rationale: THE SAFETY MODEL IS CURRENTLY INVERTED, and it is not a hypothetical: propose_heal offered 10 operations, every one a Merge that DELETES its remove_id, including a load-bearing requirement — while the check-health skill tables `duplicate` as the machine-fixable half and tells the agent in terms that requires_human_review being true 'does not mean you should withhold the mechanical merge'. So THE HALF AN AGENT IS TOLD TO APPLY UNREVIEWED IS THE DESTRUCTIVE ONE, AND THE HALF IT IS TOLD TO ESCALATE MUTATES NOTHING. An agent following the skill exactly deletes ten design nodes; the reporter stopped only because the pairings looked implausible enough to read. Root cause and the full chain are recorded in fact:defect-ingest-writes-duplicates-that-heal-then-merges. THE SHARED-GRAPH MULTIPLIER, which is why this is a separate requirement from fixing the scorer: on a solo graph a bad merge is one person's undo. Here one session's apply hits three bosses and four workers instantly, with no undo and no notification to anyone else. All three bosses stood down on it 3/3 and the whole fleet was barred from check-health. A SECOND INSTANCE OF THE SAME SHAPE, different tool: propose_heal offered generate_bridge on req:stateless_scaling where the user had explicitly ruled that drawing a SATISFIES edge would be a forgery. THE TOOL'S SUGGESTED FIX BEING THE HARM IS NOW TWICE — a bridge adds a wrong edge; this deletes a node. NOTE THE TENSION TO RESOLVE DELIBERATELY: reflow2 already holds dec:ask-not-repair (accepted) saying merge is safe only because the endpoints were asserted by a human. This requirement is arguably not new intent but a second guard for a decision that is already accepted and currently defeated — worth deciding which of those it is before building.
properties.statement: An operation that destroys design content SHALL NOT be classified as a mechanical fix an agent may apply without review, and on a shared graph it SHALL require the acting seat to acknowledge that other sessions are attached. Requested as the #6 fleet ask, and as the highest-severity item dev_storyflow has sent this channel (sb-boss ab2291fa, api-boss 5d608b85, 2026-08-07).

properties.name: A harness that cannot carry the loop nudge is told so, distinctly from one that merely has not installed it
properties.statement:
When a project runs on an agent harness reflow2 has no loop-nudge hook for, that is reported as a DISTINCT state from a harness that supports the hook and does not have it registered. The two are different situations and only one of them is actionable:

  · NOT INSTALLED HERE — the harness can carry the trigger and it is missing. Fixable: install it.
  · CANNOT BE INSTALLED HERE — the harness has no event reflow2 can register. Permanent: the coherence loop is the user's to run by hand, and saying so is the whole of what is owed.

Reporting them identically sends the second user to fix something that cannot be fixed, and leaves them believing reflow2 is misconfigured when it is working as designed.

THIS EXTENDS AN EXISTING ANNOUNCEMENT RATHER THAN ADDING A SECOND ONE. `cap:nudge-path-proven` already reports `installed | absent | broken | unknown` on the handshake instructions and as a machine-readable field on `loop_status`. `absent` currently carries both meanings above. The requirement is the distinction, not the channel — nothing new should be built to say it.

⚠️ WHAT THIS COSTS, and it is the part most likely to be missed: the backstop infers the nudge's state by looking for a registered Stop hook in the Claude settings file. It does not know WHICH harness the project uses, so it cannot presently tell "this harness has no hook" from "this hook is missing". **The harness answer that `req:init-installs-only-the-harness-you-name` collects must therefore be PERSISTED somewhere the server can read it** — otherwise the distinction has no input, and the report can only ever guess.

Raised by Alex (`who:alex`) 2026-08-14 as the parenthetical of his settings note — *"or whatever settings file is relevant for the agent harness"*; settled by Anthony the same day on `dec:idea-the-loop-nudge-exists-for-one-harness-only`.

properties.name: A coupling with no declared contract is NAMED as a finding, in any project — the seams ratio already knows which pairs they are and throws the list away
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-08-13, reframing what had been treated as a chore: "the step of adding seams for reflow2 needs to be something reflow2 does for ANY project."

He is right that it was framed wrongly. The prior plan was to hand-label reflow2's own 73 couplings, which fixes one design and teaches reflow2 nothing. Every consumer arrives in the same state — components that depend on each other with no contract recorded between them — and the tool should meet them there.

⭐ THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS AND IS DISCARDED. `crates/reflow2-core/src/maturity.rs:203` computes exactly two sets to produce the `seams` band: `couplings` (Component pairs joined by DEPENDS_ON) and `declared` (pairs joined by a real contract — counted only when BOTH a PROVIDES and a CONSUMES are recorded on the same Interface, because "one-sided is exactly the unrecorded contract the capture skill warns about"). It divides one by the other, reports a ratio, and drops the difference on the floor.

`couplings - declared` IS the answer, computed on every maturity run, for every design, and never named. On reflow2's own graph that set has 73 members and the band reads 0%.

🛑 AND NOTHING ELSE COVERS IT. `grep seam` in detect.rs returns nothing: there is no gap source for "these two components are coupled and no contract is declared between them." The two interface detectors run the OPPOSITE direction — `unprovided_interface` (an Interface nobody provides) and `unconsumed_interface` (an Interface nobody consumes) — and both require an Interface to already exist. A design that has never declared one is invisible to both.

WHAT THIS MUST NOT DO, and it is the whole constraint. reflow2 can see THAT two components are coupled. It cannot know WHAT the contract is — the medium, the payload, the auth, the direction. Proposing one would be `req:a-repair-suggestion-never-proposes-fabrication` exactly, and `cap:no-fabricated-repair` is the built answer to that class. So the finding names the PAIR and asks; it never drafts the Interface.

THE SHAPE THAT FOLLOWS FROM THE ABOVE: report each undeclared coupling as a gap whose question is answerable by the person who owns the two components — "cmp:A depends on cmp:B and no contract is recorded between them; is there one, and what is it?" — routed through the ordinary detect→ask path, with `gap_to_prompt` doing the wording.

⚠️ TWO THINGS TO GET RIGHT, both learned from detectors this project has already had to retune:
  · VOLUME. reflow2 alone would emit 73. `chg:gap-reporting-at-corpus-scale` records the same shape biting at an order of magnitude ("300 captured ideas produce 300 identical gaps"), and `unexpected_coupling` was RETIRED for firing on correct architecture. An aggregate keyed on the rule — the shape `cap:aggregate-gap-keying` exists for — is more likely right than 73 individual nags.
  · A DESIGN WITH NO COMPONENT DEPENDENCIES HAS NO SEAMS TO DECLARE, and maturity.rs already says so: "no two Components depend on each other, so there is no seam to declare." The finding must stay silent there rather than reporting a clean 0 as a fault.

📌 WHY IT IS WORTH BUILDING RATHER THAN LABELLING BY HAND: the seams band is reflow2's own frontier and has never moved. Every piece of federation machinery — pair_designs, cap:seam-incompatibility, cap:complementary-pairing, export_surface — is built and verified against fixtures, and has almost nothing to run on in any real design, because no real design has been given a reason to declare its boundaries.

properties.name: Any level of the design can be analysed on its own, and a narrowed answer says what it left out
properties.statement: A person or team responsible for one part of a design must be able to point the detectors at that part and be answered about it — "is my subsystem coherent, what is it owed" — without reading the whole program. Anthony, 2026-07-25, from the satellite case: an organisation building a satellite capability has a space segment, a ground/user segment and a control segment; his team owns the satellite, and more specifically inter-satellite laser communications. He must understand the system of systems, but day to day he needs his own part. Two properties are inseparable from the first. A narrowed answer must NAME WHAT IT WITHHELD — findings elsewhere in the design, and findings that belong to no part in particular — because a team shown only its own corner will conclude the program is healthy, which is the silent-drop failure req:no-silent-fallback forbids, one level up from a truncated read. And narrowing must never become the tool deciding what a team is allowed to worry about: a program-level finding that touches their work still reaches them, marked as the program's rather than theirs. Deliberately silent on WHERE the levels live: a subtree of one graph and a design of its own are both answers to this, and that is the architecture question recorded as dec:nested-graphs.

properties.name: As-designed vs as-built divergence is detectable
properties.statement: Real files on disk are registered as checksummed Artifacts realizing capabilities, so drift between the design and the build is visible rather than assumed.

properties.name: An assumption is recorded as something that can stop being true, and what rests on it is computed
properties.statement:
NOT FROM reflow. Raised 2026-07-28 from ordinary architecture and risk practice, after Anthony's instruction to bring judgement rather than treat reflow's workflows as canon. reflow had no equivalent either; this is a gap in both.

Designs rest on things believed true about the world that nobody controls, and those beliefs are what actually break architectures. reflow2 has no way to say so. Constraint BINDS (a limit the design must respect, and it is enforced). Decision records a choice with rationale (why WE chose, not what we BELIEVED). RISKS and MITIGATES describe something that might go wrong and what reduces it. None of them expresses "this design is sound ONLY WHILE X remains true, and X is not ours to decide" — which is a different object with a different lifecycle: an assumption is not enforced, not chosen, and not a risk to be reduced. It is a proposition that is checked, and that can be INVALIDATED, at which point everything resting on it needs revisiting.

THE MISSING COMPUTATION IS THE POINT, not the node type. Once an assumption is a node with things hanging off it, "assumption X no longer holds" becomes a propagate query with a real answer: these four capabilities and this interface were justified by it. Today that reasoning exists only in prose inside Decision rationale, where nothing can walk it. reflow2 already has every mechanism this needs — propagate_change computes blast radius, cap:freshness says when a claim was last confirmed, DriftEvent records a divergence against reality, and the Verification machinery already distinguishes proof against a model from proof against reality (cap:evidence-fidelity). An assumption is the node those mechanisms are missing.

WHY IT MATTERS PARTICULARLY IN THIS OPERATING CONTEXT. Several organisations, competing partially-built designs, coupled repositories each with its own graph, work delivered as increments. Almost everything load-bearing about the OTHER organisation's system is an assumption: that their interface will not change before your increment lands, that their component means what its name says, that the version they run is the version they declared. req:version-combination-is-an-object pins the versions; nothing records WHY a pinned combination was believed safe or what breaks when it stops being. Evolving a ten-year-old production stack on the fly is the same shape: most of what a change rests on is a belief about code nobody has read recently.

DISTINGUISH FROM WHAT EXISTS, because the boundary is what makes it useful: a Constraint that is violated is a defect in OUR design; an assumption that fails is a change in the WORLD, and the honest response is different — not fix the build, but revisit what was justified by it. Also distinct from a KPP (req:inviolable-intent), which is intent we refuse to weaken; an assumption is a fact we do not control.

OPEN and not decided: whether this is a new node type or Constraint gaining a kind that separates binds-us from believed-of-the-world (the second is cheaper and risks blurring the very distinction that makes it worth having); what edge carries "rests on" (DEPENDS_ON is lateral and already crowded; a dedicated relation may be clearer); and whether an assumption can carry an expiry or a confirmation cadence, which cap:freshness already models for claims and would make "nobody has checked this in six months" computable rather than remembered.

properties.name: Work that drifted can be frozen without freezing the work that did not
properties.statement: reflow2's response to unacceptable drift is all-or-nothing. tools/reflow2_check.py thresholds WHICH findings count — anchored gaps at or above --gap-threshold (default 0.8) fail the build — but the response is a single sys.exit(1) and the whole build goes red.
