THE PRIMARY USER DESCRIBES HIS OWN WORKING MODEL, AND ONE SESSION MEASURED IT. Anthony, 2026-08-11, unprompted.

HIS WORDS: "I guess how I've been treating reflow2 is as a 'funnel' for my instructions, ideas, feedback, requirements and brainstorming. it often comes in random order and often touches upon subjects that I had previously thought about and entered into reflow2 development... both my brother and I kind of work like this of organically developing our projects as we go. probably looking at this session is a good microcosm of how I've developed and used reflow2 so far - and it has kept up pretty well."

⭐ THE CLAIM IS TESTABLE AND THE SESSION TESTED IT. NINE times in one working day, an input that arrived as a fresh thought landed on something the graph already held. None became a duplicate:

  "what's next for governance"            -> six requirements already authored from an external report
  render the docs from the graph           -> viewpoints.md's recorded Direction, the unbuilt half of BL-40
  `claude update` as an aspiration         -> req:frictionless-update, ACCEPTED, explicitly modelled on Claude Code
  feedback as a prioritisation signal      -> req:friction-has-a-severity-bar, considered AND DROPPED, by him
  the backward-trace problem               -> req:no-idea-goes-quiet, accepted, capturing his own complaint 7 days earlier
  the MCP breakage                         -> a defect fact recorded 4 days earlier WITH ITS FIX in its evidence field
  the second user's "put the skill in"     -> report-friction, already shipped in the kit
  his own organic working model            -> req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design, proposed and unaccepted
  "make search-first automatic"            -> search-first already written into FIVE served skills, and
                                              req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue,
                                              proposed, which is exactly the delivery mechanism he asked for

The ninth happened WHILE RECORDING THE EIGHTH, which is the cleanest possible demonstration of the pattern.

⚠⚠ THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING, NOT THE COUNT. Every one of the nine was found because an agent WENT AND LOOKED. Nothing surfaced any of them. Had the search not been run, each becomes a near-duplicate node wearing different words, and the graph fills with the same idea nine times. So reflow2 is a funnel on PULL and not on PUSH: it will hold everything and volunteer nothing.

THAT IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THREE OTHER FINDINGS THE SAME DAY, which is why it is recorded as one fact rather than as praise: (1) the loop only sees what an agent hand-carries in (dec:idea-the-loop-only-sees-what-an-agent-hand-carries); (2) skills fire when a user TYPES them, confirmed twice — once by self-measurement in req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session and once from the field by the second user; (3) a fully-diagnosed defect with its fix already written sat four days because no ranking reads measured facts (dec:idea-field-evidence-is-a-prioritisation-input). Four instances, one mechanism: the design's memory is complete and entirely on demand.

⭐ WHY THIS IS FILED AGAINST req:accreted-intent-becomes-a-design RATHER THAN AS A NEW IDEA. That requirement — "a body of intent accreted over years, contradicting itself and never built, can still become a design" — IS the working model he just described, and it is `proposed` and unaccepted. The way the primary user and the second user actually work is captured in the design and never confirmed. That is the eighth collision above, and it is about reflow2's own understanding of who uses it.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: nine collisions in one session is evidence that the ORDER of his input does not cost him coherence WHEN AN AGENT SEARCHES. It is not evidence about how often a session that does not search creates duplicates — nobody has measured that, and it is the number that would say what the pull-only property actually costs.

THE SEAM PAIRS. dec:linked-repos-poc's remaining half is now satisfied, and seam_report has been exercised for the first time.

THAT PoC (2026-08-06) reported paired=0 against BOTH dynograph-foundation and flo2, with 15 and 5 published interfaces landing in dead surface, and named the cause exactly: reflow2 declared no `required` interface anywhere, so pairing — which matches complements, never like with like — could never produce a pair. It called declaring them "the cheapest next step" and deliberately left it to Anthony's word. He gave it 2026-08-09, choosing to declare the environmental boundaries alongside the code ones.

MEASURED, BEFORE AND AFTER, against dynograph-foundation:
  paired         0  ->  5   (all at name_score 100)
  dead_surface  15  ->  1   (only their /v1 REST API, which reflow2 genuinely does not use)
  unmet_needs    0  ->  3   ambient-agent, exclusive-local-store, mcp-protocol

And against flo2: unmet_needs 0 -> 4, dead_surface 5 -> 3.

⚠️ THE MOST IMPORTANT NUMBER IS THE ONE THAT STOPPED BEING ZERO. The PoC called `unmet_needs: 0` "the most dangerous number in the run" — it reads as "nothing is missing" and meant "we never said we needed anything". It is now 3 and 4, which are real findings rather than an absence.

⭐ A MODELLING ERROR MADE AND CORRECTED IN THE SAME SITTING, recorded because the correction is the lesson. The first attempt declared ONE umbrella interface for the whole dynograph dependency. Pairing returned NINE candidates and ZERO pairs: a pair needs a name match at or above 85/100, and an umbrella scored 62-78 against nine crisp names. THEY DECOMPOSED AND WE LUMPED. reflow2 links five named crates that map 1:1 onto five of their published interfaces, so the umbrella was deleted (never committed, never true — a mistake rather than history) and replaced with five requirements at the publisher's granularity, named to match. All five then paired at 100.

SEAM_REPORT, RUN FOR THE FIRST TIME EVER — the PoC listed this as what it could NOT answer, because the check needs pairs and there were none: 5 pairs checked, 10 axes agreed, 0 incompatible, 0 differing, AND 30 AXES STATED BY NOBODY. The tool refuses to read that as compatibility, and says so unprompted: "an unstated axis is not an agreed one, and this is not a claim of compatibility." It also names what it did not examine — the TYPES crossing the boundaries. So the honest verdict is that the machinery works and the contracts on both sides are almost entirely unstated, which is a true statement about two designs nobody wrote to be composed.

A REAL WEAKNESS FOUND WHILE DOING IT, worth filing rather than working around: candidate noise scales as N×M. Five requirements against nine published library APIs produced 33 candidates, of which 5 were the real pairs. Every "X API" scores 60-83 against every other "Y API" on string similarity. Worse, an interface that has ALREADY paired at 100 still appears as a candidate against seven others — ifc:req-dyno-storage-api paired exactly with storage-api and is still offered against cluster-api, game-api, graph-api and four more. Suppressing candidates for a side that already has an exact match would remove most of the noise at no cost to the signal.

🛑 **CORRECTION: ALEX'S TWO 2026-08-14 REPORTS CAME FROM TWO DIFFERENT MACHINES WITH TWO DIFFERENT AGENTS, AND THIS SESSION TREATED THEM AS ONE.** Anthony, relaying Alex's own question about which feedback was being discussed, then clarifying the setup:

```
              MACHINE            OS       AGENT    PROJECTS        REPORT
work          work laptop        macOS    Claude   real work       the 5 ideas
home          personal laptop    macOS    Grok     personal        the Grok feedback.md
```

⚠️ ON `basis`: the enum offers only `measured` or `forecast`. The machine/agent/OS attribution is REPORTED — Anthony relaying Alex — not observed by reflow2. The kit VERSIONS below are genuinely measured. Marked `measured` because most load-bearing content is, with the distinction stated here rather than lost to a missing enum value.

⚠️ WHAT THIS SESSION GOT WRONG. `fact:agent-feedback-corroborated-2026-08-14` describes the Grok file as *"a Grok 4.6 session on one of Alex's projects"*, which reads as the same context that produced the five ideas. It is not. Any inference treating the two as evidence about ONE install is unsound as stated.

═══ THE STALE-KIT CLAIM, RESTATED HONESTLY ═══

This session repeatedly said *"three independent signals that consumers run stale kits"*, implying mutual reinforcement about one user. **They are three SEPARATE installs, each stale:**
```
work / Claude / macOS ..... two of five notes describe behaviour fixed in
                            #172/#174 -> INFERRED stale, NEVER MEASURED
home / Grok / macOS ....... kit-version.json reads 0.11.0 / 0ec473e,
                            a 2026-07-25 tarball -> MEASURED
this dev machine / Linux .. kit stamp 0.28.0 / e2b05c7 -> MEASURED
```
⇒ WEAKER as evidence about Alex — only his HOME install was measured, and the five ideas came from WORK. STRONGER as evidence about the UPDATE PATH: three machines, at least two install routes, three versions, none current. **Systemic, not one person forgetting.**

🎯 THE VERSION QUESTION NEEDS A MACHINE. Anthony texted Alex asking what `reflow2 --version` says; **he has two installs and the answer differs.** The WORK one matters most — it produced the five ideas behind `epoch:a-project-is-set-up-right-on-the-first-run` and has never been measured.

═══ ⭐⭐ IT IMMEDIATELY FOUND A DEFECT IN WORK SHIPPED THE SAME HOUR ═══

`cap:init-asks-which-harness` had just been built with a deliberate decision: **`grok` is NOT a registry entry**, because Grok CLI reads `.mcp.json` and a second entry would write the same file twice under two names. A test asserted it. **The reasoning was right and the ergonomics were hostile: `--harness=grok` returned `error: unknown harness 'grok'` and exit 1** — the install REFUSING a correct answer from a user naming his own tool. Learning that Alex runs Grok at home is what surfaced it.

FIXED the same hour, keeping the reasoning and dropping the hostility: `HARNESS_ALIASES = {"grok": "claude"}` resolves the name without adding a config, the prompt line reads *"Claude Code (also read by Grok CLI — choose this for Grok)"*, and `grok,claude` collapses to one config rather than erroring. Four tests guard it, including that every alias points at a real harness and that no name is both an alias and an entry.

📌 **A GENERAL LESSON, since `rule:a-lesson-is-generalised-before-it-is-built` now exists:** a registry that is CORRECT about what to install can still be WRONG about what to accept. The two are different questions — what files does this harness need, and what might a user call it — and collapsing them refuses real answers.

═══ 📌 ENVIRONMENT FACTS NEW TO THE DESIGN ═══

  · **EVERY SECOND-USER REPORT REFLOW2 HAS EVER RECEIVED IS FROM macOS**, and **every measurement reflow2 has ever made is on Linux** — including all of 2026-08-14's installer runs and the harness wizard itself. Whether `tools/install.sh`, the `~/.local/share/reflow2/kit` layout, the merge-driver registration and `--harness` behave identically on macOS is **unverified, and nothing in the design claims it**.
  · **A TARBALL install is in use** (`0ec473e`), a different update route from a checkout. `user-iterative-release-preference` sets the goal at a ONE-WORD UPDATE; whether the tarball route reaches that is untested.

⭐ THE BREADTH IS ITSELF THE FINDING: the second user exercises reflow2 across two agents (Claude, Grok) and two project classes (work, personal) on one OS reflow2 has never been tested on. For evidence purposes his two report streams should be read as **two users**, and the two agents mean the served skills are being read by two different models.

THIRD INSTANCE, AND THE FIRST ONE WHERE THE PEOPLE LOSING THE CYCLE HAD ALREADY WRITTEN THE DEFECT DOWN. Deliberately NOT a new defect: fact:defect-a-running-server-cannot-say-it-is-stale (2026-08-07) already states this case in almost these words — '--serve-shared is detached on purpose, so every session that restarted RE-ATTACHED TO THE SAME STALE PROCESS and nothing anywhere reported a problem' — and fact:defect-stale-server-reproduced-first-hand-here records the second. This node exists for what those two do NOT say. WHAT HAPPENED, 2026-08-08 late: Anthony went home specifically to restart and pick up the new binary, restarted the session, and the served surface was unchanged. Measured rather than assumed: `describe_schema(from: DesignRule, to: Component)` still answered 'No edge type specifically models DesignRule -> Component' and still showed CONSTRAINS as `from: ["*"]`, minutes after that enumeration was built, gated and pushed. `ps` explains it: the `--serve-shared` daemon has held the graph since 10:16 that morning, while the restart spawned a NEW `--shared` CLIENT (23:50) which attached to it. WHAT IS NEW AND WORTH THE NODE: (1) THE DOCUMENTED REMEDY IS THE THING THAT FAILS. Every prior record treats 'restart' as the escape from a stale server. Under `--shared` a session restart does not touch the daemon, so the remedy silently does nothing and the user reasonably believes it worked. The actual remedy is `--stop-shared`, which appears in NEITHER prior fact. (2) IT COST A WHOLE DAY OF DOGFOODING. Five merged PRs — the seat-liveness fix, both governance detectors, the skill, the enforced tri-state — were built, gated and merged without one of them ever running through a live session, because the daemon predated all of it. The handoff note written that evening had to say 'check the version rather than assume', which is the workaround this requirement exists to abolish. (3) IT WAS CAUGHT ONLY BY DELIBERATE CHECKING. The session tested a schema fact it happened to know had changed. Nothing surfaced it, and a session without that specific memory would have proceeded on a stale surface believing it was current — which is exactly how the four sessions in the 2026-08-07 report drew opposite conclusions from the same true value. WHY THIS IS AN ARGUMENT AND NOT A COMPLAINT: `req:the-server-is-the-authority-on-its-own-currency` has NOTHING SATISFYING IT and has sat among the 0.60 unsatisfied-requirement gaps all day. The fix is not research: `/proc/self/exe` is marked `(deleted)` the moment the binary is replaced, w-6904efa6 demonstrated it live on a real pid, and it is one syscall with no second source and no version-string comparison. THREE INSTANCES ACROSS TWO PROJECTS AND TWO MACHINES, and the third landed on the maintainer. THE HONEST CAVEAT, because recurrence is not automatically corroboration: these three share a cause rather than a method — two were found by noticing an impossible value, this one by testing a remembered fact — so they add weight to the COST, not to the diagnosis, which was already certain.

REFLOW2 CAN ALREADY JUDGE TEST QUALITY STRUCTURALLY, ON THREE AXES, AND TWO OF THEM HAVE NEVER BEEN USED. Measured 2026-08-11 while asking where the line falls between test quality reflow2 can check and test quality only a person can judge.

THE LINE IS FURTHER OUT THAN IT LOOKED. The claim under test was that a test's quality is textual — valid, isolated, repeatable, focused, fast, covers edge cases and error conditions — and therefore out of reach for a deterministic core (`req:deterministic-core`). That is only partly true, and the interesting part is which half.

MEASURED:

  Verifications                                                  137
  targets per check          1 -> 130    2 -> 6    3 -> 1
  ⇒ FOCUS is already good here. 130 of 137 check exactly one thing, so a
    focus detector modelled on granularity_report would find nothing on this
    design. A useful NEGATIVE result: the metric exists and the problem does not.

  THE THREE BUILT EVIDENCE-QUALITY AXES, IN USE:
    TIME   (how old the check is)             99 of 137 carry last_run_at
    INPUT  (what it PINNED vs SWEPT)          0 VERIFIES edges carry a scope
    INDEP  (was the value fitted to it)       0 CALIBRATED_AGAINST edges

  detectors mentioning scope, narrowness or circularity           0
  surface for the two unused axes    evidence_report, confirmation_ledger
                                     — read-only, and you must know to call them

⭐ SO THE EDGE-CASE QUESTION IS ALREADY ANSWERABLE STRUCTURALLY. `set_evidence_scope` records what a check PINNED versus SWEPT, and `evidence_report` reads it: "a parameter every passing check pins is reported as NARROW; ONE check that sweeps it ends the narrowness." That is a machine-checkable proxy for "does the suite explore the boundaries" — exactly one of the eight criteria that looked textual. `req:evidence-says-what-it-covered` is ACCEPTED. The machinery is 3 functions, 643 lines of test, 18 cases, mutation-checked on all three axes.

⚠️⚠️ AND IT IS THE CONTENT STORE'S PROFILE EXACTLY. `dec:the-content-store-is-discontinued` (accepted, 2026-08-09) reads: "built, shipped, correct, and used zero times in every project that has it." Two of these three axes are in that same state today. The parallel is not loose — both had an accepted requirement behind them, both were carefully built, both were tested well, and neither was ever reached for.

📌 THE FORK THIS OPENS, and it is real rather than rhetorical:
  (a) MAKE THEM ASKED-FOR. A detector — "this passing check does not say what it covered" — would surface the axes at the moment a check is recorded. Cheap, and it is the fourth instance today of the same diagnosis: the capability exists and nothing asks for it.
  (b) DISCONTINUE THEM, on the test that killed the content store. There is now a mechanism for exactly that, shipped hours ago: an accepted Decision OBSOLETES what it withdrew, and four computations read it.
  (c) NEITHER YET — zero usage on ONE design is thin evidence, and this design is the author's own. A consumer project's suite is where narrowness would actually bite.

⭐⭐ WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE PHILOSOPHY QUESTION IT IS FILED AGAINST. `dec:idea-verification-is-planned-with-the-requirement` proposes that reflow2 guide a project to plan verification when a need is stated. This measurement is a warning about HOW: reflow2 has already built test-quality machinery once and nobody used it, because nothing asked. Adding requirement-side planning WITHOUT asking would repeat that exactly — and would be the fifth instance today of a capability that exists and never fires.

WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY TEXTUAL, and is not claimed to be checkable: VALID (does it measure what it claims, or a side effect), HAPPY PATH and ERROR CONDITIONS coverage, and whether a test reads the CONTRACT or the IMPLEMENTATION — that last being `dec:bl-185`, still open. ISOLATED, REPEATABLE and FAST are not textual but are simply ABSENT: the graph records no run history (one `last_run_at`, overwritten), no duration, and no dependency between checks, so a proxy for them would need new data rather than a new reading.

ANTHONY, 2026-08-14: *"as always is the case is that we are using reflow2 to design itself, but nothing is for reflow2 itself. what we do for reflow2 should be generalizable to whoever is using reflow2 on a project."*

🛑 **THE TEST APPLIED TO WHAT HAD JUST BEEN DONE, AND IT FAILS.** Three DesignRules were created minutes earlier from this session's lessons. **A DesignRule lives in THIS graph and governs THIS design.** A consumer project has its own graph and its own rules; nothing seeds these into it. So all three made the lessons findable BY US and delivered nothing to anybody using reflow2. That is correct for a rule about how this project works — `rule:nothing-lands-on-main-directly` should not travel — but it does NOT discharge a lesson that is general.

⭐ **THE VEHICLES THAT ACTUALLY GENERALISE** are the ones served rather than stored: the SKILLS (compiled into the binary, so every project gets the current one), the TOOL BEHAVIOUR (detectors, report shapes, what a command prints), the served INSTRUCTIONS (`get_instructions`), and the KIT (`reflow2_check.py`, `reflow2_init.py`). reflow2's own graph nodes reach nobody.

═══ ✅ MEASURED: THE `ci-gate` SKILL IS THE GENERAL HOME FOR TODAY'S GATE LESSONS, AND IT IS SILENT ON ALL OF THEM ═══

Read in full 2026-08-14. It is served to every project that wants a design gate, and:

**1. IT INVITES THE ORDERING FAILURE IT DOES NOT WARN ABOUT.** Step 3 says *"Run it locally first (`python3 <kit>/tools/reflow2_check.py --export design.json`) so the first CI run is not the first run."* **Nothing says to run it AFTER committing.** `fact:the-lineage-gate-verdict-depends-on-when-you-run-it` measured the consequence on this project the same day: the identical file FAILED before an amend and PASSED after, because the gate compares against the export committed at HEAD. A user following this skill literally as written gets a verdict about a commit that may be about to change.

**2. IT SAYS NOTHING ABOUT PIPING THE GATE.** `fact:a-piped-gate-reports-the-pipes-exit-code-not-the-gates` is a measured failure on this project — `cargo test | grep | tail` reported success because a pipeline's exit code is its LAST command's. The skill's own CI snippet is unpiped and therefore correct by luck, and a user who pipes it to filter noise gets a green build from `grep`. **`rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object` was just ENFORCED on Anthony's word, and the skill that configures the gate does not carry it.**

**3. 🛑 IT UNDER-DESCRIBES THE GATE IT CONFIGURES.** *"What it checks, and what makes it fail"* lists exactly two failure modes — unaccepted DRIFT and an open anchored GAP at/above threshold — plus exit 2 for could-not-run. **LINEAGE is not mentioned anywhere**, and a LINEAGE failure is what actually turned this session red (`FAIL LINEAGE 'docs/design/reflow2.json' does not link to the export it replaced`). A user hitting it would find no explanation in the skill that set the gate up, and the skill's *"When the build goes red"* section has no entry for it.

⇒ **SO THE GENERAL FORM OF EVERY GATE LESSON THIS SESSION LEARNED HAS AN EXISTING, SERVED, PROJECT-AGNOSTIC HOME — AND THAT HOME IS CURRENTLY EMPTY ON ALL THREE COUNTS.** The lessons were recorded where they help this project's maintainers and not where they would reach the people the tool is for.

📌 THE GENERAL PRINCIPLE WORTH KEEPING, in his framing: **reflow2 designing itself is a TEST HARNESS, not the point.** Every finding from self-hosting should be asked one question before it is filed — *does this land in the served surface, or only in our own graph?* — and a finding that lands only in our own graph is unfinished work rather than a completed capture. `rule:the-self-host-always-trails-what-it-teaches` is the nearest existing node and says something adjacent but not this: it explains why reflow2's own design lags, not that self-host findings owe a served fix.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the other served skills carry the same shape of omission. Only `ci-gate` was read against this session's evidence; `link-artifacts`, `check-health` and `parallel-work` all touch the export and were not checked.

MEASURED 2026-08-13 by reading identity sidecars only, never opening a store. Seven reflow2 designs under ~/project carry an identity file. TWO OF THEM ANSWER TO THE SAME NAME:

  ~/project/reflow2/.reflow2/graph.id.json        graph_id "reflow2"  label "reflow2"        origin adopted
  ~/project/dev_storyflow/.reflow2/graph.id.json  graph_id "reflow2"  label "dev_storyflow"  origin adopted

Both are real, both populated, and the collision has stood since 0.14.0.

⭐ THE CAUSE IS NOT A BUG IN THE ADOPT PATH, and a first diagnosis that said so was wrong. `identity::resolve` adopts THE OLD SHARED DEFAULT ID when a store already holds design data under it — not the project name, not the path. Every graph used one constant before `cap:design-identity` landed, so EVERY PRE-IDENTITY STORE SERVED BY THIS BINARY ADOPTED THE SAME STRING. Two such stores therefore collide BY CONSTRUCTION, and n of them would give n.

AND THE ADOPTION WAS RIGHT. identity.rs states the alternative plainly: minting a fresh id for a populated store would be "a catastrophe of exactly the silent kind — the design would still be on disk, and reflow2 would open a new empty one beside it and report nothing wrong." `graph_id` is also part of the export's content hash, so adoption is what kept every existing export, chain link and committed record valid across the change. The migration chose correctly; the collision is its unpriced consequence.

EVIDENCE THAT MINTING IS CLEAN: the four `minted` designs on this machine — brainmaker 683f0090c245a5f1, flo2 1a97fc1f1de4d5d2, music_graph 4a496c576800020c, quantum_benchmarking_initiative ff86353849198623 — have zero collisions. `mint()` seeds fnv1a with nanoseconds, pid and canonical path, so it is unique by construction. Only the adopted ones collide, and `dynograph-foundation` escapes only because its own codebase carried a different default constant.

🛑 WHY IT MATTERS NOW RATHER THAN IN 0.14.0: `registry.rs` (2026-08-12) makes `graph_id` the KEY a session selects a design by — `rule:a-design-is-named-by-an-id-not-a-path` calls the id primary and the path a storage detail. `Registry::discover` accumulates into a `BTreeMap<String, String>` keyed on it, so a second design under the same id does not collide, warn or fail — IT OVERWRITES, and which one survives is decided by alphabetical order of the very path the id exists to hide. Demonstrated in crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/two_designs_can_share_one_id.rs: the registry reports 1 design where 2 exist, and `attach("reflow2")` binds to whichever sorted last while the other is unreachable by its own name.

⇒ So a defect that was harmless while ids were only labels became load-bearing the moment ids became addresses. Nothing enforces or checks graph_id uniqueness anywhere.

THE ASYMMETRY WORTH KEEPING: reflow2 is careful about id collisions ONE LEVEL DOWN and has nothing one level up. `mirror_surface` refuses a colliding NODE id and leaves the local node untouched, on the stated ground that "two designs using one id for different things is a naming conversation between their owners." The same hazard between two DESIGNS is a silent overwrite.

READ FROM SOURCE 2026-08-10, not inferred: two HEAL rules fire UNCONDITIONALLY on an edge type while their message names a condition the code never evaluates.

    heal.rs:971  unresolved_setup   iterates every ANTICIPATES edge and emits
                                    "'X' anticipates 'Y' but nothing follows through"
                                    — there is no follow-through test anywhere in the loop.
    heal.rs:906  contradiction      iterates every CONTRADICTS edge (unless alignment=supporting)
                                    and suggests `generate_decision`, while the rule's own doc
                                    comment at heal.rs:47 describes it as "two nodes joined by
                                    CONTRADICTS with NO RESOLVING DECISION". Nothing looks for one.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE SAME IN BOTH CASES AND IT IS NOT NOISE: THE SUGGESTED FIX PROVABLY DOES NOT CLEAR THE FINDING. Write the resolving Decision the contradiction rule asks for and the contradiction still fires. Build the thing an ANTICIPATES edge anticipates and the unresolved_setup still fires. The only ways out are deleting the edge or acknowledging the defect — so a design is PUNISHED FOR RECORDING THE RELATIONSHIP, and the cheapest way to a clean report is to stop recording anticipation and contradiction at all.

OBSERVED LIVE, WHICH IS HOW IT WAS FOUND. Recording `dec:merge-survivor-provenance` ANTICIPATES `dec:a-tied-merge-breaks-by-degree-not-by-alphabet` — an honest edge, since the older decision's own rationale says "consider ranking unset below authored in a future revision" — took detect_defects from 7 to 8 immediately, and no amount of building will take it back to 7.

THIS EXACT CLASS IS ALREADY FIXED ONCE IN THE SAME FUNCTION, sixty lines above. heal.rs:892-905 documents the CONTRADICTS/alignment=supporting bug: the loop read the edge TYPE and never the PROPERTY, so every correctly-modelled corroboration came back as a structural defect, and `dec:commands-are-the-exception` QUALIFYING `dec:skills-served` turned the graph red. Its recorded lesson is verbatim: "A property the detector ignores is a property that lies." The same sentence applies to a CONDITION the detector never computes — and the damage named there applies here too: the only ways out were to acknowledge a defect that is not one, or to stop recording the relationship.

WHAT A FIX WOULD HAVE TO DECIDE, because neither is obvious and this is not a repair proposal. For unresolved_setup: what COUNTS as follow-through — the anticipated node existing at all (trivially true, the edge points at it), reaching `accepted`, gaining a SATISFIES/REALIZES chain, or arriving in an epoch. For contradiction: what counts as RESOLVING — a Decision edged to both endpoints, or one edged to either, and whether a `proposed` Decision resolves anything. Both questions are real design questions and answering them wrongly converts an over-firing rule into an under-firing one, which is worse.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: the ANTICIPATES edge was NOT deleted to restore the count to 7. The edge is true, and removing a true relationship to satisfy a detector that fires unconditionally is the gaming this project warns against everywhere else. The defect belongs to the rule, not to the edge.

**ALEX'S TWO MACHINES PRODUCED THE SAME SYMPTOM — "he reported a bug that is already fixed" — BY TWO DIFFERENT MECHANISMS, AND THIS SESSION GOT BOTH WRONG BEFORE MEASURING THEM.**

═══ 🛑 WORK MACHINE (the five hand-typed ideas): HE WAS SIMPLY CORRECT ═══

Alex, 2026-08-14: *"My hand typed observations were using 0.28.0."* Measured against the tags:
```
v0.28.0   2026-08-11      <- what he was running
v0.29.0   2026-08-12
v0.30.0   2026-08-13
fadc197   2026-08-13   PR #172 — write_shareable_export AND detected_indent
```
`git merge-base --is-ancestor fadc197 v0.28.0` → **NO.** **BOTH of the items this session called "already fixed" landed AFTER the version he was running.**

⇒ **HIS REPORTS WERE ACCURATE FOR HIS VERSION. There was no missing committable export and no indent-preserving merge in 0.28.0, because neither existed yet.** This session repeatedly framed those two notes as describing behaviour that no longer exists and inferred a stale user from them. **The inference was backwards: he reported current behaviour, and it was fixed two days later.**

⭐⭐ **AND THE REAL FINDING IS THE CADENCE, NOT THE USER.** Three releases in three days (0.28.0 → 0.29.0 → 0.30.0, 11th to 13th August). **At that rate every user is behind by construction**, and any report they write is against a version that has already moved. `user-iterative-release-preference` asks for BOTH frequent very-minor releases AND a one-word update — **the first without the second guarantees a stream of reports about bugs that are already fixed, and guarantees the maintainer misreads them as staleness.** That is exactly what happened here, all day.

═══ 🛑 HOME MACHINE (the Grok feedback.md): A DIFFERENT MECHANISM ENTIRELY ═══

Alex: *"0.30.0 from home"* — binary current. But the Grok agent measured the project's `.reflow2/kit-version.json` at **0.11.0 / 0ec473e (2026-07-25)** and diagnosed it in its first paragraph: *"the kit sidecar and the process you are talking to are not the same generation."* This session read that as evidence of a stale install; it was evidence of a SPLIT.

`.reflow2/kit-version.json` is written by `reflow2_init.py` INTO the project and records **which kit set that project up**. It is a receipt for an install EVENT, not a live reading. So a binary updated to 0.30.0 leaves a project initialised by kit 0.11.0 exactly where it was — and the fixes that matter to that project (`write_shareable_export`, `detected_indent`) live in `tools/reflow2_init.py`, **a KIT file, not the binary.** Re-running the installer is the only thing that applies them, and nothing says so.

═══ 🛑🛑 WHY THE MAINTAINER CANNOT REPRODUCE THE HOME CASE ═══
```
~/.local/share/reflow2/kit -> /home/ajs7/project/reflow2      A SYMLINK to the checkout
```
while `tools/install.sh` gives a consumer a **tarball extraction** — a frozen copy. **The developer's kit cannot go stale by construction; the consumer's always can.** `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` arriving in the ENVIRONMENT rather than in a detector, and the sharpest instance recorded so far.

═══ WHAT IS AND IS NOT ESTABLISHED ═══

✅ Work machine ran 0.28.0 and its reports were correct for it.
✅ Home binary is 0.30.0; the home project's sidecar was 0.11.0.
⚠️ Whether the home machine's INSTALLED KIT is also old, or only that project's receipt — `reflow2 --version` reports the BINARY and nothing surfaces the kit's version. That is the gap the Grok report's own opportunities section proposed closing.
⚠️ Whether a stale kit costs anything concrete. A 0.11.0 `reflow2_check.py` would predate the LINEAGE (BL-107) and IDENTITY (BL-169) checks, so a consumer's CI gate could be silently weaker than this project's — **not verified.**

⇒ TWO UPDATE SURFACES, ONE UPDATE COMMAND: the binary and the per-project kit. `install.sh` serves the first. A project already set up is served by nothing.

A digest is a digest whichever dialect it arrives in (crates/reflow2-core/tests/checksum_dialect.rs) — 14 cases, 9 new for BL-160. PREFIX (BL-125): a bare hex digest matches its own `sha256:`-prefixed baseline and vice versa, the drift event id is identical whichever dialect was observed, and both counterweights hold — a genuinely different digest still reports `checksum_change` with its `realizes` edges intact, and a non-hex fingerprint is left verbatim. LENGTH (BL-160): a full 64-char digest matches a 16-char baseline and a truncated observation matches a full baseline, on the drift comparison AND on `set_artifact_checksum`'s would-move-the-baseline guard — the half that is not a gate problem at all but a BL-157 bulk sweep failing on every short-registered artifact for a change that never happened. When the two dialects agree the LONGER digest stays on the record, which also makes the accept idempotent ACROSS dialects: re-stating it coarsely mints one claim, not two. FIVE COUNTERWEIGHTS, and they are what keep the length rule from being a way to stop noticing: two FULL digests sharing their first sixteen characters are still drift (the case a truncate-both-to-N would pass); a truncated observation that disagrees WITHIN its own length is still drift; a genuinely different digest is still refused as a first baseline, still naming the disposition that would be honest; prefix tolerance does not escape the `sha256:` dialect, so `blake3:zz` and `blake3:zzzz` stay different; and an EMPTY digest agrees with nothing, because every string starts with the empty string. No minimum prefix length is imposed, deliberately — a short baseline is a weak baseline, but its strength is decided when it is REGISTERED, and a read side refusing to honour what the write side accepted is the same write/read disagreement this suite exists to close. Content store round-trip and failure modes: the same bytes yield the same hash and are stored once; get(hash) returns exactly what put() took; a blob whose bytes no longer match its hash is REFUSED on read rather than returned (content addressing is only worth having if it is checked); a missing blob fails loud naming the hash and what referenced it; an interrupted write leaves no partial file, proven by writing to a temp path and renaming. PLANNED — written before the build so the shape of the proof is settled first.

The store on the MCP surface (crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/tools.rs, 5 cases): text round-trips and a re-put reports `already_present` rather than looking like new work; NON-UTF-8 BYTES survive the JSON boundary as base64 and come back base64 unchanged, which is the whole reason that field exists; passing both `text` and `base64` is REFUSED rather than resolved by picking one, and passing neither is refused as a mistake rather than stored as an empty blob; `exists` answers false for an unstored hash without erroring, because that is the call someone makes to ask "do I have everything?"; and A SERVER WITH NO --content-path CONFIGURED REFUSES BY NAME instead of inventing a directory — blobs are committed, so where they live is a decision about the consumer's repo.

A folder becomes ONE design, in the rounds a single document costs (crates/reflow2-core/tests/corpus.rs, 8 cases). The load-bearing four: two specs naming the same component converge on ONE node while each keeps its own provenance Fragment; three documents pin to ONE epoch, not three; a re-run reports the already-ingested document as SKIPPED and not failed, so resume is derived from the graph rather than bookmarked; and a document that cannot be taken is NAMED with why while its siblings still ingest. Plus the cost property — three documents cost the same ROUNDS as one, which is what makes a corpus affordable. MUTATION-CHECKED: breaking the batching (gather one document per round instead of all) takes rounds 3 to 7 and documents_pending 3 to 1, and exactly the two tests that name those properties fail.

An unmodelled subtree is reported and a modelled file is not; ONE OPAQUE ARTIFACT LEGITIMATELY CLAIMS THE MASS BENEATH IT (900 vendored files under a single registered directory report zero unclaimed — the trap a file-count ratio would fall into, since it would score correct coarse modelling as 1-of-901 and call it failure); a shared name prefix does not claim across a directory boundary; exclusions come back NAMED with the rule that excluded them and their mass does not inflate the silence; regions rank by mass so the biggest silence sorts first; a registered location the sweep never mentioned is named; and an empty sweep claims nothing rather than reading as full coverage (crates/reflow2-core/tests/coverage.rs, 7 cases)

A cycle finding names what it walked (crates/reflow2-core/tests/cycles.rs) — 6 new cases of 15. A loop through ONE shared contract names that contract and says no DEPENDS_ON is involved; a genuine TWO-contract service cycle is NOT blamed on the model but still names both; a plain DEPENDS_ON tangle says it is direct and names no contract; a MIXED cycle claims neither pure case, because saying 'no DEPENDS_ON' there would send a reader to check their interface model while real code coupling sits in the loop. PLUS the medium pair, which is the case that matters: a round trip through two library/data contracts reports the medium, and THE SAME SHAPE over REST makes no foundation claim — without that counterweight the medium sentence would print on every contract cycle and mean nothing. MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS: collapse the interface-count discriminator and exactly the two-contract counterweight fails; drop interface attribution entirely (the pre-BL-141 behaviour) and exactly the three tests naming the new behaviour fail while the direct-DEPENDS_ON case stays green; force the foundation-medium claim always-true and exactly the REST counterweight fails. THE DESIGN WAS CORRECTED BY MEASUREMENT, not reasoning: the first discriminator keyed on the INTERFACE COUNT (one shared contract = coarse model), and reproducing the reporter's own cycle on their real design showed it misses their actual case — their loop runs through TWO interfaces and is structurally identical to a genuine service cycle. Only the `medium` separates them. Verified end to end by reconstructing their pre-workaround model from a read-only snapshot of their live graph: the exact loop they reported, `cmp:fundamental-detection → cmp:midi-renderer → cmp:fundamental-detection`, now names both contracts and the medium.

A decomposition is asked what it dropped: the question fires per decomposed parent and names the parent; a requirement nobody split is silent; only DECOMPOSES counts, so satisfaction and derivation never raise it; the recorded answer stops the question and survives in reviewed_gaps; CHANGING THE SPLIT RE-ASKS with a new id, because the earlier answer was about those children; a parent already reporting delivered outranks one still open AND says so; and the finding NEVER names what is missing (crates/reflow2-core/tests/detect.rs, 7 cases). MUTATION-CHECKED FIVE WAYS, each killed by exactly the test that names it: dropping the detector registration (5 dead), flipping is_aggregate to true so a stale answer silences a changed split (1), anchoring only the parent (2), removing the delivered severity bump (1), and making the finding suggest what to add (1).

The schema's declared defaults are readable, checked, and injected only where injection is a statement (crates/reflow2-core/tests/schema_defaults.rs, 7 cases). WHY THIS EXISTS: `default:` in the schema YAML is executed by dynograph-core at WRITE time (schema.rs:507 inserts any missing property that declares one), which is where 3,207 stored values across 59% of this design came from — an injected value and a chosen one stored identically, so absence meant nothing. THE CASES: declared_defaults() parses all of them from the embedded YAML with no new dependency, and a floor assertion fails loudly if the line shape ever moves and the parser silently stops seeing them; schema_default() resolves by type and property, and answers None rather than guessing for a property that declares none — GATED_ON.min_level is deliberately undefaulted because defaulting it would pick a risk posture for the user; the ten properties removed for BL-198 step 1 are asserted ABSENT after a plain constructor call, which is the behaviour change itself; a value the caller DOES supply is still stored, so absence and choice are finally distinguishable. AND THE COUNTERWEIGHTS, which are the point rather than an afterthought: `Requirement.status = proposed` and `provenance` are asserted STILL INJECTED, because the whole certainty doctrine reads them and removing those would break derivation rather than clean it; `Requirement.lineage = original` is asserted still injected too, and it is there because it CAME OFF the confirmed removal list — requirement_lineage.rs refused the change, since `original` is the base case of a three-way classification whose other values (`decomposed`, `derived`) are set explicitly by operations. THE CASE THAT EARNS ITS KEEP BEYOND THIS ROUND: every_declared_default_is_a_legal_value_of_its_own_enum is a cross-check nothing could previously make — the validator checks stored values against `values`, the parser ignored `default` entirely, so a default naming a value its own enum forbids was invisible to both. WHAT IS NOT COVERED, stated rather than discovered later: nothing here proves the ten removed are the RIGHT ten. That was a per-property judgement made by the owner on measured evidence (single-valued in the data, no string-literal occurrence anywhere, no setter), and three mechanically-obvious candidates were kept on evidence — the reflex that single-valued means informationless was wrong three times in ten.

The degraded surface comes out of the door the caller asked for: with the graph genuinely held by another process AND --http given, an HTTP client still completes the handshake, still finds the reason in its instructions, and can still call reflow2_unavailable — plus the startup line says DEGRADED rather than letting an operator read 'serving over HTTP' and walk away. 4 cases in tools/test_degraded_server.py, measured against a real held lock. It caught the fault it was written for: against the v0.14.0 code all four fail with 'nothing ever listened on the port the caller asked for', because main.rs's Err arm called serve(stdio()) and never read cli.http (BL-105).

Measured against a REAL held lock: a peer handshakes, the reason arrives in its instructions, one unmistakable tool is served with remedies, a free graph still gets the whole surface — and a held graph exports with the caveat, leaving no residue (tools/test_degraded_server.py, 9 cases)

A dependency that is itself a reflow2 design can say so, and one that is not stays silent (crates/reflow2-core/tests/depends.rs, 2 cases added, 12 passing in the file). LINKED: graph_id round-trips through the store and appears in reflow2.toml as `graph_id = \"dynograph-foundation\"`. UNLINKED, which is the case that carries the doctrine: a second declaration without one round-trips as None AND its manifest entry contains no graph_id line at all — absence is stored as absence, so a reader can tell \"this dependency has no reflow2 design\" from \"nobody recorded whether it does\". BLANK IS NOT A VALUE: a whitespace-only graph_id is treated as unstated rather than as a design whose id happens to be blank. A TEST-AUTHORING SLIP WORTH KEEPING: the first version of the blank case asserted the whole manifest contained no \"graph_id =\", which passed for the wrong reason and then failed for the right one — the [reflow2] header always emits the design's OWN graph_id, so the assertion had to be scoped to the dependency entry. The test caught the test.
Delivery is derived from the thread, and goes backwards when the evidence does

The manifest is derived and the derivation never rewrites history (crates/reflow2-core/tests/write_side.rs) — 8 cases. Every Artifact and Component enters the manifest with its checksum frozen; looking writes nothing (the release_report is still empty after a non-applying call); a re-run adds nothing and, after the live baseline has MOVED, still reports what shipped; an artifact with no checksum still ships and is named in without_checksum; an exclusion that names nothing is refused with the whole call written back out; an exclusion that names something comes back by name rather than by omission; an unknown release is refused; and the end-to-end payoff — one call clears the unreleased_component gap that a partial hand-typed manifest leaves open. MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS, each failing exactly the one test that names it and nothing else: force apply always-true and only the looking-is-not-writing case fails; drop the exclude validation and only the typo'd-exclusion case fails; drop the already-present guard and only the frozen-checksum case fails — which is what proves the guard is doing work rather than the test passing for free. PROVEN ON THE REAL SURFACE: driven over stdio JSON-RPC against the built binary on a copy of reflow2's own 1200-node design, one call produced 160 INCLUDES edges covering all 104 capabilities, the re-run added 0, and the typo'd exclusion came back as "Node not found: Artifact or Component art:nope". It also independently surfaced art:detect as the one artifact with no baseline — the same hole a full reconcile_artifacts sweep found the same hour by a different route.

Describing a design at a path changes nothing, and something-unnamed never reads as nothing (crates/reflow2-core/tests/discover.rs, 7 cases). The load-bearing case asserts the directory tree is BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after a describe, because opening a store to inspect it writes a schema stamp and MINTS an identity where there is none — so the obvious implementation would name a design by the act of looking at it. Also pinned: a store with no identity reports `unnamed` and NEVER `absent`; a corrupt identity file warns against starting a design rather than being swallowed; a real design is named from its sidecar alone; opted-in-but-empty is its own state; and a sweep returns one row per path including the absent ones. MUTATION-CHECKED: making describe write an identity when none exists — exactly what opening would do — flips the state from `unnamed` to `design` and changes the tree, failing precisely the two tests that name those properties while the other five stay green.

A declaration round-trips intact; one without a version is REFUSED because the version is what a surface is taken as-of; a build taking something undeclared is reported (the reliance nobody agreed to); a pin the build has moved past is reported; a declaration the build no longer takes is reported; a feature forwarded by name but never declared is reported; agreement says so plainly; declaring nothing reads as "nobody has said" rather than "depends on nothing"; and the manifest names which reflow2 wrote it, empty or not (crates/reflow2-core/tests/depends.rs, 10 cases). PROVEN ON THE REAL DEPENDENCY: reflow2's actual v0.11.0 pin reconciles with 0 findings, and a simulated undeclared bump to v0.12.0 correctly reports both the version mismatch and the newly-taken crate.

A new design mints a name of its own, it survives reopening, two designs are told apart, an unreadable identity is refused rather than defaulted, the label changes while the id cannot — and the migration case: a store already holding a design under the shared id KEEPS it and stays readable. Closes with the payoff: two independently created ON-DISK designs mirroring each other's published surface, which was impossible while every graph shared one constant (tests/design_identity.rs, 7 cases)
detect.rs
dimensions.rs

A discontinued thing stops being unfinished work, and the marker is READ (crates/reflow2-core/tests/discontinued_is_read.rs, 6 cases). THE DEFECT CASE: a capability withdrawn by an accepted Decision raises no gaps — the content store had read `realized` with a `passing` check for two days after its code was deleted. THE AUTHORITY CASE: a `proposed` decision to withdraw has withdrawn nothing, which is rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word on the retire path. THE CASCADE: the requirement a withdrawn capability served drops back to unsatisfied and is asked about again, so a discontinuation is not invisible one hop away. THE VISIBLE COUNT: delivery falls AND reports satisfied_only_by_discontinued, because a number that moves with no explanation is the silent-drop failure forbidden everywhere else. TWO COUNTERWEIGHTS carry the weight: a live capability beside a discontinued one is still asked about, and OBSOLETES from something that is NOT a Decision (a superseding epoch) does not discontinue — without that, any obsoleting edge would silence a capability. MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS, each verified applied before running: dropping the accepted-only check fails the authority case alone; accepting OBSOLETES from any source fails two; disabling all three detector reads fails the defect case. ⚠️ WRITTEN AFTER THE IMPLEMENTATION, not before — the third such instance recorded on 2026-08-11 (fact:implement-first-cost-an-edge-case-2026-08-11), and the cost showed up as a first draft asserting the wrong detector would fire: deleting the only artifact zeroes unrealized_capability's population, so unverified fired instead. The assertions now name the PROPERTY (it is asked about at all) rather than a detector, which is closer to the contract. NOT COVERED: an OBSOLETES edge whose target no longer exists, and discontinuation is read for Capabilities only — Components, Interfaces and Artifacts have no reader.
Drift reports which way it went, and names what the design has wrong

An edge to a node that does not exist is refused, not written — THROUGH EVERY TYPED HELPER, not only through create_edge. Found 2026-07-25: authored_by accepted contributor id "person:anthony", which was never created; the edge was stored, get_node returned null for its target, and a phantom AUTHORED_BY sat in the graph until noticed by eye. THE GUARD LANDED IN create_edge (graph.rs:297, 2026-07-28) AND WAS ALREADY TESTED THERE — write_side.rs holds four cases: missing target refused, missing source refused, refusal leaves nothing behind, a legitimate edge still accepted, and an unknown edge type still named FIRST (vocabulary errors before instance errors). What none of those covered is the helpers: every one of them calls create_edge directly, while the original defect was in a typed helper. So crates/reflow2-core/tests/edges_need_both_ends.rs is an AUDIT over all 16 public helpers that join two pre-existing nodes, plus a size-floor test so the table cannot quietly shrink, an atomicity case (a refused authored_by leaves no edge on its source), and a counterweight across three modules so breaking all sixteen is not the cheapest way to pass. The audit shape is deliberate: BL-183 found exactly this divergence on the node side, where 16 of 18 add_* constructors had drifted from the generic path. MUTATION-CHECKED, AND THE RESULT WAS NOT THE EXPECTED ONE: disabling the guard failed 14 of 16, not 16 — `documents` and `release_includes` carry their own existence checks before delegating (artifact.rs:519/525, operate.rs:336) and still refused. That is safer rather than broken, and it is recorded because it changes what the file proves: fourteen helpers depend entirely on the shared guard and would regress together, two would hold. OUT OF SCOPE and named: constructors that create their own source node, the bulk form (covered by bulk.rs under dec:bulk-is-all-or-nothing-with-per-item-findings), and gate_on, which takes a struct and validates a rung range first.

Every served skill is named by at least one shipped slash command, and a skill that loses its command turns the lint red naming the skill (tools/skill_lint.py, `== commands ==`). The counterweight to `every command names a skill that exists`, which had guarded only the opposite direction since 2026-07-28 — a command rotting into a dangling reference — while a skill nobody fronted was checked by nothing and nothing pinned the count. Coverage is NAMED BY a command, not SAME NAME AS one, so the short aliases (/gaps → detect-and-ask, /where → where-am-i) still count. MUTATION-CHECKED: removing getting-started/commands/capture-session.md turns exactly this check red and names `capture-session` in the failure.

A capability proven only on a rig says so; ONE real check ends the simulation-only claim (reaching reality must show, since leaving the rig is the point of the progression); a passing check naming no environment is UNPLACED and explicitly not assumed real — unknown is not simulated either; and a capability with nothing passing is absent from the report entirely rather than appearing as proven-nowhere, because that is unverified_capability's question (crates/reflow2-core/tests/evidence.rs, 4 cases)

The evidence-quality family, all three axes with their counterweights (crates/reflow2-core/tests/evidence_quality.rs) — 18 cases. TIME: an accept dated after the check reports stale, a re-run after the accept is current, an undated side is UNKNOWN and counted rather than silently passed, and a failing check cannot refresh a claim. INPUT: a parameter every passing check pins is reported narrow, ONE check that sweeps it ends the narrowness however many others pinned it, one suite is broad about one claim and narrow about another through the SAME node (the case a per-node property would have to average away), a check stating no scope is unscoped and never read as broad, a comma in a parameter name is refused, and scoping a pair with no VERIFIES edge is refused. INDEPENDENCE: a check the target was calibrated against is CONSUMED, a check that produced the anchor is consumed, a calibration on the realizing artifact counts, correcting the anchor reaches what was fitted to it through the impact table — and the two counterweights, that an independent check beside the fit restores the claim and that a calibration against evidence no check rests on is not circular. MUTATION-CHECKED ON ALL THREE AXES: force freshness never-stale and exactly the two stale tests fail while both counterweights stay green; drop the swept-beats-pinned filter and exactly one test fails; mark every check consumed and BOTH independence counterweights fail — which is what proves the rule does not simply condemn every calibrated design. FOUND BY DOGFOODING BEFORE IT SHIPPED: comparing dates as whole strings called 2026-07-28 stale against 2026-07-28T14:52:00-04:00, an ordering nobody recorded, asserted by the very report that exists to stop that — now same-day is Unknown, pinned by a test, with the counterweight that an earlier DAY is still stale.
confirm.rs

The CONTRACT is checked, not the judgement. skill_lint asserts detect-and-ask states all of it: offer a reading; carry what would change it; present the options as a SELECTABLE list; put the RECOMMENDATION FIRST and mark it; give every option its consequence including the ones not recommended; and answer in the USER'S language, stated language-independently. Plus two negative checks that are the load-bearing half: NO served text hardcodes English as the answer language (so the rule cannot be implemented as English-only — the trap Anthony named), and NO requirement status, decision status or gap acknowledgement is written in the same act as a recommendation. Whether a recommendation is GOOD, and whether the language was correctly matched, are semantic and stay evidenced by trials — deliberately no LLM evals in CI. PLANNED.

test_reflow2_check.py — 13 cases, 2 new for BL-160: an untouched file whose baseline was registered at 16 hex chars gates GREEN with the gate hashing the whole file (the workaround it used to carry is gone, so green now means the CORE agreed rather than that the caller pre-truncated), and the counterweight beside it — the same short baseline on a genuinely edited file still gates RED.
genesis.rs
A mode can be chosen after genesis, preserves the project, and refuses an unknown value

The granularity reading stays quiet when it should (crates/reflow2-core/tests/granularity.rs) — 9 cases, and most of them are silences. Anthony's objection is what shaped this suite: "avoid monoliths" IS a subjective design principle, so the module deliberately does not detect monoliths — it detects that two records the design already holds disagree about how many things there are (N Capabilities vs one Artifact) and refuses to say which side is wrong. THE LOAD-BEARING TEST IS `a_uniformly_coarse_design_is_not_punished`: eight artifacts each swallowing four capabilities produce NO finding, because a breadboard-phase design where everything lives in one file has nothing to be out of line with — dec:maturity-restructuring-delta's trap as an executable guarantee. `the_observation_carries_no_verdict` asserts the serialized report contains none of severity / suggested_fix / monolith / too big / should be split / violation / defect. `two_capabilities_in_one_file_is_not_worth_saying` pins MIN_DISTINCTIONS against a real statistical weakness found while writing the tests: counts pile up at one, the standard deviation collapses, and the distributional cutoff alone fires on noise — the test asserts z clears the bar and that the finding is suppressed anyway. `several_coarse_artifacts_mask_each_other` records z-masking as a known property rather than leaving it to be discovered in the field. Verified against reality twice: run on the committed design it names exactly one artifact (art:service, 10 capabilities, z=6.46, alone in the design), and run on the v0.21.0 export — BEFORE the observation was ever made — it names the same one at 9 capabilities, z=5.75, which is what makes this discovery rather than a rule fitted to a known answer.

A seat the server HANDED OUT but never leased reads `unknown` on a shared server, not `live` — proven over the served tool surface (mint_seat → claim_region → claim_report), not by calling register_seat by hand. Six cases in two dedicated binaries: crates/reflow2-core/tests/seat_liveness_shared.rs (the predicate, plus that a leased seat still answers Live/Gone and that unknown ≠ gone) and crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/mint_seat_liveness.rs (end to end through claim_report, that an unobservable seat is not reported as a ghost, and that mint_seat's advisory says it cannot observe the session and names release_claim). SPLIT FROM ver:claim-liveness deliberately, on the 2026-08-07 precedent: that check is passing and its own name states its scope as "proven end to end over stdio", which is the single transport where #100's registry applies — so it stood for a transport it never touched. Both defect-bearing cases were run as positive controls with the fix disabled and both FAIL, so neither is vacuous. Own test binaries because declare_serving_many_sessions is a process-global one-way latch and tests/claims.rs asserts the stdio reading of the same call.

heal.rs — the structural detectors, plus propose/apply atomicity. PLUS the degree-zero Decision rule (2026-08-01, crates/reflow2-core/tests/unreachable_decision.rs, 6 cases): a Decision with NO edges in either direction is reported by `orphan_node`, Warning when its status is `accepted` and Info otherwise. FOUND BY RUNNING THE HEALTH SKILLS ON OUR OWN DESIGN AND DISBELIEVING THEM: check-health and detect-and-ask both returned clean — detect_defects 0, hierarchy_issues 0, dimension_drifts 0, propose_heal 0 operations — and a hand count of zero-degree nodes then found `dec:sanitize-spof-accepted`, an ACCEPTED single-point-of-failure disposition with no edges at all, the only one of five such dispositions not linked to what it disposes. `disconnected_community` cannot see it: it reports clusters of ≥2, and a node joined to nothing is never a cluster. THE STAKE IS NOT TIDINESS — a zero-degree Decision is unreachable by propagation so it never enters an impact analysis, and a disposition specifically can never EXPIRE, because expiry is computed from the affected set (`ver:reviewed-defects`), so a conditional judgement silently becomes permanent. THE RULE IS DEGREE-ZERO, AND MEASUREMENT CHOSE IT AGAINST THE STATED RECOMMENDATION: the narrow-looking form, an accepted Decision with no incoming GOVERNED_BY, fires on SIX of reflow2's own, five with degree 1–3 — connected, merely not through that edge. That is [BL-42] exactly, where this same detector reported a well-connected Capability missing one named link, became 20 of 31 defects, and was cut back to a single rule. Degree-zero fires on ONE and is self-limiting: ANY edge silences it. THREE COUNTERWEIGHTS, and the first is the one measurement demanded: a Decision reached by any edge at all (a CONTRADICTS, not a GOVERNED_BY) is silent; a `decision:ack:` review record is silent, because structure.rs already excludes those from the design network as judgements ABOUT the design (`ver:acknowledgement-not-structure`) and all twelve of reflow2's own are accepted by construction; and a proposed decision point is Info, never a defect, because firing on a legitimate parking spot is firing on correct work. The pre-existing Artifact-realizing-nothing rule is pinned unchanged, so BL-42's cut-back is not reopened. MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS, each failing exactly the one test that names it: key on missing GOVERNED_BY → only the any-edge counterweight fails, which is BL-42 reproduced; drop the review-record exclusion → only that case; grade everything Warning → only the proposed-is-Info case. MEASURED ON THE REAL DESIGN with a freshly built binary against a throwaway import of the committed export: 3 findings across 1225 nodes — one Warning (`dec:sanitize-spof-accepted`, now fixed by wiring `cmp:ingest GOVERNED_BY` it, matching the four sibling dispositions) and two Info, both proposed decision points.
hierarchy.rs

Computed evidence reaches its axis without becoming a verdict (crates/reflow2-core/tests/ility.rs) — 11 cases, weighted to the refusals. THREE LINES DEFENDED AT ONCE. (1) NO SCORE IS EVER DERIVED — asserted as JSON field names rather than prose, because the report legitimately says the words 'grade' and 'score' while explaining what it refuses to do, and the first version of this test tripped on its own explanation. Collapsing findings into maintainability: 0.62 is the lossy move dec:readiness-is-an-observation-the-threshold-is-the-judgement already refused for TRL. (2) ADVERSE IS INHERITED, NEVER RE-JUDGED: a finding counts against an axis only where the computation that produced it already calls it a defect. Modularity is a ratio, a trajectory band is a POSITION `maturity` refuses to grade, a granularity observation is one `granularity` refuses to call a defect, and a surprising connection may be hidden coupling OR a creative link — all reported as context, because relabelling them here would overrule a module that deliberately declined to judge and would smuggle back the thresholds those modules were built without. (3) IT MUST NOT PRETEND: performance, security, scalability and observability report NOT INFORMED with the reason rather than reading clean. THE ASYMMETRY IS DELIBERATE AND TESTED: an asserted good score over adverse evidence is flagged, but an asserted LOW score over a quiet axis is NOT — 'no detector fired' is an absence of evidence, and treating it as evidence would be the reading claiming a clean axis is healthy, which it cannot know. MUTATION-CHECKED against five seeded regressions. Four were caught. THE FIFTH WAS INERT AND EXPOSED A MIS-NAMED TEST RATHER THAN A HOLE: deleting the HealSeverity::Info guard fails nothing, because all four mapped categories are Warning-or-Critical by construction and orphan_node is already excluded by mapping to no axis — so the test was renamed from an_info_defect_... to an_unmapped_defect_category_..., which is what it actually proves, and the guard's unreachability is stated at its site. A surviving mutation is not proof a test is weak; check the mutation first.

The bulk import door describes itself, reports every fault at once, and stops demanding the receiver's own identity (crates/reflow2-core/tests/export.rs, 6 new cases of 18). BL-138: a document of nodes and edges and nothing else — which is literally what the adopt skill instructs — imports, and the edge list may be omitted entirely; `graph_id` was demanded from hand authors and then NEVER READ by the operation demanding it, which is what made it worth removing rather than documenting. COUNTERWEIGHT, and the reason this is not just deleting a requirement: `mirror_surface` still REFUSES an unidentified document by name, because mirroring records where a surface came from and guards against mirroring a design into itself, and neither question is answerable without the id — the same shape as BL-119, where one requirement was right for a round-tripped export and wrong for a hand-authored one. BL-118: four faults in one document now cost ONE round trip instead of four, each reported with its position (`nodes[1]`, `edges[0]`) so a 9,000-line document can be navigated; ATOMICITY IS PINNED SEPARATELY — a rejected import writes nothing at all, including the items that were valid, which is the half the reporting session named as working notably well and the row said must not be touched. The shape is `dec:bulk-is-all-or-nothing-with-per-item-findings` reused rather than reinvented, and it still returns an ERROR rather than an ok-with-failures report, so a rejected import can never read as success. BL-117: the document shape now rides `import_graph`'s own description — the envelope, the optionality of every metadata field, that endpoint types are recovered rather than stored, and that each node must be COMPLETE (BL-139's honest half, delivered whichever way the merge question goes).
ingest.rs

The ambient agent drives INGEST to completion with no LLM provider, and the design lands with its provenance Fragment; an ABANDONED handshake writes NOTHING (the prepare rounds replay against a throwaway graph, so a half-answered run cannot strand half a design); the same input takes the same rounds, since each call is self-contained and no session state is held; and an answer nothing asked for is reported rather than ignored. 4 Rust cases, plus an end-to-end run over real MCP against the built binary: 4 rounds, 6 nodes, with the recovered Decision and Component both present (crates/reflow2-core/tests/ingest_handshake.rs)

A FRESH project gets docs/design/<project>.json, it is not covered by any ignore rule, and it is a real chainable document — plus the three surfaces that name it (tools/test_init.py, a CI gate at ci.yml:58)

A project with NO instruction file still gets one the primary harness reads; the created file is a pointer, not a second home for instructions (size-bounded); an existing instruction file is appended to, not replaced; a project that already owns a convention gets NOTHING invented; the eight slash commands ship and match the kit source exactly; and SKILLS ARE STILL NOT COPIED, so the exception stays an exception (tools/test_init.py, 6 cases). Plus the guards that make shipping commands safe: a command naming a skill that does not exist FAILS the lint, and the .claude/commands mirror is byte-checked against the kit (tools/skill_lint.py). The nudge's counting AND its own promise are both trustworthy (tools/test_loop_nudge.py) — 47 cases, 11 new in BL-163 on top of the 8 across BL-161 and BL-111. BL-163 · PRECEDENCE, NOT PRESENCE: a session that edits code, records a ChangeEvent and never calls propagate_change is nudged — the defect was that the impact-check shape keyed on `changes == 0`, firing only when a session recorded NOTHING, so writing the ChangeEvents up AFTER the edits satisfied the very trigger meant to catch writing them up after the edits. ROOT CAUSE IN ONE LINE: `CHANGE_OPS` held `record_change` and `add_change_event`, both RECORDING ops, and no set counted `propagate_change` or `propagate_from` at all — the hook could not separate recording from looking because it never counted looking. THE COUNTERWEIGHT THE ROW DEMANDED AND THE CASE PINNED FIRST: a session that propagated gets NOTHING, and `propagate_from` counts as looking too, because the impact-check skill sends a speculative "what would this touch?" straight to it. THE CONJUNCTION IS THE GUARD, all three clauses load-bearing and each with its own test: `edits > 0` (a pure design session has no blast radius to compute), `changes > 0` (what keeps this from becoming a second, thresholdless bypass nudge), `propagates == 0`. BL-161'S PRECEDENT HELD: "you never propagated" is a NEGATIVE claim, so a tally rebuilt after an unreadable one drops it, exactly as "the graph was never consulted" does. THE WRITE NUDGE STILL TAKES PRECEDENCE and that test is not vacuous — disabling the write branch fails it. MUTATION-CHECKED SEVEN WAYS, each failing exactly the tests that name it: never count propagation (6 failures, both counterweights); drop `changes > 0` (7 failures, including BL-90's ENTIRE bypass family — the measurement that proves that clause is what stops this swallowing the older branch); drop `edits > 0` (1); drop `propagate_from` (1); drop the once-only claim (1); remove the branch entirely, i.e. ship the defect (5); and disable the write branch (14, including the precedence case). A FOURTH DEFECT WAS FOUND BY THE TESTS FAILING, not by reading: `update_state` re-serialises from an explicit key whitelist — a THIRD hand-kept copy of the state's key set beside `blank_state` and `parse_state` — so the new counter incremented in memory and was silently dropped on every write. That is BL-159's shape a third time, inside one file. BL-161 · STATE INTEGRITY: a 60-hook CONCURRENT burst against a seeded tally lands every increment and wipes no sticky field; against the pre-fix script the same burst returned touched=false, artifacts=0 and 6 of 60 edits, because a non-atomic write plus an error-swallowing read let one hook store zeros over the session's record. COUNTERWEIGHT: a tally rebuilt after an unreadable one keeps counting — an existing case required that and was right — but can no longer support the hook's negative claims, because the calls that would refute them are exactly what was lost; and the POSITIVE claim, "N writes went unchecked", still fires after a restart, so the flag is not an off switch. BULK FORMS: set_artifact_checksums, create_nodes and gaps_to_prompts tally as the singular forms they replace. BL-111 · FIRES ONCE: a second stop CYCLE does not nudge again (the promise is per SESSION, and it rested on the harness's stop_hook_active, which is per cycle and never persisted), all THREE blocking branches keep it, and TWO CONCURRENT HOOK PROCESSES on the same Stop produce exactly ONE message — which is the case it was filed from and is not exotic, since reflow2 installs machine-wide AND a project may carry its own registration and the two command spellings do not dedupe. COUNTERWEIGHT: the claim is spent by NUDGING, not by STOPPING, so a session with nothing owed stops silently and keeps its one nudge. THE MUTATION CHECK ONCE CAUGHT MY OWN TEST PASSING FOR FREE: the first concurrency helper looped communicate(), which blocks until each child exits, so the children ran serially and the test stayed green against the UNFIXED script.

loop_status answers what is owed to ONE NAMED PERSON, and a scoped answer can never be read as the design being clean (crates/reflow2-core/tests/report.rs, 5 cases). SPLIT OUT of ver:owed-to-a-contributor rather than widening it, because that check's statement is about the COUNTER and it was passing before any of this existed — a green check that quietly grows to stand for behaviour it never exercised is the failure this project has now written down twice. THE CASES: assigned decisions are LISTED, not merely counted, carrying decision_id, name and approver_id (flo2's F4, hit independently here the same day where finding two meant jq-ing the export); scoping to one contributor returns only their assigned decisions and names them in `next`; scoping does NOT make an unassigned musing somebody's problem, so the deliberate quiet around thinking out loud survives; an unknown contributor_id is REFUSED rather than answered with an empty list, with a positive control proving the same call succeeds for a real id — because a typo would otherwise produce 'nothing is owed to you', the most reassuring possible reply and the one least likely to be questioned. THE LOAD-BEARING CASE is a_scoped_answer_never_reads_as_the_design_being_clean: a contributor with nothing assigned gets clean=true, AND scope.not_attributable is non-empty, AND `next` says in words that the rest carries no per-person attribution, AND the design-wide counters come back unchanged by scoping. That is the guard against the defect class this project has now met four times — a value that cannot tell a real NONE from an I-CANNOT-SAY. WHAT IS NOT COVERED, stated rather than left to be discovered: nothing verifies attribution for any relationship OTHER than the approver edge, because none is attributed. Claim-derived ownership and gap-to-judge attribution are unbuilt, and req:the-loop-says-what-is-owed-to-a-person names that as a real open question rather than an oversight.

A position never becomes a verdict (crates/reflow2-core/tests/maturity.rs) — 10 cases, most of them restraint. THE LOAD-BEARING CASE IS `a_function_first_design_is_located_not_condemned`: function done, structure undeclared, and the profile must locate the design without calling it broken — it asserts the serialized profile contains none of severity / defect / violation / "should be" / "too low" / failing, and that `not_observed_about` says outright that where the design SHOULD be is not reflow2's to state. THE FRONTIER IS RELATIVE — the lowest-scoring band — so there is NO THRESHOLD anywhere in this reading to default, argue with or quietly tune, which is stronger than the stated cutoffs `granularity` needed. An empty population reads as UNMEASURED with its reason, never as zero, because scoring an absence invents a deficiency; an empty design reports as empty rather than immature. Bands scoring ABOVE the frontier are reported as NORMAL, since real designs run ahead of themselves — reflow2 itself has shipped 22 releases and 84.5% passing assurance with 0% of its 73 component couplings declared through a contract. A one-sided contract does not count as a declared seam. Assurance counts a PASSING check, not an existing one (dec:passing-is-verified). Requirements the user settled OUT leave the intent population, because dropping something is their word too. MUTATION-CHECKED against five seeded regressions — frontier as the highest band, empty populations scored zero, one-sided contracts counting, assurance ignoring status, and dropped requirements still counted — all five caught. The first attempt at the one-sided mutation was a no-op and was rewritten the way the bug would actually be written before it counted as evidence.

THE CASE THAT WAS FILED: a disconnected cluster is reported with NO suggested_fix_type and WITH repair_is_a_judgement naming it a judgement — `generate_bridge` used to sit there, and where the separation is correct, following it fabricates relationships nobody stated to silence a warning about a separation that is right. A process-global that is secretly per-design cannot be added without accounting for it. An allowlist over runtime `static` / `thread_local!` / `lazy_static!` declarations across every crate's `src` tree: an unlisted global FAILS the build, and adding one costs a written reason why it is not per-design. Owed by rule:per-design-state-is-never-a-process-global from the moment it was set enforced (Anthony, 2026-08-09). BOUND, stated rather than left to be discovered: it detects DECLARATIONS only. It says nothing about whether a struct field is correctly scoped — the per-design metadata riding on ReflowService today (graph_path, write_gen, read_hint) is not a global, and moving it per-graph is cap:graph-registry's planned work rather than a violation. NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN, not assumed: a static planted in crates/reflow2-core/src/temporal.rs (a different crate from every allowlist entry) failed the check by name and line, and the file was reverted. A second test guards the guard — an allowlist entry naming a global that no longer exists fails, because a stale exemption pre-authorises the name for whoever adds it back.

An open decision is owed only once somebody has been ASKED to settle it (crates/reflow2-core/tests/report.rs, 5 cases): a proposed Decision alone is silent; adding AUTHORED_BY role=author is still silent, because recording whose idea it is says nothing about who owes an answer; role=approver makes it owed and names it in `next`; settling it clears the debt. OWNED_BY attributes gaps to a person and never drags them into a blast radius (crates/reflow2-core/tests/report.rs, 2 tests). CASE 1, gaps_standing_on_ground_you_own_are_attributed_to_you: owning nothing attributes nothing (an unowned design is the ordinary state, not a finding); after taking ownership, the gap on that node appears in gaps_on_owned_ground naming WHICH owned node it stands on and never a node owned by someone else; scoped `clean` goes false, because a gap on your own ground is owed by you as surely as a decision you were asked to settle; and the `next` line says it in words. POSITIVE CONTROL: a second contributor who owns nothing gets an empty list from the identical call — without it, an implementation that attributed every gap to everybody would pass every other assertion. AND A CONSERVATION CHECK: the design-wide gap count is unchanged by scoping, so narrowing never makes the design look smaller. CASE 2, owning_something_does_not_drag_a_person_into_a_blast_radius: propagate_from over an owned node at depth 5 must not reach the Contributor — the exclusion AUTHORED_BY and CLAIMS already carry, asserted rather than assumed for the third of the kind. WHAT IS NOT COVERED, stated rather than left to be found: nothing verifies that ownership is the RIGHT attribution for any given node, because that is a judgement; and no check exists for unowned ground, because none was built.
