The function-preservation check refuses what it cannot classify (crates/reflow2-core/tests/preserve.rs) — 15 cases. The suite defends the REFUSAL half, because a classifier that recognises ALLOCATED_TO and calls everything else benign hands out green certificates for changes it never looked at (BL-170's fourth quadrant). So: an unknown node type blocks certification, an unresolvable edge endpoint blocks it, a reworded capability blocks it (a rename and a scope change are the same bytes), and a known function change OUTRANKS an unknown, because more information cannot un-move a capability. `every_schema_node_type_has_a_class` walks the live schema — all 29 types — and fails the build when a new one lands with no class, so the omission is caught before a release rather than by a false green; it also asserts three known types are present, so it cannot pass by iterating an empty set. The load-bearing case is `depends_on_is_read_from_its_endpoints_not_its_type`: DEPENDS_ON is the functional DAG between Capabilities and packaging between Components, and classifying by edge type alone would file all 51 of this design's cross-system dependencies as function changes. MUTATION-CHECKED against four seeded regressions (unknown types falling back to structure, the verdict order inverted, one function endpoint sufficing for a function edge, a reworded function node waved through) — each was caught, none silently.

Readiness gates an increment and the roadmap says why (crates/reflow2-core/tests/readiness.rs) — 15 cases, plus 7 driven over real stdio in smoke_mcp.py §7b2. THE WORKED EXAMPLE IS THE ROW'S OWN: laser satellite refuelling, where the demonstrator and the fielded increment demand TRL 3 and TRL 7 of the SAME converter and get two different answers — which is the whole reason the threshold rides the edge rather than either endpoint. THE TWO REFUSALS ARE WHAT IS ACTUALLY PINNED: an increment with no stated threshold reports `ungated` and NEVER ready (mutating that verdict to achievable_now fails exactly the one test the item rests on), and a gate whose technology has no level and no clearing forecast makes the whole answer `indeterminate` — skipping it instead, and computing a date from the gates that happen to carry evidence, fails FIVE. That second one is the subtler half: an optimistic date built by ignoring the inconvenient record is exactly the undefendable slide-roadmap BL-68 exists to replace. ALSO PINNED: the slowest gate decides (an increment waits for its slowest dependency) while within one gate the earliest clearing forecast wins; a measured TemporalFact is not a projection; TRL and MRL are not interchangeable on EITHER the measured or the forecast path; the highest measured level wins rather than the latest, because readiness is ratcheted evidence and picking by date would make the answer depend on how completely history was backfilled; a rung outside 1-9 is refused at both ends rather than clamped; a Capability is gated by the same machinery as a Release; and GATED_ON is a traceability edge, so a slipped technology reaches the blast radius of every increment gated on it. MUTATION-CHECKED NINE WAYS, each failing exactly the tests that name it. THE MUTATION CHECK FOUND A HOLE IN THIS SUITE RATHER THAN CONFIRMING IT: dropping the ladder filter from the FORECAST path passed everything, because every existing case exercised only the MEASURED path — so an MRL projection silently clearing a TRL gate would have shipped a date built on the wrong evidence entirely. The sibling case was added and the mutation now fails it. AND THE SURFACE BUG ONLY THE REAL BINARY SHOWED: the typed Rust tests were green while the served JSON carried `Ungated` and `{"GatedUntil": ...}` — Rust's default enum tagging in an otherwise snake_case surface — caught by driving it over stdio, which is AGENTS.md's "every other layer is a client we wrote" landing on new code the same day it was written.

Search-before-you-add fires from the TOOL and forces a choice, and the check cannot quietly stop working. SIX CASES in crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/search_first_fires_at_the_tool.rs. THE DEFECT CASE: two requirements stating one idea in different words — the second is REFUSED, and the refusal NAMES the match and BOTH routes, so it is a choice rather than a wall. THE ROLLBACK CASE is what makes the design sound: the node must be written before it can be searched (it needs to rank for its own text to give an in-query baseline), so a refusal that left it behind would create the very duplicate it refused — asserted by reading the node back and requiring null. BOTH DELIBERATE ROUTES are tested because the refusal recommends them: SHARPEN (call with the existing id — a revision, never refused, and its neighbour is seeded so the guard is the only reason it passes) and CREATE ANYWAY (`distinct_from` naming what was read and rejected). THE COUNTERWEIGHT decides whether this is usable at all: an unrelated requirement is created with no friction and no advisory — a check that refused often would be routed around, and a rule people route around is worse than no rule. CROSS-TYPE: a Capability restating a Requirement is caught, the pair most worth catching because a capability backed out of a requirement's own words is unmotivated_capability waiting to happen. MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS, each verified applied before running rather than assumed: disabling the refusal fails 3 cases; removing the rollback fails the rollback case alone; ignoring `distinct_from` fails both deliberate routes. ⚠️ A FOURTH MUTATION EXPOSED A VACUOUS TEST OF MY OWN and is why the neighbour seeding exists: the first revision test passed whether or not the guard was there, because a revision with no near neighbour has nothing to report either way — the same vacuous-branch failure ver:the-server-says-when-it-is-stale was written about, reproduced here and caught by mutating rather than by reading.

properties.criteria: PASSING as of 2026-07-24, proven by an automated test, not by an upstream claim. Location: crates/reflow2-core/tests/search.rs, featured arm (`cargo test -p reflow2-core --features fulltext --test search`), three cases. (1) `a_natural_language_question_finds_the_requirement_it_asks_about` — two full questions phrased in a person's own words, each of which shares only some vocabulary with its target, must rank that target first against a distractor sharing common words; pins the CLASS, not the instance. (2) `one_unmatched_word_does_not_erase_a_real_match` — the minimal pin reduced to one variable: `upgrade` matches, and `upgrade zzzznotaword` must still match. (3) `a_question_the_design_does_not_answer_still_returns_nothing` — the other half of the contract, because a disjunction that matched everything would destroy the information content of 'no hits' and bring the duplicate problem back from the other direction. REGRESSION PROOF, the step that makes this more than a decoration: the pins were temporarily reverted to dynograph-foundation v0.10.0 and the suite re-run. Cases (1) and (2) FAILED against the pre-fix build with exactly the reported symptom (SearchResult { hits: [] }) and PASS against v0.11.0; case (3) passes against both, correctly, since AND semantics also refused an unrelated question. A test that passes on the broken build proves nothing, so this was verified rather than assumed. Root cause fixed upstream in dynograph-foundation v0.11.0 (PRs #76, #77): TextIndex::search now matches tokens as a ranked disjunction — at least one token required, BM25 ordering — instead of requiring every token.

A write lands in the attached design ONLY — two designs open simultaneously in one process, written to in interleaved turns, and each store proven to contain only its own nodes; plus the two properties that half rests on: the STORE is the isolation boundary rather than the id (naming another design's graph_id from a different store serves nothing and writes nothing into it), and a reopen re-attaches to the same design even with a different design opened first and still held. NARROWED 2026-08-07 (epoch:isolation-check-scope-split): this node previously also claimed "a graph_id it was not attached to is REFUSED rather than served" and "a path is not an alternative route in", and was set PASSING while no test could reach either — both need a surface on which a session NAMES a design, and cmp:registry is planned. Those two clauses are now ver:a-session-cannot-name-another-design, which is PLANNED and says so. dec:one-process-many-stores was accepted conditional on ALL FOUR, so its condition is HALF MET, and the graph now computes that instead of resting on a comment in a test file.

Against a real server over real HTTP: two sessions get distinct MCP sessions, a write by one is visible to the other immediately with no export or merge, their claims carry DIFFERENT seats (the bug that would have been silent — seats were minted per process), four concurrent readers all finish, and the served kit reaches an HTTP client exactly as it reaches a stdio one (tools/test_shared_sessions.py, 4 cases)

A similarity score does not decide identity: sibling names stay apart and true duplicates still converge (crates/reflow2-core/tests/sibling_merge.rs, 5 cases). Nine crates sharing the `dynograph-` prefix survive as nine nodes each carrying its OWN name — before BL-213 this was five, with two carrying a sibling's name. An abbreviation (Auth / Authentication) is never reported as distinguished; a version suffix (Auth Service v2) is; reordered tokens (Read Path Cache / Cache Read Path) still converge, so BL-186's ordering fix is untouched; and a held-back merge names the word that held it. MUTATION-CHECKED: disabling the discriminator restores the 5-of-9 loss and fails exactly the three tests naming those properties, while the two that should be insensitive to it still pass. FIELD-CHECKED against the real dev_storyflow document that found the defect: 9 of 9 crates survive.

skill_lint.py — the contracts the build refuses to let drift, enforced in CI on every push. (1) THE SKILLS' contract with the served surface: every tool a skill names is served, the three mirrors are byte-identical, frontmatter, the standing rule, the tool-convention register and its description budget, the detect-and-ask obligations. (2) THE BUILD'S OWN GATE LIST (BL-159, 2026-08-01), four checks over AGENTS.md's "A change is done when all of these are clean" block and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — two hand-kept records of one contract, where following the documented one exactly still produced a red build (PR #27). COVERAGE: every cargo/python3 gate ci.yml runs is either in the block or named in the blockquote as deliberately omitted, because a gate in neither is one a developer cannot know to run. FIDELITY: a listed gate is spelled exactly as CI runs it, FLAGS INCLUDED — and this is the load-bearing one the row did not ask for, because the defect that filed BL-159 was a flags difference on a gate that WAS listed (`-p reflow2-core` clippy lacking `-D warnings`), which coverage alone cannot see. Both rot directions are closed too: a documented gate ci.yml does not run, and an omitted name ci.yml has stopped running. THE SPLIT THAT KEEPS IT HONEST: the lint OBSERVES (is this line a gate at all — mechanical) and the document JUDGES (does it belong in the everyday subset — in AGENTS.md, where a human reads it). FOUND ON DAY ONE: `cargo test -p reflow2-core --no-default-features` and `test_check_doc_versions` sat in ci.yml and in neither list — the second being the exact trap the design anticipated, since `check_doc_versions` is a SUBSTRING of it and a substring match would have called it covered. MUTATION-CHECKED SEVEN WAYS, each failing exactly the check that names it: an undeclared gate in ci.yml → coverage; stripping `-D warnings` from the block → fidelity, which is BL-159's own defect reproduced; ci.yml dropping a listed gate → the phantom check; ci.yml dropping an omitted one → the stale-omission check; dropping the comment stripper → fidelity plus its own hermetic case; dropping the paragraph scoping → its two hermetic cases; dropping scoping AND the runner-word exclusion → the stale-omission check. THE CHECK CAUGHT A DEFECT IN ITSELF ON ITS OWN COMMIT: scanning the whole blockquote read the backticked words `cargo` and `python3` out of the new paragraph describing the lint and reported them as gates CI had stopped running. AND ONE REDUNDANCY IS REPORTED RATHER THAN HIDDEN — reverting the paragraph scoping ALONE leaves every real-file check green, because the runner-word exclusion covers the only two words today's prose backticks; the two are not redundant in general, so the scoping is pinned on synthetic text in tools/test_skill_lint.py where the redundancy cannot hide it. 14 hermetic cases there covering the parsing the real files cannot exercise.

A session that did design work, moved files, and never opened a skill is told so before it ends — and the correct sessions around it are not (tools/test_loop_nudge.py, class SkillLoadsAreCounted, 9 cases). MOST OF THE CASES ARE COUNTERWEIGHTS, because this branch ARMS a nudge where cap:skill-triggers only ever refined one: loading a single skill silences it; listing skills does NOT count as loading one (knowing the menu is not reading the recipe, and counting it would let a session tick the box); a session below the edit floor is left alone; a session that never touched reflow2 gets the blunter bypass message and NOT this one; and where another branch already fired, exactly one message is printed. Plus the two invariants every blocking branch here owes: it fires once per session, and a tally rebuilt after an unreadable one never makes the negative claim, because the get_skill calls that would refute it are exactly what was lost. THE LINE dec:adoption-is-reported-the-loop-still-computes DRAWS IS HELD AS A PROPERTY: the hook leaves the designed project byte-identical (no export, no store, no stray file), and a grep with a positive control asserts no skill counter is readable by anything in reflow2-core that computes debt. FOUND BY RUNNING IT: the first implementation incremented both new counters in memory and threw them away on every write, because the state key set is duplicated in three places and only two were updated — the same defect BL-163 hit, in the same file, under a comment that warns about it by name.

Shape-matching fires on the situation and stays silent otherwise: a file edit with no ChangeEvent names impact-check; a change recorded but never propagated ALSO names impact-check (BL-163); a recorded change with no artifact link names link-artifacts; a capture batch with no gap pass names detect-and-ask; a rendering with nothing stored names session-artifacts. AND THE COUNTERWEIGHT, which is the case that matters most: a session that did the right thing gets NOTHING — a trigger that fires on correct work is the failure BL-23 and BL-42 both name, and this capability exists to reduce nagging rather than add it. BL-163 CHANGED WHAT "THE RIGHT THING" MEANS, and the counterweight fixture with it: the sequence edit → record_change → link_artifact → add_requirement → detect_gaps used to pass this test, and now correctly fires, because it never once asked what the change reached. The assertion is untouched — correct work is still met with silence — and the old fixture is pinned by its own test as the defect. THE SHAPES STILL CANNOT ARM THE HOOK (`test_shapes_never_arm_the_hook_by_themselves` passes unchanged); the one branch that arms is BL-163's and lives outside the matcher, because the session it catches has no unchecked writes and has touched reflow2, so no nudge existed for a shape to refine.

A supporting CONTRADICTS edge produces no contradiction; an opposing one still does; and one with no alignment still does, so no design written before the fix changes behaviour (crates/reflow2-core/tests/contradiction_alignment.rs, 3 cases). The conduct rule is pinned where an edit that drops it turns red: both capture-intent and genesis must forbid asking the user which node type to use AND name describe_schema as the alternative (forbidding a question without naming the alternative is half a rule), and capture-intent must carry the routing table as a lookup table that names where it runs out. 2 cases in crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/served_skills.rs, 8 in the file, all passing. MUTATION-CHECKED: replacing "Never ask the user which node type" with its opposite across all three skill trees turned exactly the conduct test red and left the routing-table test green; reverting restored both. THE POINT OF PINNING IT HERE: this is a rule about how an agent behaves in conversation, and conversation leaves no node — loop_status reads perfectly clean through a session that breaks it, so a test on the served text is the only place it can be observed at all.

The LINEAGE clause of tools/reflow2_check.py, run in CI on every pull request: the committed export must record `prev_content_hash` equal to the content hash of the export it replaced, and a severed chain FAILS the build. Deliberately narrower than `ver:gate-suite`, which verifies `art:check` as one artifact — the gate makes several distinct guarantees (drift, orphan attachment, dependency reconcile, lineage) and one Verification standing for all of them cannot say which clause is still working. This one stands for the lineage clause and nothing else, so `rule:the-export-is-written-once-per-branch` has a check that is ABOUT IT. FIELD-EVIDENCED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: it fired twice on 2026-08-11 in one day's work — once on a double export across a `commit --amend`, chaining through a content hash no commit would ever hold, and once after a rebase where the three-way merge driver had merged CONTENT correctly and could not repair the chain. Both were real, both were caught before merge, and both are recorded in the rule's own how-to-follow-it text. WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, stated so the green is not read wider than it is: it checks the CHAIN, not whether the export is CURRENT with the live graph (that is the drift clause), and it cannot see a second export that was never committed. It also cannot distinguish a deliberate re-baseline from an accident — the message names three causes and asks the reader to pick, which is a refusal to guess rather than a hole.

A committed export survives export → import → re-export (tools/test_reflow2_check.py) — 5 cases. END TO END through the real binary: a coherent design round-trips clean and gates 0. THREE DETECTION CASES against a stub re-export, because driving these through the real binary could only ever produce a FAITHFUL round trip — which is the case that must NOT fire: a dropped node is caught AND NAMED, a dropped EDGE is caught and named (the dev_storyflow case was two VERIFIES edges, so a check watching only nodes would have missed it), and a property that comes back different is caught (import is an upsert and the schema has defaults, so a document can return COMPLETE and still not be the same design — the half a count cannot see). THE COUNTERWEIGHT IS THE FOURTH: a faithful round trip reports NOTHING, because a check that fires on a correct design runs on every commit and would be switched off inside a day. MUTATION-CHECKED TWICE, each killing exactly what it should: forcing the comparison to always agree fails the three detection cases and leaves the counterweight passing, which is what proves the counterweight carries weight; ignoring edges fails exactly the edge case and nothing else. PROVEN ON THE REAL DESIGN: run against reflow2's own 2,308-node export through the built binary, the round trip is clean and the gate's only finding was the checksum of the file this change edited.

A moved record reaches an ORDINARY read and names import_graph, an untouched one stays silent, and the installer writes both halves of the merge rule while leaving a driver somebody else set alone (crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/the_record_moved_and_the_session_is_told.rs + tools/test_init.py, both CI gates)

Three of four harnesses were made to LOAD reflow2 from the file the installer writes — OpenCode reports it CONNECTED, Copilot CLI lists it as a workspace server, Claude Code is daily use. VS Code remains unconfirmed and is named as such. Run 2026-08-14 on Ubuntu 24 by installing the harnesses (npm, no sudo) into a project set up by tools/reflow2_init.py, then asking each tool what it sees: `opencode mcp list` -> "✓ reflow2 connected", `copilot mcp list` -> "Workspace servers: reflow2 (local)". THIS IS THE CHECK THE 96-CASE SUITE CANNOT MAKE: those cases assert which FILES are written, and assert nothing about whether any harness reads them. It also CORRECTED the registry rather than confirming it — `copilot mcp --help` names its sources as ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json and workspace .mcp.json / .github/mcp.json, so Copilot CLI does NOT read .vscode/mcp.json and the entry labelled "Copilot / VS Code" was promising a harness that file does not serve.

properties.description: `docker/smoke.sh`, run by release.yml against the candidate image BEFORE the push. Starts the container on a uid-1000 volume, refuses immediately if the process exited (the failure this exists for is an instant exit, and waiting on a health probe would report it as a timeout instead of naming the cause), then waits on the image's OWN HEALTHCHECK, then makes one request from OUTSIDE the container — because an in-container probe cannot catch a bind to loopback. DEMONSTRATED 2026-08-15 both ways on a locally built image: PASSES in ~8s on the fixed Dockerfile, and FAILS in ~3s on a Dockerfile with the pre-v0.27.0 `--content-path` restored, printing `error: unexpected argument '--content-path' found` and exit 2. SCOPE, stated so this is not read as more than it is: it has not yet run in CI, and it proves the image SERVES, not that any tool behaves correctly.
properties.name: The published image starts, reports healthy, and answers on its port

The two absences are told apart, and neither is invented: an OpenCode project reports no_hook_for_this_harness with an advisory that asks for nothing to be installed; a Claude project with no hook still reports absent; a project that never named a harness reports absent rather than impossible; and a hook the user wired themselves wins over the recorded harness, so a working nudge is never called unreachable. 7 cases in crates/reflow2-mcp/src/nudge.rs (19 in the module, 190 in the crate, all passing). ALSO DEMONSTRATED LIVE against real projects with the rebuilt binary — loop_status returned {"no_hook_for_this_harness":{"harnesses":"opencode"}} for an OpenCode project and "absent" for one that never said. THAT LIVE RUN EARNED ITS KEEP: the unit tests passed while target/debug/reflow2-mcp was still the previous build, so `cargo test --lib` was proving the library and not the binary a user runs — rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object, caught on the day it was enforced.

A record that moved ahead of this seat is reported, and one that has not is silent. COVERS: the three consumption-free states (in_step / moved_but_current / behind) and the two fault states (missing / unreadable); that ordinary unexported work is NEVER reported, which is the property the whole design rests on; that two targets are independent and neither hides the other; that every known target is listed so an empty answer cannot read as all-clear; that the finding names both `import_graph` and the path and never reads as a refusal (no "refused"/"error"/"cannot"/"blocked"); that the expensive export is NOT built on the in-step path and is built exactly once when needed; and THE REGRESSION THAT MATTERS MOST — a record edited without restamping is still caught, because the check computes the content hash instead of believing the one the document states about itself. That last case was found end-to-end rather than by any unit test, after the first cut shipped believing the stamp and reported "in step" while somebody else's work sat in the file. NOT COVERED: the live MCP surface end-to-end (the served tool was exercised against a scratch graph via the CLI, not against a running server), and any behaviour of `import_graph` itself.

`served_by` STATES staleness rather than leaving a literal to be compared: the block carries `stale` and `stale_note`; an intact binary reads a definite `false`; `stale` is three-valued and a null SAYS unknown rather than borrowing the wording of a definite answer; the stale note names `--stop-shared`, says why a bare session restart changes nothing (`--shared` re-attaches to the same daemon), and warns that the respawn itself fails when the client's binary was replaced too. Five cases in crates/reflow2-mcp/tests/the_server_says_when_it_is_stale.rs. VERIFIED LIVE ON A RUNNING DAEMON, not only in fixtures, because the `true` branch cannot occur in a test process: a fresh daemon reported `stale: false, binary_mtime_unix: 1786248674`; `cargo build` was then run to relink the binary under it, and the SAME server reported `stale: true, binary_mtime_unix: null` on the next call. That second observation also settled an old puzzle — the `null` mtime dev_storyflow reported as 'best-effort, unavailable' is THIS SAME SIGNAL, since current_exe() returns a path carrying the `(deleted)` marker and metadata() fails on it. The note's wording is asserted against public constants rather than inside `if stale == true`, because a first draft guarded those assertions with that condition and they silently never ran — the vacuous-branch problem this work exists to catch, reproduced in its own test.

The served vocabulary connects the two halves of retirement: Capability.status's description names OBSOLETES, names `discontinued`, and says `cancelled`/`dropped` is absent ON PURPOSE rather than merely missing; and OBSOLETES's hint names the Decision as the source end, names what it computes, says only an ACCEPTED decision discontinues anything, and says the target's own status does NOT move (crates/reflow2-core/tests/discontinued_is_read.rs, 2 cases, 8 in the file). MUTATION-CHECKED BOTH WAYS: reverting Capability.status to the bare enum kills the first and nothing else; reverting OBSOLETES to its old one-line hint kills the second and nothing else. Pinned rather than trusted for the reason the standing rule is pinned in every skill — a description nothing reads back is one edit from silently disappearing.

The dependency check works without tomllib, and says what it cannot read (tools/reflow2_check.py, 2026-08-06, 3 cases). EQUIVALENCE: with tomllib blocked, the line reader returns results BYTE-IDENTICAL to tomllib on reflow2's own three Cargo manifests — same source, same v0.12.0 pin, the same five grouped crates. HONEST ABOUT ITS LIMITS: on a synthetic manifest holding a multi-line inline table and a [dependencies.X] sub-table, it read the one shape it understands and NAMED BOTH it did not — \"'spans' spans lines, not read\" and \"[dependencies.subtable] sub-table form not read\" — rather than returning a short list that would read as a complete one. WHY IT EXISTS: the check shipped reading only tomllib and its first CI run on reflow2's own repo reported \"could not read any build file to check them\", because ubuntu-22.04 carries Python 3.10. Correct locally, inert on most CI in the world. No `tomli`, no pip: the kit installs into other people's projects and a runtime dependency is a cost they did not agree to.

The convention rides the tool and stays bounded: the tools whose skills carry a non-inferable rule have that one sentence in their served description (checked against a named list, so adding a tool without considering it is caught); no description exceeds the sentence budget, because the cost of this is context paid on every session; and the toolsnap goldens still match, so the addition is a deliberate surface change rather than drift. Enforced in skill_lint alongside the existing served-tool-name checks. PLANNED.
find_tools answers a described job with the right tool, ranks an exact name first, and reports a miss as a miss (tools.rs)
A served tool refuses an argument it does not know — including a tool whose FIRST parameter is new, where the old surface has nothing to reject with (friction 2026-07-25, unwritten)
A coupling with no contract is named as one aggregate question, asks rather than drafts, and stays silent where there is nothing to declare (crates/reflow2-core/tests/detect.rs)

`reflow2 update` keeps its word distinct from `init`: a project carrying an install receipt may be updated; a project that was never set up is REFUSED and told to run `reflow2 init`; a project holding a DESIGN but no kit is refused too and told WHY (machine-wide install, in-repo half never run) rather than silently receiving a first install; and the shipped wrapper both dispatches `--update` and states that it never downloads, so nobody expects a new binary from it (tools/test_init.py, 4 cases, 100 in the file). Pins the DISTINCTION, not the refresh — the refresh is `install` and every other case in the file covers it. MUTATION-CHECKED THREE WAYS: accepting any directory kills two cases, dropping the design-without-kit branch kills exactly the one that names it, and dispatching `update` as a plain `init` kills the wrapper case. All refusals exit 1, verified by running them.

what_next answers in four bands, the exploration slot is not optional, and liveness is what makes the shaping band readable (crates/reflow2-core/tests/what_next.rs, 11 cases). THE ONE THAT MUST NEVER REGRESS is a_marked_decision_is_never_ranked_however_it_would_score: a `proposed` Decision carrying AUTHORED_BY role=approver is the user's own durable self-prioritisation — it already existed and was simply never named one — and no computed score may reorder it or demote it into the ranked band, so the test gives a marked decision every scoring signal available and asserts it still never appears there. MUTATION-CHECKED: removing the band-1 short-circuit fails exactly that test and no other. THE SECOND LOAD-BEARING CASE is a_decision_nothing_points_at_is_still_surfaced. Every ranking signal here is built on connectedness, so a decision nothing points at scores zero forever and would never be shown — dec:bl-155's unused-versus-unreachable trap arriving through a ranking instead of a usage count. A suite that only checked the ranking would stay green while the fifth slot was dropped as over-engineering, which is precisely what the two independent derivations of that slot (the Q-table framing, and Anthony's own "top 4 and bottom 1") exist to prevent. THE SHAPING BAND'S CASES PIN A CAVEAT THIS DESIGN RECORDED BEFORE THE CODE EXISTED: cap:what-next warned that raw GOVERNED_BY in-degree is the wrong signal because its top hit was a pruning decision governing ten DROPPED requirements, and a_decision_governing_only_retired_work_does_not_shape_anything IS that fixture — a 9-dead-node decision must lose to a 3-live-node one. MUTATION-CHECKED: removing the liveness filter fails exactly the two liveness tests and no others. breadth_of_governed_types_is_reported_but_never_ranks pins the refinement that was TRIED AND REJECTED on measurement — weighting by distinct governed types demotes every exemplar the capability names as correct, because governing eight Components is shaping and single-typedness is not shallowness — so `shapes` is reported and kept out of the score. ALSO PINNED: retired governed nodes are COUNTED and reported rather than silently dropped; the shaping band holds only ACCEPTED decisions, never open ones, because it answers a different question for a different reader; `alignment: supporting` on a CONTRADICTS edge is corroboration and must not raise the score, which heal.rs paid for once already; `decision:ack:` review records are excluded both as decisions and as governed sources, because they dominate raw GOVERNED_BY counts (measured, excluding them took that edge type from 867 to 255) so leaving them in makes the answer confidently wrong rather than merely noisy; the unexplored pick is stable across two readings of an unchanged design and ADVANCES when a decision is settled, since the core takes no clock and no RNG and the rotation is derived from the count of accepted decisions; and `not_shown` accounts for every open decision the answer omitted. WHAT IS NOT COVERED, stated rather than left to be discovered: nothing here checks that the WEIGHTS are right. They are a deliberately coarse guide against a stated acceptance criterion of "general ballpark", and the tests assert the ORDER the signals produce, never the absolute numbers.
